# Data Model

## A01: ProBuilderMesh core data structures

### FIELDS

ProBuilderMesh is the core MonoBehaviour component that stores all geometry and attribute data for editable meshes. Below is the complete enumeration of every constant, serialized field, non-serialized field, and internal property:

1. Constants:
- `k_MeshFilterHideFlags` (`HideFlags`): Set to `HideFlags.DontSave | HideFlags.HideInInspector | HideFlags.NotEditable` (when `ENABLE_DRIVEN_PROPERTIES` is defined) or `HideFlags.HideInInspector | HideFlags.NotEditable`. Conceals the internal backing `MeshFilter` component from the inspector.
- `k_HelpUrl` (`string`): Value `"https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.probuilder@latest"`.
- `k_IconPath` (`string`): Value `"Packages/com.unity.probuilder/Editor Default Resources/Icons/EditableMesh/EditableMesh.png"`.
- `k_UVChannelCount` (`int`): Value `4`. Maximum UV channels supported by the data model.
- `k_MeshFormatVersion` (`int`): Current mesh format version, value `2` (`k_MeshFormatVersionAutoUVScaleOffset`).
- `k_MeshFormatVersionSubmeshMaterialRefactor` (`int`): Value `1`.
- `k_MeshFormatVersionAutoUVScaleOffset` (`int`): Value `2`.
- `maxVertexCount` (`uint`): Maximum addressable vertex count per mesh, value `ushort.MaxValue` (65535).
- `k_UnitializedVersionIndex` (`ushort`): Value `0`.

2. Serialized Fields (Backing Mesh Data):
- `m_MeshFormatVersion` (`int`): Serialized version number for upgrading legacy data formats during `ToMesh()`.
- `m_Faces` (`Face[]`): Serialized array of `Face` objects representing polygons, triangle indices, submesh indices, and unwrapping settings (formerly serialized as `_quads`).
- `m_SharedVertices` (`SharedVertex[]`): Serialized array of `SharedVertex` objects grouping coincident spatial vertex indices (formerly serialized as `_sharedIndices`, `m_SharedVertexes`).
- `m_SharedTextures` (`SharedVertex[]`): Serialized array of `SharedVertex` objects grouping coincident UV0 texture coordinates (formerly serialized as `_sharedIndicesUV`).
- `m_Positions` (`Vector3[]`): Serialized array of local vertex positions (formerly serialized as `_vertices`).
- `m_Textures0` (`Vector2[]`): Serialized array of UV channel 0 texture coordinates (formerly serialized as `_uv`).
- `m_Textures2` (`List<Vector4>`): Serialized list of UV channel 2 texture coordinates (formerly serialized as `_uv3`).
- `m_Textures3` (`List<Vector4>`): Serialized list of UV channel 3 texture coordinates (formerly serialized as `_uv4`).
- `m_Tangents` (`Vector4[]`): Serialized array of explicit or generated vertex tangents (formerly serialized as `_tangents`).
- `m_Colors` (`Color[]`): Serialized array of per-vertex RGBA colors (formerly serialized as `_colors`).
- `m_UnwrapParameters` (`UnwrapParameters`): Lightmap UV2 generation settings struct containing `hardAngle`, `packMargin`, `angleError`, and `areaError` (formerly serialized as `unwrapParameters`).
- `m_PreserveMeshAssetOnDestroy` (`bool`): Determines if the underlying `UnityEngine.Mesh` asset is kept on disk when the component is destroyed (formerly serialized as `dontDestroyMeshOnDelete`).
- `assetGuid` (`string`): GUID identifier used when the 'Meshes are Assets' workflow is enabled.
- `m_Mesh` (`Mesh`): Direct reference to the compiled `UnityEngine.Mesh` instance.
- `m_VersionIndex` (`ushort`, default `0`): Monotonically incrementing counter used to track modifications and detect synchronization state with the compiled mesh.
- `m_IsSelectable` (`bool`, default `true`): Controls whether elements on this mesh can be selected in editor tools.
- `m_SelectedFaces` (`int[]`, default empty array): Serialized array of selected face indices pointing into `m_Faces`.
- `m_SelectedEdges` (`Edge[]`, default empty array): Serialized array of selected `Edge` structs.
- `m_SelectedVertices` (`int[]`, default empty array): Serialized array of selected vertex indices pointing into `m_Positions`.

3. Non-Serialized & Runtime State Fields:
- `m_CacheValid` (`CacheValidState` enum bitfield: `SharedVertex = 1 << 0`, `SharedTexture = 1 << 1`): Tracks validity of lookup caches.
- `m_SharedVertexLookup` (`Dictionary<int, int>`): Maps vertex index `i` to its corresponding group index in `m_SharedVertices`.
- `m_SharedTextureLookup` (`Dictionary<int, int>`): Maps vertex index `i` to its corresponding group index in `m_SharedTextures`.
- `m_Normals` (`Vector3[]`): Runtime cached normal vectors.
- `m_MeshRenderer` (`MeshRenderer`): Cached reference to sibling `MeshRenderer` component.
- `m_MeshFilter` (`MeshFilter`): Cached reference to sibling `MeshFilter` component.
- `m_InstanceVersionIndex` (`ushort`, default `0`): Runtime instance version counter used to detect duplication, instance creation, and session modification state.
- `m_SelectedCacheDirty` (`bool`): Dirty flag indicating cached selection counts and arrays need recalculation.
- `m_SelectedSharedVerticesCount` (`int`): Cached count of unique shared vertex groups in the current selection.
- `m_SelectedCoincidentVertexCount` (`int`): Cached total count of all coincident vertices across selected shared groups.
- `m_SelectedSharedVertices` (`HashSet<int>`): Cached set of shared vertex indices in the current selection.
- `m_SelectedCoincidentVertices` (`List<int>`): Cached list of all coincident vertex indices in the current selection.
- `s_CachedHashSet` (`static HashSet<int>`): Shared static hash set used to avoid allocations during UV projection and coincident vertex queries.

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, a custom Resource or Node (e.g. ProBuilderMesh3D extending Node3D or MeshInstance3D) can store these arrays in PackedVector3Array, PackedColorArray, PackedVector2Array, and PackedInt32Array. Godot ArrayMesh uses SurfaceTool/MeshDataTool and surface arrays (Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX, Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL, Mesh.ARRAY_TEX_UV, Mesh.ARRAY_TEX_UV2, Mesh.ARRAY_COLOR, Mesh.ARRAY_TANGENT, Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX).

### MESH REPRESENTATION

ProBuilderMesh uses a per-face unique-vertex topology model. In this representation, no two `Face` instances share identical vertex indices in `m_Positions`; every face owns its own discrete vertex indices. Coincident spatial positions and texture coordinates across faces are maintained through separate index grouping arrays:

1. Vertex Attribute Arrays:
- Positions are stored in `Vector3[] m_Positions`, where `m_Positions.Length == vertexCount`.
- Vertex colors are stored in `Color[] m_Colors`. If `m_Colors` is null, `GetColors()` returns an array filled with `Color.white`.
- Normals are stored in `Vector3[] m_Normals` (calculated on demand via `Normals.CalculateNormals(this)`).
- Tangents are stored in `Vector4[] m_Tangents` (calculated on demand via `Normals.CalculateTangents(this)`).
- Texture channels: Channel 0 is stored in `Vector2[] m_Textures0`; Channel 1 (lightmap UV) is stored directly on the `UnityEngine.Mesh.uv2` property; Channels 2 and 3 are stored in `List<Vector4> m_Textures2` and `List<Vector4> m_Textures3`.
- `HasArrays(MeshArrays channels)` tests for the presence of requested attribute arrays and verifies that each array's length matches `vertexCount`.

2. Faces and Polygons:
- Stored in `Face[] m_Faces`. Each `Face` encapsulates its triangulation (`int[] indexesInternal`, with length divisible by 3), material mapping (`int submeshIndex`), unwrapping parameters (`AutoUnwrapSettings uv`), smoothing group (`int smoothingGroup`), texture group (`int textureGroup`), and element group (`int elementGroup`).
- `faceCount` returns `m_Faces.Length`. `triangleCount` returns the sum of `face.indexesInternal.Length / 3`. `indexCount` returns the total count of vertex indices across all faces.
- `edgeCount` computes the sum of `face.edgesInternal.Length` across all faces.

3. Shared Vertices (Spatial Coincidence):
- `m_SharedVertices` (`SharedVertex[]`) defines groups of vertex indices that share identical 3D spatial positions. Each `SharedVertex` wraps an `int[]` of coincident vertex indices.
- `sharedVertexLookup` (`Dictionary<int, int>`) maps each vertex index `v` to its group index `k` in `m_SharedVertices`. When `(m_CacheValid & CacheValidState.SharedVertex) == 0`, `SharedVertex.GetSharedVertexLookup(m_SharedVertices, m_SharedVertexLookup)` rebuilds the lookup table and sets the cache flag.
- `GetCoincidentVertices()` retrieves all vertex indices coincident with a single vertex, a list of vertices, a set of edges, or a set of faces.

4. Shared Textures (UV0 Coincidence):
- `m_SharedTextures` (`SharedVertex[]`) defines groups of vertex indices that share continuous UV coordinates in channel 0.
- Cached via `sharedTextureLookup` (`Dictionary<int, int>`) and `CacheValidState.SharedTexture`.

5. Index Buffers & Formats:
- In `ToMesh()`, if `vertexCount > ushort.MaxValue` (65535), `mesh.indexFormat` is set to `Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt32`; otherwise it is set to `Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt16`.

```csharp
        public bool HasArrays(MeshArrays channels)
        {
            bool missing = false;

            int vc = vertexCount;

            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Position) == MeshArrays.Position && m_Positions == null;
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Normal) == MeshArrays.Normal && (m_Normals == null || m_Normals.Length != vc);
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Texture0) == MeshArrays.Texture0 && (m_Textures0 == null || m_Textures0.Length != vc);
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Texture2) == MeshArrays.Texture2 && (m_Textures2 == null || m_Textures2.Count != vc);
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Texture3) == MeshArrays.Texture3 && (m_Textures3 == null || m_Textures3.Count != vc);
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Color) == MeshArrays.Color && (m_Colors == null || m_Colors.Length != vc);
            missing |= (channels & MeshArrays.Tangent) == MeshArrays.Tangent && (m_Tangents == null || m_Tangents.Length != vc);

            // UV2 is a special case. It is not stored in ProBuilderMesh, does not necessarily match the vertex count,
            // and it has a cost to check.
            if ((channels & MeshArrays.Texture1) == MeshArrays.Texture1 && mesh != null)
                missing |= !mesh.HasVertexAttribute(VertexAttribute.TexCoord1);

            return !missing;
        }

        public IList<SharedVertex> sharedVertices
        {
            get { return new ReadOnlyCollection<SharedVertex>(m_SharedVertices); }

            set
            {
                if (value == null)
                    throw new ArgumentNullException("value");

                int len = value.Count;
                m_SharedVertices = new SharedVertex[len];
                for (var i = 0; i < len; i++)
                    m_SharedVertices[i] = new SharedVertex(value[i]);

                InvalidateSharedVertexLookup();

        internal Dictionary<int, int> sharedVertexLookup
        {
            get
            {
                if ((m_CacheValid & CacheValidState.SharedVertex) != CacheValidState.SharedVertex)
                {
                    if (m_SharedVertexLookup == null)
                        m_SharedVertexLookup = new Dictionary<int, int>();
                    SharedVertex.GetSharedVertexLookup(m_SharedVertices, m_SharedVertexLookup);
                    m_CacheValid |= CacheValidState.SharedVertex;

> **Godot Note:** Godot 4's ArrayMesh uses separate surfaces for each material. The ProBuilder data model corresponds to an intermediate editable representation where faces keep per-vertex attributes unshared, and an exporter compiles surfaces into an ArrayMesh or ImporterMesh.

### SUBMESH STRUCTURE

ProBuilderMesh organizes triangles and quads into submeshes corresponding to the materials assigned to the `MeshRenderer` component. The submesh mapping algorithm in `ToMesh()` proceeds through the following concrete steps:

1. Material Count Determination:
- `MaterialUtility.GetMaterialCount(renderer)` queries the `MeshRenderer.sharedMaterials` array length.
- `Submesh.GetSubmeshes(facesInternal, materialCount, preferredTopology)` is called to group faces by `face.submeshIndex` into `Submesh` objects containing `m_Indexes`, `m_Topology` (`MeshTopology.Triangles` or `MeshTopology.Quads`), and `m_SubmeshIndex`.

2. Empty Submesh Pruning and Material Compaction:
- `mesh.subMeshCount` is assigned `submeshes.Length`.
- `currentSubmeshIndex` starts at 0.
- For each submesh `i` from 0 to `mesh.subMeshCount - 1`:
  - If `submeshes[i].m_Indexes.Length == 0`, the submesh is empty. ProBuilder removes the corresponding material from `MaterialUtility.s_MaterialArray` at `currentSubmeshIndex`, sets `submeshes[i].submeshIndex = -1`, and decrements `face.submeshIndex` by 1 for all faces where `face.submeshIndex > currentSubmeshIndex`.
  - If `submeshes[i].m_Indexes.Length > 0`, `submeshes[i].submeshIndex` is assigned `currentSubmeshIndex`.

3. Degenerate Triangle Detection and Removal:
- For triangle topology (`MeshTopology.Triangles`), the algorithm iterates through triangle index triplets `tri` at step 3 (`indexes[tri]`, `indexes[tri+1]`, `indexes[tri+2]`):
  - Computes edge vectors: `ab = positions[indexes[tri + 1]] - positions[indexes[tri]]` and `ac = positions[indexes[tri + 2]] - positions[indexes[tri]]`.
  - Evaluates cross product magnitude: `if (Vector3.Cross(ab, ac).sqrMagnitude < Mathf.Epsilon)`, the triangle is degenerate. `numBadIndices` is incremented by 3.
  - Non-degenerate triangle indices are shifted left by `numBadIndices`: `indexes[tri - numBadIndices + k] = indexes[tri + k]` for `k in {0, 1, 2}`.
- If `numBadIndices > 0`, creates a compacted index array `fixedIndices` of length `indexes.Length - numBadIndices`.
- Calls `mesh.SetIndices(fixedIndices, submeshes[i].m_Topology, submeshes[i].submeshIndex, false)`.
- `currentSubmeshIndex` is incremented by 1.

4. Material Array Synchronization:
- If `mesh.subMeshCount < materialCount`, trailing unused materials are removed from `MaterialUtility.s_MaterialArray` via `RemoveRange`.
- If materials were modified, `renderer.sharedMaterials = MaterialUtility.s_MaterialArray.ToArray()` reassigns the updated material array to the `MeshRenderer`.

5. Face Material Assignment (`SetMaterial`):
- When `SetMaterial(IEnumerable<Face> faces, Material material)` is called, it searches `renderer.sharedMaterials` for `material`.
- If not found, it scans for an unused `submeshIndex` among `m_Faces` to replace.
- If all submesh indices are in use, it appends `material` to `renderer.sharedMaterials`.
- It sets `face.submeshIndex = index` on all target faces and calls `IncrementVersionIndex()`.

### REFRESH PIPELINE

The compilation pipeline converts the editable ProBuilderMesh data model into a hardware-ready `UnityEngine.Mesh`. The pipeline is split into two primary methods: `ToMesh()` (which establishes vertex buffers, index buffers, submesh topology, and material bindings) and `Refresh(RefreshMask)` (which updates vertex attributes on top of the existing topology).

1. `RefreshMask` Enum Bitfield:
- `RefreshMask.UV = 1 << 0`: Rebuilds UV channel 0 for Auto-UV faces and copies UV channels 2 and 3.
- `RefreshMask.Colors = 1 << 1`: Reapplies `m_Colors` to `mesh.colors`.
- `RefreshMask.Normals = 1 << 2`: Recomputes vertex normals based on face smoothing groups and assigns to `mesh.normals`.
- `RefreshMask.Tangents = 1 << 3`: Recomputes tangent vectors and assigns to `mesh.tangents`.
- `RefreshMask.Collisions = 1 << 4`: Updates `MeshCollider.sharedMesh` if a `MeshCollider` is present.
- `RefreshMask.Bounds = 1 << 5`: Calls `mesh.RecalculateBounds()`.
- `RefreshMask.All = 0xFF`: Executes all refresh operations.

2. Step-by-Step Execution in `Refresh(RefreshMask mask)`:
- Step 1 (`RefreshMask.UV`): Calls `RefreshUV(facesInternal)`. If `m_Textures0` is missing or desynchronized with `vertexCount`, initializes `m_Textures0 = new Vector2[vertexCount]`, sets `manualUV = false` on all faces, and processes all faces. For each face, if `face.manualUV` is false and `face.indexesInternal.Length >= 3`:
  - If `face.textureGroup` is 0 or invalid (`<= 0`), calls `UvUnwrapping.Unwrap(this, face)`.
  - If `face.textureGroup > 0` and `s_CachedHashSet.Add(textureGroup)` succeeds, calls `UvUnwrapping.ProjectTextureGroup(this, textureGroup, face.uv)` to project all faces in that group simultaneously.
  - Assigns `mesh.uv = m_Textures0`. If channels 2 or 3 exist, uploads them via `mesh.SetUVs(2, m_Textures2)` and `mesh.SetUVs(3, m_Textures3)`.
- Step 2 (`RefreshMask.Colors`): Calls `RefreshColors()`, which sets `filter.sharedMesh.colors = m_Colors`.
- Step 3 (`RefreshMask.Normals`): Calls `RefreshNormals()`, which executes `Normals.CalculateNormals(this)` (handling hard edges and smoothing groups) and sets `mesh.normals = m_Normals`.
- Step 4 (`RefreshMask.Tangents`): Calls `RefreshTangents()`, which executes `Normals.CalculateTangents(this)` using vertex normals and UV0 coordinates, then sets `mesh.tangents = m_Tangents`.
- Step 5 (`RefreshMask.Collisions`): Calls `EnsureMeshColliderIsAssigned()`. If `userCollisions` is false and a `MeshCollider` exists on the GameObject, assigns `collider.sharedMesh = mesh`.
- Step 6 (`RefreshMask.Bounds`): If `mesh != null`, invokes `mesh.RecalculateBounds()`.
- Step 7: Invokes `IncrementVersionIndex()`, incrementing `m_VersionIndex` and `m_InstanceVersionIndex`, and firing the `versionChanged` event.

3. Method Relationships:
- `Rebuild()`: Calls `ToMesh()` followed by `Refresh()`.
- `meshSyncState` (`MeshSyncState` enum: `Null`, `NeedsRebuild`, `Lightmap`, `InSync`): Evaluates whether `m_VersionIndex == m_InstanceVersionIndex` and checks whether lightmap UV2 is present.

        public void Refresh(RefreshMask mask = RefreshMask.All)
        {
            // Mesh
            if ((mask & RefreshMask.UV) > 0)
                RefreshUV(facesInternal);

            if ((mask & RefreshMask.Colors) > 0)
                RefreshColors();

            if ((mask & RefreshMask.Normals) > 0)
                RefreshNormals();

            if ((mask & RefreshMask.Tangents) > 0)
                RefreshTangents();

            if ((mask & RefreshMask.Collisions) > 0)
                EnsureMeshColliderIsAssigned();

            if ((mask & RefreshMask.Bounds) > 0 && mesh != null)
                mesh.RecalculateBounds();

            IncrementVersionIndex();
        }

        public void RefreshUV(IEnumerable<Face> facesToRefresh)
        {
            // If the UV array has gone out of sync with the positions array, reset all faces to Auto UV so that we can
            // correct the texture array.
            if (!HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture0))
            {
                m_Textures0 = new Vector2[vertexCount];
                foreach (Face f in facesInternal)
                    f.manualUV = false;
                facesToRefresh = facesInternal;
            }

            s_CachedHashSet.Clear();

            foreach (var face in facesToRefresh)
            {
                if (face.manualUV || face.indexesInternal?.Length < 3)
                    continue;

                int textureGroup = face.textureGroup;

                if (!IsValidTextureGroup(textureGroup))
                    UvUnwrapping.Unwrap(this, face);
                else if (s_CachedHashSet.Add(textureGroup))
                    UvUnwrapping.ProjectTextureGroup(this, textureGroup, face.uv);
            }

            mesh.uv = m_Textures0;

            if (HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture2))
                mesh.SetUVs(2, m_Textures2);
            if (HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture3))
                mesh.SetUVs(3, m_Textures3);

### SELECTION STATE

ProBuilderMesh stores selection state directly within the component for faces, edges, and vertices, enabling integration with Unity's undo system and editor tooling. The selection state architecture is structured as follows:

1. Selection Storage Fields:
- `m_SelectedFaces` (`int[]`): Array of selected face indices in `m_Faces`.
- `m_SelectedEdges` (`Edge[]`): Array of selected `Edge` structs, each containing vertex index pair `.a` and `.b`.
- `m_SelectedVertices` (`int[]`): Array of selected vertex indices in `m_Positions`.
- `m_IsSelectable` (`bool`): Determines whether elements can be selected on this mesh instance.

2. Selection Query Properties and Methods:
- `selectedFaceCount`, `selectedEdgeCount`, `selectedVertexCount` return the lengths of `m_SelectedFaces`, `m_SelectedEdges`, and `m_SelectedVertices`.
- `GetSelectedFaces()` returns a newly allocated `Face[]` array resolved by mapping `m_SelectedFaces[i]` into `m_Faces`.
- `selectedFaceIndexes`, `selectedEdges`, `selectedVertices` expose read-only collections (`ReadOnlyCollection<int>`, `ReadOnlyCollection<Edge>`).
- `GetActiveFace()` returns the most recently selected face (`m_Faces[m_SelectedFaces[selectedFaceCount - 1]]`), or `null` if selection is empty.
- `GetActiveEdge()` returns the most recently selected edge (`m_SelectedEdges[selectedEdgeCount - 1]`), or `Edge.Empty` if empty.
- `GetActiveVertex()` returns the most recently selected vertex index (`m_SelectedVertices[selectedVertexCount - 1]`), or `-1` if empty.

3. Coincident and Shared Selection Caching (`CacheSelection()`):
- When `m_SelectedCacheDirty` is true, `CacheSelection()` recomputes `m_SelectedSharedVertices` (HashSet of unique shared vertex indices from `sharedVertexLookup`) and `m_SelectedCoincidentVertices` (List of all vertex indices coincident with the selection).
- `selectedSharedVerticesCount` returns `m_SelectedSharedVerticesCount`.
- `selectedCoincidentVertexCount` returns `m_SelectedCoincidentVertexCount`.
- `selectedSharedVertices` and `selectedCoincidentVertices` expose the cached enumerables.

4. Selection Setter Synchronization:
- `SetSelectedFaces(IEnumerable<int> selected)`: Sets `m_SelectedFaces`; updates `m_SelectedVertices` to all distinct vertex indices belonging to those faces (`facesInternal[x].distinctIndexesInternal`); updates `m_SelectedEdges` to all edges belonging to those faces (`facesInternal[x].edges`); sets `m_SelectedCacheDirty = true`; invokes `elementSelectionChanged?.Invoke(this)`.
- `SetSelectedEdges(IEnumerable<Edge> edges)`: Clears `m_SelectedFaces` to empty array; sets `m_SelectedEdges`; updates `m_SelectedVertices` to all vertex indices from those edges (`m_SelectedEdges.AllTriangles()`); sets `m_SelectedCacheDirty = true`; invokes `elementSelectionChanged?.Invoke(this)`.
- `SetSelectedVertices(IEnumerable<int> vertices)`: Clears `m_SelectedFaces` and `m_SelectedEdges` to empty arrays; sets `m_SelectedVertices` to distinct vertex indices; sets `m_SelectedCacheDirty = true`; invokes `elementSelectionChanged?.Invoke(this)`.
- `ClearSelection()`: Sets `m_SelectedFaces = new int[0]`, `m_SelectedEdges = new Edge[0]`, `m_SelectedVertices = new int[0]`, and sets `m_SelectedCacheDirty = true`.
- `AddToFaceSelection(int index)`: Appends face index and updates selection arrays.
- `RemoveFromFaceSelectionAtIndex(int index)`: Removes face at array index and updates selection arrays.

        void CacheSelection()
        {
            if (m_SelectedCacheDirty)
            {
                m_SelectedCacheDirty = false;
                m_SelectedSharedVertices.Clear();
                m_SelectedCoincidentVertices.Clear();

### LIFECYCLE

ProBuilderMesh implements a rigorous lifecycle managing component initialization, duplication, destruction, undo/redo serialization, and prefab synchronization:

1. Factory Creation Methods:
- `ProBuilderMesh.Create()`: Instantiates a `GameObject`, adds `ProBuilderMesh`, sets `m_MeshFormatVersion = k_MeshFormatVersion`, calls `Clear()`, and returns the component.
- `ProBuilderMesh.Create(IEnumerable<Vector3> positions, IEnumerable<Face> faces)`: Instantiates a `GameObject`, adds component, and invokes `RebuildWithPositionsAndFaces(positions, faces)`.
- `ProBuilderMesh.Create(IList<Vertex> vertices, IList<Face> faces, IList<SharedVertex> sharedVertices, IList<SharedVertex> sharedTextures, IList<Material> materials)`: Full-attribute factory. Sets `renderer.sharedMaterials`, calls `SetVertices(vertices)`, sets `faces`, `sharedVertices`, `sharedTextures`, and executes `ToMesh()` followed by `Refresh()`.
- `ProBuilderMesh.CreateInstanceWithPoints(Vector3[] positions)`: Quad-point builder. Verifies `positions.Length % 4 == 0`, generates two triangles per 4 points (`[i, i+1, i+2, i+1, i+3, i+2]`), sets shared vertices via `SharedVertex.GetSharedVerticesWithPositions`, and compiles the mesh.

2. Initialization (`Awake` and `Reset`):
- `Awake()`: Calls `EnsureMeshFilterIsAssigned()`, `EnsureMeshColliderIsAssigned()`, and `ClearSelection()`. If `vertexCount > 0 && faceCount > 0 && meshSyncState == MeshSyncState.Null`, enters a `NonVersionedEditScope(this)`, executes `Rebuild()`, and invokes `meshWasInitialized?.Invoke(this)`.
- `Reset()`: When component is reset, if `meshSyncState != MeshSyncState.Null`, executes `Rebuild()` and invokes `componentHasBeenReset?.Invoke(this)`.

3. Destruction (`OnDestroy` and `DestroyUnityMesh`):
- `OnDestroy()`: Resets `m_MeshFilter.hideFlags = HideFlags.None`. Invokes `componentWillBeDestroyed?.Invoke(this)`.
- If `!preserveMeshAssetOnDestroy && Application.isEditor && !Application.isPlaying && Time.frameCount > 0`, invokes `DestroyUnityMesh()`. (The `Time.frameCount > 0` guard prevents destroying shared scene meshes during editor scene loading).
- `DestroyUnityMesh()`: Invokes `meshWillBeDestroyed?.Invoke(this)` if subscribers exist; otherwise executes `DestroyImmediate(gameObject.GetComponent<MeshFilter>().sharedMesh, true)`.

4. Mesh Uniqueness and Duplication (`MakeUnique` and `CopyFrom`):
- `MakeUnique()`: When duplicating or instantiating a GameObject, the new component shares the reference to the original `UnityEngine.Mesh`. Calling `MakeUnique()` creates an independent copy via `Instantiate(mesh)` (or `new Mesh()`), assigns `name = $"pb_Mesh{this.GetObjectId()}"`, and if `meshSyncState == MeshSyncState.InSync`, sets `filter.mesh = mesh`; otherwise calls `ToMesh()` and `Refresh()`.
- `CopyFrom(ProBuilderMesh other)`: Deep copies `positions`, `sharedVertices`, `sharedTextures`, cloned `faces`, UV channels 0 through 3, `tangents`, `colors`, `userCollisions`, `selectable`, and `unwrapParameters`.

5. Undo Integration & Serialization Callbacks:
- All mesh topology arrays (`m_Positions`, `m_Faces`, `m_SharedVertices`, `m_SharedTextures`, `m_Colors`, `m_Textures0`, `m_Tangents`) and selection arrays (`m_SelectedFaces`, `m_SelectedEdges`, `m_SelectedVertices`) are `[SerializeField]`, allowing Unity's `Undo.RecordObject` to serialize and restore full mesh state.
- Implements `ISerializationCallbackReceiver`: `OnAfterDeserialize()` calls `InvalidateCaches()` to invalidate `m_SharedVertexLookup`, `m_SharedTextureLookup`, and face caches.
- `NonVersionedEditScope`: An `IDisposable` struct that captures `m_VersionIndex` on construction and restores `m_Mesh.m_VersionIndex` and `m_Mesh.m_InstanceVersionIndex` on `Dispose()`, preventing transient initialization edits from marking version indices dirty.

6. Driven Properties & Prefab Support:
- Under `ENABLE_DRIVEN_PROPERTIES`, `ApplyDrivenProperties()` registers `m_Mesh` on `ProBuilderMesh` and `MeshCollider` using `SerializationUtility.RegisterDrivenProperty` to prevent prefab instance modifications from recording spurious overrides.
- Modifying `mesh` property calls `EditorUtility.SetDirty(this)` and `PrefabUtility.RecordPrefabInstancePropertyModifications(this)`.

## A02: Face, Edge, Vertex, SharedVertex types

### FACE: All fields (indexes, smoothingGroup, textureGroup, manualUV, submeshIndex, elementGroup). How indexes relate to mesh vertex array. Distinct vs shared vertex semantics.

The `Face` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Face`) encapsulates a polygonal surface element composed of one or more planar or non-planar triangles, mapping them to a specific submesh index, material assignment, UV unwrapping parameters, and smoothing group configuration.

### Serialized and Internal Fields
1. `m_Indexes` (`int[]`, serialized, legacy alias `_indices`): Stores the flat array of vertex indices forming the triangles of this face. The length of `m_Indexes` MUST be a multiple of 3 (`m_Indexes.Length % 3 == 0`). Every three consecutive entries `(m_Indexes[i], m_Indexes[i+1], m_Indexes[i+2])` define one triangle in clockwise winding order.
2. `m_SmoothingGroup` (`int`, serialized, legacy alias `_smoothingGroup`): Identifies the smoothing group ID assigned to the face. Default value is `Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone` (0). Faces assigned a positive smoothing group ID (`m_SmoothingGroup > 0`) share averaged vertex normals across coincident boundary vertices with other faces sharing the exact same group ID.
3. `m_Uv` (`AutoUnwrapSettings`, serialized, legacy alias `_uv`): Defines automatic UV projection parameters (anchor, fill, offset, rotation, scale, stretch, swapUV, flipU, flipV, useWorldSpace) used when `m_ManualUV` is false.
4. `m_Material` (`Material`, serialized, legacy alias `_mat`): Deprecated material reference, retained for serialization backward compatibility; superseded by `m_SubmeshIndex`.
5. `m_SubmeshIndex` (`int`, serialized): Zero-based index into the mesh renderer material array / submesh list. Defaults to 0.
6. `m_ManualUV` (`bool`, serialized, legacy alias `manualUV`): Boolean flag. When false, UVs are dynamically calculated using `m_Uv` (`AutoUnwrapSettings`). When true, UV coordinates are authored manually and preserved during mesh refreshes.
7. `elementGroup` (`internal int`, serialized): UV element group integer identifier used by the UV Editor window to group faces together for UV operations. Defaults to 0.
8. `m_TextureGroup` (`int`, serialized): Integer identifier used to group adjacent faces for continuous texture projection and tiling in Auto UV mode. Defaults to -1 (no texture group).
9. `m_DistinctIndexes` (`int[]`, non-serialized): Cached array of distinct, unique vertex indices referenced in `m_Indexes`. Initialized lazily via `CacheDistinctIndexes()`.
10. `m_Edges` (`Edge[]`, non-serialized): Cached perimeter boundary edges of the face, calculated lazily via `CacheEdges()`.

### Index Layout and Mesh Vertex Array Relationship
ProBuilder utilizes a disjoint per-face vertex storage architecture in its editable mesh representation (`ProBuilderMesh`). Every `Face` owns a dedicated subset of vertex entries in the mesh-wide vertex arrays (`positionsInternal`, `normalsInternal`, `texturesInternal`, `colorsInternal`). Consequently, the integers in `Face.m_Indexes` are direct index pointers into the `ProBuilderMesh` vertex arrays. Two adjacent faces that share a physical edge in 3D space do NOT point to the same vertex indices in `m_Indexes`; instead, each face references its own distinct vertex slots.

### Distinct Indexes vs Shared Vertex Semantics
- `distinctIndexes` (`ReadOnlyCollection<int>`): Represents the deduplicated set of local vertex indices referenced by this single face. For example, a quad composed of two triangles referencing 6 indices in `m_Indexes` `[0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0]` produces 4 distinct indices `[0, 1, 2, 3]`. Distinct indexes are strictly local to the individual face.
- `SharedVertex` (`sharedVertices`): Geometric coincidence across distinct faces is tracked in a separate top-level data structure (`ProBuilderMesh.sharedVertices` and `ProBuilderMesh.sharedVertexLookup`). While local vertex index 0 on Face A and local vertex index 12 on Face B are separate entries in `m_Indexes` and `positionsInternal`, they map to the same `SharedVertex` group index if their 3D positions are coincident.

### Cache Management and Geometry Algorithms
- `InvalidateCache()`: Nulls out `m_Edges` and `m_DistinctIndexes`. Invoked whenever `indexesInternal`, `SetIndexes()`, `ShiftIndexes()`, `ShiftIndexesToZero()`, or `Reverse()` modifies `m_Indexes`.
- `CacheEdges()`: Extracts perimeter edges from `m_Indexes`. Iterates over all triangles in steps of 3, constructing three directed `Edge` instances per triangle: `Edge(i0, i1)`, `Edge(i1, i2)`, and `Edge(i2, i0)`. It adds edges to a `HashSet<Edge> dist`. If `dist.Add(edge)` returns false (indicating an internal edge shared between two triangles of the same polygon), the edge is added to a duplicate list `dup`. Finally, `dist.ExceptWith(dup)` removes all internal edges, leaving only the boundary perimeter edges stored in `m_Edges`.
- `IsQuad()`: Evaluates `edgesInternal != null && edgesInternal.Length == 4`.
- `ToQuad()`: Validates quad topology and constructs an ordered array of 4 vertex indices `int[4] { edges[0].a, edges[0].b, c, d }` by matching contiguous endpoints around the perimeter.
- `ShiftIndexes(int offset)`: Adds `offset` to every integer in `m_Indexes` and invalidates caches.
- `ShiftIndexesToZero()`: Finds the minimum index value via `SmallestIndexValue()` and subtracts that minimum from every entry in `m_Indexes`.
- `Reverse()`: Invokes `Array.Reverse(m_Indexes)` to invert the triangle winding order (flipping the face rendering normal) and invalidates caches.
- `TryGetNextEdge(Edge source, int index, ref Edge nextEdge, ref int nextIndex)`: Traverses perimeter edges to find an edge connected at `index` that is not `source`.

### Face Rebuilding Pipeline (`FaceRebuildData`)
When modifying or appending faces, ProBuilder uses `FaceRebuildData` to bundle the `Face face`, `List<Vertex> vertices`, `List<int> sharedIndexes`, and `List<int> sharedIndexesUV`. The static method `FaceRebuildData.Apply` offsets the face indices by the current vertex buffer length (`index = vertices.Count`), updates the shared vertex and texture lookup dictionaries (`sharedVertexLookup.Add(localIndex + index, sharedIndexes[localIndex])`), shifts `face.indexesInternal` by `index`, and appends the vertices and face to the mesh.

        Edge[] CacheEdges()
        {
            if (m_Indexes == null)
                return null;

            HashSet<Edge> dist = new HashSet<Edge>();
            List<Edge> dup = new List<Edge>();

            for (int i = 0; i < indexesInternal.Length; i += 3)
            {
                Edge a = new Edge(indexesInternal[i + 0], indexesInternal[i + 1]);
                Edge b = new Edge(indexesInternal[i + 1], indexesInternal[i + 2]);
                Edge c = new Edge(indexesInternal[i + 2], indexesInternal[i + 0]);

                if (!dist.Add(a)) dup.Add(a);
                if (!dist.Add(b)) dup.Add(b);
                if (!dist.Add(c)) dup.Add(c);
            }

            dist.ExceptWith(dup);
            m_Edges = dist.ToArray();
            return m_Edges;

        /// <summary>
        /// Finds the smallest value in the triangles array.
        /// </summary>
        /// <returns>The smallest value in the indices array.</returns>
        int SmallestIndexValue()
        {
            int smallest = m_Indexes[0];

            for (int i = 1; i < m_Indexes.Length; i++)
            {
                if (m_Indexes[i] < smallest)
                    smallest = m_Indexes[i];
            }

            return smallest;

        /// <summary>
        /// Finds the smallest value in the indices array, then offsets by subtracting that value from each index.
        /// </summary>
        /// <example>
        /// ```
        /// // sets the indexes array to `{0, 1, 2}`.
        /// new Face(3,4,5).ShiftIndexesToZero();
        /// ```
        /// </example>
        public void ShiftIndexesToZero()
        {
            int offset = SmallestIndexValue();

            for (int i = 0; i < m_Indexes.Length; i++)
                m_Indexes[i] -= offset;

            InvalidateCache();
        }

```csharp
        public static void Apply(
            IEnumerable<FaceRebuildData> newFaces,
            List<Vertex> vertices,
            List<Face> faces,
            Dictionary<int, int> sharedVertexLookup,
            Dictionary<int, int> sharedTextureLookup = null)
        {
            int index = vertices.Count;

            foreach (FaceRebuildData rd in newFaces)
            {
                Face face = rd.face;
                int faceVertexCount = rd.vertices.Count;

                bool hasSharedIndexes = sharedVertexLookup != null && rd.sharedIndexes != null && rd.sharedIndexes.Count == faceVertexCount;
                bool hasSharedIndexesUV = sharedTextureLookup != null && rd.sharedIndexesUV != null && rd.sharedIndexesUV.Count == faceVertexCount;

                for (int n = 0; n < faceVertexCount; n++)
                {
                    int localIndex = n;

                    if (sharedVertexLookup != null)
                        sharedVertexLookup.Add(localIndex + index, hasSharedIndexes ? rd.sharedIndexes[localIndex] : -1);

                    if (sharedTextureLookup != null && hasSharedIndexesUV)
                        sharedTextureLookup.Add(localIndex + index, rd.sharedIndexesUV[localIndex]);
                }

                rd._appliedOffset = index;
                int[] faceIndexes = face.indexesInternal;

                for (int n = 0, c = faceIndexes.Length; n < c; n++)
                    faceIndexes[n] += index;

                index += rd.vertices.Count;
                face.indexesInternal = faceIndexes;
                faces.Add(face);
                vertices.AddRange(rd.vertices);

ProBuilder's `Face` class represents a logical polygon that owns a submesh index (`m_SubmeshIndex`), auto-UV settings (`AutoUnwrapSettings`), and smoothing group (`m_SmoothingGroup`). ### EDGE: Local vs common edge representation. EdgeLookup purpose. How edges reference vertices.

ProBuilder defines edges using two primary structures: `Edge` (representing a connection between two vertex indices) and `EdgeLookup` (associating a local face edge with its corresponding topological shared edge).

### `Edge` Structure Definition
`Edge` (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Edge`) is a serializable struct implementing `IEquatable<Edge>` with public integer fields:
- `public int a`: Start vertex index.
- `public int b`: End vertex index.
- `public static readonly Edge Empty = new Edge(-1, -1)`: Sentinel value for uninitialized or invalid edges.

### Local vs Common Edge Representation
1. **Local Edge**: An `Edge` whose endpoints `a` and `b` are direct indices into the `ProBuilderMesh` vertex array (`positionsInternal`). Because ProBuilder faces do not share local vertex indices, an edge shared geometrically between two adjacent faces consists of two distinct local edges (for instance, `Edge(0, 1)` on Face 1 and `Edge(4, 5)` on Face 2).
2. **Common (Universal/Shared) Edge**: An `Edge` whose endpoints `a` and `b` are indices into the `sharedVertices` array (the cluster IDs of coincident 3D points). For adjacent faces meeting at the same physical edge, both local edges map to the exact same common edge `Edge(ca, cb)`.

### Undirected Equality and Hashing Semantics
- `Edge` represents an undirected segment. `Edge.Equals(Edge other)` evaluates `true` if `(a == other.a && b == other.b) || (a == other.b && b == other.a)`.
- `Edge.GetHashCode()` computes an order-independent hash by sorting the indices before hashing:
  ```csharp
  int hash = 27;
  unchecked {
      hash = hash * 29 + (a < b ? a : b);
      hash = hash * 29 + (a < b ? b : a);
  }
  return hash;
  ```
- `Edge.Equals(Edge other, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)`: Compares two local edges in common coordinate space by resolving both edges through `lookup` (evaluating `x0 = lookup[a], y0 = lookup[b], x1 = lookup[other.a], y1 = lookup[other.b]`) and verifying `(x0 == x1 && y0 == y1) || (x0 == y1 && y0 == x1)`.
- `Edge.IsValid()`: Checks `a > -1 && b > -1 && a != b`.
- `Edge.Contains(int index)`: Returns `a == index || b == index`.
- `Edge.Contains(Edge other)`: Checks if this edge shares any vertex index with `other` (`a == other.a || b == other.a || a == other.b || b == other.a`).
- Operators: Supports `+` and `-` with `Edge` (component-wise addition/subtraction) and `int` (offsetting both `a` and `b`).

### `EdgeLookup` Struct and Purpose
`EdgeLookup` (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.EdgeLookup`) encapsulates a pair of edges:
- `public Edge local { get; set; }`: The local edge referencing `positionsInternal` indices.
- `public Edge common { get; set; }`: The common edge referencing `sharedVertices` indices.

**Purpose and Key Invariant**:
`EdgeLookup` exists to enable topological edge comparisons and deduplication across adjacent faces while maintaining a reference back to a concrete local face edge.
- `EdgeLookup.Equals(EdgeLookup other)` compares ONLY the `common` edge: `return other.common.Equals(common);`.
- `EdgeLookup.GetHashCode()` returns `common.GetHashCode()`.
- When inserting `EdgeLookup` instances from multiple faces into a `HashSet<EdgeLookup>` via `GetEdgeLookupHashSet(IEnumerable<Edge> edges, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)`, duplicates across adjacent faces are automatically collapsed into a solitary unique topological edge, retaining one representative `local` edge.

### `EdgeUtility` Functions
- `GetSharedVertexHandleEdges(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Edge> edges)` / `GetSharedVertexHandleEdge(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Edge edge)`: Converts local edges to common edges using `mesh.sharedVertexLookup` (`new Edge(mesh.sharedVertexLookup[edge.a], mesh.sharedVertexLookup[edge.b])`).
- `GetEdgeWithSharedVertexHandles(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Edge edge)`: Converts a common edge back to local indices by selecting the first index in each shared vertex group (`new Edge(mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[edge.a][0], mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[edge.b][0])`).
- `ValidateEdge(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Edge edge, out (Face face, Edge edge) validEdge)`: Takes an edge (local or universal), maps to universal, and iterates through `facesInternal` to find a face whose `distinctIndexesInternal` contains both endpoints. Returns the matching `Face` and the valid local `Edge` paired in `validEdge`.

        /// <returns>A set of EdgeLookup edges that you can iterate over.</returns>
        public static IEnumerable<EdgeLookup> GetEdgeLookup(IEnumerable<Edge> edges, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)

        /// <summary>
        /// Creates a hashset of edge lookup values from a collection of local edges and a shared indexes lookup.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="edges">A collection of local edges.</param>
        /// <param name="lookup">A shared index lookup dictionary (see <see cref="ProBuilderMesh.sharedVertices" />).</param>
        /// <returns>A HashSet of EdgeLookup edges. EdgeLookup values are compared by their common property only: local edges are not compared.</returns>
        public static HashSet<EdgeLookup> GetEdgeLookupHashSet(IEnumerable<Edge> edges, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)
        {
            if (lookup == null || edges == null)
                return null;
            var hash = new HashSet<EdgeLookup>();
            foreach (var local in edges)
                hash.Add(new EdgeLookup(new Edge(lookup[local.a], lookup[local.b]), local));
            return hash;
        }

### VERTEX: All 8 channels (position, color, uv0-3, normal, tangent). Equals/hash semantics.

The `Vertex` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Vertex`) represents a single multi-channel geometric point, managing up to 8 individual vertex attributes, bitmask tracking, arithmetic operations, interpolation, and mesh buffer population.

### All 8 Vertex Attribute Channels
1. `m_Position` / `position` (`Vector3`): 3D local coordinate. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Position`.
2. `m_Color` / `color` (`Color`): Vertex RGBA color. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Color`.
3. `m_Normal` / `normal` (`Vector3`): Unit normal vector. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Normal`.
4. `m_Tangent` / `tangent` (`Vector4`): Vector4 tangent containing 3D direction in `(x, y, z)` and bitangent sign/handedness (`-1.0f` or `1.0f`) in `w`. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Tangent`.
5. `m_UV0` / `uv0` (`Vector2`): Primary texture coordinate channel (channel 0). Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Texture0`.
6. `m_UV2` / `uv2` (`Vector2`): Secondary texture / lightmap coordinate channel (channel 1). Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Texture1`.
7. `m_UV3` / `uv3` (`Vector4`): 4D floating-point UV channel 2. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Texture2`.
8. `m_UV4` / `uv4` (`Vector4`): 4D floating-point UV channel 3. Bitmask flag `MeshArrays.Texture3`.

### Attribute Mask Tracking
`Vertex` maintains a `MeshArrays m_Attributes` bitmask field. Setting any property (e.g. `vertex.position = val`) sets the internal boolean property (e.g. `hasPosition = true`), which applies a bitwise OR (`m_Attributes |= MeshArrays.Position`). Clearing a property applies a bitwise AND with the bitwise NOT (`m_Attributes &= ~MeshArrays.Position`). The method `HasArrays(MeshArrays attribute)` checks `(m_Attributes & attribute) == attribute`.

### Equals and Hash Semantics
- `Vertex.Equals(Vertex other)`: Performs an approximate component-wise equality comparison across all 8 channels using `float.Epsilon` tolerance via `Math.Approx3(m_Position, other.m_Position)`, `Math.ApproxC(m_Color, other.m_Color)`, `Math.Approx3(m_Normal, other.m_Normal)`, `Math.Approx4(m_Tangent, other.m_Tangent)`, `Math.Approx2(m_UV0, other.m_UV0)`, `Math.Approx2(m_UV2, other.m_UV2)`, `Math.Approx4(m_UV3, other.m_UV3)`, and `Math.Approx4(m_UV4, other.m_UV4)`.
- `Vertex.Equals(Vertex other, MeshArrays mask)`: Masked equality comparison. Compares only the specific channels enabled in the `mask` bitmask. For each channel bit not set in `mask`, the comparison is bypassed.
- `Vertex.GetHashCode()`: Computes hash code incorporating ONLY `position`, `uv0`, and `normal` via `VectorHash.GetHashCode`:
  ```csharp
  unchecked {
      int hash = 783 + VectorHash.GetHashCode(position); // 783 = 27 * 29
      hash = hash * 29 + VectorHash.GetHashCode(uv0);
      hash = hash * 31 + VectorHash.GetHashCode(normal);
      return hash;
  }
  ```
  Attributes like `color`, `tangent`, `uv2`, `uv3`, and `uv4` are omitted from the hash computation.

### Arithmetic, Averaging, and Interpolation
- Arithmetic Operators: Implements `+`, `-`, `*` (scalar `float`), and `/` (scalar `float`). Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division are performed component-wise across all 8 attribute channels. Normals, tangents, and colors are NOT automatically normalized during arithmetic operators.
- `Normalize()`: Explicitly normalizes `m_Position`, `m_Color` (treated as Vector4), `m_Normal`, `m_Tangent`, `m_UV0`, `m_UV2`, `m_UV3`, and `m_UV4` in place.
- `Average(IList<Vertex> vertices, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Calculates the arithmetic mean across populated channels. For each channel, tracks the count of vertices possessing that attribute (`positionCount`, `colorCount`, `uv0Count`, `normalCount`, `tangentCount`, `uv2Count`, `uv3Count`, `uv4Count`), sums the vectors, and multiplies by `(1f / count)`.
- `Mix(Vertex x, Vertex y, float weight)`: Linearly interpolates between vertex `x` and vertex `y` with factor `weight` (`float i = 1f - weight`). For each channel, if both vertices have the channel populated, it calculates `x * i + y * weight`; if only one vertex has the channel, it copies that vertex's value.

### Mesh Buffer Binding (`GetArrays` and `SetMesh`)
- `GetArrays(IList<Vertex> vertices, out Vector3[] position, ...)`: Allocates and extracts typed parallel arrays for all 8 channels based on the provided `MeshArrays attributes` bitmask.
- `SetMesh(Mesh mesh, IList<Vertex> vertices)`: Clears the Unity `Mesh` (`mesh.Clear()`), extracts arrays via `GetArrays`, assigns `mesh.vertices`, `mesh.colors`, `mesh.uv`, `mesh.normals`, `mesh.tangents`, `mesh.uv2`, `mesh.SetUVs(2, uv3s)`, `mesh.SetUVs(3, uv4s)`, and sets `mesh.indexFormat = mesh.vertexCount > ushort.MaxValue ? IndexFormat.UInt32 : IndexFormat.UInt16`.

### `Normal` Struct (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Normal`)
`Normal` is a standalone struct holding `Vector3 normal`, `Vector4 tangent`, and `Vector3 bitangent`. It implements `IEquatable<Normal>` comparing `Math.Approx3(normal, other.normal)`, `Math.Approx4(tangent, other.tangent)`, and `Math.Approx3(bitangent, other.bitangent)`. Its hash code combines the three vectors using `(hashCode * 397) ^ VectorHash.GetHashCode(...)`.

### SHARED VERTEX: Mapping from local index to shared index. Purpose for welding, merging. GetSharedVertexLookup.

The `SharedVertex` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.SharedVertex`) models topological vertex equivalence, grouping disjoint local vertex array indices that occupy coincident 3D positions in space.

### `SharedVertex` Class Structure
- `SharedVertex` implements `ICollection<int>` and `IEnumerable<int>`.
- `m_Vertices` (`int[]`, serialized, legacy aliases `array`, `m_Vertexes`): Backing array containing the local vertex indices that share this geometric point.
- `arrayInternal` property exposes `m_Vertices`.
- Collection operations: `Count => m_Vertices.Length`, `Add(int item)` calls `ArrayUtility.Add(m_Vertices, item)`, `Remove(int item)` calls `ArrayUtility.RemoveAt`, `Contains(int item)` performs `Array.IndexOf(m_Vertices, item) > -1`, `Clear()` sets `m_Vertices = new int[0]`.

### Architectural Role and Topological Purpose
Because ProBuilder stores meshes with per-face vertex duplication (disjoint vertices for each face to allow independent face materials, hard normals, and distinct UV islands), a single corner in a cube model is represented by 3 distinct local vertex entries in `positionsInternal`. `SharedVertex` provides the bridge connecting these distinct indices into a single topological vertex.
- **Welding / Merging**: When welding vertices or collapsing edges, ProBuilder unifies multiple `SharedVertex` clusters into a single group.
- **Transformation Gizmos**: Moving a vertex in the editor moves all local vertices belonging to the same `SharedVertex` group simultaneously, maintaining solid mesh topology.
- **Topology Traversal & WingedEdge**: Topology graphs (WingedEdge) rely on shared vertex handles to discover face adjacency across borders.
- **Normal Smoothing**: Smoothing algorithms iterate over each `SharedVertex` cluster to average normals of adjacent faces with matching smoothing groups.

### `GetSharedVertexLookup` Algorithm
`SharedVertex.GetSharedVertexLookup(IList<SharedVertex> sharedVertices, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)` builds a reverse lookup table mapping local vertex index $\rightarrow$ shared vertex cluster index.
1. `lookup.Clear()` clears the output dictionary.
2. Loops `i = 0` to `sharedVertices.Count - 1`.
3. For each local vertex `index` in `sharedVertices[i]`:
   - If `!lookup.ContainsKey(index)`, executes `lookup.Add(index, i)`.
4. Time complexity is $O(V)$ where $V$ is the total number of local vertices, allowing $O(1)$ shared group queries during mesh operations.

### Shared Vertex Manipulation and Utility Methods
- `ToSharedVertices(IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<int, int>> lookup)`: Reconstructs an array of `SharedVertex` objects from a `Dictionary<int, int>` mapping local vertex indices to shared group IDs. Negative group IDs (`kvp.Value < 0`) are treated as unshared vertices and placed into single-element groups.
- `GetSharedVerticesWithPositions(IList<Vector3> positions)`: Reconstructs shared vertices from raw 3D positions using spatial quantization via `IntVec3` hashing (`Dictionary<IntVec3, List<int>> sorted`). Vertices whose coordinates round to the same integer hash bucket are grouped into a `SharedVertex`.
- `RemoveAndShift(Dictionary<int, int> lookup, IEnumerable<int> remove)` / `SortedRemoveAndShift(Dictionary<int, int> lookup, List<int> remove)`: When vertices are deleted from a mesh, this method sets `lookup[i] = -1` for all removed indices, rebuilds the active groups via `ToSharedVertices`, and decrements remaining vertex index pointers using `ArrayUtility.NearestIndexPriorToValue(remove, shared[i][n]) + 1` to account for index collapse.
- `SetCoincident(ref Dictionary<int, int> lookup, IEnumerable<int> vertices)`: Welds a collection of vertex indices together by assigning each of them a new shared index equal to `lookup.Count`.
- `ShiftIndexes(int offset)`: Adds `offset` to all vertex indices in the `m_Vertices` array.

        {

                throw new ArgumentNullException("positions");

        internal static SharedVertex[] SortedRemoveAndShift(Dictionary<int, int> lookup, List<int> remove)
        {
            foreach (int i in remove)
                lookup[i] = -1;

            var shared = ToSharedVertices(lookup.Where(x => x.Value > -1));

            for (int i = 0, c = shared.Length; i < c; i++)
            {
                for (int n = 0, l = shared[i].Count; n < l; n++)
                {
                    int index = ArrayUtility.NearestIndexPriorToValue(remove, shared[i][n]);
                    // add 1 because index is zero based
                    shared[i][n] -= index + 1;
                }
            }

            return shared;
        }

In a ProBuilder-like tool for Godot, maintaining an explicit `Array[PackedInt32Array]` of shared vertices allows the editor to preserve hard edges, separate UVs, and material seams while providing topological vertex dragging and normal smoothing across coincident points.

### NORMAL CALCULATION: CalculateNormals algorithm - per-face, per-smoothing-group averaging. Hard vs soft edge normals.

Normal and tangent calculation in ProBuilder is implemented in the static class `Normals` (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Normals`), utilizing a two-pass algorithm that first computes un-smoothed facet normals and subsequently averages them across coincident vertices according to per-face smoothing groups.

### Static Working Buffers
To prevent per-frame garbage collection allocations during normal calculation, `Normals` maintains reusable static buffers:
- `static Vector3[] s_SmoothAvg = new Vector3[Smoothing.smoothRangeMax]` (initial size 30).
- `static float[] s_SmoothAvgCount = new float[Smoothing.smoothRangeMax]` (initial size 30).
- `static int[] s_CachedIntArray = new int[ushort.MaxValue]` (initial size 65535, dynamically resized via `ClearIntArray(int count)` if vertex count exceeds capacity).

### Phase 1: Hard Normal Calculation (`CalculateHardNormals`)
`CalculateHardNormals(ProBuilderMesh mesh)` computes per-triangle facet normals and accumulates them across the local vertices of each face:
1. Initializes `mesh.normalsInternal = new Vector3[vertexCount]` if unallocated, and zeroes out all normal entries `normals[i] = Vector3.zero`.
2. Calls `ClearIntArray(vertexCount)` to initialize `s_CachedIntArray` as a per-vertex triangle accumulation counter.
3. Iterates over all faces in `mesh.facesInternal`. For each face, iterates its triangle index buffer `indexesInternal` in steps of 3 (`int a = indexes[tri], b = indexes[tri+1], c = indexes[tri+2]`):
   - Computes the unnormalized face normal via `Math.Normal(positions[a], positions[b], positions[c])` (cross product `Vector3.Cross(p1 - p0, p2 - p0)`).
   - Normalizes the cross product: `cross.Normalize()`.
   - Adds `cross` to `normals[a]`, `normals[b]`, and `normals[c]`.
   - Increments the vertex triangle counter: `s_CachedIntArray[a]++`, `s_CachedIntArray[b]++`, `s_CachedIntArray[c]++`.
4. Iterates over each vertex `i = 0` to `vertexCount - 1` and divides the accumulated normal by the triangle count: `normals[i] = normals[i] / s_CachedIntArray[i]`.

### Phase 2: Smoothing Group Averaging (`CalculateNormals`)
`CalculateNormals(ProBuilderMesh mesh)` extends the hard normals with smoothing group averaging:
1. Invokes `CalculateHardNormals(mesh)` to initialize all vertex normals to facet normals.
2. Clears `s_CachedIntArray` (`ClearIntArray(mesh.vertexCount)`), which is repurposed as a vertex-to-smoothing-group lookup table (`s_CachedIntArray[vertexIndex] = face.smoothingGroup`).
3. Initializes `int smoothGroupMax = 24`. Loops through all faces and their `distinctIndexesInternal`, assigning `s_CachedIntArray[index] = face.smoothingGroup`. If `face.smoothingGroup >= smoothGroupMax`, sets `smoothGroupMax = face.smoothingGroup + 1`.
4. If `smoothGroupMax > s_SmoothAvg.Length`, resizes `s_SmoothAvg` and `s_SmoothAvgCount` to `smoothGroupMax`.
5. Iterates through every coincident vertex group in `sharedVerticesInternal` (`i = 0` to `sharedVertices.Length - 1`):
   - Clears `s_SmoothAvg[n] = Vector3.zero` and `s_SmoothAvgCount[n] = 0f` for `n = 0` to `smoothGroupMax - 1`.
   - **Accumulation Loop**: Iterates through each local vertex index `index = sharedVertices[i][n]` in the shared group. Reads `group = s_CachedIntArray[index]`. If `group <= Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone` (0 or negative, indicating no smoothing / hard edge), it skips the vertex. Otherwise, adds `normals[index]` to `s_SmoothAvg[group]` and increments `s_SmoothAvgCount[group] += 1f`.
   - **Assignment Loop**: Re-iterates through each local vertex index `index = sharedVertices[i][n]` in the shared group. Reads `group = s_CachedIntArray[index]`. If `group <= Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone`, the vertex retains its hard facet normal from Phase 1. Otherwise, computes the average normal `normals[index] = s_SmoothAvg[group] / s_SmoothAvgCount[group]` and normalizes the vector with `normals[index] = Math.EnsureUnitVector(normals[index])`.

### Hard vs Soft Edge Normals
- **Hard Edge Criteria**: An edge between two adjacent faces renders with a sharp lighting crease (hard edge) if:
  1. Either (or both) of the adjacent faces has `smoothingGroup <= 0` (`Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone = 0`).
  2. The adjacent faces are assigned different positive smoothing group IDs (e.g. Face A has group 1, Face B has group 2).
  In both scenarios, the coincident vertices at the edge remain un-averaged, preserving distinct normal vectors per face.
- **Soft Edge Criteria**: An edge between two adjacent faces renders with smooth Gouraud/Phong lighting (soft edge) if and only if:
  1. Both adjacent faces have positive smoothing group IDs (`smoothingGroup > 0`).
  2. Both adjacent faces share the exact same smoothing group ID (`faceA.smoothingGroup == faceB.smoothingGroup`).
  Coincident vertices on both faces receive the identical averaged normal vector.

### Tangent Calculation (`CalculateTangents`)
`CalculateTangents(ProBuilderMesh mesh)` computes vertex tangents using Lengyel's method:
1. Solves per-triangle tangent vector `sdir` and bitangent vector `tdir` in UV0 coordinate space from vertex positions `v1, v2, v3` and UV coordinates `w1, w2, w3` with reciprocal determinant `r = 1.0f / (s1 * t2 - s2 * t1)`.
2. Accumulates `sdir` into `tan1` and `tdir` into `tan2` for triangle vertices `i1, i2, i3`.
3. For each vertex `a = 0` to `vc - 1`, orthonormalizes the tangent against the normal using Gram-Schmidt: `Vector3.OrthoNormalize(ref n, ref t)`.
4. Computes handedness sign in `tangents[a].w = (Vector3.Dot(Vector3.Cross(n, t), tan2[a]) < 0.0f) ? -1.0f : 1.0f`.

> **Godot Note:** Godot's default `SurfaceTool.generate_normals()` smooths all coincident vertices without considering smoothing groups. To support ProBuilder-style hard/soft edge control in Godot, developers must implement this two-pass normal calculation, averaging coincident vertices only when their parent faces share identical positive smoothing group IDs.

## A03: Enums, preferences, and configuration

### EVERY ENUM: COMPLETE SPECIFICATION OF ALL PROBUILDER ENUMERATIONS AND BITMASKS

ProBuilder defines a comprehensive suite of enumerations and bitmasks across its runtime and editor architectures. Each enumeration specifies exact integer values, underlying bit flags, and operational meanings:

1. `SelectMode` (`[System.Flags]`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines which object and sub-mesh element types are active and selectable in the scene tool:
- `None = 0x0` (`0`): No selection mode defined.
- `Vertex = 1 << 0` (`0x1` / `1`): Vertices are selectable in the Scene view.
- `Edge = 1 << 1` (`0x2` / `2`): Edges are selectable in the Scene view.
- `Face = 1 << 2` (`0x4` / `4`): Faces are selectable in the Scene view.
- `TextureVertex = 1 << 3` (`0x8` / `8`): Texture vertices (UV vertices) are selectable in the UV Editor.
- `TextureEdge = 1 << 4` (`0x10` / `16`): Texture edges (UV edges) are selectable in the UV Editor.
- `TextureFace = 1 << 5` (`0x20` / `32`): Texture faces (UV faces) are selectable in the UV Editor.
- `InputTool = 1 << 6` (`0x40` / `64`): Custom input tool mode engaged (e.g. `PolyShape` editor, `BezierShape` editor).
- `Any = 0xFF` (`255`): Wildcard bitmask matching any selection mode.

2. `ComponentMode` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines the element selection mode for geometry components:
- `Vertex = 0x0` (`0`): Vertex component mode active.
- `Edge = 0x1` (`1`): Edge component mode active.
- `Face = 0x2` (`2`): Face component mode active.

3. `EditLevel` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines the operational target layer for active scene interaction tools:
- `Top = 0`: Transform tools interact directly with GameObjects / Node transforms.
- `Geometry = 1`: Tools interact with editable mesh sub-elements (`Face`, `Edge`, `Vertex`).
- `Texture = 2`: Tools affect texture coordinates in scene view (corresponds to in-scene UV editing).
- `Plugin = 3`: A custom external or ProBuilder plugin tool mode is engaged.

4. `EntityType` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Specifies the functional metadata flag assigned to a ProBuilder mesh object:
- `Detail = 0`: Non-structural detail geometry.
- `Occluder = 1`: Occlusion culling static occluder volume.
- `Trigger = 2`: Trigger volume geometry (renders with trigger material, collider set to trigger).
- `Collider = 3`: Invisible collision volume geometry.
- `Mover = 4`: Dynamic moving object geometry.

5. `ColliderType` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Specifies the type of physics collision component attached to instantiated ProBuilder meshes:
- `None = 0`: No collider component is attached.
- `BoxCollider = 1`: Attaches a standard `UnityEngine.BoxCollider` sized to the mesh bounding box.
- `MeshCollider = 2`: Attaches a `UnityEngine.MeshCollider` referencing the compiled mesh geometry.

6. `ProjectionAxis` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Indicates the cardinal projection direction used during planar UV unwrapping:
- `X = 0`: Projects on the positive X axis ($+X$).
- `Y = 1`: Projects on the positive Y axis ($+Y$).
- `Z = 2`: Projects on the positive Z axis ($+Z$).
- `XNegative = 3`: Projects on the negative X axis ($-X$).
- `YNegative = 4`: Projects on the negative Y axis ($-Y$).
- `ZNegative = 5`: Projects on the negative Z axis ($-Z$).

7. `HandleAxis` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Bitmask indicating which translation or snapping grid axes are active:
- `X = 1 << 0` (`0x1` / `1`): X axis is active.
- `Y = 1 << 1` (`0x2` / `2`): Y axis is active.
- `Z = 1 << 2` (`0x4` / `4`): Z axis is active.
- `Free = 1 << 3` (`0x8` / `8`): All axes are active simultaneously for unrestricted movement.

8. `Axis` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Describes 3D cardinal spatial directions in human-readable terms:
- `Right = 0`: Positive X direction ($+X$).
- `Left = 1`: Negative X direction ($-X$).
- `Up = 2`: Positive Y direction ($+Y$).
- `Down = 3`: Negative Y direction ($-Y$).
- `Forward = 4`: Positive Z direction ($+Z$).
- `Backward = 5`: Negative Z direction ($-Z$).

9. `WindingOrder` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Describes the vertex traversal orientation for triangle polygon faces:
- `Unknown = 0`: Winding orientation cannot be determined.
- `Clockwise = 1`: Clockwise vertex ordering (right-handed normal orientation in screen space).
- `CounterClockwise = 2`: Counter-clockwise vertex ordering (left-handed normal orientation in screen space).

10. `SortMethod` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines sorting direction when ordering 2D planar polygon vertices:
- `Clockwise = 0`: Order planar polygon vertices clockwise around centroid.
- `CounterClockwise = 1`: Order planar polygon vertices counter-clockwise around centroid.

11. `CullingMode` (`[System.Flags]`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines triangle face backface and frontface visibility culling during scene rendering and element picking:
- `None = 0 << 0` (`0x0` / `0`): Double-sided rendering; neither front nor back faces are culled.
- `Back = 1 << 0` (`0x1` / `1`): Back-facing triangles are culled from rendering and raycast picking.
- `Front = 1 << 1` (`0x2` / `2`): Front-facing triangles are culled from rendering and raycast picking.
- `FrontBack = Front | Back` (`0x3` / `3`): Both front and back faces are culled.

12. `RectSelectMode` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines the intersection criteria for marquee drag selection in the Scene view:
- `Partial = 0`: Selects any mesh element that intersects, touches, or overlaps the drag rectangle.
- `Complete = 1`: Selects only mesh elements whose vertices are completely enclosed within the drag rectangle.

13. `MeshSyncState` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Describes the synchronization state between a `ProBuilderMesh` data structure and its compiled `MeshFilter.sharedMesh`:
- `Null = 0`: The `MeshFilter` mesh reference is null.
- `InstanceIDMismatch = 1`: Legacy status indicating instance ID mismatch (`[Obsolete]`).
- `Lightmap = 2`: The mesh is valid but lacks a generated secondary UV2 lightmap channel.
- `InSync = 3`: The component data is fully synchronized with the compiled `UnityEngine.Mesh`.
- `NeedsRebuild = 4`: The `ProBuilderMesh` internal geometry attributes differ from the compiled mesh and require a full rebuild.

14. `MeshArrays` (`[System.Flags]`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Bitmask describing which vertex attribute channels are allocated and populated on a mesh:
- `Position = 0x1` (`1`): Vertex 3D local position array (`m_Positions`).
- `Texture0 = 0x2` (`2`): Primary UV channel 0 coordinates (`m_Textures0`).
- `Texture1 = 0x4` (`4`): Secondary UV channel 1 coordinates (Lightmap UV channel).
- `Lightmap = 0x4` (`4`): Alias for `Texture1`.
- `Texture2 = 0x8` (`8`): Tertiary UV channel 2 coordinates (`m_Textures2`).
- `Texture3 = 0x10` (`16`): Quaternary UV channel 3 coordinates (`m_Textures3`).
- `Color = 0x20` (`32`): Per-vertex RGBA color array (`m_Colors`).
- `Normal = 0x40` (`64`): Per-vertex normal vector array (`m_Normals`).
- `Tangent = 0x80` (`128`): Per-vertex tangent vector array (`m_Tangents`).
- `All = 0xFF` (`255`): All vertex attribute channels combined.

15. `IndexFormat` (internal enum, underlying type `int`):
Specifies the vertex index reference scope for topology lookup structures:
- `Local = 0x0` (`0`): References unique per-face vertex indices in `m_Positions`.
- `Common = 0x1` (`1`): References shared vertex indices in `m_SharedVertices`.
- `Both = 0x2` (`2`): References both local and common indices.

16. `RefreshMask` (`[System.Flags]`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Bitmask for selectively updating vertex attribute channels during `ProBuilderMesh.Refresh()`:
- `UV = 0x1` (`1`): Rebuilds UV channel 0 for auto-unwrapped faces and syncs channels 2 and 3.
- `Colors = 0x2` (`2`): Reapplies vertex colors to the underlying `Mesh`.
- `Normals = 0x4` (`4`): Recalculates vertex normals based on smoothing groups and assigns to `Mesh.normals`.
- `Tangents = 0x8` (`8`): Recalculates vertex tangents and assigns to `Mesh.tangents`.
- `Collisions = 0x10` (`16`): Reassigns the `MeshCollider.sharedMesh` reference.
- `Bounds = 0x16` (`22`): Recalculates mesh spatial bounding box (`Mesh.RecalculateBounds()`).
- `All = UV | Colors | Normals | Tangents | Collisions | Bounds` (`0x1F` / `31`): Refreshes all optional vertex attributes and collisions.

17. `ExtrudeMethod` (public enum, underlying type `int`):
Describes face extrusion topology and normal generation methods:
- `IndividualFaces = 0`: Extrudes each selected face independently as a disconnected prism.
- `VertexNormal = 1`: Extrudes adjacent selected faces as a continuous group, projecting along averaged vertex normals.
- `FaceNormal = 2`: Extrudes adjacent selected faces as a connected group, but translates each face along its own individual face normal vector.

18. `HandleOrientation` (in `HandleOrientation.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Specifies scene gizmo orientation space for element manipulation:
- `World = 0`: Scene gizmo aligns to identity in global world coordinate space.
- `ActiveObject = 1`: Scene gizmo aligns to the active GameObject's transform rotation.
- `ActiveElement = 2`: Scene gizmo aligns to the normal and tangent frame of the active selected element.

19. `PivotPoint` (in `PivotPoint.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Specifies the transformation origin for element manipulations:
- `Center = 0`: Transformations calculate origin from the center point of the collective selection bounding box.
- `IndividualOrigins = 1`: Transformations execute from the centroid of each disconnected selection group independently.
- `ActiveElement = 2`: Transformations calculate origin from the active element's centroid.

20. `SelectionModifierBehavior` (in `SelectionModifierBehaviour.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines how modifier keys adjust element selections:
- `Add = 0`: Always performs a set union (`UnionWith`) adding elements to selection.
- `Subtract = 1`: Always performs a set difference (`RemoveWhere`) subtracting elements from selection.
- `Difference = 2`: Inverts selection state for elements within the target marquee area.

21. `ActionResult.Status` (in `ActionResult.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Describes the execution outcome of an editor menu or geometry operation:
- `Success = 0`: Action completed successfully.
- `Failure = 1`: Critical error prevented execution.
- `Canceled = 2`: Action aborted due to invalid arguments or user cancellation.
- `NoChange = 3`: Action terminated because target geometry was already in requested state.

22. `AutoUnwrapSettings.Anchor` (in `AutoUnwrapSettings.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Defines 2D origin anchor for UV projection transformations:
- `UpperLeft = 0`: Bounding top-left aligns with $(0, 1)$.
- `UpperCenter = 1`: Bounding top-center aligns with $(0.5, 1)$.
- `UpperRight = 2`: Bounding top-right aligns with $(1, 1)$.
- `MiddleLeft = 3`: Bounding middle-left aligns with $(0, 0.5)$.
- `MiddleCenter = 4`: Bounding center aligns with $(0.5, 0.5)$.
- `MiddleRight = 5`: Bounding middle-right aligns with $(1, 0.5)$.
- `LowerLeft = 6`: Bounding lower-left aligns with $(0, 0)$.
- `LowerCenter = 7`: Bounding lower-center aligns with $(0.5, 0)$.
- `LowerRight = 8`: Bounding lower-right aligns with $(1, 0)$.
- `None = 9`: UV coordinates undergo no anchor translation.

23. `AutoUnwrapSettings.Fill` (in `AutoUnwrapSettings.cs`, public enum, underlying type `int`):
Controls UV bounds normalization and aspect ratio fitting:
- `Fit = 0`: Fits UV bounds into unit $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ square while preserving aspect ratio.
- `Tile = 1`: Retains original metric scaling without normalization.
- `Stretch = 2`: Stretches UV bounds into unit $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ square ignoring aspect ratio.

### HANDLE ORIENTATION: WORLD, ACTIVEOBJECT, AND ACTIVEELEMENT TRANSFORMATION SPACES

Handle orientation governs the rotation of the 3D scene gizmo during element transformation. The `HandleOrientation` enumeration defines three distinct transformation coordinate spaces: `World`, `ActiveObject`, and `ActiveElement`.

1. `HandleOrientation.World` (`0`):
The scene handle aligns directly to identity in global world coordinates (`Quaternion.identity`). Translations and delta movements occur along the global $+X$, $+Y$, and $+Z$ axes regardless of the mesh transform or element face orientation.

2. `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject` (`1`):
The scene handle aligns to the local orientation of the target `ProBuilderMesh` transform (`mesh.transform.rotation`). Transformations occur relative to the model coordinate axes of the GameObject.

3. `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement` (`2`):
The scene handle aligns to the local normal and tangent coordinate frame of the active selected element. When multiple elements are selected, the active element is the most recently selected item (`elementGroups.Last()`). The mathematical calculation of element orientation is implemented in `HandleUtility.cs`:

A. Face Normal Orientation (`HandleUtility.GetFaceRotation`):
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, `GetFaceRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces)` evaluates `GetFaceRotation(mesh, faces.Last())`.
- The method computes the face orthonormal basis using `Normal nrm = Math.NormalTangentBitangent(mesh, face)`.
- If `nrm.normal == Vector3.zero || nrm.bitangent == Vector3.zero`, the method defaults to `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- Otherwise, the orientation is computed by constructing a look rotation from the face normal vector and bitangent vector:
  `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm.normal, nrm.bitangent)`
  In this frame, the Z axis corresponds to the outward face normal vector, while the Y axis corresponds to the bitangent.
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- For `HandleOrientation.World`, returns `Quaternion.identity`.

B. Edge Normal Orientation (`HandleUtility.GetEdgeRotation`):
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, `GetEdgeRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Edge> edges)` evaluates `GetEdgeRotation(mesh, edges.Last())`.
- The method queries the parent `Face` containing the edge using `EdgeUtility.GetFace(mesh, edge)`.
- It evaluates `GetFaceRotation(mesh, face)` using the containing face's normal and bitangent frame.
- If the edge has no valid containing face, it falls back to `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- For `HandleOrientation.World`, returns `Quaternion.identity`.

C. Vertex Normal Orientation (`HandleUtility.GetVertexRotation`):
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, `GetVertexRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> vertices)` checks if `mesh.selectedVertexCount < 1`, falling back to `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- Otherwise, it evaluates `GetRotation(mesh, vertices)`:
  - Ensures vertex normals and tangents exist via `Normals.CalculateNormals(mesh)` and `Normals.CalculateTangents(mesh)`.
  - Computes the arithmetic mean vector for normals `nrm` and tangents `tan` across all selected vertex indices in `vertices`:
    $nrm = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i \in indices} normals[i]$
    $tan = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i \in indices} tangents[i]$
  - If $nrm = \vec{0}$ or $tan = \vec{0}$, returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
  - Calculates the orthogonal bitangent vector via cross product:
    $bit = nrm \times (tan.xyz \cdot tan.w)$
  - Constructs the rotation quaternion:
    `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm, bit)`
- For `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
- For `HandleOrientation.World`, returns `Quaternion.identity`.

4. Editor Tool Synchronization (`VertexManipulationTool.cs`):
- `VertexManipulationTool.handleOrientation` maintains bidirectional synchronization with Unity's global `Tools.pivotRotation` property.
- When `Tools.pivotRotation` changes to `PivotRotation.Local`, `handleOrientation` updates to `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`.
- When `Tools.pivotRotation` changes to `PivotRotation.Global`, `handleOrientation` updates to `HandleOrientation.World`.
- When `handleOrientation` is explicitly set to `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, Unity's global `Tools.pivotRotation` is left unmodified, preserving the custom ProBuilder element alignment.

        public static Quaternion GetRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indices)
        {
            if (!mesh.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Normal))
                Normals.CalculateNormals(mesh);

            if (!mesh.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Tangent))
                Normals.CalculateTangents(mesh);

            var normals = mesh.normalsInternal;
            var tangents = mesh.tangentsInternal;

            var nrm = Vector3.zero;
            var tan = Vector4.zero;
            float count = 0;

            foreach (var index in indices)
            {
                var n = normals[index];
                var t = tangents[index];

                nrm.x += n.x;
                nrm.y += n.y;
                nrm.z += n.z;

                tan.x += t.x;
                tan.y += t.y;
                tan.z += t.z;
                tan.w += t.w;

                count++;
            }

            nrm.x /= count;
            nrm.y /= count;
            nrm.z /= count;

            tan.x /= count;
            tan.y /= count;
            tan.z /= count;
            tan.w /= count;

            if (nrm == Vector3.zero || tan == Vector4.zero)
                return mesh.transform.rotation;

            var bit = Vector3.Cross(nrm, tan * tan.w);

        public static Quaternion GetFaceRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Face> faces)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                return Quaternion.identity;

            switch (orientation)
            {
                case HandleOrientation.ActiveElement:
                    // Intentionally not using coincident vertices here. We want the normal of just the face, not an
                    // average of it's neighbors.
                    return GetFaceRotation(mesh, faces.Last());

                case HandleOrientation.ActiveObject:
                    return mesh.transform.rotation;

                default:
                    return Quaternion.identity;
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Returns the rotation of a <see cref="Face"/> in world space.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="mesh">The mesh that the face belongs to.</param>
        /// <param name="face">The face you want to calculate the rotation for.</param>
        /// <returns>The rotation of the face in world space coordinates.</returns>
        public static Quaternion GetFaceRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                return Quaternion.identity;

            if (face == null)
                return mesh.transform.rotation;

            // Intentionally not using coincident vertices here. We want the normal of just the face, not an
            // average of it's neighbors.
            Normal nrm = Math.NormalTangentBitangent(mesh, face);

            if (nrm.normal == Vector3.zero || nrm.bitangent == Vector3.zero)
                return mesh.transform.rotation;

            return mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm.normal, nrm.bitangent);
        }

        public static Quaternion GetEdgeRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Edge> edges)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                return Quaternion.identity;

            switch (orientation)
            {
                case HandleOrientation.ActiveElement:
                    // Getting an average of the edge normals isn't very helpful in real world uses, so we just use the
                    // first selected edge for orientation.
                    // This function accepts an enumerable because in the future we may want to do something more
                    // sophisticated, and it's convenient because selections are stored as collections.
                    return GetEdgeRotation(mesh, edges.Last());

                case HandleOrientation.ActiveObject:
                    return mesh.transform.rotation;

                default:
                    return Quaternion.identity;
            }
        }

            if (mesh == null)
                return Quaternion.identity;

            return GetFaceRotation(mesh, EdgeUtility.GetFace(mesh, edge));

        public static Quaternion GetVertexRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<int> vertices)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
