            {
                case HandleOrientation.ActiveElement:

        /// <returns>The rotation of a vertex normal in world space coordinates.</returns>
        public static Quaternion GetVertexRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int vertex)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                return Quaternion.identity;

            if (vertex < 0)
                return mesh.transform.rotation;

            return GetRotation(mesh, new int[] { vertex });

### PIVOT POINT: SELECTION CENTER, INDIVIDUAL ORIGINS, AND ACTIVE ELEMENT ALGORITHMS

Pivot point computation establishes the spatial origin around which geometric transformations (translation, rotation, and scaling) are evaluated. The `PivotPoint` enumeration provides three distinct origin modes: `Center`, `IndividualOrigins`, and `ActiveElement`.

1. `PivotPoint` Enumeration Definition (`PivotPoint.cs`):
- `Center = 0`: Transformations evaluate from the centroid of the collective bounding box enclosing all selected elements across all selected meshes. Corresponds to `UnityEditor.PivotMode.Center`.
- `IndividualOrigins = 1`: Transformations evaluate from the local centroid of each disconnected selection group independently. Each element island rotates or scales around its own local origin.
- `ActiveElement = 2`: Transformations evaluate from the center position of the most recently selected element (`elementGroups.Last()`).

2. Scene Handle Position Calculation (`MeshSelection.GetHandlePosition`):
In `MeshSelection.cs`, `GetHandlePosition()` calculates the 3D position where the scene transform gizmo renders:
- Queries the active selection group `var active = GetActiveSelectionGroup()`. If null or `active.mesh == null`, returns `Vector3.zero`.
- Switches on `VertexManipulationTool.pivotPoint`:
  - `case PivotPoint.ActiveElement:`
  - `case PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins:`
    If `active.elementGroups.Count == 0`, defaults to `bounds.center`.
    Otherwise, returns the position of the last element group: `active.elementGroups.Last().position`.
  - `case PivotPoint.Center:`
  - `default:`
    Returns `bounds.center`, where `bounds` is the collective world-space bounding box enclosing all selected elements across all active meshes.

3. Element Group Pivot Position Algorithms (`HandleUtility.cs`):
Element groups calculate their local origin `group.position` according to active selection mode:
- Active Face Position: `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(Math.GetBounds(mesh.positionsInternal, faces.Last().distinctIndexesInternal).center)`
  Transforms the local bounding box center of the face's distinct vertex positions into world space.
- Active Edge Position: `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(Math.GetBounds(mesh.positionsInternal, new int[] { edge.a, edge.b }).center)`
  Transforms the midpoint of the edge's two endpoint vertices into world space.
- Active Vertex Position: `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(mesh.positionsInternal[vertices.First()])`
  Transforms the local position of the first coincident vertex in the group into world space.

4. Transformation Matrix Construction (`PositionTool.GetPostApplyMatrix`):
During transform execution in `PositionTool.cs`, `GetPostApplyMatrix(ElementGroup group)` constructs the transformation reference frame:
- `PivotPoint.Center`: Returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(handlePositionOrigin, handleRotationOrigin, Vector3.one)`. All vertices transform around the common selection center.
- `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`: Returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(handlePositionOrigin, handleRotationOrigin, Vector3.one)`. All vertices transform around the active element origin.
- `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins`: Returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(group.position, group.rotation, Vector3.one)`. Each individual `ElementGroup` transforms around its own local group origin and rotation frame.

5. Element Group Decomposition (`MeshAndElementSelection.GetElementGroups`):
Selection islands are segregated into distinct `ElementGroup` instances to support `IndividualOrigins`:
- Faces: `GetFaceSelectionGroups(mesh)` constructs winged-edge topology representations via `WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, mesh.selectedFacesInternal, true)` and invokes `CollectAdjacentFaces` to gather contiguous topological face islands. The active face is placed at the tail of the group list.
- Edges: `GetEdgeSelectionGroups(mesh)` constructs an `EdgeLookup` map and connects edges that share common vertex indices into contiguous edge clusters.
- Vertices: `GetVertexSelectionGroups(mesh, collectCoincident)` groups coincident spatial vertices using `mesh.sharedVerticesInternal`.

6. Editor Pivot Mode Synchronization (`VertexManipulationTool.cs`):
- `VertexManipulationTool.SyncPivotPoint()` listens for `Tools.pivotModeChanged`.
- When Unity's tool mode switches to `PivotMode.Center`, `s_PivotPoint` updates to `PivotPoint.Center`.
- When Unity's tool mode switches to `PivotMode.Pivot`, `s_PivotPoint` updates to `s_PivotModePivotEquivalent.value` (which defaults to `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`).

### AUTO UNWRAP SETTINGS: UV PROJECTION CONFIGURATION AND PROPERTIES

The `AutoUnwrapSettings` struct defines all parameters and projection rules used by ProBuilder's automated UV mapping pipeline. It is serialized per `Face` and contains the complete specification for projecting 3D planar polygons onto 2D texture coordinate surfaces.

1. Struct Definition and Serialized Fields (`AutoUnwrapSettings.cs`):
- `m_UseWorldSpace` (`bool`): Serialized backing field for `useWorldSpace`. When `true`, vertex positions are converted into world-space coordinates prior to UV planar projection (`trs.TransformPoint(positions[i])`). When `false`, projection executes in local object coordinates. Default is `false`.
- `m_FlipU` (`bool`): Serialized backing field for `flipU`. When `true`, inverts the projected horizontal texture coordinate: $U \leftarrow -U$ or $U \leftarrow 1.0 - U$. Default is `false`.
- `m_FlipV` (`bool`): Serialized backing field for `flipV`. When `true`, inverts the projected vertical texture coordinate: $V \leftarrow -V$ or $V \leftarrow 1.0 - V$. Default is `false`.
- `m_SwapUV` (`bool`): Serialized backing field for `swapUV`. When `true`, transposes the coordinate axes: $(U, V) \leftarrow (V, U)$. Default is `false`.
- `m_Fill` (`AutoUnwrapSettings.Fill`): Serialized backing field for `fill`. Controls UV bounds normalization mode. Default is `Fill.Tile`.
- `m_Scale` (`Vector2`): Serialized backing field for `scale`. Specifies scaling factors applied to $(U, V)$ coordinates post-projection. Default is `Vector2(1f, 1f)`.
- `m_Offset` (`Vector2`): Serialized backing field for `offset`. Specifies 2D translation offsets $(U_{offset}, V_{offset})$ added to texture coordinates post-projection. Default is `Vector2(0f, 0f)`.
- `m_Rotation` (`float`): Serialized backing field for `rotation`. Specifies clockwise rotation angle in degrees applied to projected UV coordinates. Default is `0f`.
- `m_Anchor` (`AutoUnwrapSettings.Anchor`): Serialized backing field for `anchor`. Specifies the 2D bounding alignment anchor point. Default is `Anchor.None`.

2. `AutoUnwrapSettings.Anchor` Enumeration:
Defines the reference point from which UV transformations execute:
- `UpperLeft = 0`: Projected UV bounding top-left corner aligns with $(0, 1)$.
- `UpperCenter = 1`: Projected UV bounding top-center aligns with $(0.5, 1)$.
- `UpperRight = 2`: Projected UV bounding top-right aligns with $(1, 1)$.
- `MiddleLeft = 3`: Projected UV bounding middle-left aligns with $(0, 0.5)$.
- `MiddleCenter = 4`: Projected UV bounding center aligns with $(0.5, 0.5)$.
- `MiddleRight = 5`: Projected UV bounding middle-right aligns with $(1, 0.5)$.
- `LowerLeft = 6`: Projected UV bounding lower-left aligns with $(0, 0)$.
- `LowerCenter = 7`: Projected UV bounding lower-center aligns with $(0.5, 0)$.
- `LowerRight = 8`: Projected UV bounding lower-right aligns with $(1, 0)$.
- `None = 9`: UV coordinates undergo no anchor alignment translation.

3. `AutoUnwrapSettings.Fill` Enumeration:
Controls how projected UV bounds fit into normalized coordinate space:
- `Fit = 0`: Scales UV bounds to fit inside a $1.0 \times 1.0$ unit texture square while strictly preserving the geometric aspect ratio.
- `Tile = 1`: Preserves metric geometric scale directly without normalizing or resizing bounds.
- `Stretch = 2`: Non-uniformly scales UV bounds to stretch and completely fill the $1.0 \times 1.0$ unit texture square, ignoring geometric aspect ratio.

4. Factory Presets and Lifecycle Methods:
- `defaultAutoUnwrapSettings`: Static property returning an `AutoUnwrapSettings` instance initialized via `Reset()`.
- `tile`: Static property returning default settings with `fill = Fill.Tile`.
- `fit`: Static property returning default settings with `fill = Fill.Fit`.
- `stretch`: Static property returning default settings with `fill = Fill.Stretch`.
- `Reset()`: Restores all fields to default state:
  `m_UseWorldSpace = false`, `m_FlipU = false`, `m_FlipV = false`, `m_SwapUV = false`, `m_Fill = Fill.Tile`, `m_Scale = Vector2.one`, `m_Offset = Vector2.zero`, `m_Rotation = 0f`, `m_Anchor = Anchor.None`.
- Copy Constructor `AutoUnwrapSettings(AutoUnwrapSettings unwrapSettings)`: Copies all 9 serialized property values from source instance.
- `ToString()`: Formats multiline debug string containing string representations of all 9 fields.

### UNWRAP PARAMETERS: LIGHTMAP UV2 UNWRAP CONSTRAINTS AND TOLERANCES

The `UnwrapParameters` class encapsulates the geometric constraints, chart seam angle thresholds, and packaging margins utilized when generating secondary UV channels (UV2) for lightmapping.

1. Class Constants (`UnwrapParameters.cs`):
- `internal const float k_HardAngle = 88f`: Default dihedral angle threshold in degrees for cutting UV chart seams.
- `internal const float k_PackMargin = 20f`: Default packaging margin in pixels between neighboring UV charts on a 1024x1024 lightmap texture.
- `internal const float k_AngleError = 8f`: Default maximum permitted angular distortion percentage.
- `internal const float k_AreaError = 15f`: Default maximum permitted triangle surface area distortion percentage.

2. Serialized Fields and Property Specifications:
- `m_HardAngle` / `hardAngle` (`float`, `[Range(1f, 180f)]`, `[FormerlySerializedAs("hardAngle")]`):
  Specifies the dihedral angle threshold between adjacent triangle face normals. When the angle between neighboring triangles exceeds this threshold, the unwrapper cuts a chart seam along the shared edge. Default value is `88f`.
- `m_PackMargin` / `packMargin` (`float`, `[Range(1f, 64f)]`, `[FormerlySerializedAs("packMargin")]`):
  Specifies the spacing between neighboring UV charts measured in texels/pixels, assuming the mesh occupies a standard $1024 \times 1024$ lightmap texture. Prevents lightmap texel bleeding across UV chart boundaries. Default value is `20f`.
- `m_AngleError` / `angleError` (`float`, `[Range(1f, 75f)]`, `[FormerlySerializedAs("angleError")]`):
  Specifies the maximum permissible deviation percentage between 2D UV triangle angles and corresponding 3D geometry triangle angles. Controls angular deformation during chart flattening. Default value is `8f`.
- `m_AreaError` / `areaError` (`float`, `[Range(1f, 75f)]`, `[FormerlySerializedAs("areaError")]`):
  Specifies the maximum permissible deviation percentage between 2D UV triangle surface area and uniformly scaled 3D geometry triangle surface area. Prevents localized texel density stretching or compression. Default value is `15f`.

3. Methods and Constructors:
- Parameterless Constructor `UnwrapParameters()`: Instantiates class and calls `Reset()` to apply all `k_*` constant defaults.
- Copy Constructor `UnwrapParameters(UnwrapParameters other)`: Validates that `other` is not null (throwing `System.ArgumentNullException` if null) and copies `hardAngle`, `packMargin`, `angleError`, and `areaError`.
- `Reset()`: Restores all 4 properties to `k_HardAngle` (`88f`), `k_PackMargin` (`20f`), `k_AngleError` (`8f`), and `k_AreaError` (`15f`).
- `ToString()`: Formats parameters into string:
  `string.Format("hardAngle: {0}\npackMargin: {1}\nangleError: {2}\nareaError: {3}", hardAngle, packMargin, angleError, areaError)`.

            areaError = k_AreaError;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Returns a string representation of the UnwrapParameters.
        /// </summary>
        /// <returns>String formatted as follows:
        ///
        /// `hardAngle: [hardAngle]`
        ///
        /// `packMargin: [packMargin]`
        ///
        /// `angleError: [angleError]`
        ///
        /// `areaError: [areaError]`</returns>
        public override string ToString()
        {
            return string.Format("hardAngle: {0}\npackMargin: {1}\nangleError: {2}\nareaError: {3}",
                hardAngle,
                packMargin,
                angleError,
                areaError);
        }
    }
```

</details>

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, lightmap UV generation is performed via Mesh.lightmap_unwrap(Transform3D, texel_size) or xatlas / the built-in unwrapper, which accepts pack margin, max angle error, and chart angle thresholds equivalent to UnwrapParameters.

### PREFERENCE KEYS: CONFIGURATION STRINGS, TYPES, DEFAULTS, AND CONSTANTS

ProBuilder maintains a centralized repository of preference configuration keys, menu index offsets, UI colors, and keyboard symbol constants in `PreferenceKeys.cs`, integrated with modern `SettingsManagement.Pref<T>` storage in `PreferencesUpdater.cs`.

1. Product and UI Constant Values (`PreferenceKeys.cs`):
- `pluginTitle`: Value `"ProBuilder"` (`string`). Product name string.
- `k_MaxPointDistanceFromControl`: Value `20f` (`float`). Maximum mouse screen pixel distance for snapping/hovering control points.
- `DEGREE_SYMBOL`: Value `(char)176` (`'°'`). Degree symbol for rotation readouts.
- `CMD_SUPER`: Value `'\u2318'` (`'⌘'`). Command key symbol on macOS.
- `CMD_SHIFT`: Value `'\u21E7'` (`'⇧'`). Shift key symbol.
- `CMD_OPTION`: Value `'\u2325'` (`'⌥'`). Option key symbol on macOS.
- `CMD_ALT`: Value `'\u2387'` (`'⎇'`). Alt key symbol on Windows.
- `CMD_DELETE`: Value `'\u232B'` (`'⌫'`). Delete key symbol.
- `proBuilderBlue`: Value `Color(0f, .682f, .937f, 1f)`. Brand accent color.
- `proBuilderLightGray`: Value `Color(.35f, .35f, .35f, .4f)`. UI separator color.
- `proBuilderDarkGray`: Value `Color(.1f, .1f, .1f, .3f)`. UI panel background color.

2. Menu Starting Index Offsets:
- `menuEditor`: Value `100`. Base priority for editor window menu items.
- `menuSelection`: Value `200`. Base priority for selection menu items.
- `menuGeometry`: Value `200`. Base priority for geometry operations.
- `menuActions`: Value `300`. Base priority for action menu items.
- `menuMaterialColors`: Value `400`. Base priority for material palette actions.
- `menuVertexColors`: Value `400`. Base priority for vertex color palette actions.
- `menuRepair`: Value `600`. Base priority for mesh repair actions.
- `menuMisc`: Value `600`. Base priority for miscellaneous tool actions.
- `menuExport`: Value `800`. Base priority for asset export actions.

3. Preference Key Strings, Types, Defaults, and Scopes:
Below is the complete catalog of all preference keys mapping obsolete string identifiers from `PreferenceKeys.cs` to their modern `Pref<T>` keys in `PreferencesUpdater.cs` and active `[UserSetting]` declarations:

- `graphics.handlesUseUnityColors` (legacy: `pbUseUnityColors`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Use standard Unity scene color preferences.
- `graphics.ditherFaceHandles` (legacy: `pbSelectedFaceDither`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Use dithered pattern for selected and hover face overlays.
- `graphics.userSelectedFaceColor` (legacy: `pbSelectedFaceColor` / `pbDefaultFaceColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0f, 0.824f, 0.937f, 1f)` (`#00D2EF`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Overlay color for selected faces.
- `graphics.userWireframeColor` (legacy: `pbWireframeColor` / `pbDefaultEdgeColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0.490f, 0.608f, 0.725f, 1f)` (`#7D9BB9`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Wireframe edge rendering color.
- `graphics.userUnselectedEdgeColor` (legacy: `pbUnselectedEdgeColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0.173f, 0.173f, 0.173f, 1f)` (`#2C2C2C`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Unselected edge line color.
- `graphics.userSelectedEdgeColor` (legacy: `pbSelectedEdgeColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0f, 0.824f, 0.937f, 1f)` (`#00D2EF`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Selected edge highlight color.
- `graphics.userUnselectedVertexColor` (legacy: `pbUnselectedVertexColor` / `pbDefaultVertexColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0.173f, 0.173f, 0.173f, 1f)` (`#2C2C2C`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Unselected vertex point color.
- `graphics.userSelectedVertexColor` (legacy: `pbSelectedVertexColor` / `pbDefaultSelectedVertexColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0f, 0.824f, 0.937f, 1f)` (`#00D2EF`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Selected vertex highlight color.
- `graphics.userPreselectionColor` (legacy: `pbPreselectionColor`): Type `Color`, default `Color(0.702f, 0.965f, 1f, 1f)` (`#B3F6FF`), Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Highlight color for hovered elements.
- `graphics.wireframeLineSize` (legacy: `pbWireframeSize`): Type `float`, default `0.5f`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Line width for mesh wireframes.
- `graphics.edgeLineSize` (legacy: `pbLineHandleSize`): Type `float`, default `1.0f`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Line width for interactive edge handles.
- `graphics.vertexPointSize` (legacy: `pbVertexHandleSize`): Type `float`, default `3.0f`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Point size for interactive vertex handles.
- `graphics.xRayView` (legacy: `pbEnableBackfaceSelection`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Renders occluded selected elements with faded appearance.
- `editor.showEditorNotifications` (legacy: `pbShowEditorNotifications`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Displays notification popups in Scene view on action execution.
- `mesh.defaultStaticEditorFlags` (legacy: `pbDefaultStaticFlags`): Type `StaticEditorFlags`, default `0` (`Nothing`), Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Default static flags for new ProBuilder meshes.
- `mesh.userMaterial` (legacy: `pbDefaultMaterial`): Type `Material`, default `null`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Default material applied to newly created shapes.
- `mesh.meshColliderIsConvex` (legacy: `pbForceConvex`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Sets convex flag on attached `MeshCollider`.
- `mesh.newShapesSnapToGrid` (legacy: `pbForceGridPivot`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Instantiates new shapes aligned to nearest grid coordinate.
- `mesh.shadowCastingMode` (legacy: `pbShadowCastingMode`): Type `ShadowCastingMode`, default `ShadowCastingMode.On`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Default shadow casting mode for `MeshRenderer`.
- `mesh.newShapeColliderType` (legacy: `pbDefaultCollider`): Type `ColliderType`, default `ColliderType.MeshCollider`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Default collider type applied to new shapes.
- `experimental.enabled` (legacy: `pbEnableExperimental`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Enables experimental features in menus.
- `experimental.meshesAreAssets` (legacy: `pbMeshesAreAssets`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Saves mesh assets to Project folder instead of scene files.
- `lightmapping.autoUnwrapLightmapUV` (legacy: `pbDisableAutoUV2Generation`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Automatically generates UV2 lightmap array upon geometry edits.
- `lightmapping.showMissingLightmapWarning` (legacy: `pb_Lightmapping::showMissingLightmapUvWarning`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Logs console warning if baking lightmaps on meshes without UV2.
- `lightmapping.defaultLightmapUnwrapParameters` (legacy: `defaultUnwrapParameters`): Type `UnwrapParameters`, default `new UnwrapParameters()`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Default lightmap unwrap parameters.
- `editor.showSceneInfo` (legacy: `pbShowSceneInfo`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Displays face, vertex, and triangle counts in Scene view overlay.
- `editor.showPreselectionHighlight` (legacy: `pbShowPreselectionHighlight`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Enables hover highlighting for closest mesh elements.
- `editor.stripProBuilderScriptsOnBuild` (legacy: `pbStripProBuilderOnBuild`): Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Strips ProBuilder scripts during executable build.
- `uv.uvEditorGridSnapIncrement` (legacy: `pbUVGridSnapValue`): Type `float`, default `0.125f`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Grid snap increment in UV Editor.
- `editor.autoRecalculateCollisions` (legacy: `pbAutoRecalculateCollisions`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Automatically recalculates collider bounds as mesh geometry is edited.
- `editor.allowNonManifoldActions` (legacy: `pbManifoldEdgeExtrusion`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Enables advanced operations capable of producing non-manifold topology.
- `editor.autoUpdatePreview` (legacy: `pbAutoUpdatePreview`): Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.Project`. Continuously updates action preview in real time without interaction delay.
- `editor.dragSelectRectMode` (legacy: `pbRectSelectMode` / `pbDragSelectMode`): Type `RectSelectMode`, default `RectSelectMode.Partial`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Drag marquee selection mode (`Partial` vs `Complete`).
- `editor.handleOrientation` (legacy: `pbHandleAlignment`): Type `HandleOrientation`, default `HandleOrientation.World`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Scene gizmo orientation mode.
- `editor.pivotPoint` (legacy: `pbDefaultEditLevel`): Type `PivotPoint`, default `PivotPoint.Center`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Transformation pivot calculation mode.
- `editor.pivotModePivotEquivalent`: Type `PivotPoint`, default `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Internal pivot mode mapped to Unity's `PivotMode.Pivot` setting.
- `editor.showHandleDelta`: Type `bool`, default `false`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Displays numeric delta readouts next to scene handles during translation, rotation, and scaling.
- `ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAsGroup`: Type `bool`, default `true`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Preserves relative offsets among selected elements during grid snapping.
- `ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAxis`: Type `SnapAxis`, default `SnapAxis.ActiveAxis`, Scope `SettingsScope.User`. Snaps vertices only along the active translation axis.

### RECT SELECT: PARTIAL VS COMPLETE DRAG SELECTION GEOMETRY INTERSECTION

The marquee drag selection system allows selecting sub-mesh geometry (`Face`, `Edge`, `Vertex`) via a 2D screen-space drag rectangle. The selection behavior is governed by the `RectSelectMode` enumeration, which defines two distinct intersection modes: `Partial` and `Complete`.

1. `RectSelectMode.Complete` (`1`):
In `Complete` mode, a mesh element is selected only if all of its constituent vertices are positioned in front of the camera near clip plane and are completely enclosed within the screen-space drag rectangle.

A. Face Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickFacesInRect`):
- Projects all mesh vertex positions to GUI screen space:
  `screenPoints[nn] = cam.ScreenToGuiPoint(cam.WorldToScreenPoint(trs.TransformPoint(positions[nn])), pixelsPerPoint)`
- For each `Face face` in `pb.facesInternal`:
  - Validates that the first vertex index is in front of the camera: `if (screenPoints[face.indexesInternal[0]].z < cam.nearClipPlane) continue;`
  - Tests if `rect.Contains(screenPoints[face.indexesInternal[0]])` is `true`.
  - Iterates through all remaining distinct indices $q \in [1, \text{face.distinctIndexesInternal.Length}-1]$:
    If `screenPoints[index].z < cam.nearClipPlane` or `!rect.Contains(screenPoints[index])`, the face fails enclosure (`nope = true`) and is rejected.
  - If all distinct vertices lie inside `rect`, verifies depth occlusion if `options.depthTest` is enabled via `HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, trs.TransformPoint(Math.Average(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal)))`.
  - If unoccluded, appends `face` to `selectedFaces`.

B. Edge Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickEdgesInRect`):
- Transforms edge endpoints $a$ and $b$ to screen GUI points.
- Validates that both endpoints are in front of the camera: `if (a.z < cam.nearClipPlane || b.z < cam.nearClipPlane) continue;`
- Tests if both endpoints are contained in the rectangle: `if (rect.Contains(a) && rect.Contains(b))`
- If `options.depthTest` is active, evaluates `!HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, (posA + posB) * 0.5f)`.
- If valid, appends `edge` to `selectedEdges`.

2. `RectSelectMode.Partial` (`0`):
In `Partial` mode, a mesh element is selected if any part of its 2D projected screen geometry intersects, touches, or overlaps the drag rectangle.

A. Face Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickFacesInRect`):
- When `options.depthTest` is enabled with `RectSelectMode.Partial`, selection delegates to GPU color-buffer picking via `SelectionPickerRenderer.PickFacesInRect`, rendering face index colors into an off-screen render texture and sampling pixels inside `rect`.
- When software picking is evaluated (depth test disabled):
  - Constructs a 2D bounding box `Bounds2D poly = new Bounds2D(screenPoints, face.edgesInternal)`.
  - Fast rejection: tests if `poly.Intersects(rect)` is `false`. If no bounds overlap, skips face.
  - Point-in-Rectangle Test: checks if any polygon vertex is enclosed by `rect` with $z > \text{cam.nearClipPlane}$.
  - Rectangle-in-Polygon Test: if no vertex is inside `rect`, checks if any of the 4 drag rectangle corners (`tl`, `tr`, `bl`, `br`) is enclosed inside the face polygon using `Math.PointInPolygon(screenPoints, poly, face.edgesInternal, corner)`.
  - Edge-Edge Intersection Test: tests whether any of the face's projected edge segments intersect any of the 4 boundary line segments of `rect` using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect`.
  - If any intersection test returns `true`, appends `face` to `selectedFaces`.

B. Edge Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickEdgesInRect`):
- When `options.depthTest` is active, delegates to GPU color-buffer picking via `SelectionPickerRenderer.PickEdgesInRect`.
- When software picking is evaluated, tests if the line segment between projected endpoints $a$ and $b$ intersects the 2D rectangle using `Math.RectIntersectsLineSegment(rect, a, b)`.
- If line segment intersects or lies inside `rect`, appends `edge` to `selectedEdges`.

3. Vertex Selection (`SelectionPicker.PickVerticesInRect`):
Vertex selection evaluates individual point inclusion `rect.Contains(screenPoint)` with $z > \text{cam.nearClipPlane}$, followed by optional occlusion testing `HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded`. Vertex picking behaves identically across both `Partial` and `Complete` modes.

        public static Dictionary<ProBuilderMesh, HashSet<Edge>> PickEdgesInRect(
            Camera cam,
            Rect rect,
            IList<ProBuilderMesh> selectable,
            PickerOptions options,
            float pixelsPerPoint = 1f)
        {
            if (options.depthTest && options.rectSelectMode == RectSelectMode.Partial)
            {
                return SelectionPickerRenderer.PickEdgesInRect(
                    cam,
                    rect,
                    selectable,
                    true,
                    (int)(cam.pixelWidth / pixelsPerPoint),
                    (int)(cam.pixelHeight / pixelsPerPoint));
            }

            var selected = new Dictionary<ProBuilderMesh, HashSet<Edge>>();

            foreach (var pb in selectable)
            {
                if (!pb.selectable)
                    continue;

                Transform trs = pb.transform;
                var selectedEdges = new HashSet<Edge>();

                for (int i = 0, fc = pb.faceCount; i < fc; i++)
                {
                    var edges = pb.facesInternal[i].edgesInternal;

                    for (int n = 0, ec = edges.Length; n < ec; n++)
                    {
                        var edge = edges[n];

                        var posA = trs.TransformPoint(pb.positionsInternal[edge.a]);
                        var posB = trs.TransformPoint(pb.positionsInternal[edge.b]);

                        Vector3 a = cam.ScreenToGuiPoint(cam.WorldToScreenPoint(posA), pixelsPerPoint);
                        Vector3 b = cam.ScreenToGuiPoint(cam.WorldToScreenPoint(posB), pixelsPerPoint);

                        switch (options.rectSelectMode)
                        {
                            case RectSelectMode.Complete:
                            {
                                // if either of the positions are clipped by the camera we cannot possibly select both, skip it
                                if ((a.z < cam.nearClipPlane || b.z < cam.nearClipPlane))
                                    continue;

                                if (rect.Contains(a) && rect.Contains(b))

                                // partial + depth test is covered earlier
                                if (Math.RectIntersectsLineSegment(rect, a, b))

### SELECTION MODIFIER: ADD, SUBTRACT, AND DIFFERENCE BEHAVIOR WITH KEYBOARD MODIFIERS

The selection modifier system defines how keyboard modifier combinations (Shift, Control, and Command) adjust element selection during single-click raycasting and marquee drag operations.

1. `SelectionModifierBehavior` Enumeration (`SelectionModifierBehaviour.cs`):
- `Add = 0`: Always performs a set union, adding target elements to the existing selection.
- `Subtract = 1`: Always performs a set difference, removing target elements from the existing selection.
- `Difference = 2`: Inverts the selection status of target elements (elements currently selected are deselected; unselected elements are selected).

2. Modifier Key Detection (`EditorHandleUtility.cs`):
Modifier states are queried from `EventModifiers` flags:
- `IsAppendModifier(EventModifiers em)`: Returns `true` if Shift, Control, Alt, or Command is active:
  `(em & EventModifiers.Shift) == EventModifiers.Shift || (em & EventModifiers.Control) == EventModifiers.Control || (em & EventModifiers.Alt) == EventModifiers.Alt || (em & EventModifiers.Command) == EventModifiers.Command`
- `IsSelectionAddModifier(EventModifiers em)`: Returns `true` if Shift is active:
  `(em & EventModifiers.Shift) == EventModifiers.Shift`
- `IsSelectionAppendOrRemoveIfPresentModifier(EventModifiers em)`: Platform-aware toggle modifier. Returns `true` if Command is active on macOS (`RuntimePlatform.OSXEditor`), or if Control is active on Windows/Linux:
  `((Application.platform == RuntimePlatform.OSXEditor) && (em & EventModifiers.Command) == EventModifiers.Command) || ((Application.platform != RuntimePlatform.OSXEditor) && (em & EventModifiers.Control) == EventModifiers.Control)`

3. Single-Click Element Selection Logic (`EditorSceneViewPicker.DoMouseClick`):
When the user clicks in the Scene view:
- If no append modifier is active (`!appendModifier`):
  Calls `mesh.ClearSelection()` and `MeshSelection.ClearElementSelection()` before applying the new selection.
- If Shift is pressed (`addToSelectionModifier`):
  Appends the clicked element to the active selection. If the element is already selected and is the active element on the current active mesh, it is removed from the selection.
- If Control/Command is pressed (`addOrRemoveIfPresentFromSelectionModifier`):
  Toggles the element selection state: if the element is already selected, removes it via `RemoveFromFaceSelectionAtIndex` / `SetSelectedEdges` / `SetSelectedVertices`; if not selected, appends it.

4. Marquee Drag Selection Logic (`EditorSceneViewPicker.DoMouseDrag`):
When dragging a marquee rectangle in the Scene view:
- Evaluates modifier states: `isSelectionAddModifier` (Shift), `isSelectionRemoveModifier` (Control/Command), and `isAppendModifier = isSelectionAddModifier || isSelectionRemoveModifier`.
- If no modifier is pressed (`!isAppendModifier`), calls `MeshSelection.ClearElementSelection()` before applying results.
- For Vertex Selection:
  - Gathers existing shared vertex handles: `common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`
  - If `isSelectionAddModifier` (Shift): executes set union `common.UnionWith(kvp.Value)`.
  - If `isSelectionRemoveModifier` (Ctrl/Cmd): executes set difference `common.RemoveWhere(x => kvp.Value.Contains(x))`.
  - Applies updated vertices: `mesh.SetSelectedVertices(common.SelectMany(x => sharedIndexes[x]))`.
- For Face Selection:
  - Instantiates set of current faces: `current = new HashSet<Face>(kvp.Key.selectedFacesInternal)`.
  - If `isSelectionAddModifier` (Shift): executes set union `current.UnionWith(kvp.Value)`.
  - If `isSelectionRemoveModifier` (Ctrl/Cmd): executes set difference `current.RemoveWhere(x => kvp.Value.Contains(x))`.
  - Applies updated faces: `kvp.Key.SetSelectedFaces(current)`.
- For Edge Selection:
  - Maps edges to shared vertex space: `current = EdgeLookup.GetEdgeLookupHashSet(mesh.selectedEdges, common)`.
  - If `isSelectionAddModifier` (Shift): executes set union `current.UnionWith(selectedEdges)`.
  - If `isSelectionRemoveModifier` (Ctrl/Cmd): executes set difference `current.RemoveWhere(x => selectedEdges.Contains(x))`.
  - Applies updated edges: `mesh.SetSelectedEdges(current.Select(x => x.local))`.

5. Auxiliary Transformation and Mask Structures:
- `HandleConstraint2D` (`HandleConstraint2D.cs`): Class encapsulating 2D coordinate masks with integer fields `x` and `y`. Provides `Mask(Vector2 v)` ($v.x \cdot x, v.y \cdot y$), `InverseMask(Vector2 v)` ($v.x \cdot (x==1?0:1), v.y \cdot (y==1?0:1)$), and static constant `HandleConstraint2D.None = new HandleConstraint2D(1, 1)`.
- `Vector2Mask` and `Vector3Mask` (`VectorMask.cs`): Value-type structs storing bitmasked axes (`X = 1 << 0`, `Y = 1 << 1`, `Z = 1 << 2`). Implements bitwise operators (`|`, `&`, `^`), vector multiplication, rotation transformations `Quaternion * Vector3Mask`, component indexers, and `active` axis count property.
- `ActionResult` (`ActionResult.cs`): Encapsulates operation results with `Status` (`Success`, `Failure`, `Canceled`, `NoChange`), notification message string, implicit `bool` conversion operator, and static helpers `Success`, `NoSelection`, and `UserCanceled`.

    struct Vector3Mask : IEquatable<Vector3Mask>
    {
        const byte X = 1 << 0;
        const byte Y = 1 << 1;
        const byte Z = 1 << 2;

        public static readonly Vector3Mask XYZ = new Vector3Mask(X | Y | Z);

        byte m_Mask;

        public float x
        {
            get { return (m_Mask & X) == X ? 1f : 0f; }
        }

        public float y
        {
            get { return (m_Mask & Y) == Y ? 1f : 0f; }
        }

        public float z
        {
            get { return (m_Mask & Z) == Z ? 1f : 0f; }
        }

        public Vector3Mask(Vector3 v, float epsilon = float.Epsilon)
        {
            m_Mask = 0x0;

            if (Mathf.Abs(v.x) > epsilon)
                m_Mask |= X;
            if (Mathf.Abs(v.y) > epsilon)
                m_Mask |= Y;
            if (Mathf.Abs(v.z) > epsilon)
                m_Mask |= Z;
        }

## A04: Math, projection, snapping utilities

### SNAPPING

ProBuilder provides a dedicated geometric snapping subsystem implemented across `ProBuilderSnapping` (runtime math) and `EditorSnapping` (editor settings and tool orchestration). Snapping operates in scalar, 3D vector, per-vertex, and ray-constrained modes.

1. Scalar and Vector Snapping Algorithms:
- `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(float val, float snap)`: Evaluates whether `snap == 0`. If zero, returns `val` unmodified. Otherwise, computes `snap * Mathf.Round(val / snap)`, quantizing the value to the nearest integer multiple of `snap`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(Vector3 val, Vector3 snap)`: Quantizes each coordinate independently. Evaluates whether `Mathf.Abs(snap.x) > 0.0001f` (using a minimum epsilon threshold to ignore floating-point noise). If true, calculates `Snap(val.x, snap.x)`; otherwise leaves `val.x` unmodified. The same check applies to `val.y` and `val.z`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapVertices(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, Vector3 snap)`: Snaps mesh vertices in world space. For every index in `indexes`, retrieves the local vertex position from `mesh.positionsInternal`, transforms it to world space via `mesh.transform.TransformPoint`, applies `Snap(worldPoint, snap)`, and converts the result back to local space using `mesh.transform.InverseTransformPoint`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.GetSnappingMaskBasedOnNormalVector(Vector3 normal)`: Generates a vector mask based on face orientation. For each axis (X, Y, Z), if `Mathf.Approximately(Mathf.Abs(normal[axis]), 1f)`, the mask component is set to `0f`; otherwise `1f`. This prevents snapping along the normal direction of an aligned surface while permitting snapping across the plane of the face.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.IsCardinalDirection(Vector3 direction)`: Returns true if exactly one component is non-zero (`Mathf.Abs(direction[axis]) > 0f`) and the remaining two components are approximately zero (`Mathf.Approximately(direction[other], 0f)`).

2. Ray Snapping Algorithm (`SnapValueOnRay`):
- `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay(Ray ray, float distance, float snap, Vector3Mask mask)`: Determines the closest discrete grid snap point along a movement ray.
  a. Initializes `nearest = k_MaxRaySnapDistance` (`Mathf.Infinity`).
  b. Constructs `forwardRay = new Ray(ray.origin, ray.direction)` and `backwardsRay = new Ray(ray.origin, -ray.direction)`.
  c. Iterates through the 3 primary axes (i = 0, 1, 2). If `mask[i] > 0f`:
     - Creates axis mask `dir = new Vector3Mask((byte)(1 << i))`.
     - Projects the movement ray vector `ray.direction * Math.MakeNonZero(distance)` onto `dir * Mathf.Sign(ray.direction[i])` using `Vector3.Project`.
     - Computes projected point `pnt = ray.origin + prj` and creates a snapping plane: `plane = new Plane(dir, Snap(pnt, dir * snap))`.
     - If `Mathf.Abs(plane.GetDistanceToPoint(ray.origin)) < 0.0001f`, sets `nearest = 0f` and continues.
     - Raycasts `forwardRay` against `plane`; if intersection distance `d` satisfies `Mathf.Abs(d) < Mathf.Abs(nearest)`, updates `nearest = d`.
     - Raycasts `backwardsRay` against `plane`; if intersection distance `d` satisfies `Mathf.Abs(d) < Mathf.Abs(nearest)`, updates `nearest = -d`.
  d. Returns the snapped 3D position `ray.origin + ray.direction * (Mathf.Abs(nearest) >= k_MaxRaySnapDistance ? distance : nearest)`.

3. ProGrids Integration and Snap Modes:
- ProGrids integration operates through `ProGridsInterface`, a reflection bridge that probes for types `UnityEditor.ProGrids.ProGridsEditor`, `ProGrids.Editor.ProGridsEditor`, `ProGrids.Editor.pg_Editor`, `ProGrids.pg_Editor`, and `pg_Editor`.
- Delegates bind to ProGrids methods: `s_ProGridsActiveDelegate`, `s_SnapEnabledDelegate`, `s_ProGridsSnapAsGroupDelegate`, `s_IsFullGridEnabledDelegate`, `s_GetActiveGridOffsetDelegate`, `s_SnapValueDelegate`, and `s_GetPivotDelegate`.
- `ProBuilderEditor.PushToGrid(float snapVal)` subscribes to `ProGridsInterface.SubscribePushToGridEvent`. When triggered, it queries coincident vertices via `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`, invokes `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapVertices(mesh, indexes, Vector3.one * snapVal)`, and calls `mesh.ToMesh()` followed by `mesh.Refresh()`.
- `EditorSnapping.snapMode` resolves to:
  - `SnapMode.Relative`: Active when `EditorSnapSettings.incrementalSnapActive` is enabled. Snapping increments are relative to the drag start.
  - `SnapMode.World`: Active when `ProGridsInterface.SnapEnabled()` is true or when `EditorSnapSettings.gridSnapActive` is true and `Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Global`. Snaps directly to absolute world grid coordinates.
  - `SnapMode.None`: Snapping is inactive.

4. Element Snapping During Movement:
- In `ProbuilderMoveTool` and `VertexManipulationTool`, element translation respects `EditorSnapping.snapAsGroup` (backed by user preference `ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAsGroup`, default `true`, or ProGrids `GetSnapAsGroup()`):
  - Group Snapping (`m_SnapAsGroup == true`): The tool calculates the global handle position, snaps the handle pivot to the grid via `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap` or `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay`, and applies the resulting delta uniformly to all selected vertices/faces/edges. This preserves relative offsets between elements.
  - Individual Snapping (`m_SnapAsGroup == false`): When `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World`, each vertex is transformed to world space (`wp`), snapped individually to the grid via `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(wp, snapValue)` (or along constrained single axes with `SnapValueOnRay`), and converted back to model space using `worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(snap)`.

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, scalar and vector snapping can be implemented using `Mathf.snapped()` or `Vector3.snapped(step)`. World-space vertex snapping is performed by transforming vertex arrays with `Node3D.global_transform`, calling `.snapped(snap_step)`, and converting back via `global_transform.affine_inverse()`. Group vs individual snapping modes in Godot editor gizmos correspond to snapping the gizmo transform origin vs snapping individual vertex coordinates.

### MATH

The `Math` static class defines the foundational geometric and linear algebra functions utilized throughout mesh generation, editing, UV manipulation, and spatial queries.

1. Constants and Tolerances:
- `phi`: The golden ratio constant `1.618033988749895f`.
- `k_FltEpsilon`: Machine epsilon `float.Epsilon`.
- `k_FltCompareEpsilon`: Vertex comparison tolerance `0.0001f`.
- `handleEpsilon`: Minimum handle movement threshold `0.0001f`.

2. Geometric Point Generation and Angles:
- `PointInCircumference(float radius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin)`: Converts degrees to radians with `Mathf.Deg2Rad * angleInDegrees`, computing `x = radius * Mathf.Cos(rad) + origin.x` and `y = radius * Mathf.Sin(rad) + origin.y`.
- `PointInEllipseCircumference(float xRadius, float yRadius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin, out Vector2 tangent)`: Computes ellipse perimeter point `x = xRadius * cosA + origin.x`, `y = yRadius * sinA + origin.y`, and normalizes tangent vector `tangent = new Vector2(-y / (yRadius * yRadius), x / (xRadius * xRadius)).normalized`.
- `PointInEllipseCircumferenceWithConstantAngle(float xRadius, float yRadius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin, out Vector2 tangent)`: Calculates constant angular perimeter distribution using `tan = Mathf.Tan(rad)`, `tan2 = tan * tan`, `newX = (xRadius * yRadius) / Mathf.Sqrt(yRadius * yRadius + xRadius * xRadius * tan2)` (negated if `cosA < 0`), and `newY = (xRadius * yRadius) / Mathf.Sqrt(xRadius * xRadius + yRadius * yRadius / tan2)` (negated if `sinA < 0`).
- `PointInSphere(float radius, float latitudeAngle, float longitudeAngle)`: Computes spherical 3D coordinates `x = radius * Cos(lat) * Sin(lon)`, `y = radius * Sin(lat) * Sin(lon)`, `z = radius * Cos(lon)`.
- `SignedAngle(Vector2 a, Vector2 b)`: Calculates `t = Vector2.Angle(a, b)`. If `b.x - a.x < 0`, returns `360f - t`; otherwise returns `t`.

3. Distance, Area, and Centroid Metrics:
- `SqrDistance(Vector3 a, Vector3 b)`: Computes squared distance `dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz` without square root evaluation.
- `TriangleArea(Vector3 x, Vector3 y, Vector3 z)`: Implements high-precision triangle area calculation using squared edge lengths `a = SqrDistance(x, y)`, `b = SqrDistance(y, z)`, `c = SqrDistance(z, x)`:
  $$\text{Area} = \sqrt{\frac{2ab + 2bc + 2ca - a^2 - b^2 - c^2}{16}}$$
- `PolygonArea(Vector3[] vertices, int[] indexes)`: Sums `TriangleArea` for every triangle triple `indexes[i]`, `indexes[i+1]`, `indexes[i+2]` in the polygon index buffer.
- `Average(IList<Vector2>/Vector3/Vector4 array, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Computes the arithmetic mean (centroid) across all vectors or subset `indexes`.

4. 2D Transformations, Reflections, and Line Distances:
- `RotateAroundPoint(this Vector2 v, Vector2 origin, float theta)`: Rotates 2D vector around pivot `origin` by angle `theta` in degrees using standard sine/cosine translation matrices.
- `ScaleAroundPoint(this Vector2 v, Vector2 origin, Vector2 scale)`: Scales 2D vector relative to pivot: `(v - origin) * scale + origin`.
- `Perpendicular(Vector2 value)`: Returns 2D orthogonal vector `new Vector2(-value.y, value.x)`.
- `ReflectPoint(Vector2 point, Vector2 lineStart, Vector2 lineEnd)`: Reflects point across a 2D line segment using orthogonal projection and angle distance.
- `SqrDistanceRayPoint(Ray ray, Vector3 point)`: Computes squared distance from 3D point to ray: `Vector3.Cross(ray.direction, point - ray.origin).sqrMagnitude`.
- `DistancePointLineSegment(Vector2/Vector3 point, lineStart, lineEnd)`: Computes minimum distance from a point to a finite segment. Projects point onto segment with parameter `t = Dot(point - lineStart, lineEnd - lineStart) / l2`. If `t < 0.0`, returns distance to `lineStart`; if `t > 1.0`, returns distance to `lineEnd`; otherwise returns distance to `lineStart + t * (lineEnd - lineStart)`.
- `GetNearestPointRayRay(Vector3 ao, Vector3 ad, Vector3 bo, Vector3 bd)`: Finds the closest point on ray A to ray B in 3D skew space using dot products:
  $$c = bo - ao, \quad n = -\text{dot}(ad, bd) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, c) + \text{dot}(ad, c) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, bd)$$
  $$d = \text{dot}(ad, ad) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, bd) - \text{dot}(ad, bd)^2, \quad \text{Result} = ao + ad \cdot (n / d)$$

5. Line Segment, Polygon, and Ray Intersections:
- `GetLineSegmentIntersect(Vector2 p0, Vector2 p1, Vector2 p2, Vector2 p3, ref Vector2 intersect)`: 2D segment intersection solver. Uses parametric cross products `s` and `t`. Returns `true` if `0 <= s <= 1` and `0 <= t <= 1`, setting `intersect = p0 + t * s1`.
- `PointInPolygon(Vector2[] polygon, Vector2 point, int[] indexes = null)`: Ray-casting parity point-in-polygon algorithm. First tests `Bounds2D(polygon, indexes).ContainsPoint(point)`. If contained, casts a horizontal/directional ray from outside the bounds `bounds.center + dir * (bounds.size.y + bounds.size.x + 2f)` to `point`. Counts line segment intersections against all polygon edges; returns `collisions % 2 != 0`.
- `RectIntersectsLineSegment(Rect rect, Vector2/Vector3 a, Vector2/Vector3 b)`: Invokes `Clipping.RectContainsLineSegment(rect, a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y)`. Implements Cohen-Sutherland clipping using `OutCode` bitmask flags (`Inside = 0`, `Left = 1`, `Right = 2`, `Bottom = 4`, `Top = 8`), repeatedly testing immediate bitwise acceptance (`outcode0 | outcode1 == Inside`), immediate bitwise rejection (`(outcode0 & outcode1) != Inside`), and clipping outside points against rectangle boundaries.
- `RayIntersectsTriangle(Ray InRay, Vector3 InTriangleA, Vector3 InTriangleB, Vector3 InTriangleC, out float OutDistance, out Vector3 OutPoint)`: Möller–Trumbore ray-triangle intersection algorithm. Calculates edge vectors `e1 = B - A`, `e2 = C - A`, determinant vector `P = Cross(dir, e2)`, and determinant `det = Dot(e1, P)`. Non-culling branch rejects `det` near zero. Computes distance vector `T = origin - A`, barycentric coordinate `u = Dot(T, P) * inv_det` (rejecting `u < 0` or `u > 1`), vector `Q = Cross(T, e1)`, barycentric coordinate `v = Dot(dir, Q) * inv_det` (rejecting `v < 0` or `u + v > 1`), and ray distance `t = Dot(e2, Q) * inv_det`. If `t > Epsilon`, sets `OutDistance = t` and reconstructs intersection point `OutPoint = u*B + v*C + (1 - u - v)*A`.
- `RayIntersectsTriangle2`: Non-allocating variant of Möller–Trumbore using pre-allocated static scratch vectors `tv1`, `tv2`, `tv3`, `tv4` and outputting `ref float distance` and `ref Vector3 normal`.

6. Normal, Tangent, and Bitangent Calculations:
- `Normal(Vector3 p0, Vector3 p1, Vector3 p2)`: Calculates `Cross(p1 - p0, p2 - p0).normalized`.
- `Normal(IList<Vertex> vertices, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Averages triangle normals across index triples.
- `Normal(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)`: Evaluates face normal. If face has `<= 6` indices (triangles/quads), returns `Normal(p0, p1, p2)`. If face has `> 6` indices (n-gons), calculates the best fitting plane normal using `Projection.FindBestPlane(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal).normal`, ensuring positive alignment with the first triangle normal via `Vector3.Dot(nrm, prj)`.
- `NormalTangentBitangent(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)`: Derives orthonormal surface basis from vertex positions and UV coordinates:
  a. Extracts positions `v1, v2, v3` and UV coordinates `w1, w2, w3` for the first triangle.
  b. Computes spatial vectors `x1 = v2.x - v1.x`, `y1 = v2.y - v1.y`, `z1 = v2.z - v1.z`, `x2 = v3.x - v1.x`, `y2 = v3.y - v1.y`, `z2 = v3.z - v1.z`, and UV deltas `s1 = w2.x - w1.x`, `s2 = w3.x - w1.x`, `t1 = w2.y - w1.y`, `t2 = w3.y - w1.y`.
  c. Calculates reciprocal determinant `r = 1.0f / (s1 * t2 - s2 * t1)` and derives surface tangents:
     $$sdir = \frac{(t_2 \Delta v_1 - t_1 \Delta v_2)}{s_1 t_2 - s_2 t_1}, \quad tdir = \frac{(s_1 \Delta v_2 - s_2 \Delta v_1)}{s_1 t_2 - s_2 t_1}$$
  d. Orthonormalizes tangent against normal with `Vector3.OrthoNormalize(ref n, ref tan1)`.
  e. Determines tangent handedness sign `tan.w = Dot(Cross(n, tan1), tan2) < 0f ? -1f : 1f`.
  f. Computes bitangent `bitangent = Cross(nrm, ((Vector3)tan) * tan.w)`.

7. Vector Helpers and Transform Utilities:
- Vector approximations: `Approx2`, `Approx3`, `Approx4`, `ApproxC`, `Approx` compare vector components against `delta = 0.0001f`.
- Component utilities: `Abs`, `Sign`, `Sum`, `DivideBy`, `IsCardinalAxis`, `MakeNonZero`, `FixNaN`, `EnsureUnitVector`.
- `TransformUtility.TransformVertex(this Transform transform, Vertex vertex)`: Converts vertex position via `transform.TransformPoint`, normal via `transform.TransformDirection`, and tangent via `transform.rotation * vertex.tangent`, preserving colors and UV channels 0 through 4.
- `TransformUtility.InverseTransformVertex(this Transform transform, Vertex vertex)`: Converts vertex position with `transform.InverseTransformPoint`, normal with `transform.InverseTransformDirection`, and tangent with `transform.InverseTransformDirection`.

        internal static Vector2 PointInEllipseCircumferenceWithConstantAngle(float xRadius, float yRadius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin, out Vector2 tangent)
        {
            // Convert from degrees to radians via multiplication by PI/180
            var cosA = Mathf.Cos(Mathf.Deg2Rad * angleInDegrees);
            var sinA = Mathf.Sin(Mathf.Deg2Rad * angleInDegrees);

            float tan = Mathf.Tan(Mathf.Deg2Rad * angleInDegrees);
            float tan2 = tan * tan;
            float newX = ( xRadius * yRadius ) / Mathf.Sqrt(yRadius * yRadius + xRadius * xRadius * tan2);
            if(cosA < 0)
                newX = -newX;
            float newY = ( xRadius * yRadius ) / Mathf.Sqrt(xRadius * xRadius + yRadius * yRadius / tan2);
            if(sinA < 0)
                newY = -newY;

            tangent = new Vector2( -newY / (yRadius * yRadius), newX / (xRadius * xRadius));
            tangent.Normalize();

            return new Vector2(newX, newY);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Returns the distance between a point and a finite line segment using Vector2s.
        /// </summary>
        /// <remarks>See [Shortest distance between a point and a line segment](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/849211/shortest-distance-between-a-point-and-a-line-segment).</remarks>
        /// <param name="point">The point.</param>
        /// <param name="lineStart">Where the line starts.</param>
        /// <param name="lineEnd">Where the line ends.</param>
        /// <returns>The distance from the point to the nearest point on a line segment.</returns>
        public static float DistancePointLineSegment(Vector2 point, Vector2 lineStart, Vector2 lineEnd)
        {
            // Return minimum distance between line segment vw and point p
            float l2 = ((lineStart.x - lineEnd.x) * (lineStart.x - lineEnd.x)) + ((lineStart.y - lineEnd.y) * (lineStart.y - lineEnd.y));  // i.e. |w-v|^2 -  avoid a sqrt

            if (l2 == 0.0f) return Vector2.Distance(point, lineStart);   // v == w case

            // Consider the line extending the segment, parameterized as v + t (w - v).
            // We find projection of point p onto the line.
            // It falls where t = [(p-v) . (w-v)] / |w-v|^2
            float t = Vector2.Dot(point - lineStart, lineEnd - lineStart) / l2;

            if (t < 0.0)
                return Vector2.Distance(point, lineStart);              // Beyond the 'v' end of the segment
            else if (t > 1.0)
                return Vector2.Distance(point, lineEnd);            // Beyond the 'w' end of the segment

            Vector2 projection = lineStart + t * (lineEnd - lineStart);     // Projection falls on the segment

            return Vector2.Distance(point, projection);
        }

        internal static bool PointInPolygon(Vector3[] positions, Bounds2D polyBounds, Edge[] edges, Vector2 point)

        public static Vector3 Normal(Vector3 p0, Vector3 p1, Vector3 p2)
        {

                    bz = p2.z - p0.z;

            Vector3 cross = new Vector3(
                ay * bz - az * by,
                az * bx - ax * bz,
                ax * by - ay * bx);

            if (cross.magnitude < Mathf.Epsilon)

            cross.Normalize();
            return cross;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Finds and returns the best normal for a face.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="mesh">The mesh that the target face belongs to.</param>
        /// <param name="face">The face to calculate a normal for.</param>
        /// <returns>A normal that most closely matches the face orientation in model coordinates.</returns>
        public static Vector3 Normal(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)
        {
            if (mesh == null || face == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            var positions = mesh.positionsInternal;

            // if the face is just a quad, use the first triangle normal. otherwise it's not safe to assume that the
            // face has even generally uniform normals
            Vector3 nrm = Normal(
                    positions[face.indexesInternal[0]],
                    positions[face.indexesInternal[1]],
                    positions[face.indexesInternal[2]]);

            if (face.indexesInternal.Length > 6)
            {
                Vector3 prj = Projection.FindBestPlane(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal).normal;

                if (Vector3.Dot(nrm, prj) < 0f)
                {
                    nrm.x = -prj.x;
                    nrm.y = -prj.y;
                    nrm.z = -prj.z;
                }
                else
                {
                    nrm.x = prj.x;
                    nrm.y = prj.y;
                    nrm.z = prj.z;
                }
            }

            return nrm;
        }

        /// <summary>

        public static Vertex TransformVertex(this Transform transform, Vertex vertex)
        {
            var v = new Vertex();

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Position))
                v.position = transform.TransformPoint(vertex.position);

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Color))
                v.color = vertex.color;

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Normal))
                v.normal = transform.TransformDirection(vertex.normal);

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Tangent))
                v.tangent = transform.rotation * vertex.tangent;

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture0))
                v.uv0 = vertex.uv0;

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture1))
                v.uv2 = vertex.uv2;

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture2))
                v.uv3 = vertex.uv3;

            if (vertex.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture3))
                v.uv4 = vertex.uv4;

            return v;
        }

> **Godot Note:** Godot 4's `Geometry3D` and `Geometry2D` provide built-in equivalents for segment-segment intersection (`Geometry2D.segment_intersects_segment`), ray-triangle intersection (`Geometry3D.ray_intersects_triangle`), and point-in-polygon (`Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon`). The `Transform3D` class directly handles vertex transformations with `transform * position` (points) and `transform.basis * normal` (directions). Tangent and bitangent generation matches the standard MikkTSpace / Gram-Schmidt conventions used in Godot's `SurfaceTool.generate_tangents()`.

### PROJECTION

The `Projection` static class provides 3D-to-2D projection, planar fitting, spherical mapping, and 2D contour polygon sorting methods. These functions are critical for UV unwrapping, Auto-UV texture projection, face triangulation, and polygon hole cutting.

1. Least-Squares Best Plane Fitting (`FindBestPlane`):
- `Projection.FindBestPlane(IList<Vector3> points, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Fits an optimal 3D plane through an arbitrary set of non-coplanar or coplanar points using covariance matrix analysis.
  a. Computes centroid `c` by averaging coordinates across all target vertices:
     $$c = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} p_i$$
  b. Computes centered second-moment sums (elements of the covariance matrix):
     $$xx = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)^2, \quad yy = \sum (p_{iy} - c_y)^2, \quad zz = \sum (p_{iz} - c_z)^2$$
     $$xy = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)(p_{iy} - c_y), \quad xz = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)(p_{iz} - c_z), \quad yz = \sum (p_{iy} - c_y)(p_{iz} - c_z)$$
  c. Calculates the 2x2 minor determinants:
     $$det_x = yy \cdot zz - yz^2, \quad det_y = xx \cdot zz - xz^2, \quad det_z = xx \cdot yy - xy^2$$
  d. Selects the primary normal component based on the largest determinant:
     - If `det_x > det_y` and `det_x > det_z`: Sets $n_x = 1.0$, $n_y = \frac{xz \cdot yz - xy \cdot zz}{det_x}$, $n_z = \frac{xy \cdot yz - xz \cdot yy}{det_x}$.
     - Else if `det_y > det_z`: Sets $n_x = \frac{yz \cdot xz - xy \cdot zz}{det_y}$, $n_y = 1.0$, $n_z = \frac{xy \cdot xz - yz \cdot xx}{det_y}$.
     - Otherwise: Sets $n_x = \frac{yz \cdot xy - xz \cdot yy}{det_z}$, $n_y = \frac{xz \cdot xy - yz \cdot xx}{det_z}$, $n_z = 1.0$.
  e. Normalizes `n` and returns `new Plane(n, c)`.
- `Projection.FindBestPlane(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int textureGroup)`: Iterates across all faces matching `face.textureGroup == textureGroup`, accumulates vertices from their index buffers, and executes the identical covariance fitting algorithm to generate a shared projection plane for the entire texture group.

2. Planar Projection Algorithm (`PlanarProject`):
- `PlanarProject(IList<Vector3> positions, IList<int> indexes, Vector3 direction, List<Vector2> results)`:
  a. Ensures unit normal vector `nrm = Math.EnsureUnitVector(direction)`.
  b. Maps `nrm` to dominant axis enum `axis = VectorToProjectionAxis(nrm)`.
  c. Retrieves projection tangent vector `prj = GetTangentToAxis(axis)`:
     - `ProjectionAxis.X` / `ProjectionAxis.XNegative`: returns `Vector3.up`.
     - `ProjectionAxis.Y` / `ProjectionAxis.YNegative`: returns `Vector3.forward`.
     - `ProjectionAxis.Z` / `ProjectionAxis.ZNegative`: returns `Vector3.up`.
  d. Computes orthonormal 2D projection axes:
     $$u = (nrm \times prj).\text{normalized}, \quad v = (u \times nrm).\text{normalized}$$
  e. Projects each 3D point `p` into 2D UV coordinates using dot products:
     $$uv.x = u \cdot p, \quad uv.y = v \cdot p$$
- `PlanarProject(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face, Vector3 projection = default)`: Projects face vertices to `mesh.texturesInternal`. If `face.uv.useWorldSpace` is enabled, vertex positions are transformed using `mesh.transform.TransformPoint` and normals with `mesh.transform.TransformDirection` prior to projection.
- `PlanarProject(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int textureGroup, AutoUnwrapSettings unwrapSettings)`: Computes an average normal across all faces in the texture group, optionally transforms it to world space, and projects texture group vertices uniformly into UV space.

3. Spherical Projection and Contour Sorting:
- `SphericalProject(IList<Vector3> vertices, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Computes centroid `cen = Math.Average(vertices, indexes)`. For each vertex, computes normalized vector `p = (v - cen).normalized`, generating equirectangular UVs:
  $$uv.x = 0.5 + \frac{\text{atan2}(p.z, p.x)}{2\pi}, \quad uv.y = 0.5 - \frac{\text{asin}(p.y)}{\pi}$$
- `Projection.Sort(IList<Vector2> verts, SortMethod method = SortMethod.CounterClockwise)`: Sorts 2D points into a continuous polygon boundary. Computes 2D centroid `cen = Math.Average(verts)` and calculates `Math.SignedAngle(Vector2.up, verts[i] - cen)` for every vertex. Sorts vertices ascending by angle (or reverses the list for `SortMethod.Clockwise`).
- `VectorToProjectionAxis(Vector3 direction)`: Determines dominant projection axis (`X`, `XNegative`, `Y`, `YNegative`, `Z`, `ZNegative`) by comparing absolute values `|x|`, `|y|`, `|z|` with `Math.Approx` tie-breaking.
- `ProjectionAxisToVector(ProjectionAxis axis)`: Maps `ProjectionAxis` enum directly to `Vector3.right`, `Vector3.up`, `Vector3.forward`, `-Vector3.right`, `-Vector3.up`, or `-Vector3.forward`.

        internal static void PlanarProject(IList<Vector3> positions, IList<int> indexes, Vector3 direction, List<Vector2> results)
        {
            if(positions == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("positions");

            if(results == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("results");

            var nrm = Math.EnsureUnitVector(direction);
            var axis = VectorToProjectionAxis(nrm);
            var prj = GetTangentToAxis(axis);
            var len = indexes == null ? positions.Count : indexes.Count;
            results.Clear();

            var u = Vector3.Cross(nrm, prj);
            var v = Vector3.Cross(u, nrm);

            u.Normalize();
            v.Normalize();

            if (indexes != null)

                for (int i = 0, ic = len; i < ic; ++i)

                for (int i = 0, ic = len; i < ic; ++i)
                    results.Add(new Vector2(Vector3.Dot(u, positions[i]), Vector3.Dot(v, positions[i])));

        /// <summary>
        /// Returns a projection axis based on which axis is the largest
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="direction"></param>
        /// <returns></returns>
        internal static ProjectionAxis VectorToProjectionAxis(Vector3 direction)
        {
            float x = System.Math.Abs(direction.x);
            float y = System.Math.Abs(direction.y);
            float z = System.Math.Abs(direction.z);

            // Prior to 2019.1 Vector3.Normalize did not use System.Math for Magnitude calculations. There is a slight
            // difference between 2018.3 and 2019.1 in accuracy, with 2019.1 being more correct. This inaccuracy results
            // in float comparison problems (ex, .00700000001 > .007). To account for that we add an additional equality
            // check here.
            // In most other cases this doesn't matter, but since we need this function to be deterministic regardless
            // of floating point inaccuracy it is necessary here.
            if (!Math.Approx(x, y) && x > y && !Math.Approx(x, z) && x > z)
                return direction.x > 0 ? ProjectionAxis.X : ProjectionAxis.XNegative;

            if (!Math.Approx(y, z) && y > z)
                return direction.y > 0 ? ProjectionAxis.Y : ProjectionAxis.YNegative;

            return direction.z > 0 ? ProjectionAxis.Z : ProjectionAxis.ZNegative;
        }

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, planar projection for Auto-UV unwrapping and polygon triangulation is performed by fitting a `Plane` to 3D surface vertices using least-squares covariance, constructing a `Basis` whose Z axis aligns with the plane normal, and transforming points into the basis plane where $(X, Y)$ become UV coordinates. Polygon contour winding sorting can be accomplished with `Geometry2D.is_polygon_clockwise()`.

### HANDLE UTILITY

`HandleUtility` provides spatial raycasting, camera-to-GUI coordinate transformation, selection orientation calculations, and picking utilities for ProBuilder editor tools.

1. Screen and GUI Point Conversions:
- `ScreenToGuiPoint(this Camera camera, Vector3 point, float pixelsPerPoint)`: Converts a screen coordinate (`(0,0)` bottom-left in pixels) to a GUI coordinate (`(0,0)` top-left in points):
  $$\text{guiPoint} = \left( \frac{\text{point.x}}{\text{pixelsPerPoint}}, \frac{\text{camera.pixelHeight} - \text{point.y}}{\text{pixelsPerPoint}}, \text{point.z} \right)$$

2. Face Raycasting Algorithms (`FaceRaycast`):
- `FaceRaycast(Ray worldRay, ProBuilderMesh mesh, out RaycastHit hit, float distance, CullingMode cullingMode, HashSet<Face> ignore = null)`:
  a. Transforms `worldRay` into mesh model space:
     - `worldRay.origin -= mesh.transform.position`
     - `worldRay.origin = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.origin`
     - `worldRay.direction = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.direction`
  b. Iterates through all faces in `mesh.facesInternal` (skipping any face in `ignore`).
  c. For each face, iterates over triangle index triples `j, j+1, j+2`:
     - Retrieves triangle vertices `a = positions[indexes[j]]`, `b = positions[indexes[j+1]]`, `c = positions[indexes[j+2]]`.
     - Calculates face normal `nrm = Vector3.Cross(b - a, c - a)` and ray dot product `dot = Vector3.Dot(worldRay.direction, nrm)`.
     - Evaluates `cullingMode`:
       - `CullingMode.Front`: Skips if `dot < 0f` (front-facing triangle).
       - `CullingMode.Back`: Skips if `dot > 0f` (back-facing triangle).
       - `CullingMode.FrontBack`: Tests both sides.
     - Calls `Math.RayIntersectsTriangle(worldRay, a, b, c, out dist, out point)`.
     - If intersected and `dist < OutHitPoint` and `dist <= distance`, records `OutHitPoint = dist`, `OutHitFace = i`, and `OutNrm = nrm`.
  d. Returns `RaycastHit(OutHitPoint, worldRay.GetPoint(OutHitPoint), OutNrm, OutHitFace)`.
- `FaceRaycastBothCullModes`: In a single pass, tracks the nearest front-facing face and nearest back-facing face intersecting `worldRay`, returning results via two reference item pairs for front and back hit geometry.
- `FaceRaycast(Ray InWorldRay, ProBuilderMesh mesh, out List<RaycastHit> hits, CullingMode cullingMode, HashSet<Face> ignore = null)`: Returns all intersected faces sorted by occurrence.

3. Raw Mesh Raycasting and Occlusion:
- `MeshRaycast(Ray InWorldRay, GameObject gameObject, out RaycastHit hit, float distance = Mathf.Infinity)`: Raycasts against standard `MeshFilter.sharedMesh` geometry using model-space transformed ray `transform.InverseTransformRay(InWorldRay)` and invokes `MeshRaycast(ray, mesh.vertices, mesh.triangles, out hit, distance)`.
- `MeshRaycast(Ray InRay, Vector3[] mesh, int[] triangles, out RaycastHit hit, float distance)`: Iterates over triangles using non-allocating `Math.RayIntersectsTriangle2(o, d, a, b, c, ref distance, ref n)`, tracking the closest hit face index `hitFace = CurTri / 3`.
- `InverseTransformRay(this Transform transform, Ray InWorldRay)`: Converts a world ray to local coordinates:
  $$\text{origin} = \text{worldToLocalMatrix} * (\text{InWorldRay.origin} - \text{position}), \quad \text{direction} = \text{worldToLocalMatrix.MultiplyVector}(\text{InWorldRay.direction})$$
- `PointIsOccluded(Camera cam, ProBuilderMesh pb, Vector3 worldPoint)`: Constructs a ray from `worldPoint + dir * 0.0001f` towards camera position `cam.transform.position`. Executes `FaceRaycast` with `CullingMode.Front`; returns true if an intervening triangle occludes the point.

4. Handle and Gizmo Orientation Calculations:
- `GetRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indices)`: Calculates gizmo rotation from vertex normals and tangents:
  a. Ensures normals and tangents are computed via `Normals.CalculateNormals(mesh)` and `Normals.CalculateTangents(mesh)`.
  b. Averages vertex normals `nrm` and tangents `tan` across all selected vertex indices.
  c. Computes bitangent `bit = Vector3.Cross(nrm, tan * tan.w)`.
  d. Returns `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm, bit)`.
- `GetFaceRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Face> faces)`:
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`: Evaluates `GetFaceRotation(mesh, faces.Last())` using `Math.NormalTangentBitangent(mesh, face)` and returns `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm.normal, nrm.bitangent)`.
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`: Returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
  - Default: Returns `Quaternion.identity` (World orientation).
- `GetEdgeRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Edge> edges)`: Computes rotation for `edges.Last()` by looking up its associated face with `EdgeUtility.GetFace(mesh, edge)`.
- `GetVertexRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<int> vertices)`: Invokes `GetRotation(mesh, vertices)` for `ActiveElement` orientation.
- `GetActiveElementPosition(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face>/<Edge>/<int>)`: Computes world-space centroid `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(Math.GetBounds(mesh.positionsInternal, indexes).center)`.

        internal static bool PointIsOccluded(Camera cam, ProBuilderMesh pb, Vector3 worldPoint)
        {

            Ray ray = new Ray(worldPoint + dir * .0001f, dir);

### BOUNDS 2D

`Bounds2D` is an axis-aligned 2D bounding box data structure designed for 2D spatial queries, UV unwrapping, UV editor layout, polygon containment tests, and screen-space element selection.

1. Data Structure and Properties:
- `center` (`Vector2`): The 2D midpoint of the bounding box, initialized to `Vector2.zero`.
- `m_Size` (`Vector2`): The width and height dimensions of the bounding box.
- `m_Extents` (`Vector2`): Half-size extents along X and Y axes (`m_Size * 0.5f`).
- `size` property getter/setter: Updating `size` automatically recalculates `m_Extents.x = m_Size.x * 0.5f` and `m_Extents.y = m_Size.y * 0.5f`.
- `extents` property: Read-only access to `m_Extents`.
- `corners` property: Returns a 4-element `Vector2[]` array containing the bounding box corners ordered top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right:
  - Corner 0: `new Vector2(center.x - extents.x, center.y + extents.y)`
  - Corner 1: `new Vector2(center.x + extents.x, center.y + extents.y)`
  - Corner 2: `new Vector2(center.x - extents.x, center.y - extents.y)`
  - Corner 3: `new Vector2(center.x + extents.x, center.y - extents.y)`

2. Constructors and Encapsulation:
- `Bounds2D()`: Default constructor initializing center and size to zero.
- `Bounds2D(Vector2 center, Vector2 size)`: Explicit initialization of center and size.
- `Bounds2D(IList<Vector2> points)`: Automatically invokes `SetWithPoints(points)` to compute bounds encapsulating all points.
- `Bounds2D(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Invokes `SetWithPoints(points, indexes)` to encapsulate the subset of points referenced by `indexes`.
- `Bounds2D(Vector3[] points, Edge[] edges)`: Extracts 2D $(X, Y)$ components from 3D points referenced by an array of `Edge` structs, computing `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax` across edge vertices `.a` and `.b`.
- `Bounds2D(Vector2[] points, int length)`: Computes bounding rectangle across array elements up to `length`.
- `SetWithPoints(IList<Vector2> points)` / `SetWithPoints(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Iterates through coordinate list tracking `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax`, then calculates:
  $$\text{center.x} = \frac{xMin + xMax}{2}, \quad \text{center.y} = \frac{yMin + yMax}{2}$$
  $$\text{m\_Size.x} = xMax - xMin, \quad \text{m\_Size.y} = yMax - yMin$$
  $$\text{m\_Extents.x} = \text{m\_Size.x} \cdot 0.5, \quad \text{m\_Extents.y} = \text{m\_Size.y} \cdot 0.5$$

3. Spatial Intersection and Containment Queries:
- `ContainsPoint(Vector2 point)`: Tests whether a 2D point lies within the bounding box bounds:
  $$\text{Inside} = !(point.x > center.x + extents.x \;\lor\; point.x < center.x - extents.x \;\lor\; point.y > center.y + extents.y \;\lor\; point.y < center.y - extents.y)$$
- `IntersectsLineSegment(Vector2 lineStart, Vector2 lineEnd)`: Evaluates if any portion of a 2D line segment intersects or lies within the bounding box:
  a. If `ContainsPoint(lineStart)` or `ContainsPoint(lineEnd)` is true, returns `true`.
  b. Otherwise, queries segment intersection against the four boundary edges formed by `corners` (`[0]-[1]`, `[1]-[3]`, `[3]-[2]`, `[2]-[0]`) using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect`.
- `Intersects(Bounds2D bounds)`: Separating Axis Test between two `Bounds2D` instances:
  $$\text{Overlap} = |\text{this.center.x} - \text{bounds.center.x}| \cdot 2 < (\text{this.size.x} + \text{bounds.size.x}) \;\land\; |\text{this.center.y} - \text{bounds.center.y}| \cdot 2 < (\text{this.size.y} + \text{bounds.size.y})$$
- `Intersects(Rect rect)`: Overlap test against a Unity `Rect` using the identical separating axis formulation.

4. Static Aggregation Utilities:
- `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector2> points)` / `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Computes the geometric center `(xMin + xMax) / 2, (yMin + yMax) / 2` without instantiating a `Bounds2D` object.
- `Bounds2D.Size(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Computes the bounding size `new Vector2(xMax - xMin, yMax - yMin)`.
- `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector4> points, IEnumerable<int> indexes)`: Extracts $(X, Y)$ components from 4D vectors (such as UV3/UV4 arrays) and returns their 2D bounding center.

            return Mathf.Abs(dist.x) * 2f < size.x &&
                Mathf.Abs(dist.y) * 2f < size.y;
        }

        {
            Vector2 dist = this.center - rect.center;
            Vector2 size = this.size + rect.size;

            return Mathf.Abs(dist.x) * 2f < size.x &&
                Mathf.Abs(dist.y) * 2f < size.y;
        }

### INT VECTORS

The `IntVec2`, `IntVec3`, and `IntVec4` structs along with the `VectorHash` static utility provide integer-quantized vector representation and fuzzy hashing.

1. Purpose and Design Rationale:
- In geometric modeling and mesh manipulation, spatial algorithms (transformations, extrusions, rotations, planar projections) subject vertex coordinates to floating-point drift. Two vertices that are geometrically coincident may differ by negligible precision noise (for example, `0.00700000001f` versus `0.00700000000f`).
- Standard floating-point equality (`operator==`) and default `GetHashCode` implementations fail to match these coincident coordinates, causing vertex welding, shared vertex table generation (`SharedVertex`), seam calculation, and winged-edge topology building to create redundant or disconnected vertices.
- `IntVec` solves this by scaling floating-point components by a fixed resolution multiplier `VectorHash.FltCompareResolution = 1000f` and quantizing them to integer values using `System.Convert.ToInt32(v * 1000f)`. This establishes an automatic tolerance threshold of $0.001$ ($1 / 1000$), grouping all vertices within that epsilon into identical integer buckets.

2. Structure and Properties:
- `IntVec2`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec2>`. Contains `public Vector2 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, and constructor `IntVec2(Vector2 vector)`.
- `IntVec3`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec3>`. Contains `public Vector3 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, `z => value.z`, and constructor `IntVec3(Vector3 vector)`.
- `IntVec4`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec4>`. Contains `public Vector4 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, `z => value.z`, `w => value.w`, and constructor `IntVec4(Vector4 vector)`.

3. Quantization and Equality Operations:
- Quantization method:
  `private static int round(float v) => System.Convert.ToInt32(v * VectorHash.FltCompareResolution);`
- `Equals(IntVec3 p)` / `Equals(Vector3 p)`: Compares quantized integer coordinates across all axes:
  `round(x) == round(p.x) && round(y) == round(p.y) && round(z) == round(p.z)`
- `operator==` and `operator!=`: Delegate directly to `a.Equals(b)`.
- `Equals(object b)`: Supports comparisons against both `IntVecN` and raw `VectorN` instances.
- Zero-cost implicit conversions:
  - `public static implicit operator Vector3(IntVec3 p) => p.value;`
  - `public static implicit operator IntVec3(Vector3 p) => new IntVec3(p);`
  (Identical bidirectional implicit conversions exist for `IntVec2` <-> `Vector2` and `IntVec4` <-> `Vector4`).

4. Fuzzy Hashing Utility (`VectorHash`):
- `VectorHash` provides high-performance hash code generation directly from floating-point vectors without requiring `IntVec` struct instantiation or heap allocations.
- Constant: `public const float FltCompareResolution = 1000f;`
- Quantized float hash function:
  `static int HashFloat(float f) { ulong u = (ulong)(f * FltCompareResolution); return (int)(u % int.MaxValue); }`
- Hash combination algorithm: Employs a polynomial rolling hash initialized with prime seed `27` and multiplied by prime `29` within an `unchecked` block:
  - `GetHashCode(Vector2 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); return hash;`
  - `GetHashCode(Vector3 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.z); return hash;`
  - `GetHashCode(Vector4 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.z); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.w); return hash;`

    /// </summary>
    static class VectorHash
    {
        public const float FltCompareResolution = 1000f;

        static int HashFloat(float f)
        {
            ulong u = (ulong)(f * FltCompareResolution);
            return (int)(u % int.MaxValue);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Return the rounded hashcode for a vector2
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="v"></param>
        /// <returns></returns>
        public static int GetHashCode(Vector2 v)
        {
            // http://stackoverflow.com/questions/263400/what-is-the-best-algorithm-for-an-overridden-system-object-gethashcode/263416#263416
            int hash = 27;

            unchecked
            {
                hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x);
                hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y);
            }

            return hash;
        }

            int hash = 27;

            unchecked
            {
                hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x);
                hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y);
                hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.z);
            }

            return hash;

To implement spatial quantization for shared vertex tables in Godot, coordinates can be converted using `Vector3i((v * 1000.0).round())` or `Vector3.snapped(Vector3(0.001, 0.001, 0.001))`.
