```csharp
        /// <param name="pairs">The list of face pairs to merge.</param>
        /// <param name="collapseCoincidentVertices">True to condense coincident vertex positions on each face.</param>
        /// <returns>A list of the new faces created.</returns>
        public static List<Face> MergePairs(ProBuilderMesh target, IEnumerable<SimpleTuple<Face, Face>> pairs, bool collapseCoincidentVertices = true)
        {
            HashSet<Face> remove = new HashSet<Face>();
            List<Face> add = new List<Face>();

            foreach (SimpleTuple<Face, Face> pair in pairs)
            {
                Face left = pair.item1;
                Face right = pair.item2;
                int leftLength = left.indexesInternal.Length;
                int rightLength = right.indexesInternal.Length;
                int[] indexes = new int[leftLength + rightLength];
                System.Array.Copy(left.indexesInternal, 0, indexes, 0, leftLength);
                System.Array.Copy(right.indexesInternal, 0, indexes, leftLength, rightLength);
                add.Add(new Face(indexes,
                        left.submeshIndex,
                        left.uv,
                        left.smoothingGroup,
                        left.textureGroup,
                        left.elementGroup,
                        left.manualUV));
                remove.Add(left);
                remove.Add(right);
            }

            List<Face> faces = target.facesInternal.Where(x => !remove.Contains(x)).ToList();
            faces.AddRange(add);
            target.faces = faces;

            if (collapseCoincidentVertices)
                CollapseCoincidentVertices(target, add);

            return add;
        }
```

```csharp
        /// <param name="faces">The collection of faces to move.</param>
        /// <returns>The single merged Face.</returns>
        public static Face Merge(ProBuilderMesh target, IEnumerable<Face> faces)
        {
            int mergedCount = faces != null ? faces.Count() : 0;

            if (mergedCount < 1)
                return null;

            Face first = faces.First();

            Face mergedFace = new Face(faces.SelectMany(x => x.indexesInternal).ToArray(),
                    first.submeshIndex,
                    first.uv,
                    first.smoothingGroup,
                    first.textureGroup,
                    first.elementGroup,
                    first.manualUV);

            Face[] rebuiltFaces = new Face[target.facesInternal.Length - mergedCount + 1];

            int n = 0;

            HashSet<Face> skip = new HashSet<Face>(faces);

            foreach (Face f in target.facesInternal)
            {
                if (!skip.Contains(f))
                    rebuiltFaces[n++] = f;
            }

            rebuiltFaces[n] = mergedFace;

            target.faces = rebuiltFaces;

            CollapseCoincidentVertices(target, new Face[] { mergedFace });

            return mergedFace;
        }
```

### COLLAPSE

The `CollapseVertices` action collapses all selected vertices into a single vertex point, offering options to place the resulting point at either the average center position or the position of the first selected vertex.

1. Configuration and UI Architecture (`CollapseVertices.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Vert_Collapse"`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Vertex`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedSharedVertexCountObjectMax > 1`.
- Options menu state: `MenuActionState.VisibleAndEnabled`.
- Preference: `Pref<bool> m_CollapseToFirst = new Pref<bool>("CollapseVertices.collapseToFirst", false)`.
- UI: A `Toggle("Collapse to First")` controls whether vertices collapse to `indexes[0]` or the centroid average.
- Action execution:
  - Iterates over `MeshSelection.topInternal`.
  - If `mesh.selectedIndexesInternal.Length > 1`: calls `int newIndex = mesh.MergeVertices(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal, collapseToFirst)`.
  - If `newIndex > -1`, sets vertex selection to `new int[] { newIndex }`.
  - Calls `mesh.ToMesh()`, `mesh.Refresh()`, `mesh.Optimize()`.

2. Core Vertex Collapse Algorithm (`VertexEditing.MergeVertices` in `VertexEditing.cs`):
- Parameters: `this ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `int[] indexes`, `bool collapseToFirst = false`.
- Step 1: Validates parameters: throws `ArgumentNullException` if `mesh` or `indexes` is null.
- Step 2: Obtains full vertex array `Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices()`.
- Step 3: Computes collapsed vertex attributes:
  `Vertex cen = collapseToFirst ? vertices[indexes[0]] : Vertex.Average(vertices, indexes);`
- Step 4: Makes all specified vertex indices coincident in the shared vertex tables: `mesh.SetVerticesCoincident(indexes)`.
- Step 5: Splits UV seams for the affected indices: `UVEditing.SplitUVs(mesh, indexes)`.
- Step 6: Fetches shared vertex group index: `int sharedVertexHandle = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandle(indexes[0])`.
- Step 7: Updates all coincident vertices in the group to position and attributes `cen`: `mesh.SetSharedVertexValues(sharedVertexHandle, cen)`.
- Step 8: Captures the merged group `SharedVertex merged = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[sharedVertexHandle]`.
- Step 9: Eliminates triangles that have collapsed to zero area or duplicate vertex indices: `MeshValidation.RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removedIndexes)`.
- Step 10: Determines surviving non-deleted local vertex index `ind` from `merged` that is not present in `removedIndexes`.
- Step 11: Calculates index shift for the surviving vertex:
  `int res = ind;`
  `for (int i = 0; i < removedIndexes.Count; i++) if (ind > removedIndexes[i]) res--;`
- Step 12: Returns `res` (the updated index of the collapsed vertex).

```csharp
        public static int MergeVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes, bool collapseToFirst = false)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (indexes == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("indexes");

            Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices();
            Vertex cen = collapseToFirst ? vertices[indexes[0]] : Vertex.Average(vertices, indexes);
            mesh.SetVerticesCoincident(indexes);
            UVEditing.SplitUVs(mesh, indexes);
            int sharedVertexHandle = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandle(indexes[0]);
            mesh.SetSharedVertexValues(sharedVertexHandle, cen);

            SharedVertex merged = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[sharedVertexHandle];
            List<int> removedIndexes = new List<int>();

            MeshValidation.RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removedIndexes);

            // get a non-deleted index to work with
            int ind = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < merged.Count; i++)
                if (!removedIndexes.Contains(merged[i]))
                    ind = merged[i];

            int res = ind;

            for (int i = 0; i < removedIndexes.Count; i++)
                if (ind > removedIndexes[i])
                    res--;

            return res;
        }
```

### SPLIT

The `SplitVertices` action disconnects coincident vertices that share the same spatial position across multiple faces, creating distinct independent vertices so that adjacent faces can be moved or transformed independently. This operation directly reverses vertex welding.

1. Menu Action Architecture (`SplitVertices.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Vert_Split"`.
- Shortcut: `keyCommandAlt, 'X'`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Vertex`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedVertexCountObjectMax > 0 && !(MeshSelection.selectedVertexCountObjectMax == 1 && MeshSelection.selectedCoincidentVertexCountMax == 1)`.
- Action execution:
  - Iterates over `MeshSelection.topInternal`.
  - Gathers coincident vertex indices: `var coincident = mesh.selectedCoincidentVertices`.
  - Increments split counter: `splitCount += mesh.selectedSharedVerticesCount`.
  - Invokes `mesh.SplitVertices(coincident)`.
  - Refreshes editor via `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

2. Core Split Algorithm (`VertexEditing.SplitVertices` in `VertexEditing.cs`):
- Parameters: `this ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IEnumerable<int> vertices` (and `Edge` overload `SplitVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Edge edge)`).
- Step 1: Validates `mesh` and `vertices` arguments, throwing `ArgumentNullException` if null.
- Step 2: Obtains `Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
- Step 3: Determines the next available unique shared vertex ID: `int max = lookup.Count`.
- Step 4: Assigns a new unique shared vertex ID to each vertex in the list:
  `foreach (int i in vertices) lookup[i] = ++max;`
- Step 5: Updates mesh shared vertex state: `mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup)`.

3. Mechanism and Data Representation:
- In ProBuilder's per-face unique vertex model, vertices of adjacent faces already possess separate storage in `positionsInternal` and distinct face indices. They are grouped into unified spatial handles strictly via `sharedVertices` and `sharedVertexLookup`.
- Assigning `lookup[i] = ++max` gives each face's vertex a unique shared handle ID.
- As a consequence, transform gizmos and translation operations moving one face's vertex no longer pull or affect coincident vertices belonging to adjacent faces.

```csharp
        public static void SplitVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> vertices)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (vertices == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("vertices");

            // ToDictionary always sets the universal indexes in ascending order from 0+.
            Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup;
            int max = lookup.Count;
            foreach (int i in vertices)
                lookup[i] = ++max;
            mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup);
```

### WELD

The `WeldVertices` action searches selected vertices for pairs/groups located within a user-defined distance threshold and merges them into unified shared vertices.

1. Configuration and UI Architecture (`WeldVertices.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Vert_Weld"`.
- Shortcut: `keyCommandAlt, 'V'`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Vertex`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedSharedVertexCountObjectMax > 1`.
- Options menu state: `MenuActionState.VisibleAndEnabled`.
- Constants and Settings:
  - Minimum weld threshold: `const float k_MinWeldDistance = .00001f`.
  - Preference: `Pref<float> m_WeldDistance = new Pref<float>("WeldVertices.weldDistance", .01f)`.
  - UI: `FloatField` bound to `m_WeldDistance`, with delayed preview support via `PreviewActionManager.delayedPreview`.

2. Action Execution Workflow (`WeldVertices.PerformActionImplementation` in `WeldVertices.cs`):
- Iterates over `MeshSelection.topInternal`.
- Calls `mesh.ToMesh()`.
- Captures `selectedVertices = mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(mesh.selectedVertices)`.
- Invokes `int[] welds = mesh.WeldVertices(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal, m_WeldDistance)`.
- Checks for degenerate triangles: `if (MeshValidation.ContainsDegenerateTriangles(mesh))`.
- If degenerate triangles exist:
  - Invokes `MeshValidation.RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removedIndices)`.
  - Re-indexes surviving selection vertices by shifting each index down based on prior removed indices:
    `newlySelectedVertices.Add(selectedVertices[i] - ArrayUtility.NearestIndexPriorToValue(removedIndices, selectedVertices[i]) - 1);`
  - Re-assigns selection with `mesh.SetSelectedVertices(newSelection)`.
- Rebuilds and optimizes: `mesh.Refresh()`, `mesh.Optimize()`.

3. KD-Tree Welding Algorithm (`VertexEditing.WeldVertices` in `VertexEditing.cs`):
- Parameters: `this ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IEnumerable<int> indexes`, `float neighborRadius`.
- Step 1: Fetches `vertices = mesh.GetVertices()`, `sharedIndexes = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal`, and `common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(indexes)`.
- Step 2: Initializes a 3-dimensional KD-Tree:
  `KdTree<float, int> tree = new KdTree<float, int>(3, new FloatMath(), AddDuplicateBehavior.Collect);`
- Step 3: Inserts each unique shared vertex coordinate into the KD-Tree:
  `tree.Add(new float[] { v.x, v.y, v.z }, i);`
- Step 4: Iterates through each `commonIndex` in `common`:
  - Skips if already grouped in `remapped.ContainsKey(commonIndex)`.
  - Performs radial search: `KdTreeNode<float, int>[] neighbors = tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, maxNearestNeighbors)`.
  - If search filled `maxNearestNeighbors`, doubles capacity and re-searches: `tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, vertexCount)`.
  - Accumulates centroid `avg` of all neighbors and duplicates.
  - Maps each neighbor `c` to new shared ID `index`: `remapped.Add(c, index)`.
  - Stores centroid `averages.Add(index, avg)`.
  - Increments `index++`.
- Step 5: Updates shared vertex tables and vertex positions:
  - For each `(commonIndex, newGroup)` in `remapped`:
    - For each local vertex `tris[i]` in `sharedIndexes[kvp.Key]`:
      - `lookup[tris[i]] = kvp.Value;`
      - `vertices[tris[i]].position = averages[kvp.Value];`
- Step 6: Applies updates via `mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup)` and `mesh.SetVertices(vertices)`.
- Step 7: Returns array of welded vertex indices `welds`.

```csharp
        public static int[] WeldVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, float neighborRadius)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (indexes == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("indexes");

            Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices();
            SharedVertex[] sharedIndexes = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal;

            HashSet<int> common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(indexes);
            int vertexCount = common.Count;

            // Make assumption that there will rarely be a time when a single weld encompasses more than 32 vertices.
            // If a radial search returns neighbors matching the max count, the search is re-done and maxNearestNeighbors
            // is set to the resulting length. This will be slow, but in most cases shouldn't happen ever, or if it does,
            // should only happen once or twice.
            int maxNearestNeighbors = System.Math.Min(32, common.Count);

            // 3 dimensions, duplicate entries allowed
            KdTree<float, int> tree = new KdTree<float, int>(3, new FloatMath(), AddDuplicateBehavior.Collect);

            foreach (int i in common)
            {
                Vector3 v = vertices[sharedIndexes[i][0]].position;
                tree.Add(new float[] { v.x, v.y, v.z }, i);
            }

            float[] point = new float[3] { 0, 0, 0 };
            Dictionary<int, int> remapped = new Dictionary<int, int>();
            Dictionary<int, Vector3> averages = new Dictionary<int, Vector3>();
            int index = sharedIndexes.Length;

            foreach (int commonIndex in common)
            {
                // already merged with another
                if (remapped.ContainsKey(commonIndex))
                    continue;

                Vector3 v = vertices[sharedIndexes[commonIndex][0]].position;

                point[0] = v.x;
                point[1] = v.y;
                point[2] = v.z;

                // Radial search at each point
                KdTreeNode<float, int>[] neighbors = tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, maxNearestNeighbors);

                // if first radial search filled the entire allotment reset the max neighbor count to 1.5x.
                // the result hopefully preventing double-searches in the next iterations.
                if (maxNearestNeighbors < vertexCount && neighbors.Length >= maxNearestNeighbors)
```

```csharp
                avg.x /= count;
```

### BEVEL

The `Bevel` class provides edge and face beveling operations, splitting sharp edges into transitional chamfer faces and reconstructing corner intersections.

1. Action and Configuration Architecture (`BevelEdges.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Edge_Bevel"`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedEdgeCount > 0`.
- Options menu state: `MenuActionState.VisibleAndEnabled`.
- Constants and Settings:
  - Minimum distance: `const float k_MinBevelDistance = .0001f`.
  - Preference: `Pref<float> m_BevelSize = new Pref<float>("BevelEdges.size", .2f)`.
- Face Beveling: In ProBuilder, face beveling is executed by selecting all perimeter edges of the face and running `BevelEdges`.

2. Core Bevel Algorithm (`Bevel.BevelEdges` in `Bevel.cs`):
- Parameters: `ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IList<Edge> edges`, `float amount`.
- Step 1: Builds winged edge topology: `wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh)`. Resolves `m_edges = EdgeLookup.GetEdgeLookup(edges, lookup).Distinct().ToList()`.
- Step 2: Distance Clamping:
  - Queries `spokes = WingedEdge.GetSpokes(wings)`.
  - For each edge in `m_edges`, clamps `amount` against the shortest incident spoke edge: `amount = Mathf.Min(Vector3.Distance(vertices[le.a].position, vertices[le.b].position) - .001f, amount)`.
  - If `amount < .001f`, logs "Bevel Distance > Available Surface" and aborts.
- Step 3: Edge Sliding and Bridge Face Generation:
  - For each `EdgeLookup lup` in `m_edges`:
    - Locates `WingedEdge we = wings.FirstOrDefault(x => x.edge.Equals(lup))`.
    - If `we == null || we.opposite == null`, skips (cannot bevel open boundary edges).
    - Populates `ignore` dictionary with incident faces and common vertices.
    - Adds common vertices to `slide` set.
    - Calls `SlideEdge(vertices, we, amount)` and `SlideEdge(vertices, we.opposite, amount)`:
      - Sets `manualUV = true`, `textureGroup = -1`.
      - Gets leading edges via `GetLeadingEdge(we, common)` and displaces vertices along normalized edge vectors: `vertices[we.edge.local.a].Add(x * amount)`.
    - Calls `GetBridgeFaces(vertices, we, we.opposite, holes)`:
      - Constructs a quad face connecting the separated edges.
      - Checks winding: if `Vector3.Dot(an, bn) < 0f`, reverses triangle index array `{ 2, 1, 0, 2, 3, 1 }`.
      - Records corner hole vertex pairings in `holes` dictionary.
- Step 4: Exploding Corner Vertices on Adjacent Faces:
  - Gathers adjacent faces touching `slide` vertices into `sorted`.
  - For each face, invokes `VertexEditing.ExplodeVertex(vertices, kvp.Value, amount, out appended)`:
    - Splits the corner vertex into two vertices displaced along adjacent edges.
    - Retriangulates face polygon via `Triangulation.TriangulateVertices`.
    - Registers resulting hole loops in `holes`.
- Step 5: Applying Rebuilt Faces & Removing Old Faces:
  - `FaceRebuildData.Apply(appendFaces, mesh, vertices)`.
  - Deletes replaced original faces: `mesh.DeleteFaces(sorted.Keys)`.
  - Reconstructs shared vertices: `mesh.sharedVertices = SharedVertex.GetSharedVerticesWithPositions(mesh.positionsInternal)`.
- Step 6: Corner Hole Filling (Caps):
  - For each hole loop in `holesCommonIndexes`:
    - If 3 vertices: builds triangle face via `AppendElements.FaceWithVertices(v)`.
    - If > 3 vertices: sorts loop with `WingedEdge.SortCommonIndexesByAdjacency` and creates tent fan cap via `AppendElements.TentCapWithVertices(v)`.
  - Applies hole faces: `FaceRebuildData.Apply(holeFaces, mesh, vertices)`.
- Step 7: Normal and Property Conforming:
  - Iterates through all new faces, matching submesh index, `AutoUnwrapSettings`, and winding against adjacent faces using `SurfaceTopology.ConformOppositeNormal(w.opposite)`.
- Step 8: Invokes `mesh.ToMesh()` and returns `createdFaces`.

```csharp
            appendFaces.AddRange(holeFaces);

            List<WingedEdge> allNewFaceEdges = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, appendFaces.Select(x => x.face));

            for (int i = 0; i < allNewFaceEdges.Count && newFaces.Count > 0; i++)

                if (newFaces.Contains(wing.face))
                {
                    newFaces.Remove(wing.face);

                    // find first edge whose opposite face isn't a filled hole* then
                    // conform normal by that.
                    // *or is a filled hole but has already been conformed
                    using (var it = new WingedEdgeEnumerator(wing))

                        while (it.MoveNext())

                            if (w.opposite != null && !newFaces.Contains(w.opposite.face))
                            {

                                w.face.uv = new AutoUnwrapSettings(w.opposite.face.uv);
                                SurfaceTopology.ConformOppositeNormal(w.opposite);
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
```

### FILL HOLE

The `FillHole` action identifies open boundary loops (holes) touching selected edges or vertices and generates new polygonal faces to close the mesh openings.

1. Configuration and UI Architecture (`FillHole.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Edge_FillHole"`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Vertex`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedEdgeCount > 0 || MeshSelection.selectedSharedVertexCount > 0`.
- Options menu state: `MenuActionState.VisibleAndEnabled`.
- Preference: `Pref<bool> m_SelectEntirePath = new Pref<bool>("FillHole.selectEntirePath", true)`.
- UI: A `Toggle("Fill Entire Hole")` switches between filling complete boundary loops versus building a face only between the selected open vertices.

2. Hole Detection Algorithm (`ElementSelection.FindHoles` in `ElementSelection.cs`):
- Parameters: `List<WingedEdge> wings`, `HashSet<int> common`.
- Step 1: Iterates through all winged edges in `wings`.
- Step 2: Identifies boundary edges: an edge belongs to a hole candidate if `c.opposite == null`, has not been visited (`!used.Contains(c)`), and touches a selected vertex (`common.Contains(c.edge.common.a) || common.Contains(c.edge.common.b)`).
- Step 3: Perimeter traversal:
  - Traverses the hole loop using `it = FindNextEdgeInHole(it, ind)` up to `k_MaxHoleIterations = 2048`.
  - Appends each boundary edge to `hole`.
- Step 4: Nested loop splitting: checks for internal self-intersections where `wing.edge.common.b == hole[p].edge.common.a` and isolates individual closed loops.

3. Triangulation and Polygon Creation (`FillHole.PerformActionImplementation` & `AppendElements.cs`):
- Case A: `wholePath == true` (Default):
  - In edge selection mode, validates that `hole` contains at least one complete selected edge (`common.Contains(x.edge.common.a) && common.Contains(x.edge.common.b)`).
  - Extracts ordered local vertex indices: `holeIndexes = hole.Select(x => x.edge.local.a).ToList()`.
  - Calls `face = AppendElements.CreatePolygon(mesh, holeIndexes, unordered: false)`.
- Case B: `wholePath == false`:
  - Filters to selected winged edges: `hole.Where(x => common.Contains(x.edge.common.a))`.
  - Extracts indices and calls `face = AppendElements.CreatePolygon(mesh, holeIndexes, unordered: true)`.
- Core Polygon Creation (`AppendElements.CreatePolygon` in `AppendElements.cs`):
  - Collects `appendVertices` from mesh vertex data.
  - Calls `FaceWithVertices(appendVertices, unordered)` which executes `Triangulation.TriangulateVertices(vertices, out triangles, unordered)`.
  - In `Triangulation`, planar-projects vertices onto their best-fit plane and applies ear-clipping triangulation.
  - Applies new face to mesh via `FaceRebuildData.Apply(new FaceRebuildData[] { data }, vertices, faces, lookup, null)`.

4. Normal and Submesh Conforming (`FillHole.cs`):
- Rebuilds winged edges: `wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh)`.
- For each `appendedFace`:
  - Traverses incident edges with `WingedEdgeEnumerator`.
  - Finds the first adjacent non-appended face `oppositeFace`.
  - Synchronizes properties: `currentWing.face.submeshIndex = oppositeFace.submeshIndex; currentWing.face.uv = new AutoUnwrapSettings(oppositeFace.uv);`.
  - Conforms winding order: `SurfaceTopology.ConformOppositeNormal(currentWing.opposite)`.
- Synchronizes with `mesh.ToMesh()`, `mesh.Refresh()`, `mesh.Optimize()`.

```csharp
        public static Face CreatePolygon(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IList<int> indexes, bool unordered)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            SharedVertex[] sharedIndexes = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal;
            Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup;
            HashSet<int> common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(indexes);
            List<Vertex> vertices = new List<Vertex>(mesh.GetVertices());
            List<Vertex> appendVertices = new List<Vertex>();

            foreach (int i in common)
            {
                int index = sharedIndexes[i][0];
                appendVertices.Add(new Vertex(vertices[index]));
            }

            FaceRebuildData data = FaceWithVertices(appendVertices, unordered);

            if (data != null)
            {
                data.sharedIndexes = common.ToList();
                List<Face> faces = new List<Face>(mesh.facesInternal);
                FaceRebuildData.Apply(new FaceRebuildData[] {data}, vertices, faces, lookup, null);
                mesh.SetVertices(vertices);
                mesh.faces = faces;
                mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup);

                return data.face;
            }

            const string insufficientPoints = "Too Few Unique Points Selected";
            const string badWinding = "Points not ordered correctly";

            Log.Info(unordered ? insufficientPoints : badWinding);
```

### FLIP FACE EDGE

The `FlipFaceEdge` action swaps the shared diagonal triangle edge in a quad face, reversing the triangulation orientation to resolve smoothing ridges or geometric pinching across non-planar quads.

1. Menu Action Architecture (`FlipFaceEdge.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Face_FlipTri"`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Face`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
- Execution:
  - Iterates through `pb.selectedFacesInternal`.
  - Invokes `pb.FlipEdge(face)`.
  - If successful, increments `success++`.
  - Rebuilds mesh: `pb.ToMesh()`, `pb.Refresh()`, `pb.Optimize()`.
  - Reports `ActionResult.Status.Success` ("Flipped N Edges") or `ActionResult.Status.Failure` ("Faces Must Be Quads").

2. Edge Flip Algorithm (`SurfaceTopology.FlipEdge` in `SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Parameter validation:
  - Checks if `indexes.Length == 6` (a quad face composed of exactly 2 triangles: `[0,1,2, 3,4,5]`). Returns `false` if length is not 6.
- Step 1: Mode/Frequency Array Initialization:
  - Initializes `int[] mode = ArrayUtility.Fill<int>(1, indexes.Length)` (array of 6 ones).
  - Counts vertex index sharing between triangles:
    `for (int x = 0; x < indexes.Length - 1; x++)`
    `    for (int y = x + 1; y < indexes.Length; y++)`
    `        if (indexes[x] == indexes[y]) { mode[x]++; mode[y]++; }`
- Step 2: Quad Topology Verification:
  - In a valid quad sharing exactly two diagonal vertices, each triangle has two shared vertices (count = 2) and one unique apex vertex (count = 1).
  - Verifies `mode[0] + mode[1] + mode[2] == 5` and `mode[3] + mode[4] + mode[5] == 5`. If condition fails, returns `false`.
- Step 3: Apex Extraction:
  - Extracts the unique apex vertex of triangle 0: `int i0 = indexes[mode[0] == 1 ? 0 : mode[1] == 1 ? 1 : 2];`.
  - Extracts the unique apex vertex of triangle 1: `int i1 = indexes[mode[3] == 1 ? 3 : mode[4] == 1 ? 4 : 5];`.
- Step 4: Diagonal Substitution:
  - Replaces one shared vertex in triangle 0 with apex `i1`, recording `used = indexes[k]`.
  - Replaces the other shared vertex in triangle 1 (where `indexes[n] != used`) with apex `i0`.
  - Implementation:
    `int used = -1;`
    `if (mode[0] == 2) { used = indexes[0]; indexes[0] = i1; }`
    `else if (mode[1] == 2) { used = indexes[1]; indexes[1] = i1; }`
    `else if (mode[2] == 2) { used = indexes[2]; indexes[2] = i1; }`
    `if (mode[3] == 2 && indexes[3] != used) indexes[3] = i0;`
    `else if (mode[4] == 2 && indexes[4] != used) indexes[4] = i0;`
    `else if (mode[5] == 2 && indexes[5] != used) indexes[5] = i0;`
- Step 5: Cache Invalidation:
  - Calls `face.InvalidateCache()` to update distinct index and edge caches.
  - Returns `true`.

```csharp
        public static bool FlipEdge(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (face == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("face");

            int[] indexes = face.indexesInternal;

            if (indexes.Length != 6)
                return false;

            int[] mode = ArrayUtility.Fill<int>(1, indexes.Length);

            for (int x = 0; x < indexes.Length - 1; x++)
            {
                for (int y = x + 1; y < indexes.Length; y++)
                {
                    if (indexes[x] == indexes[y])
                    {
                        mode[x]++;
                        mode[y]++;
                    }
                }
            }

            if (mode[0] + mode[1] + mode[2] != 5 ||
                mode[3] + mode[4] + mode[5] != 5)
                return false;

            int i0 = indexes[mode[0] == 1 ? 0 : mode[1] == 1 ? 1 : 2];
            int i1 = indexes[mode[3] == 1 ? 3 : mode[4] == 1 ? 4 : 5];

            int used = -1;

            if (mode[0] == 2)
            {
                used = indexes[0];
                indexes[0] =  i1;
            }
            else if (mode[1] == 2)
            {
                used = indexes[1];
                indexes[1] = i1;
            }
            else if (mode[2] == 2)
            {
                used = indexes[2];
                indexes[2] = i1;
            }

            if (mode[3] == 2 && indexes[3] != used)
                indexes[3] = i0;
            else if (mode[4] == 2 && indexes[4] != used)
                indexes[4] = i0;
            else if (mode[5] == 2 && indexes[5] != used)
                indexes[5] = i0;

            face.InvalidateCache();

            return true;

```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, turning/flipping a quad's diagonal edge involves swapping the shared edge between two adjacent triangles forming a quad. In an index buffer `[A, B, C]` and `[A, C, D]` (sharing diagonal AC), swapping yields `[A, B, D]` and `[B, C, D]` (sharing diagonal BD).

### CONFORM NORMALS

The `ConformFaceNormals`, `FlipFaceNormals`, and `TriangulateFaces` actions provide topological normal orientation and face tessellation utilities.

1. Actions Overview:
- `ConformFaceNormals` (`ConformFaceNormals.cs`): Group `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`, icon `"Toolbar/Face_ConformNormals"`, SelectMode `Face`, enabled when `MeshSelection.selectedFaceCountObjectMax > 1`. Calls `SurfaceTopology.ConformNormals(pb, faces)`.
- `FlipFaceNormals` (`FlipFaceNormals.cs`): Group `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`, icon `"Toolbar/Face_FlipNormals"`, shortcut `Alt+N`, SelectMode `Face`. Iterates selected faces and calls `face.Reverse()`.
- `TriangulateFaces` (`TriangulateFaces.cs`): Group `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`, icon `"Toolbar/Face_Triangulate"`, SelectMode `Face`. Breaks faces down to individual triangles via `mesh.ToTriangles(mesh.selectedFacesInternal)`.

2. Normal Conforming Algorithm (`SurfaceTopology.ConformNormals` in `SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Parameters: `this ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IEnumerable<Face> faces`.
- Step 1: Builds winged edge structures: `List<WingedEdge> wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, faces)`.
- Step 2: Tracks visited faces in `HashSet<Face> used = new HashSet<Face>()`.
- Step 3: Traverses connected face islands:
  - For each unvisited wing `wings[i]` where `!used.Contains(wings[i].face)`:
    - Allocates `Dictionary<Face, bool> flags = new Dictionary<Face, bool>()`.
    - Invokes recursive propagation `GetWindingFlags(wings[i], true, flags)`.
- Step 4: Recursive Winding Propagation (`GetWindingFlags` in `SurfaceTopology.cs`):
  - Records `flags.Add(edge.face, flag)`.
  - Walks the perimeter of `edge.face` using `next = next.next` until returning to `edge`.
  - For each adjacent opposite face `opp = next.opposite` where `!flags.ContainsKey(opp.face)`:
    - Queries edge directions in winding order:
      `Edge cea = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(next);`
      `Edge ceb = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(opp);`
    - In consistent manifold winding, an edge shared between two faces is traversed in opposite directions (`cea.a == ceb.b`).
    - If `cea.a == ceb.a`, winding directions conflict. Sets `nextFlag = (cea.a == ceb.a ? !flag : flag)`.
    - Recurses via `GetWindingFlags(opp, nextFlag, flags)`.
- Step 5: Island Majority Voting:
  - Sums orientation votes across the island: `int flip = 0; foreach (var kvp in flags) flip += kvp.Value ? 1 : -1;`.
  - Sets majority direction: `bool direction = flip > 0;`.
  - Reverses faces that conflict with the majority:
    `foreach (var kvp in flags) if (direction != kvp.Value) { count++; kvp.Key.Reverse(); }`
  - Unions visited faces: `used.UnionWith(flags.Keys)`.
- Step 6: Returns `ActionResult.Status.Success` ("Flipped N faces") or `ActionResult.Status.NoChange` ("Faces Uniform").

3. Single Face Opposite Conforming (`SurfaceTopology.ConformOppositeNormal` in `SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Compares `cea = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(source)` and `ceb = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(source.opposite)`.
- If `cea.a == ceb.a`, calls `source.opposite.face.Reverse()` and returns `ActionResult.Status.Success`.

4. Face Triangulation Algorithm (`SurfaceTopology.ToTriangles` in `SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- For each face in `faces`, calls `BreakFaceIntoTris(face, vertices, lookup)`.
- `BreakFaceIntoTris`: iterates through `tris = face.indexesInternal` in steps of 3 (`i += 3`). Creates a new `FaceRebuildData` instance for each triangle triplet with `indexesInternal = new int[] { 0, 1, 2 }`, copying vertex attributes and shared index handles.
- Replaces original faces using `FaceRebuildData.Apply(rebuild, mesh, vertices, null)` and `mesh.DeleteFaces(faces)`.
- Calls `mesh.ToMesh()` and returns the new triangular `Face` array.

```csharp
        public static Face[] ToTriangles(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IList<Face> faces)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new System.ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (faces == null)
                throw new System.ArgumentNullException("faces");

            List<Vertex> vertices = new List<Vertex>(mesh.GetVertices());
            Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup;

            List<FaceRebuildData> rebuild = new List<FaceRebuildData>();

            foreach (Face face in faces)
            {
                List<FaceRebuildData> res = BreakFaceIntoTris(face, vertices, lookup);
                rebuild.AddRange(res);
            }

            FaceRebuildData.Apply(rebuild, mesh, vertices, null);
            mesh.DeleteFaces(faces);
            mesh.ToMesh();

            return rebuild.Select(x => x.face).ToArray();
        }

        static List<FaceRebuildData> BreakFaceIntoTris(Face face, List<Vertex> vertices, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)
        {
            int[] tris = face.indexesInternal;
            int triCount = tris.Length;
            List<FaceRebuildData> rebuild = new List<FaceRebuildData>(triCount / 3);

            for (int i = 0; i < triCount; i += 3)
            {
                FaceRebuildData r = new FaceRebuildData();

                r.face = new Face(face);
                r.face.indexesInternal = new int[] { 0, 1, 2};

                r.vertices = new List<Vertex>() {
                    vertices[tris[i]],
                    vertices[tris[i + 1]],
                    vertices[tris[i + 2]]
                };

                r.sharedIndexes = new List<int>() {
                    lookup[tris[i]],
                    lookup[tris[i + 1]],
                    lookup[tris[i + 2]]
                };
```

```csharp
        public static ActionResult ConformNormals(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces)
        {
            List<WingedEdge> wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, faces);
            HashSet<Face> used = new HashSet<Face>();
            int count = 0;

            // this loop adds support for multiple islands of grouped selections
            for (int i = 0; i < wings.Count; i++)
            {
                if (used.Contains(wings[i].face))
                    continue;

                Dictionary<Face, bool> flags = new Dictionary<Face, bool>();

                GetWindingFlags(wings[i], true, flags);

                int flip = 0;

                foreach (var kvp in flags)
                    flip += kvp.Value ? 1 : -1;

                bool direction = flip > 0;

                foreach (var kvp in flags)
                {
                    if (direction != kvp.Value)
                    {
                        count++;
                        kvp.Key.Reverse();
                    }
                }

                used.UnionWith(flags.Keys);
            }

            if (count > 0)
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Success, count > 1 ? string.Format("Flipped {0} faces", count) : "Flipped 1 face");
            else
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.NoChange, "Faces Uniform");
        }
```

### SET PIVOT

The `SetPivotToSelection` action relocates the object's Transform pivot position to the geometric center of currently selected elements (vertices, edges, or faces) while applying compensating vertex translations so that the mesh geometry remains stationary in world space.

1. Menu Action Architecture (`SetPivotToSelection.cs`):
- Group: `ToolbarGroup.Geometry`.
- Icon: `"Toolbar/Pivot_CenterOnElements"`.
- Valid selection modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face`.
- Enabled condition: `MeshSelection.selectedVertexCount > 0 || MeshSelection.selectedEdgeCount > 0 || MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
- Execution:
  - Allocates undo object array: `Object[] objects = new Object[MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount * 2]`. Registers both `ProBuilderMesh` and `Transform` components via `UndoUtility.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(objects, "Set Pivot")`.
  - For each `ProBuilderMesh mesh` in `MeshSelection.topInternal`:
    - Unparents children: `TransformUtility.UnparentChildren(mesh.transform)` (prevents child objects from shifting).
    - Calls `mesh.CenterPivot(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`.
    - Optimizes mesh: `mesh.Optimize()`.
    - Restores children: `TransformUtility.ReparentChildren(mesh.transform)`.
  - Refreshes editor: `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

2. Core Center Pivot Algorithm (`MeshTransform.CenterPivot` in `MeshTransform.cs`):
- Parameters: `this ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `int[] indexes`.
- Step 1: Validates `mesh`, throwing `ArgumentNullException` if null.
- Step 2: Calculates selection centroid in world space:
  - If `indexes != null && indexes.Length > 0`:
    - Sums local positions: `foreach (int i in indexes) center += positions[i];`
    - Computes average and transforms to world coordinates: `center = mesh.transform.TransformPoint(center / (float)indexes.Length);`
  - Else (no indices provided):
    - Uses bounding box center: `center = mesh.transform.TransformPoint(mesh.mesh.bounds.center);`
- Step 3: Computes world translation delta:
  `Vector3 dir = (mesh.transform.position - center);`
- Step 4: Updates Transform component position to the new pivot:
  `mesh.transform.position = center;`
- Step 5: Offsets vertex positions in world space by `dir` to keep geometry stationary:
  `mesh.ToMesh();`
  `mesh.TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(mesh.mesh.triangles, dir);`
  `mesh.Refresh();`

3. Related Pivot Manipulation Functions in `MeshTransform.cs`:
- `SetPivot(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, PivotLocation pivotLocation)`:
  - Calculates `bounds = mesh.GetBounds()`.
  - Chooses `bounds.center` if `pivotLocation == PivotLocation.Center`, or `bounds.center - bounds.extents` if corner.
  - Transforms to world space and delegates to `SetPivot(mesh, worldPosition)`.
- `SetPivot(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Vector3 worldPosition)`:
  - Calculates delta `offset = transform.position - worldPosition`.
  - Sets `transform.position = worldPosition`.
  - Displaces vertices via `mesh.TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(mesh.mesh.triangles, offset)` and refreshes mesh.

## B04: Mesh transforms and vertex positioning

### VERTEX POSITIONING: TRANSLATE VERTICES, SET SHARED VERTEX POSITION, AND COINCIDENT VERTEX SYNCHRONIZATION

The vertex positioning subsystem in ProBuilder (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.VertexPositioning`) provides the mathematical and buffer-synchronization routines for translating and repositioning mesh vertices across local (model) space and global (world) space.

### Coordinate Spaces and Spatial Transformations
1. `VerticesInWorldSpace(this ProBuilderMesh mesh)`:
- Purpose: Extracts an array of all vertex positions transformed into global world coordinates.
- Algorithm: Allocates a new array `Vector3[] worldPoints` of length `mesh.vertexCount`. Reads the local positions directly from `mesh.positionsInternal`. Iterates through each index $i \in [0, \text{len}-1]$ and applies `worldPoints[i] = mesh.transform.TransformPoint(localPoints[i])`. Returns the populated `worldPoints` array without mutating mesh state.

2. `TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes, Vector3 offset, float snapValue, bool snapAxisOnly)`:
- Purpose: Translates a target set of vertices by a world-space delta vector `offset`, optionally applying world-grid snapping, and writes the results directly to both `ProBuilderMesh.positionsInternal` and the underlying `UnityEngine.Mesh.vertices` buffer.
- Step 1 (Coincident Vertex Collection): Calls `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(indexes, s_CoincidentVertices)` using the static list `s_CoincidentVertices` to identify all vertices that share topological coordinates with the passed `indexes`.
- Step 2 (Coordinate Space Conversion): Computes the world-to-local transformation matrix `Matrix4x4 w2l = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix` and converts the world offset into local coordinates via `Vector3 localOffset = w2l * offset`.
- Step 3 (Buffer Access): Obtains the raw local vertex array reference `Vector3[] verts = mesh.positionsInternal`.
- Step 4 (Snapping Branch vs Direct Branch):
  - When `Mathf.Abs(snapValue) > Mathf.Epsilon`: Computes `Matrix4x4 l2w = mesh.transform.localToWorldMatrix`. Evaluates `var mask = snapAxisOnly ? new Vector3Mask(offset, Math.handleEpsilon) : Vector3Mask.XYZ`. For every vertex index $j$ in `s_CoincidentVertices`, transforms the candidate position into world space via `var v = l2w.MultiplyPoint3x4(verts[s_CoincidentVertices[j]] + localOffset)`, snaps the world position to the nearest grid step using `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(v, ((Vector3)mask) * snapValue)`, and transforms the snapped point back into local space using `w2l.MultiplyPoint3x4(...)`.
  - When snapping is disabled (`Mathf.Abs(snapValue) <= Mathf.Epsilon`): Directly offsets each coincident vertex in local space: `verts[s_CoincidentVertices[j]] += localOffset`.
- Step 5 (Fast Direct Synchronization): Assigns `mesh.positionsInternal = verts` and `mesh.mesh.vertices = verts`. Bypasses calling `ToMesh()` because vertex count and buffer lengths are invariant during translation, ensuring optimal frame rate performance during interactive Scene view gizmo manipulation.

### Local Space Translation Overloads
1. `TranslateVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, Vector3 offset)`:
- Populates `s_CoincidentVertices` via `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(indexes, s_CoincidentVertices)` and invokes `TranslateVerticesInternal(mesh, s_CoincidentVertices, offset)`.
2. `TranslateVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Edge> edges, Vector3 offset)`:
- Populates `s_CoincidentVertices` via `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(edges, s_CoincidentVertices)` and invokes `TranslateVerticesInternal(mesh, s_CoincidentVertices, offset)`.
3. `TranslateVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces, Vector3 offset)`:
- Populates `s_CoincidentVertices` via `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(faces, s_CoincidentVertices)` and invokes `TranslateVerticesInternal(mesh, s_CoincidentVertices, offset)`.
4. `TranslateVerticesInternal(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indices, Vector3 offset)`:
- Obtains `Vector3[] verts = mesh.positionsInternal`, loops $i$ from 0 to `s_CoincidentVertices.Count - 1`, applies `verts[s_CoincidentVertices[i]] += offset`, and immediately assigns `mesh.mesh.vertices = verts`.

### SharedVertex Group Synchronization and Positioning
1. `SetSharedVertexPosition(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int sharedVertexHandle, Vector3 position)`:
- Sets the model-space position for an entire topological vertex cluster identified by `sharedVertexHandle`.
- Algorithm: Reads `Vector3[] v = mesh.positionsInternal`. Iterates through each index in `mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[sharedVertexHandle]` and sets `v[index] = position`. Writes back `mesh.positionsInternal = v` and `mesh.mesh.vertices = v`.
2. `SetSharedVertexValues(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int sharedVertexHandle, Vertex vertex)`:
- Overwrites all 8 vertex attribute channels (position, normal, tangent, color, UV0-UV3) across all coincident indices in `mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[sharedVertexHandle]` with the provided `Vertex` instance and applies changes via `mesh.SetVertices(vertices)`.
3. Synchronized Movement Semantics:
- In ProBuilder's unique-vertex-per-face architecture, a single geometric corner shared by $N$ faces is represented by $N$ distinct indices in `positionsInternal`.
- Coincident vertex groupings are stored in `SharedVertex[] m_SharedVertices` and indexed via `Dictionary<int, int> m_SharedVertexLookup`.
- When an editing operation translates or repositions an element, `GetCoincidentVertices` resolves the universal shared vertex handle for every selected index and retrieves all coincident indices belonging to that handle. Applying identical translations to all coincident indices ensures connected faces move together smoothly without cracking or tearing the surface topology.

```csharp
        /// <param name="snapAxisOnly">If true vertices will only be snapped along the active axis.</param>
        internal static void TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(this ProBuilderMesh mesh,
            int[] indexes,
            Vector3 offset,
            float snapValue,
            bool snapAxisOnly)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            int i = 0;

            mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(indexes, s_CoincidentVertices);

            Matrix4x4 w2l = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix;

            Vector3 localOffset = w2l * offset;

            Vector3[] verts = mesh.positionsInternal;

            // Snaps to world grid
            if (Mathf.Abs(snapValue) > Mathf.Epsilon)
            {
                Matrix4x4 l2w = mesh.transform.localToWorldMatrix;
                var mask = snapAxisOnly ? new Vector3Mask(offset, Math.handleEpsilon) : Vector3Mask.XYZ;

                for (i = 0; i < s_CoincidentVertices.Count; i++)
                {
                    var v = l2w.MultiplyPoint3x4(verts[s_CoincidentVertices[i]] + localOffset);
                    verts[s_CoincidentVertices[i]] = w2l.MultiplyPoint3x4(ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(v, ((Vector3)mask) * snapValue));
                }
            }
            else
            {
                for (i = 0; i < s_CoincidentVertices.Count; i++)
                    verts[s_CoincidentVertices[i]] += localOffset;
            }

            // don't bother calling a full ToMesh() here because we know for certain that the vertices and msh.vertices arrays are equal in length
            mesh.positionsInternal = verts;
            mesh.mesh.vertices = verts;
        }
```

### MESH TRANSFORM: FREEZE TRANSFORM, FREEZE SCALE TRANSFORM, SET PIVOT, CENTER PIVOT, AND OBJECT MIRRORING

The mesh transform subsystem (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.MeshTransform`, `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.FreezeTransform`, and `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.MirrorObjects`) bakes transformation matrices into vertex buffers, recalculates object pivots, and reflects geometry across principal axes.

### Freeze Scale Transform and Freeze Transform Algorithms
1. `FreezeScaleTransform(this ProBuilderMesh mesh)` (`MeshTransform.cs`):
- Multiplies each local vertex position in `mesh.positionsInternal` by the transform's current local scale: `v[i] = Vector3.Scale(v[i], mesh.transform.localScale)`.
- Resets `mesh.transform.localScale = new Vector3(1f, 1f, 1f)`.

2. `FreezeTransform` Action (`FreezeTransform.cs`):
- Purpose: Resets the GameObject's world transform position to `(0, 0, 0)`, rotation to `Quaternion.identity`, and scale to `(1, 1, 1)` while preserving the exact world-space position, scale, and shape of all mesh vertices.
- Step 1 (Undo Registration): Registers the selection via `UndoUtility.RecordMeshAndTransformSelection("Freeze Transforms")`.
- Step 2 (World Position Caching): Gathers absolute world coordinates for all selected meshes into `Vector3[][] positions` by invoking `selection[i].VerticesInWorldSpace()`.
- Step 3 (Reflection and Winding Assessment): Evaluates `ShouldFlipFaces(pb.transform.localScale)` by computing the sign product `var globalSign = Mathf.Sign(scale.x) * Mathf.Sign(scale.y) * Mathf.Sign(scale.z)`. If `globalSign < 0`, an odd number of scale axes are negative, necessitating a polygon winding reversal to preserve outward-facing normals.
- Step 4 (Transform Reset): Sets `pb.transform.SetPositionAndRotation(Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity)` and `pb.transform.localScale = Vector3.one`.
- Step 5 (Face and UV Invariant Updates): For each `Face face` in `pb.facesInternal`, sets `face.manualUV = true` (to prevent automatic UV reprojection from distorting texture mapping) and calls `face.Reverse()` if `flipFaces` is true.
- Step 6 (Vertex Assignment and Compilation): Assigns `pb.positions = positions[i]`, then invokes `pb.ToMesh()`, `pb.Refresh()`, and `pb.Optimize()`.

### Set Pivot and Center Pivot Algorithms
1. `CenterPivot(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes)` (`MeshTransform.cs`):
- Centroid Calculation: When `indexes` is provided and contains $\ge 3$ entries, computes the centroid `center += positions[i]` for all $i \in \text{indexes}$, divides by `indexes.Length`, and converts to world space via `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(...)`. Otherwise, converts the bounding box center `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(mesh.mesh.bounds.center)`.
- Delta Calculation: Calculates the world translation delta `Vector3 dir = (mesh.transform.position - center)`.
- Transform Relocation: Updates `mesh.transform.position = center`.
- Vertex Counter-Translation: Calls `mesh.ToMesh()`, counter-translates all vertex indices in world space via `mesh.TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(mesh.mesh.triangles, dir)`, and refreshes the mesh with `mesh.Refresh()`.

2. `SetPivot(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Vector3 worldPosition)` (`MeshTransform.cs`):
- Calculates `Vector3 offset = transform.position - worldPosition`.
- Repositions `transform.position = worldPosition`.
- Counter-translates all mesh triangles: `mesh.ToMesh()`, `mesh.TranslateVerticesInWorldSpace(mesh.mesh.triangles, offset)`, `mesh.Refresh()`.

3. `SetPivot(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, PivotLocation pivotLocation)` (`MeshTransform.cs`):
- Queries mesh bounding box `var bounds = mesh.GetBounds()`.
- Sets pivot coordinate to `bounds.center` if `pivotLocation == PivotLocation.Center`, or `bounds.center - bounds.extents` if `pivotLocation == PivotLocation.FirstVertex`. Converts the local bound point to world coordinates via `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(pivot)` and delegates to `SetPivot(mesh, worldPoint)`.

### Mirror Objects Algorithm
1. `Mirror(ProBuilderMesh pb, Vector3 scale, bool duplicate = true)` (`MirrorObjects.cs`):
- Configuration Flags: `MirrorSettings` bitmask defines `X = 0x1`, `Y = 0x2`, `Z = 0x4`, and `Duplicate = 0x8`. Constructs `Vector3 scale` where active axes receive `-1f` and inactive axes receive `1f`.
- Duplication Logic: When `duplicate` is true, calls `Object.Instantiate(pb.gameObject, pb.transform.parent, false)`, calls `MakeUnique()`, aligns transform parent and local rotation, and registers `Undo.RegisterCreatedObjectUndo`. When false, records object state with `UndoUtility.RecordObject(pb, "Mirror")`.
- Reflection Scaling: Caches original local scale `Vector3 lScale = mirroredObject.gameObject.transform.localScale` and assigns `mirroredObject.transform.localScale = scale`.
- Winding Inversion: If `(scale.x * scale.y * scale.z) < 0` (reflection across 1 or 3 axes), inverts polygon face winding by iterating `mirroredObject.facesInternal` and invoking `face.Reverse()`.
- Scale Baking: Calls `mirroredObject.FreezeScaleTransform()` to bake the reflection scale directly into the vertex positions.
- Scale Restoration: Re-applies `mirroredObject.transform.localScale = lScale`.
- Mesh Rebuilding: Completes pipeline compilation via `mirroredObject.ToMesh()`, `mirroredObject.Refresh()`, and `mirroredObject.Optimize()`.

```csharp
        public static ProBuilderMesh Mirror(ProBuilderMesh pb, Vector3 scale, bool duplicate = true)
        {
            ProBuilderMesh mirroredObject;

            if (duplicate)
            {
                mirroredObject = Object.Instantiate(pb.gameObject, pb.transform.parent, false).GetComponent<ProBuilderMesh>();
                mirroredObject.MakeUnique();
                mirroredObject.transform.parent = pb.transform.parent;
                mirroredObject.transform.localRotation = pb.transform.localRotation;
                Undo.RegisterCreatedObjectUndo(mirroredObject.gameObject, "Mirror Object");
            }
            else
            {
                UndoUtility.RecordObject(pb, "Mirror");
                mirroredObject = pb;
            }

            Vector3 lScale = mirroredObject.gameObject.transform.localScale;
            mirroredObject.transform.localScale = scale;

            // if flipping on an odd number of axes, flip winding order
            if ((scale.x * scale.y * scale.z) < 0)
            {
                foreach (var face in mirroredObject.facesInternal)
                    face.Reverse();
            }

            mirroredObject.FreezeScaleTransform();
            mirroredObject.transform.localScale = lScale;

            mirroredObject.ToMesh();
            mirroredObject.Refresh();
            mirroredObject.Optimize();

            return mirroredObject;
        }
    }
}
```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, freezing a `Node3D` transform involves transforming each vertex in the mesh's surface arrays by `node.global_transform` and resetting `node.transform = Transform3D.IDENTITY`. For mirroring, Godot's `ArrayMesh` surfaces require negative scaling along the chosen axes and reversing triangle index triplets `(i0, i1, i2) -> (i0, i2, i1)` to prevent inverted backface culling.

### SURFACE TOPOLOGY: CONNECTED ELEMENTS, WINGED-EDGE TRAVERSAL, WINDING ORDER, NORMALS CONFORMANCE, AND EDGE FLIPPING

The surface topology subsystem (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.SurfaceTopology` and `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.ElementSelection`) implements topological graph construction, connected element searches, normal conformance across polygon islands, edge flipping in quads, and winding order calculation.

### Connected Elements Algorithms
1. `GetConnectedEdges(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes)` (`ElementSelection.cs`):
- Input: `ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `int[] indexes` (array of local vertex indices).
- Algorithm:
  - Retrieves `Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
  - Populates `HashSet<int> shared` with the shared vertex handles for all input indices: `shared.Add(lookup[indexes[i]])`.
  - Instantiates `List<Edge> connectedEdges` and `HashSet<Edge> used`.
  - Iterates through every `Face face` in `mesh.facesInternal` and every `Edge edge` in `face.edges`.
  - Converts edge local vertex indices to universal shared vertex handles: `Edge key = new Edge(lookup[edge.a], lookup[edge.b])`.
  - Evaluates connectivity: If `shared.Contains(key.a) || shared.Contains(key.b)` and `key` has not been added to `used`, adds `edge` to `connectedEdges` and registers `used.Add(key)`.
  - Returns `connectedEdges.ToArray()`.

### Winged-Edge Traversal and Normal Conformance
1. `ConformNormals(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces)` (`SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Purpose: Unifies the outward orientation of face normals across one or more connected polygonal islands.
- Step 1 (Winged Edge Graph): Builds a complete topological graph using `List<WingedEdge> wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, faces)`.
- Step 2 (Island Iteration): Maintains `HashSet<Face> used`. Iterates through `wings[i]`. If `used.Contains(wings[i].face)`, skips to the next wing.
- Step 3 (Recursive Traversal): Instantiates `Dictionary<Face, bool> flags` and invokes `GetWindingFlags(wings[i], true, flags)`.
- Step 4 (Majority Vote Evaluation): Sums `flip += kvp.Value ? 1 : -1` across all faces in `flags`. Sets `bool direction = flip > 0`.
- Step 5 (Winding Inversion): For every face where `direction != kvp.Value`, increments `count` and inverts the face indices via `kvp.Key.Reverse()`.
- Step 6 (Island Registration): Unions `flags.Keys` into `used`. Returns `ActionResult.Status.Success` with the count of flipped faces, or `Status.NoChange` if faces were already uniform.

2. `GetWindingFlags(WingedEdge edge, bool flag, Dictionary<Face, bool> flags)` (`SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Registers `flags.Add(edge.face, flag)`.
- Traverses around the polygon perimeter: `WingedEdge next = edge; do { ... next = next.next; } while (next != edge)`.
- For each edge where `opp = next.opposite` exists and `!flags.ContainsKey(opp.face)`:
  - Determines directed universal edge orientations: `Edge cea = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(next)` and `Edge ceb = GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(opp)`.
  - In a continuous manifold surface, adjacent faces traverse the shared edge in opposite directions (`cea.a != ceb.a`). If `cea.a == ceb.a`, both faces traverse in the same direction (inconsistent winding).
  - Recursively calls `GetWindingFlags(opp, cea.a == ceb.a ? !flag : flag, flags)`.

3. `GetCommonEdgeInWindingOrder(WingedEdge wing)` (`SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Scans triangle triplets `(a, b, c)` in `wing.face.indexesInternal`. Matches local edge `(e.a, e.b)` to the triangle index sequence and returns the shared edge `wing.edge.common` directed according to the true triangle winding order.

4. `ConformOppositeNormal(WingedEdge source)` and `MatchNormal(Face source, Face target, Dictionary<int, int> lookup)`:
- Pairwise normal alignment functions. `MatchNormal` checks universal edges between adjacent faces `source` and `target`, reversing `target` via `target.Reverse()` if `src.a == tar.a`.

### Winding Order Detection and Edge Flipping
1. `GetWindingOrder(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)` (`SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Projects face 3D positions onto a 2D best-fit plane using `Projection.PlanarProject(mesh.positionsInternal, face.distinctIndexesInternal)`.
- Evaluates the Shoelace sum across all polygon vertices: `sum += ((b.x - a.x) * (b.y + a.y))`.
- Returns `WindingOrder.Clockwise` if `sum > 0f`, `WindingOrder.CounterClockwise` if `sum < 0f`, or `WindingOrder.Unknown` if `sum == 0f`.

2. `FlipEdge(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)` (`SurfaceTopology.cs`):
- Reverses the diagonal edge of a quad face composed of two triangles (`indexesInternal.Length == 6`).
- Counts vertex occurrences across the 6 indices into an array `int[] mode`: the two shared diagonal vertices appear twice (`mode == 2`), while the two opposite corner vertices appear once (`mode == 1`).
- Validates quad topology: checks `mode[0] + mode[1] + mode[2] == 5` and `mode[3] + mode[4] + mode[5] == 5`.
- Rewires triangle index triplets so the diagonal connects the corner vertices `i0` and `i1`.
- Calls `face.InvalidateCache()` and returns `true`.

```csharp
        /// <param name="indexes"></param>
        /// <returns></returns>
        internal static Edge[] GetConnectedEdges(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes)
        {
            var lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup;

            List<Edge> connectedEdges = new List<Edge>();

            HashSet<int> shared = new HashSet<int>();

            for (int i = 0; i < indexes.Length; i++)
                shared.Add(lookup[indexes[i]]);

            HashSet<Edge> used = new HashSet<Edge>();

            Edge uni = new Edge(0, 0);

            foreach (var face in mesh.facesInternal)
            {
                foreach (var edge in face.edges)
                {
                    Edge key = new Edge(lookup[edge.a], lookup[edge.b]);

                    if (shared.Contains(key.a) || shared.Contains(key.b) && !used.Contains(uni))
                    {
                        connectedEdges.Add(edge);
                        used.Add(key);
                    }
                }
            }

            return connectedEdges.ToArray();
        }
```

> **Godot Note:** Godot 4's rendering engine requires consistent triangle winding (counter-clockwise by default for front-facing polygons). Half-edge graph structures built over `ArrayMesh` surfaces allow implementing BFS/DFS normal propagation matching ProBuilder's `ConformNormals` algorithm.

### VERTEX EDITING: SHARED VERTEX MAINTENANCE, MERGING, SPLITTING, WELDING, AND EXPLODING VERTICES

The vertex editing subsystem (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.VertexEditing` and `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.ProBuilderMeshFunction`) manages topological connectivity, coincident vertex consolidation, vertex splitting, radial welding, and vertex extrusion.

### Shared Vertex Map Architecture and Maintenance
1. Map Representation:
- `SharedVertex[] m_SharedVertices`: Serialized array where each `SharedVertex` holds an integer array `m_Vertices` containing coincident local vertex indices sharing the same spatial coordinate.
- `Dictionary<int, int> m_SharedVertexLookup`: Non-serialized dictionary providing $O(1)$ lookup from local vertex index $\to$ shared vertex handle index in `m_SharedVertices`.
2. Cache Invalidation and Updates:
- Any vertex creation, deletion, or splitting operation invokes `InvalidateSharedVertexLookup()`, clearing `m_SharedVertexLookup` and resetting `m_CacheValid &= ~CacheValidState.SharedVertex`.
- `SetSharedVertices(IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<int, int>> indexes)`: Reconstructs `m_SharedVertices` using `SharedVertex.ToSharedVertices(indexes)` and invalidates the lookup cache.
- `SetVerticesCoincident(IEnumerable<int> vertices)`: Collects coincident indices via `GetCoincidentVertices(vertices, coincident)`, invokes `SharedVertex.SetCoincident(ref lookup, coincident)` to assign a common universal handle, and applies the lookup via `SetSharedVertices(lookup)`.
- `AddToSharedVertex(int sharedVertexHandle, int vertex)`: Appends `vertex` to `m_SharedVertices[sharedVertexHandle]` and invalidates the cache.
- `AddSharedVertex(SharedVertex vertex)`: Appends `vertex` to `m_SharedVertices` and invalidates the cache.

### Vertex Merging Algorithm (`MergeVertices`)
1. Signature: `public static int MergeVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes, bool collapseToFirst = false)`
2. Target Calculation: Evaluates `cen = collapseToFirst ? vertices[indexes[0]] : Vertex.Average(vertices, indexes)`.
3. Coincident Mapping: Invokes `mesh.SetVerticesCoincident(indexes)` to map all target indices to the same shared vertex handle.
4. UV Seam Splitting: Calls `UVEditing.SplitUVs(mesh, indexes)` to prevent UV coordinate distortion across collapsed faces.
5. Attribute Assignment: Gets `int sharedVertexHandle = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandle(indexes[0])` and calls `mesh.SetSharedVertexValues(sharedVertexHandle, cen)`.
6. Degenerate Removal: Calls `MeshValidation.RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removedIndexes)` to clean up zero-area triangles produced by collapsing polygon edges.
7. Return Index Compensation: Identifies a surviving index in the merged `SharedVertex` cluster not present in `removedIndexes`, decrements it by the count of preceding removed indices, and returns the compacted index.

### Vertex Splitting Algorithm (`SplitVertices`)
1. Signatures: `SplitVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, Edge edge)` and `SplitVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> vertices)`
2. Algorithm:
- Obtains `Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
- Calculates current maximum shared index `int max = lookup.Count`.
- Iterates each index $i \in \text{vertices}$, assigning a unique new shared vertex handle: `lookup[i] = ++max`.
- Re-applies the updated dictionary: `mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup)`.
- Consequence: The split vertices now move independently during translation without affecting neighboring coincident faces.

### Vertex Welding Algorithm (`WeldVertices`)
1. Signature: `public static int[] WeldVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, float neighborRadius)`
2. Step 1 (KD-Tree Initialization): Extracts distinct shared vertex handles `HashSet<int> common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(indexes)`. Instantiates a 3-dimensional KD-Tree `KdTree<float, int> tree = new KdTree<float, int>(3, new FloatMath(), AddDuplicateBehavior.Collect)`. Adds the 3D position of each common vertex handle to the tree.
3. Step 2 (Radial Neighbor Search): For each unmapped handle `commonIndex` in `common`, queries `tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, maxNearestNeighbors)`. If the search fills the neighbor capacity, expands capacity and re-queries.
4. Step 3 (Centroid Averaging): Averages the 3D positions of all neighbor nodes within `neighborRadius` into `Vector3 avg`. Maps all grouped handles to a new unique index `index` in `Dictionary<int, int> remapped` and stores `avg` in `Dictionary<int, Vector3> averages`.
5. Step 4 (Lookup and Buffer Application): Iterates through `remapped`, updating `lookup[tris[i]] = kvp.Value` and setting `vertices[tris[i]].position = averages[kvp.Value]`.
6. Step 5 (Commitment): Invokes `mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup)` and `mesh.SetVertices(vertices)`, returning an array of welded vertex indices.

### Vertex Exploding Algorithm (`ExplodeVertex`)
1. Method: `ExplodeVertex(IList<Vertex> vertices, IList<KeyValuePair<WingedEdge, int>> edgeAndCommonIndex, float distance, out Dictionary<int, List<int>> appendedVertices)`
- Edge-and-common-index collection: Receives pairs of `WingedEdge` wings and their corresponding universal indices.
2. Algorithm: Splits a vertex along its adjacent perimeter edges on a face by inserting two vertices offset by `distance` along the normalized edge directions (`leading_dir` and `following_dir`), retriangulates the modified contour with `Triangulation.TriangulateVertices`, and preserves the original face normal orientation.

```csharp
        /// <remarks>
        /// Retains vertex normals.
        /// </remarks>
        /// <param name="mesh">Target mesh.</param>
        /// <param name="indexes">The indexes to merge to a single shared vertex.</param>
        /// <param name="collapseToFirst">True to collapse the vertices onto the first vertex position; false to merge all vertices to the average position.</param>
        /// <returns>The first available local index created as a result of the merge, or -1 if action failed.</returns>
        public static int MergeVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes, bool collapseToFirst = false)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (indexes == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("indexes");

            Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices();
            Vertex cen = collapseToFirst ? vertices[indexes[0]] : Vertex.Average(vertices, indexes);
            mesh.SetVerticesCoincident(indexes);
            UVEditing.SplitUVs(mesh, indexes);
            int sharedVertexHandle = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandle(indexes[0]);
            mesh.SetSharedVertexValues(sharedVertexHandle, cen);

            SharedVertex merged = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[sharedVertexHandle];
            List<int> removedIndexes = new List<int>();

            MeshValidation.RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removedIndexes);

            // get a non-deleted index to work with
            int ind = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < merged.Count; i++)
                if (!removedIndexes.Contains(merged[i]))
                    ind = merged[i];

            int res = ind;

            for (int i = 0; i < removedIndexes.Count; i++)
                if (ind > removedIndexes[i])
                    res--;

            return res;
        }
```

```csharp
        public static void SplitVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> vertices)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (vertices == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("vertices");

            // ToDictionary always sets the universal indexes in ascending order from 0+.
            Dictionary<int, int> lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup;
            int max = lookup.Count;
            foreach (int i in vertices)
                lookup[i] = ++max;
            mesh.SetSharedVertices(lookup);
        }
```

```csharp
        /// <param name="mesh">The source mesh.</param>
        /// <param name="indexes">The vertex indices to consider. For example, to weld the entire object, set this value to the return value from `pb.faces.SelectMany(x => x.indexes)`.</param>
        /// <param name="neighborRadius">The minimum distance between vertices to consider them for welding.</param>
        /// <returns>The indices of any new vertices created by a weld.</returns>
        public static int[] WeldVertices(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, float neighborRadius)
        {
            if (mesh == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("mesh");

            if (indexes == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("indexes");

            Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices();
            SharedVertex[] sharedIndexes = mesh.sharedVerticesInternal;

            HashSet<int> common = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandles(indexes);
            int vertexCount = common.Count;

            // Make assumption that there will rarely be a time when a single weld encompasses more than 32 vertices.
            // If a radial search returns neighbors matching the max count, the search is re-done and maxNearestNeighbors
            // is set to the resulting length. This will be slow, but in most cases shouldn't happen ever, or if it does,
            // should only happen once or twice.
            int maxNearestNeighbors = System.Math.Min(32, common.Count);

            // 3 dimensions, duplicate entries allowed
            KdTree<float, int> tree = new KdTree<float, int>(3, new FloatMath(), AddDuplicateBehavior.Collect);

            foreach (int i in common)
            {
                Vector3 v = vertices[sharedIndexes[i][0]].position;
                tree.Add(new float[] { v.x, v.y, v.z }, i);
            }

            float[] point = new float[3] { 0, 0, 0 };
            Dictionary<int, int> remapped = new Dictionary<int, int>();
            Dictionary<int, Vector3> averages = new Dictionary<int, Vector3>();
            int index = sharedIndexes.Length;

            foreach (int commonIndex in common)
            {
                // already merged with another
                if (remapped.ContainsKey(commonIndex))
                    continue;

                Vector3 v = vertices[sharedIndexes[commonIndex][0]].position;

                point[0] = v.x;
                point[1] = v.y;
                point[2] = v.z;

                // Radial search at each point
                KdTreeNode<float, int>[] neighbors = tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, maxNearestNeighbors);

                // if first radial search filled the entire allotment reset the max neighbor count to 1.5x.
                // the result hopefully preventing double-searches in the next iterations.
                if (maxNearestNeighbors < vertexCount && neighbors.Length >= maxNearestNeighbors)
                {
                    neighbors = tree.RadialSearch(point, neighborRadius, vertexCount);
                    maxNearestNeighbors = System.Math.Min(vertexCount, neighbors.Length + neighbors.Length / 2);
                }

                Vector3 avg = Vector3.zero;
                float count = 0;

                for (int neighborIndex = 0; neighborIndex < neighbors.Length; neighborIndex++)
                {
                    // common index of this neighbor
                    int c = neighbors[neighborIndex].Value;

                    // if it's already been added to another, skip it
                    if (remapped.ContainsKey(c))
                        continue;

                    avg.x += neighbors[neighborIndex].Point[0];
                    avg.y += neighbors[neighborIndex].Point[1];
```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, welding vertices is achieved by spatial hashing into grid cells of size `neighbor_radius` or constructing a KD-Tree/BVH, computing cluster centroids, and updating the surface index buffer. Splitting vertices requires duplicating positions, normals, and UVs in the vertex buffer so that individual faces reference independent vertex entries.

### MESH VALIDATION: REMOVE DEGENERATE TRIANGLES, REMOVE UNUSED VERTICES, ENSURE MESH IS VALID, AND ATTRIBUTE NORMALIZATION

The mesh validation subsystem (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.MeshValidation`) validates geometric invariants, removes degenerate zero-area triangles, strips unreferenced orphan vertices, repairs selection index buffers after deletions, and sanitizes vertex attribute buffers against NaN values and dimension mismatches.

### Degenerate Triangle Detection and Removal
1. `ContainsDegenerateTriangles(this ProBuilderMesh mesh)`:
- Iterates each `Face face` and evaluates `Math.TriangleArea(p0, p1, p2)`. If any triangle has `area <= Mathf.Epsilon`, returns `true`.

2. `RemoveDegenerateTriangles(ProBuilderMesh mesh, List<int> removed = null)` (`MeshValidation.cs`):
- Purpose: Prunes zero-area triangles and coincident-vertex degenerate triangles from all faces, updating shared vertex maps and purging unused vertex buffers.
- Step 1 (Lookup and Filter Initialization): Retrieves `m_Lookup` (`mesh.sharedVertexLookup`), `m_LookupUV` (`mesh.sharedTextureLookup`), and `m_Positions` (`mesh.positionsInternal`). Prepares `m_RebuiltLookup`, `m_RebuiltLookupUV`, and `m_DuplicateIndexFilter`.
- Step 2 (Triangle Inspection per Face):
  - For each `Face face` in `mesh.facesInternal`: Loops through indices in triplets `(ind[i], ind[i+1], ind[i+2])`.
  - Calculates area: `float area = Math.TriangleArea(m_Positions[ind[i+0]], m_Positions[ind[i+1]], m_Positions[ind[i+2]])`.
  - Area threshold check: If `area > Mathf.Epsilon`, inspects shared handles `sharedIndexA`, `sharedIndexB`, `sharedIndexC`.
  - Duplicate index check: If all three shared handles are distinct (`!(sharedIndexA == sharedIndexB || sharedIndexA == sharedIndexC || sharedIndexB == sharedIndexC)`), filters intra-face coincident vertex duplicates via `m_DuplicateIndexFilter`.
  - Buffer retention: Appends valid triangle indices to `tris` and registers shared mappings in `m_RebuiltLookup` and `m_RebuiltLookupUV`.
- Step 3 (Face List Rebuilding): If `tris.Count > 0`, assigns `face.indexesInternal = tris.ToArray()` and adds `face` to `m_RebuiltFaces`. (If all triangles within a face were degenerate, the entire face is dropped).
- Step 4 (Map Application): Assigns `mesh.faces = m_RebuiltFaces`, `mesh.SetSharedVertices(m_RebuiltLookup)`, and `mesh.SetSharedTextures(m_RebuiltLookupUV)`.
- Step 5 (Unused Vertex Purge): Calls `RemoveUnusedVertices(mesh, removed)` and returns whether any vertices were deleted.

### Unused Vertex Purge (`RemoveUnusedVertices`)
1. Signature: `public static bool RemoveUnusedVertices(ProBuilderMesh mesh, List<int> removed = null)`
2. Algorithm:
- Collects all referenced vertex indices from faces into `HashSet<int> tris = new HashSet<int>(mesh.facesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.indexes))`.
- Loops through all indices $i \in [0, \text{positionsInternal.Length}-1]$. If `!tris.Contains(i)`, appends $i$ to `del`.
- Invokes `mesh.DeleteVertices(del)` to compact vertex positions, colors, normals, tangents, UVs, and shared vertex arrays.
- Returns `del.Count > 0`.

### Index and Selection Rebuilding Algorithms
1. `RebuildIndexes(IEnumerable<int> indices, List<int> removed)`:
- For each index, computes `var nearestIndex = ArrayUtility.NearestIndexPriorToValue(removed, index) + 1`. If the index itself was deleted, skips it; otherwise adds `index - nearestIndex` to the output list.
2. `RebuildEdges(IEnumerable<Edge> edges, List<int> removed)`:
- Rebuilds edge endpoints `.a` and `.b` by subtracting their respective prior deletion counts: `new Edge(edge.a - nearestIndexA, edge.b - nearestIndexB)`.
3. `RebuildSelectionIndexes(ProBuilderMesh mesh, ref Face[] faces, ref Edge[] edges, ref int[] indices, IEnumerable<int> removed)`:
- Compacts selection arrays (`faces`, `edges`, `indices`) in-place after vertex removals.

### Comprehensive Mesh Integrity Assurance (`EnsureMeshIsValid`)
1. `EnsureMeshIsValid(ProBuilderMesh mesh, out int removedVertices)`:
- Checks `ContainsDegenerateTriangles(mesh)`. If true:
  - Caches current selection state (`selectedFacesInternal`, `selectedEdgesInternal`, `selectedIndexesInternal`).
  - Calls `RemoveDegenerateTriangles(mesh, removed)`.
  - Recomputes shared vertices from remaining positions: `mesh.sharedVertices = SharedVertex.GetSharedVerticesWithPositions(mesh.positionsInternal)`.
  - Rebuilds selection index arrays with `RebuildSelectionIndexes`.
  - Sets `removedVertices = removed.Count` and returns `false`.
- Calls `EnsureValidAttributes(mesh)` and returns `true`.

### Attribute Validation and Normalization (`EnsureValidAttributes`)
1. Buffer Dimension Synchronization:
- Compares lengths of `normalsInternal`, `colorsInternal`, `tangentsInternal`, `texturesInternal` (UV0), `textures2Internal` (UV2), and `textures3Internal` (UV3) against `mesh.vertexCount`.
- Invokes `EnsureArraySize` or `EnsureListSize` to resize or nullify mismatched arrays.
2. Floating-Point Sanitization:
- Invokes `EnsureRealNumbers` on normals, tangents, colors, and UV coordinates, calling `Math.FixNaN` on each vector component to replace `float.NaN` and `float.PositiveInfinity`/`float.NegativeInfinity` with `0f`.

```csharp
        static void EnsureListSize<T>(ref List<T> attribute,
            int expectedVertexCount,
            AttributeValidationStrategy strategy = AttributeValidationStrategy.Nullify,
            T fill = default)
        {
            if (attribute == null || attribute.Count == expectedVertexCount)
                return;

            if (strategy == AttributeValidationStrategy.Nullify)
            {
                attribute = null;
                return;
            }

            var prev = attribute.Count;
            var copy = new List<T>(expectedVertexCount);
            for (int i = 0, c = Mathf.Min(prev, expectedVertexCount); i < c; i++)
                copy.Add(attribute[i]);
            for (int i = copy.Count - 1; i < expectedVertexCount; i++)
                copy.Add(fill);
            attribute = copy;
        }
```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, degenerate triangles in `ArrayMesh` surfaces degrade physics convex hull generation and raycasting collision checks. Rebuilding index arrays and discarding zero-area triangles during mesh compilation ensures robust physics collision and visual rendering.
