### EACH ACTION

Each selection menu action in ProBuilder specifies distinct valid selection modes, enabled verification criteria, settings preferences, modifier shortcuts, and undo registration contracts:

1. `SelectEdgeLoop`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Edge`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedEdgeCount > 0`.
   - Settings: `m_SelectIterative` (`Pref<bool>("SelectEdgeLoop.selectIterative", false)`).
   - Modifiers & Shortcuts: `Alt + L` menu shortcut; Double-Click on an edge in Scene view.
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Edge Loop")`.
   - Result: Returns Success if `loop.Length > pb.selectedEdgeCount`, else Failure ("Nothing to Loop").

2. `SelectEdgeRing`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Edge`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedEdgeCount > 0`.
   - Settings: `m_SelectIterative` (`Pref<bool>("SelectEdgeRing.selectIterative", false)`).
   - Modifiers & Shortcuts: `Alt + R` menu shortcut; `Shift + Double-Click` on an edge in Scene view.
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Edge Ring")`.
   - Result: Returns Success if `edges.Length > mesh.selectedEdgeCount`, else Failure ("Nothing to Ring").

3. `SelectFaceLoop`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
   - Modifiers & Shortcuts: `Shift + Double-Click` on a face in Scene view.
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Face Loop")`.
   - Result: Returns Success ("Select Face Loop").

4. `SelectFaceRing`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
   - Modifiers & Shortcuts: `Control + Double-Click` on a face executes `SelectFaceRing.PerformAction()`; `Shift + Control + Double-Click` executes `SelectFaceRing.MenuRingAndLoopFaces(MeshSelection.topInternal)` (selects both ring and loop).
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Face Ring")` or `UndoUtility.RecordSelection(selection.ToArray(), "Select Face Ring and Loop")`.
   - Result: Returns Success ("Select Face Ring" / "Select Face Ring and Loop").

5. `SelectHole`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount > 0` (operates on whole mesh if vertex/edge count is 0).
   - Shortcuts: Menu `Tools > ProBuilder > Selection > Select Hole`.
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Hole")`.
   - Result: Returns Success formatted as `"{0} holes found"` or `"No Holes in Selection"`.

6. `SelectLoop` (Contextual Menu Proxy):
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: Delegates to `SelectEdgeLoop.enabled` in Edge mode or `SelectFaceLoop.enabled` in Face mode.
   - Shortcuts: `Alt + L`.
   - Undo Registration: Delegated to underlying action.

7. `SelectRing` (Contextual Menu Proxy):
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: Delegates to `SelectEdgeRing.enabled` in Edge mode or `SelectFaceRing.enabled` in Face mode.
   - Shortcuts: `Alt + R`.
   - Undo Registration: Delegated to underlying action.

8. `SelectMaterial`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
   - Settings: `m_RestrictToSelectedObjects` (`Pref<bool>("SelectMaterial.restrictToSelectedObjects", false, SettingsScope.Project)`).
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Faces with Material")`.
   - Result: Returns Success ("Select Faces with Material").

9. `SelectSmoothingGroup`:
   - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
   - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`.
   - Visibility: `hidden => true`.
   - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Faces with Smoothing Group")`.
   - Result: Returns Success ("Select Faces with Smoothing Group").

10. `SelectVertexColor`:
    - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
    - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && MeshSelection.selectedVertexCount > 0`.
    - Settings: `m_SearchSelectedObjectsOnly` (`Pref<bool>("SelectVertexColor.restrictToSelectedObjects", false)`).
    - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Select Faces with Vertex Colors")`.
    - Result: Returns Success ("Select Faces with Vertex Colors").

11. `GrowSelection`:
    - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
    - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && VerifyGrowSelection()` where `VerifyGrowSelection()` checks `selectedCount > 0 && selectedCount < totalCount`.
    - Settings: `m_GrowSelectionWithAngle` (`Pref<bool>("GrowSelection.useAngle", true)`), `m_GrowSelectionAngleIterative` (`Pref<bool>("GrowSelection.iterativeGrow", false)`), `m_GrowSelectionAngleValue` (`Pref<float>("GrowSelection.angleValue", 15f)`).
    - Shortcuts: `Alt + G`.
    - Mode Actions: In Vertex/Edge mode, executes `ElementSelection.GetConnectedEdges(pb, pb.selectedIndexesInternal)`. In Face mode, executes `ElementSelection.GrowSelection` (if iterative) or `ElementSelection.FloodSelection` (if flood/non-iterative) with optional normal angle threshold.
    - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Grow Selection")`.
    - Result: Returns Success if `grown > 0`, else Failure ("Nothing to Grow").

12. `ShrinkSelection`:
    - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`.
    - Enabled Condition: `base.enabled && VerifyShrinkSelection()` where `VerifyShrinkSelection()` checks `selectedCount > 1 && selectedCount < totalCount`.
    - Shortcuts: `Alt + Shift + G`.
    - Mode Actions: In Edge mode, calls `ElementSelection.GetPerimeterEdges` and removes perimeter edges. In Face mode, calls `ElementSelection.GetPerimeterFaces` and removes perimeter faces. In Vertex mode, calls `ElementSelection.GetPerimeterVertices` with `universalEdges` and removes perimeter vertices.
    - Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Shrink Selection")`.
    - Result: Returns Success if `rc > 0`, else Canceled ("Nothing to Shrink").

```csharp

            UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Grow Selection");

            int grown = 0;
            bool angleGrow = m_GrowSelectionWithAngle;
            bool iterative = m_GrowSelectionAngleIterative;
            float growSelectionAngle = m_GrowSelectionAngleValue;

            if (!angleGrow && !iterative)
                iterative = true;

            foreach (ProBuilderMesh pb in InternalUtility.GetComponents<ProBuilderMesh>(Selection.transforms))
            {
                int previousTriCount = pb.selectedVertexCount;

                switch (ProBuilderEditor.selectMode)
                {
                    case SelectMode.Vertex:
                        pb.SetSelectedEdges(ElementSelection.GetConnectedEdges(pb, pb.selectedIndexesInternal));
                        break;

                    case SelectMode.Edge:
                        pb.SetSelectedEdges(ElementSelection.GetConnectedEdges(pb, pb.selectedIndexesInternal));
                        break;

                    case SelectMode.TextureFace:
                    case SelectMode.Face:

                        Face[] selectedFaces = pb.GetSelectedFaces();

                        HashSet<Face> sel;

                        if (iterative)
                        {
                            sel = ElementSelection.GrowSelection(pb, selectedFaces, angleGrow ? growSelectionAngle : -1f);
                            sel.UnionWith(selectedFaces);
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            sel = ElementSelection.FloodSelection(pb, selectedFaces, angleGrow ? growSelectionAngle : -1f);
                        }

                        pb.SetSelectedFaces(sel.ToArray());

                        break;
                }

                grown += pb.selectedVertexCount - previousTriCount;
            }

            ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();
            SceneView.RepaintAll();

            if (grown > 0)
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Success, "Grow Selection");

            return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Failure, "Nothing to Grow");
        }
```

```csharp
        }

        public override bool enabled
        {
            get { return base.enabled && VerifyShrinkSelection(); }
        }

        protected override ActionResult PerformActionImplementation()
        {
            var selection = MeshSelection.topInternal;
            var selectionCount = MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount;

            UndoUtility.RecordSelection("Shrink Selection");

            // find perimeter edges
            int rc = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < selectionCount; i++)
            {
                ProBuilderMesh mesh = selection[i];

                switch (ProBuilderEditor.selectMode)
                {
                    case SelectMode.Edge:
                    {
                        int[] perimeter = ElementSelection.GetPerimeterEdges(mesh, mesh.selectedEdges);
                        mesh.SetSelectedEdges(mesh.selectedEdges.RemoveAt(perimeter));
                        rc += perimeter != null ? perimeter.Length : 0;
                        break;
                    }

                    case SelectMode.TextureFace:
                    case SelectMode.Face:
                    {
                        Face[] perimeter = ElementSelection.GetPerimeterFaces(mesh, mesh.selectedFacesInternal).ToArray();
                        mesh.SetSelectedFaces(mesh.selectedFacesInternal.Except(perimeter).ToArray());
                        rc += perimeter.Length;
                        break;
                    }

                    case SelectMode.Vertex:
                    {
                        var universalEdges = mesh.GetSharedVertexHandleEdges(mesh.facesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.edges)).ToArray();
                        int[] perimeter = ElementSelection.GetPerimeterVertices(mesh, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal, universalEdges);
                        mesh.SetSelectedVertices(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal.RemoveAt(perimeter));
                        rc += perimeter != null ? perimeter.Length : 0;
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }

            ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();

            if (rc > 0)
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Success, "Shrink Selection");

            return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Canceled, "Nothing to Shrink");
        }
```

# Editor Tools

## F01: ProBuilder Move/Rotate/Scale tools

### MOVE TOOL

The `ProbuilderMoveTool` class inherits from `PositionTool` (which derives from `VertexManipulationTool : EditorTool`) and is decorated with `[EditorTool("ProBuilder Move Tool", typeof(ProBuilderMesh), typeof(PositionToolContext))]`. It applies translation transformations to selected vertices, edges, or faces across one or more `ProBuilderMesh` components.

1. State Fields and Constants:
- `k_CardinalAxisError = .001f`: Tolerance threshold for identifying movement aligned with a single cardinal axis.
- `k_MinTranslateDeltaSqrMagnitude = .0001f`: Minimum squared delta required before starting an edit session.
- `m_Position` (`Vector3`): Current handle position in world space.
- `m_RawHandleDelta` (`Vector3`): Translation delta computed as `m_Position - handlePositionOrigin`.
- `m_ActiveAxesModel` (`Vector3Mask`): Tracks active translation axes in local model coordinate space.
- `m_ActiveAxesWorld` (`Vector3Mask`): Tracks active translation axes in world coordinate space.
- `m_SnapAsGroup` (`bool`): Initialized in `OnToolEngaged()` from `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World && EditorSnapping.snapAsGroup`.

2. Tool Engagement and GUI Pipeline (`OnToolEngaged` & `DoToolGUI`):
- `OnToolEngaged()`: Initializes `m_ActiveAxesModel` to `Vector3Mask.XYZ` if `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World && !snapAxisConstraint`, otherwise `new Vector3Mask(0x0)`. Caches `m_SnapAsGroup`.
- `DoToolGUI()`: When `!isEditing`, initializes `m_Position = m_HandlePosition` where `m_HandlePosition` is retrieved from `MeshSelection.GetHandlePosition()`.
- Renders the position handle in SceneView using `m_Position = Handles.PositionHandle(m_Position, m_HandleRotation)`.
- Computes `m_RawHandleDelta = m_Position - handlePositionOrigin`.
- On handle interaction (`EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()`):
  - Checks if `delta.sqrMagnitude > k_MinTranslateDeltaSqrMagnitude * HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_Position) || isEditing`.
  - Calls `BeginEdit("Translate Selection")` on the first movement frame.
  - If `Tools.vertexDragging` is active (holding the 'V' vertex snap key):
    - Finds nearest scene vertex via `HandleUtility.FindNearestVertex(currentEvent.mousePosition, null, null, out nearest)`.
    - Transforms delta to local space: `unrotated = handleRotationOriginInverse * delta`.
    - Evaluates cardinal alignment `dir = new Vector3Mask(unrotated, k_CardinalAxisError)`.
    - If single active axis (`dir.active == 1`), projects `nearest` point onto the cardinal ray line using `HandleUtility.ProjectPointLine(nearest, handlePositionOrigin + rotationDirection, handlePositionOrigin - rotationDirection)`.
    - If not constrained to 1 axis, sets `m_Position = nearest`.
    - Recomputes `delta = m_Position - handlePositionOrigin`.
  - Else if `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World`:
    - If `snapAxisConstraint` is active (`EditorSnapping.snapMethod == SnapAxis.ActiveAxis`):
      - Accumulates `m_ActiveAxesModel |= new Vector3Mask(handleRotationOriginInverse * delta, k_CardinalAxisError)`.
      - Converts to world space: `m_ActiveAxesWorld = new Vector3Mask(m_HandleRotation * m_ActiveAxesModel)`.
      - If `m_ActiveAxesWorld.active == 1`, calculates `m_Position = ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay(new Ray(handlePositionOrigin, delta), delta.magnitude, GetSnapValueForAxis(m_ActiveAxesModel), m_ActiveAxesWorld)`.
      - If multiple axes, calls `m_Position = ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(m_Position, snapValue)`.
    - Else (all axes snap): `m_Position = ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(m_Position, snapValue)`.
    - Recomputes `delta = m_Position - handlePositionOrigin`.
  - Calls `ApplyTranslation(handleRotationOriginInverse * delta)`.
- When `showHandleInfo && isEditing`, renders HUD info via `DrawDeltaInfo(string.Format("Translate: <b>{0:F2}</b>  {1}", delta.magnitude, (handleRotationOriginInverse * delta).ToString("0.00")))`.

3. Vertex Translation Algorithm (`ApplyTranslation`):
- Iterates through each `MeshAndPositions` entry in `elementSelection`.
- Retrieves `origins = kvp.positions` (pre-transformation vertex coordinates in world space cached at the start of the edit) and `positions = mesh.positionsInternal`.
- For each `ElementGroup` in `kvp.elementGroups`:
  - Retrieves `postApplyMatrix = GetPostApplyMatrix(group)` and computes `preApplyMatrix = postApplyMatrix.inverse`.
  - For each vertex `index` in `group.indices`:
    - If `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World && !m_SnapAsGroup` (individual vertex grid snapping):
      - If `snapAxisConstraint && m_ActiveAxesWorld.active == 1`:
        - Evaluates world vertex point `wp = postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index]))`.
        - Computes snapped position `snap = ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay(new Ray(wp, m_RawHandleDelta), translationMagnitude, GetSnapValueForAxis(m_ActiveAxesWorld), m_ActiveAxesWorld)`.
        - Assigns `positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(snap)`.
      - Else:
        - Computes `wp = postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(translation + preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index]))`.
        - Computes `snap = ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(wp, snapValue)`.
        - Assigns `positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(snap)`.
    - Else (group translation):
      - Assigns `positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(translation + preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index])))`.
- Applies updated positions to the underlying Unity mesh `mesh.mesh.vertices = positions`.
- Recomputes UVs for modified faces via `mesh.RefreshUV(MeshSelection.selectedFacesInEditZone[mesh])`.
- Recomputes vertex normals via `mesh.Refresh(RefreshMask.Normals)`.
- Triggers editor repaint via `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh(false)`.

4. Coordinate Space and Gizmo Orientation:
- Coordinate spaces are configured via `VertexManipulationTool.handleOrientation`:
  - `HandleOrientation.World`: Gizmo orientation is `Quaternion.identity`.
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`: Gizmo orientation matches `active.mesh.transform.rotation`.
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`: Gizmo orientation matches `active.elementGroups.Last().rotation`, which reflects the active face normal and tangent, active edge direction, or active vertex normal.

### ROTATE TOOL

The `ProbuilderRotateTool` class inherits from `PositionTool` and is registered with `[EditorTool("ProBuilder Rotation Tool", typeof(ProBuilderMesh), typeof(PositionToolContext))]`. It applies 3D rotational deltas to selected elements.

1. Tool GUI Cycle (`DoToolGUI`):
- When `showHandleInfo && isEditing` is true, extracts `euler = m_Rotation.eulerAngles` and displays degrees formatted via `DrawDeltaInfo(string.Format("Rotate: {0,5:##0.00}, {1,5:##0.00}, {2,5:##0.00}", euler.x, euler.y, euler.z))`.
- When `!isEditing`, resets `m_Rotation = Quaternion.identity`.
- Preserves previous handle matrix: `hm = Handles.matrix`.
- Sets current handle matrix: `Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one)`.
- Draws rotation gizmo at origin: `m_Rotation = Handles.RotationHandle(m_Rotation, Vector3.zero)`.
- Restores `Handles.matrix = hm`.
- If `EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()` detects interaction:
  - Calls `BeginEdit("Rotate Selection")` on the first frame of rotation.
  - Invokes `ApplyRotation(m_Rotation)`.

2. Rotation Pivot Calculation (`GetPostApplyMatrix`):
The transformation matrix for an `ElementGroup` is determined by `VertexManipulationTool.pivotPoint`:
- `PivotPoint.Center`: `GetPostApplyMatrix(group)` returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(handlePositionOrigin, handleRotationOrigin, Vector3.one)`. The rotation pivot is the bounding box center of all selected elements (`MeshSelection.bounds.center`). All selected vertices rotate as a single grouped cluster.
- `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`: `GetPostApplyMatrix(group)` returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(handlePositionOrigin, handleRotationOrigin, Vector3.one)`. The rotation pivot is the world position of the active element group (`active.elementGroups.Last().position`). All elements rotate together around this active pivot.
- `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins`: `GetPostApplyMatrix(group)` returns `Matrix4x4.TRS(group.position, group.rotation, Vector3.one)`. Each `ElementGroup` (individual face, edge group, or vertex cluster) uses its own local position `group.position` and local orientation `group.rotation` as the rotation pivot and coordinate axes. Selected elements rotate independently around their respective individual centers.

3. Vertex Rotation Algorithm (`ApplyRotation`):
- Iterates through each `MeshAndPositions` in `elementSelection`.
- Retrieves `origins = kvp.positions` (world space vertex positions at edit start) and `positions = mesh.positionsInternal`.
- For each `ElementGroup` in `kvp.elementGroups`:
  - `postApplyMatrix = GetPostApplyMatrix(group)`
  - `preApplyMatrix = postApplyMatrix.inverse`
  - Transforms each vertex: `positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(rotation * preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index])))`.
- Updates Unity mesh vertices: `mesh.mesh.vertices = positions`.
- Recomputes UVs: `mesh.RefreshUV(MeshSelection.selectedFacesInEditZone[mesh])`.
- Recomputes normals: `mesh.Refresh(RefreshMask.Normals)`.
- Refreshes editor: `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh(false)`.

4. Rotation Handle Appearance per Element Type:
- `SelectMode.Vertex`: Handle is placed at the vertex coordinate or centroid of selected vertices. Orientation aligns with global axes (`World`), mesh transform (`ActiveObject`), or vertex normal (`ActiveElement`).
- `SelectMode.Edge`: Handle is placed at the midpoint of the selected edge. In `ActiveElement`, one axis aligns along the edge vector while another aligns with the shared face normal.
- `SelectMode.Face`: Handle is placed at the face center. In `ActiveElement`, the primary axis aligns with the face normal vector and secondary axes align with the face tangent and bitangent.

### SCALE TOOL

The `ProbuilderScaleTool` class inherits from `PositionTool` and is registered with `[EditorTool("ProBuilder Scale Tool", typeof(ProBuilderMesh), typeof(PositionToolContext))]`. It applies 3D scaling transformations to sub-mesh elements.

1. Tool GUI Cycle (`DoToolGUI`):
- When `showHandleInfo && isEditing` is true, displays the scale readout via `DrawDeltaInfo("Scale: " + m_Scale.ToString("0.00"))`.
- When `!isEditing`, resets `m_Scale = Vector3.one`.
- Obtains handle screen size via `size = HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_HandlePosition)`.
- Saves matrix stack `EditorHandleUtility.PushMatrix()`, sets `Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one)`.
- Invokes Unity scale gizmo: `m_Scale = Handles.ScaleHandle(m_Scale, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity, size)`.
- Restores matrix stack `EditorHandleUtility.PopMatrix()`.
- When `EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()` detects interaction:
  - Calls `BeginEdit("Scale Selection")` on the initial interaction frame.
  - Passes the scale matrix to `PositionTool.Apply(Matrix4x4.Scale(m_Scale))`.

2. Scale Pivot, Coordinate Axes, and Sub-Mesh Element Scaling (`PositionTool.Apply`):
- Method `PositionTool.Apply(Matrix4x4 delta)` performs the transformation pipeline:
  `positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(delta.MultiplyPoint3x4(preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index]))))`
- Behavior across Pivot Modes:
  - In `PivotPoint.Center`: `postApplyMatrix` is `Matrix4x4.TRS(handlePositionOrigin, handleRotationOrigin, Vector3.one)`. Elements scale along the gizmo orientation axes relative to the collective selection centroid.
  - In `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`: Elements scale along the active element's orientation relative to the active element's center.
  - In `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins`: `postApplyMatrix` is `Matrix4x4.TRS(group.position, group.rotation, Vector3.one)`. The `preApplyMatrix` transforms vertex world positions into each element group's local coordinate frame centered at `group.position`. `Matrix4x4.Scale(m_Scale)` then scales the vertices relative to `Vector3.zero` (the group's centroid). `postApplyMatrix` transforms vertices back to world coordinates. As a result, sub-mesh elements (such as multiple separate selected faces) scale inward or outward around their own individual centers rather than collapsing toward the mesh center.

3. Uniform vs Non-Uniform Scaling:
- Unity's `Handles.ScaleHandle` provides 3 single-axis handles (X, Y, Z), 3 planar dual-axis handles (XY, XZ, YZ), and 1 central uniform scaling cube.
- Non-uniform scaling modifies individual components of `m_Scale` (e.g., `Vector3(2.0, 1.0, 1.0)`). The scale is applied along the local axes defined by `m_HandleRotation` (or `group.rotation` in `IndividualOrigins`).
- Uniform scaling modifies all three axes simultaneously by the same factor (`m_Scale.x == m_Scale.y == m_Scale.z`), preserving element aspect ratios.

> **Godot Note:** Godot implements sub-element scaling by transforming local vertex positions: `v' = center + basis * (scale_vec * (basis.inverse() * (v - center)))`. In IndividualOrigins mode, `center` is each face centroid and `basis` is the face tangent-normal orientation.

### SHIFT+MOVE/SCALE

ProBuilder integrates an automatic extrusion and inset shortcut into transformation tools via the Shift modifier key.

1. Exact Trigger and State Tracking:
- In `VertexManipulationTool.cs`, editing state is tracked by the private field `m_IsEditing`.
- When a handle is dragged, `EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()` detects the change and invokes `BeginEdit(undoMessage)` on the first frame where movement exceeds `k_MinTranslateDeltaSqrMagnitude`.
- Inside `BeginEdit()`:
  - Checks `if (m_IsEditing) return;`.
  - Registers complete object undo for selected meshes: `UndoUtility.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(selection, undoMessage)`.
  - Dispatches `beforeMeshModification(selection)`.
  - Evaluates Shift modifier: `if (currentEvent.shift) Extrude();`.
  - Sets `m_IsEditing = true`.
- **Crucial Trigger Rule**: The extrusion is triggered ONLY if Shift is held down at the exact instant the drag operation begins (when `BeginEdit` executes on the initial drag frame). Once `m_IsEditing` is set to `true`, pressing, toggling, or releasing Shift during the remainder of the drag has no effect because subsequent frames skip `BeginEdit()`.
- When the mouse button is released (`EventType.MouseUp` or `EventType.Ignore`), `FinishEdit()` resets `m_IsEditing = false`.

2. Extrusion Algorithm (`VertexManipulationTool.Extrude`):
- Uses constant offset `const float epsilon = .00001f` to prevent newly created faces from collapsing into degenerate zero-area triangles during initial mesh validation.
- Evaluates current `ProBuilderEditor.selectMode`:
  - `SelectMode.Face` / `SelectMode.TextureFace`:
    - Checks `mesh.selectedFacesInternal.Length > 0`.
    - Calls `mesh.Extrude(mesh.selectedFacesInternal, s_ExtrudeMethod, epsilon)` where `s_ExtrudeMethod` defaults to `ExtrudeMethod.FaceNormal`.
    - Updates selection to the newly created extruded faces: `mesh.SetSelectedFaces(mesh.selectedFacesInternal)`.
  - `SelectMode.Edge` / `SelectMode.TextureEdge`:
    - If `mesh.selectedFaceCount == 0`, calls `mesh.Extrude(mesh.selectedEdges, epsilon, s_ExtrudeEdgesAsGroup, ProBuilderEditor.s_AllowNonManifoldActions)` where `s_ExtrudeEdgesAsGroup` defaults to `true`.
    - Updates selection to the newly created extruded edges: `mesh.SetSelectedEdges(newEdges)`.
- Executes `mesh.ToMesh()` and `mesh.Refresh()` to update mesh geometry.
- Displays SceneView notification: `EditorUtility.ShowNotification("Extrude")`.
- Calls `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

3. Extrude-on-Move vs Inset-on-Scale:
- **Shift + Move**: `BeginEdit("Translate Selection")` triggers `Extrude()`, generating new faces separated by `epsilon`. As the user continues dragging the move handle, `ApplyTranslation` pulls the newly extruded faces along the translation delta, forming an extended 3D extrusion.
- **Shift + Scale**: `BeginEdit("Scale Selection")` triggers `Extrude()`, creating zero-thickness extruded faces. As the user drags the scale handle inward in `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins` (or `PivotPoint.Center`), `PositionTool.Apply(Matrix4x4.Scale(m_Scale))` shrinks the new faces inward toward their centroids, forming a face Inset.

### VERTEX MANIPULATION TOOL BASE

The `VertexManipulationTool` class is the abstract base class extending Unity's `EditorTool`. It coordinates selection state, undo registration, Unity toolbar synchronization, and the mesh rebuild lifecycle across all element transformation tools.

1. Settings and Toolbar Synchronization:
- `s_HandleOrientation` (`Pref<HandleOrientation>("editor.handleOrientation", HandleOrientation.World)`): Tracks gizmo rotation mode.
- `s_PivotPoint` (`Pref<PivotPoint>("editor.pivotPoint", PivotPoint.Center)`): Tracks gizmo position mode.
- `s_PivotModePivotEquivalent` (`Pref<PivotPoint>("editor.pivotModePivotEquivalent", PivotPoint.ActiveElement)`): Configures which ProBuilder pivot point corresponds to Unity's `PivotMode.Pivot` toolbar button.
- `s_ShowHandleSettingsInScene` (`Pref<bool>("developer.showHandleSettingsInScene", false)`): Enables scene view dropdown overlays.
- Synchronization in static constructor:
  - `Tools.pivotRotationChanged += SyncPivotRotation`
  - `Tools.pivotModeChanged += SyncPivotPoint`
  - Maps Unity `Tools.pivotMode == PivotMode.Pivot` to `pivotModePivotEquivalent` (defaults to `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`), and `PivotMode.Center` to `PivotPoint.Center`.
  - Maps Unity `Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Local` to `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, and `PivotRotation.Global` to `HandleOrientation.World`.
  - Supports ProBuilder-specific `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement` without altering Unity's global toolbar state.
  - Changing `handleOrientation` programmatically triggers `MeshSelection.InvalidateCaches()`, `pivotRotationChanged`, toolbar repaint via `UnityEditor.Toolbar.RepaintToolbar`, and `handleOrientationChanged`.

2. Undo Registration and Lightmapping:
- In `BeginEdit(string undoMessage)`:
  - Calls `Lightmapping.PushGIWorkflowMode()` to pause background lightmap baking.
  - Invokes `UndoUtility.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(selection, undoMessage)` (default message `"Modify Vertices"`).
  - Invokes `beforeMeshModification(selection)` action event.
  - Rebuilds base meshes with `mesh.ToMesh()` and `mesh.Refresh()`.

3. Mesh Refresh Pipeline (During Drag vs On Release):
- **During Drag (Per-Frame Interaction)**:
  - High-performance, low-latency pathway.
  - Updates vertex positions directly in `positionsInternal` and assigns `mesh.mesh.vertices = positions`.
  - Refreshes UV coordinates only for faces in the active edit zone: `mesh.RefreshUV(MeshSelection.selectedFacesInEditZone[mesh])`.
  - Recomputes vertex normals: `mesh.Refresh(RefreshMask.Normals)`.
  - Calls lightweight `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh(false)` without recreating submeshes or regenerating colliders.
- **On Release (`FinishEdit`)**:
  - Invokes `Lightmapping.PopGIWorkflowMode()`.
  - Calls `OnToolDisengaged()`.
  - For every modified mesh in `selection`:
    - `mesh.ToMesh()`: Reconstructs submesh index buffers and triangle topology.
    - `mesh.Refresh()`: Full refresh of normals, tangents, vertex colors, UVs, and mesh bounds.
    - `mesh.Optimize()`: Welds shared vertex attributes, removes unused vertices, and updates mesh collider physics.
  - Calls `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh(false)`.
  - Invokes `afterMeshModification(selection)` action event.
  - Resets `m_IsEditing = false`.

<details><summary>Source Evidence</summary>

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/VertexManipulationTool.cs:51-83**

```csharp
        /// <remarks>
        /// Relates to the UnityEditor.PivotMode enum, with additional options.
        /// </remarks>
        public static PivotPoint pivotPoint
        {
            get
            {
                SyncPivotPoint();

                return Tools.pivotMode == PivotMode.Pivot
                    ? pivotModePivotEquivalent
                    : PivotPoint.Center;
            }
        }

        static void SyncPivotPoint()
        {
```

### SNAPPING DURING TRANSFORM

ProBuilder provides transform snapping through integration with ProGrids and Unity EditorSnap settings via `EditorSnapping.cs`.

1. Snapping Modes and Priority (`EditorSnapping.snapMode`):
- Evaluates snapping hierarchy:
  1. If `EditorSnapSettings.incrementalSnapActive` is true -> `SnapMode.Relative`
  2. If `ProGridsInterface.SnapEnabled()` is true or (`EditorSnapSettings.gridSnapActive && Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Global`) -> `SnapMode.World`
  3. Otherwise -> `SnapMode.None`
- `VertexManipulationTool.gridSnapEnabled` returns `Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Global`.

2. Active Snap Values:
- Move snapping (`activeMoveSnapValue`):
  - `SnapMode.Relative`: returns `EditorSnapSettings.move` (`incrementalSnapMoveValue`).
  - `SnapMode.World`: returns `ProGridsInterface.SnapValue() * Vector3.one` (if ProGrids active) or `GridSettings.size` (`worldSnapMoveValue`).
  - `SnapMode.None`: returns `Vector3.zero`.
- Rotate snapping (`activeRotateSnapValue`):
  - `SnapMode.Relative` or `SnapMode.World`: returns `EditorSnapSettings.rotate` (`incrementalSnapRotateValue` in degrees).
  - `SnapMode.None`: returns `0f`.
- Scale snapping (`activeScaleSnapValue`):
  - `SnapMode.Relative` or `SnapMode.World`: returns `Vector3.one * EditorSnapSettings.scale` (`incrementalSnapScaleValue`).
  - `SnapMode.None`: returns `Vector3.zero`.

3. Move Tool Snapping Pipeline (`ProbuilderMoveTool.cs`):
- Axis snapping constraint (`snapAxisConstraint = EditorSnapping.snapMethod == SnapAxis.ActiveAxis`):
  - When moving a gizmo axis, calculates local mask `m_ActiveAxesModel |= new Vector3Mask(handleRotationOriginInverse * delta, k_CardinalAxisError)`.
  - Calculates world mask `m_ActiveAxesWorld = new Vector3Mask(m_HandleRotation * m_ActiveAxesModel)`.
  - Single active axis (`m_ActiveAxesWorld.active == 1`): Snaps position along the ray using `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay(new Ray(handlePositionOrigin, delta), delta.magnitude, GetSnapValueForAxis(m_ActiveAxesModel), m_ActiveAxesWorld)`.
  - Multi-axis or unconstrained: Snaps all coordinates using `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(m_Position, snapValue)`.
- Group Snapping vs Individual Vertex Snapping (`m_SnapAsGroup` / `EditorSnapping.snapAsGroup`):
  - When `m_SnapAsGroup` is `true`: The handle position snaps to the grid; all selected vertices move together, maintaining their relative offsets.
  - When `m_SnapAsGroup` is `false` (in `SnapMode.World`): Each vertex in the selection snaps independently to the nearest grid coordinate in world space (`positions[index] = worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(snap)`).
- Vertex Dragging / Hotkey Snapping (`Tools.vertexDragging`):
  - When holding the 'V' key, `HandleUtility.FindNearestVertex` finds the nearest scene vertex.
  - If dragging along a single cardinal axis (`dir.active == 1`), projects `nearest` onto the cardinal ray line via `HandleUtility.ProjectPointLine`.
  - If unconstrained, sets handle position directly to `nearest`.

### TOOL SETTINGS

ProBuilder transformation tools expose configuration options across toolbar overlays, scene view HUD panels, and user preferences.

1. Scene View Overlay Toolbar Elements (`PositionToolEditor` in `PositionTool.cs`):
- `PositionToolEditor : Editor, ICreateToolbar` defines overlay elements via `toolbarElements`:
  - `"Tool Settings/Pivot Mode"`: Toggles between selection bounding center (`PivotMode.Center`) and active element pivot (`PivotMode.Pivot` / `pivotModePivotEquivalent`).
  - `"ProBuilder Settings/Handle Orientation"`: Selects coordinate space orientation (`HandleOrientation.World`, `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`).
  - `"ProBuilder Settings/Select Mode"`: Switches element selection mode (`SelectMode.Vertex`, `SelectMode.Edge`, `SelectMode.Face`, `SelectMode.Object`).
  - `"ProBuilder Settings/Select Back Faces"`: Toggles selection of hidden/occluded back-facing geometry.
  - `"ProBuilder Settings/Drag Rect Mode"`: Sets box selection intersection behavior (`RectSelectMode.Partial` vs `RectSelectMode.Complete`).

2. Scene View Developer Mode HUD (`VertexManipulationToolSettings.cs`):
- In developer mode (when `VertexManipulationTool.showHandleSettingsInScene` / `"developer.showHandleSettingsInScene"` is enabled), `SceneView.duringSceneGui` renders an interactive panel at `Rect(8, view.position.height - 40, 400f, 48f)`:
  - `Pivot Point`: Enum dropdown for `PivotPoint.Center`, `PivotPoint.ActiveElement`, `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins`.
  - `Orientation`: Enum dropdown for `HandleOrientation.World`, `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`.
  - Modifications trigger `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

3. Delta Info HUD Display (`PositionTool.DrawDeltaInfo`):
- Controlled by user preference `s_ShowHandleInfo` (`Pref<bool>("editor.showHandleDelta", false, SettingsScope.User)`).
- Renders a floating text box in the bottom-right corner of Scene View using `UI.EditorStyles.sceneTextBox`:
  - Move Tool: `Translate: <b>{delta.magnitude:F2}</b> {unrotated_delta:0.00}`
  - Rotate Tool: `Rotate: {euler.x,5:##0.00}, {euler.y,5:##0.00}, {euler.z,5:##0.00}`
  - Scale Tool: `Scale: {scale_vector:0.00}`

4. Extrusion and Snapping Preferences:
- `s_ExtrudeEdgesAsGroup` (`Pref<bool>("editor.extrudeEdgesAsGroup", true)`): Controls whether adjacent selected edges extrude as a unified group or separate edges.
- `s_ExtrudeMethod` (`Pref<ExtrudeMethod>("editor.extrudeMethod", ExtrudeMethod.FaceNormal)`): Sets face extrusion direction (`ExtrudeMethod.FaceNormal`, `ExtrudeMethod.VertexNormal`, `ExtrudeMethod.IndividualFaces`).
- `s_SnapAsGroup` (`Pref<bool>("ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAsGroup", true)`): Determines whether elements maintain relative spacing or snap independently.
- `s_SnapAxis` (`Pref<SnapAxis>("ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAxis", SnapAxis.ActiveAxis)`): Constrains snapping to the active gizmo axis or all axes.

## F02: Cut tool

### POINT PLACEMENT

Point placement in `CutTool` (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.CutTool`) coordinates mouse interactions, raycasting, geometric snapping to vertices and edges, path validation, and point modification.

1. Raycasting and Surface Hit Detection:
- During `OnToolGUI(EditorWindow window)`, the method `DoPointPlacement(window)` executes every frame.
- Surface picking is evaluated by `UpdateHitPosition()`: it transforms the GUI mouse coordinate into a 3D ray using `UHandleUtility.GUIPointToWorldRay(evt.mousePosition)` and tests against the target mesh via `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.HandleUtility.FaceRaycast(ray, m_Mesh, out pbHit)`.
- If a face is hit, `UpdateCurrentPosition(Face face, Vector3 position, Vector3 normal)` sets `m_CurrentFace = face`, `m_CurrentPosition = position`, `m_CurrentPositionNormal = normal`, and initializes `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.None`.

2. Snapping to Existing Cut Points (`CheckPointInCutPath`):
- Snapping to the start point (loop closure): If `!m_ModifyingPoint && m_CutPath.Count > 1`, proximity to `m_CutPath[0].position` is tested with a fixed threshold of `0.1f` using `Math.Approx3(vertexData.position, m_CurrentPosition, 0.1f)`. When matched, `m_CurrentPosition` snaps to `vertexData.position`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes` is assigned `vertexData.types | VertexTypes.VertexInShape`, and `m_SelectedIndex = 0`.
- Snapping to arbitrary cut points: When `m_SnappingPoint` (active if `m_SnapToGeometry` is enabled or Ctrl is held: `(evt.modifiers & EventModifiers.Control) != 0`) or `m_ModifyingPoint` (active if Shift is held: `evt.shift`) is true, the tool searches all vertices in `m_CutPath` within `m_SnappingDistance` (default `0.1f`, key `VertexInsertion.snappingDistance`). The closest vertex index is stored in `m_SelectedIndex`, its types are bitwise-ORed with `VertexTypes.VertexInShape`, and `m_CurrentPosition` snaps to the vertex position (if not modifying).

3. Snapping to Mesh Vertices and Edges (`CheckPointInMesh`):
- Invoked when `m_CurrentVertexTypes == VertexTypes.None && !m_ModifyingPoint`. Defaults `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.NewVertex`.
- Boundary edges of the current/target face are retrieved in loop order using `WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency`.
- Vertex snapping: Compares `m_CurrentPosition` against edge start vertices `vertices[peripheralEdges[i].a].position` using `Math.Approx3` with distance threshold `m_SnappingDistance` (or `0.01f` when `m_TargetFace == null && !m_SnappingPoint`). When cursor hovers outside the target face (`m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`), vertex proximity `vertexDist` takes strict precedence over edge proximity `edgeDist` whenever `vertexDist <= bestDistance`.
- When a vertex snap is detected: `m_CurrentPosition = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.ExistingVertex`, `m_SelectedIndex = -1`, `m_SnapedVertexId = peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a`, followed by a call to `CheckPointInCutPath()`.
- Edge snapping: When no vertex snap matches but an edge is within `bestDistance`, the point is orthogonally projected:
  - If `m_TargetFace == null || m_TargetFace == m_CurrentFace`, projection along segment `[left, right]` is computed as:
    `float x = (m_CurrentPosition - left).magnitude;`
    `float y = (m_CurrentPosition - right).magnitude;`
    `m_CurrentPosition = left + (x / (x + y)) * (right - left);`
  - If `m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`, the hit is projected onto the infinite line of the target face peripheral edge:
    `Vector3 a = m_CurrentPosition - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
    `Vector3 b = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].b].position - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
    `float angle = Vector3.Angle(b, a);`
    `m_CurrentPosition = Vector3.Magnitude(a) * Mathf.Cos(angle * Mathf.Deg2Rad) * b / Vector3.Magnitude(b) + vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  - Sets `m_SnapedEdge = peripheralEdges[bestIndex]`, `m_CurrentVertexTypes = VertexTypes.AddedOnEdge`, and `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.

4. Point Addition and Path Construction:
- `CanAppendCurrentPointToPath()` verifies: (a) `Math.IsNumber(m_CurrentPosition)` is true; (b) `polyCount == 0 || m_SelectedIndex != polyCount - 1` (cannot click same vertex twice consecutively); (c) no intermediate point duplicates: `for (int i = 1; i < polyCount; i++) if (Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[i].position, m_CurrentPosition)) return false;`; (d) loop completion is permitted only when `polyCount >= 3`.
- `AddCurrentPositionToPath(bool optimize = true)`: Registers undo `UndoUtility.RecordObject(this, "Add Vertex On Path")`. If `m_TargetFace == null`, binds `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace` and caches `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges`. Appends `new CutVertexData(m_CurrentPosition, m_CurrentPositionNormal, m_CurrentVertexTypes)` to `m_CutPath`, sets `m_PlacingPoint = true`, `m_SelectedIndex = m_CutPath.Count - 1`, and calls `RebuildCutShape(optimize)`.

5. Point Modification / Dragging:
- When Shift is held (`m_ModifyingPoint`), left-clicking an existing point sets `m_PlacingPoint = true`.
- On `EventType.MouseDrag`, if `hasHitPosition && m_SelectedIndex >= 0`, updates `m_CutPath[m_SelectedIndex].position = m_CurrentPosition` and flags `m_Dirty = true`.
- On `MouseUp`, `Ignore`, `KeyDown`, or `KeyUp`, resets `m_PlacingPoint = false` and `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.

```csharp
        bool CanAppendCurrentPointToPath()
        {
            int polyCount = m_CutPath.Count;

            if (!Math.IsNumber(m_CurrentPosition))
                return false;

            if (!(polyCount == 0 || m_SelectedIndex != polyCount - 1))
                return false;

            // duplicate points are not permitted, except the special case where placing a final point on the starting
            // point finishes the cut operation.
            for(int i = 1; i < polyCount; i++)
                if (Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[i].position, m_CurrentPosition))
                    return false;

            // when the existing vertex count is less than 3, don't allow the special duplicate first vertex position
            return polyCount < 2 || !(polyCount < 3 && Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[0].position, m_CurrentPosition));
        }
```

### VISUAL FEEDBACK

The visual feedback system in `CutTool` renders path segments, preview guide lines, mesh connections, vertex handles, face overlays, and contextual cursors.

1. Color Palette and Constants:
- `k_HandleColor`: `new Color(0.8f, 0.8f, 0.8f, 1f)` (light gray default handle color).
- `k_HandleColorAddNewVertex`: `new Color(0.01f, 0.9f, 0.3f, 1f)` (bright green for new vertices on face).
- `s_HandleColorAddVertexOnEdge`: `Handles.selectedColor` (cyan/blue for splitting an existing edge; fallback `new Color(0.3f, 0.01f, 0.9f, 1f)`).
- `s_HandleColorUseExistingVertex`: `Handles.selectedColor` (cyan/blue for snapping to an existing vertex; fallback `new Color(0.01f, 0.5f, 1f, 1f)`).
- `k_HandleColorModifyVertex`: `new Color(1f, 0.75f, 0.0f, 1f)` (amber/orange when Shift-modifying an existing point).
- `k_LineColor`: `new Color(0f, 55f / 255f, 1f, 1f)` (deep blue for valid cut paths).
- `k_InvalidLineColor`: `Color.red` (red for self-intersecting or overlapping cuts).
- `k_ConnectionsLineColor`: `new Color(0f, 200f / 255f, 170f / 200f, 1f)` (teal for connection lines to boundary vertices).
- `k_DrawingLineColor`: `new Color(0.01f, 0.9f, 0.3f, 1f)` (bright green for the active cursor guide line).
- `k_HandleSize`: `0.05f` multiplier applied to `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(point)`.

2. Vertex Dot Rendering:
- `DoExistingPointsGUI()`: Iterates through `m_CutPath`, transforms each position via `trs.TransformPoint(m_CutPath[index].position)`, computes size with `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(point) * k_HandleSize`, and draws a dot handle using `Handles.DotHandleCap(-1, point, Quaternion.identity, size, evt.type)` colored with `k_HandleColor`.
- `DoCurrentPointsGUI()`: Transforms `m_CurrentPosition` (or `m_CutPath[m_SelectedIndex].position` when dragging) to world space and renders a dot cap with `m_CurrentHandleColor`.

3. Polyline and Guide Line Rendering:
- `DrawCutLine()`: Sets `Handles.color` to `m_IsCutValid ? k_LineColor : k_InvalidLineColor`, transforms all points in `m_CutPath` into world coordinates, and calls `Handles.DrawPolyLine`.
- `DrawGuideLine()`: If `m_CutPath.Count > 0` and `!m_ModifyingPoint`, draws a dotted line between `m_CutPath[m_CutPath.Count - 1].position` and `m_CurrentPosition` using `Handles.DrawDottedLine(..., 5f)` with `k_DrawingLineColor`.
- `DrawMeshConnectionsHandles()`: If `m_MeshConnections.Count > 0`, draws dotted lines between each cut vertex `m_CutPath[connection.item1].position` and target boundary vertex `vertices[connection.item2].position` using `Handles.DrawDottedLine(..., 5f)` in `k_ConnectionsLineColor`.

4. Geometry Highlighting (`DoVisualCues`):
- When `m_TargetFace == null && m_CurrentFace != null`, the hovered face is shaded using `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightFaces(m_Mesh, new Face[]{m_CurrentFace}, Color.Lerp(Color.blue, Color.cyan, 0.5f))`.
- Mesh vertices and edges available for snapping are highlighted via `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightVertices(m_Mesh, m_SelectedVertices, false)` and `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightEdges(m_Mesh, m_SelectedEdges, false)`.
- When actively snapped, specific elements are highlighted: `m_SnapedVertexId != -1` highlights the vertex, and `m_SnapedEdge != Edge.Empty` highlights the edge.

5. Mouse Cursor Management:
- `cursorTexture` returns `m_CutCursorTexture` ("Cursors/cutCursor") when `m_CutPath.Count == 0`, and `m_CutAddCursorTexture` ("Cursors/cutCursor-add") when `m_CutPath.Count > 0`.
- Applied in `OnToolGUI` via `Cursor.SetCursor(m_CurrentCutCursor, Vector2.zero, CursorMode.Auto)` and registered with `SceneView.AddCursorRect(sceneViewRect, MouseCursor.CustomCursor)`.

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, 3D viewport handles and lines can be rendered using `ImmediateMesh` with unshaded vertex colors or using `RenderingServer` 3D line drawing functions (`line_3d`). Dotted lines can be achieved using a custom shader with a stepped `fract(uv.x * dot_count)` alpha discard.

### CUT EXECUTION

Cut execution in `CutTool` transforms the user-defined cut path into concrete topology modifications, splitting `m_TargetFace` into new polygon faces.

1. Completion Triggers:
- Keyboard: Pressing Return, KeypadEnter, or Space (`HandleKeyEvent`) invokes `ExecuteCut()` followed by `ExitTool()`.
- UI Button: Clicking "Complete" in the Cut Settings overlay GUI (`OnOverlayGUI`) calls `ExecuteCut()`.
- Automatic Loop Closure: When the user places a final point onto the starting vertex with `m_CutPath.Count >= 3`, `isALoop` evaluates to `true`. In `RebuildCutShape(optimize: true)`, if `m_IsCutValid` is `true`, `ExecuteCut()` is called automatically.
- Tool Deactivation: `OnWillBeDeactivated()` calls `ExecuteCut(restorePrevious: false)` to commit pending valid cuts.

2. Execution Pipeline in `DoCut()`:
- Validation: Checks `if (m_TargetFace == null || m_CutPath.Count < 2)` (returns `ActionResult.Status.Canceled`) and `if (!m_IsCutValid)` (returns `ActionResult.Status.Failure`).
- Undo Registration: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Execute Cut")`.
- Vertex Snapshot & Insertion:
  - Snapshots initial connection vertices: `formerVertices[i] = meshVertices[m_MeshConnections[i].item2]`.
  - Dispatches vertex insertion via `InsertVertices()`:
    - `VertexTypes.ExistingVertex` / `VertexInShape`: Calls `InsertVertexOnExistingVertex(vertexData.position)` which searches `m_Mesh.GetVertices()` for an approx matching position with valid normal.
    - `VertexTypes.AddedOnEdge`: Calls `InsertVertexOnExistingEdge(vertexData.position)` which identifies the nearest peripheral edge of `m_TargetFace` using `Math.DistancePointLineSegment` and calls `m_Mesh.InsertVertexOnEdge(peripheralEdges[bestIndex], vertexPosition)`.
    - `VertexTypes.NewVertex`: Calls `m_Mesh.InsertVertexInMesh(vertexData.position, vertexData.normal)`.
  - Maps inserted vertex references to mesh indices `cutIndexes = cutVertices.Select(vert => meshVertices.IndexOf(vert)).ToArray()`.
  - Remaps `m_MeshConnections`: `connection.item1` becomes the new mesh index of `cutVertices[connection.item1]`, and `connection.item2` becomes the new mesh index of `formerVertices[i]`.

3. Closed Loop Creation:
- If `isALoop` is true:
  - Creates central face: `Face f = m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(cutIndexes, false)`.
  - Assigns `f.submeshIndex = m_TargetFace.submeshIndex`.
  - Computes normals `Vector3 nrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, f)` and `Vector3 targetNrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, m_TargetFace)`.
  - If `Vector3.Dot(nrm, targetNrm) < 0f`, inverts winding order via `f.Reverse()`.
  - Appends `f` to `newFaces`.

4. Outer/Subdivided Face Computation (`ComputeNewFaces`):
- Obtains continuous peripheral edges of `m_TargetFace` using `WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency(face)`.
- Maps edge vertex indices to shared universal indices via `m_Mesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
- Identifies `startIndex`: the first edge whose `.a` vertex matches a cut vertex shared index or a mesh connection endpoint.
- Traverses the peripheral edge loop from `startIndex` to `peripheralEdgesUnique.Count + startIndex`:
  - Appends `peripheralEdges[i % peripheralEdgesUnique.Count].a` to `polygon`.
  - When a cut vertex or connection endpoint is reached:
    - If a connection endpoint, appends `connection.item1` to `polygon`.
    - If `polygon.Count != 2`, invokes `ComputeFaceClosure(polygon, index, cutVertexSharedIndexes, out toDelete)`.
    - Assigns `newFace.submeshIndex = m_TargetFace.submeshIndex`, records `newFace` in `newFaces`, and aggregates `facesToDelete`.
    - Starts a new polygon list starting with the current peripheral edge vertex.
- Deletes temporary candidate faces: `m_Mesh.DeleteFaces(facesToDelete)`.
- If `!isALoop`, adds computed peripheral faces to `newFaces`.

5. Face Closure Path Resolution (`ComputeFaceClosure`):
- For a given starting peripheral polygon segment `polygonStart`, the algorithm searches both reverse and forward paths along `cutIndexes` starting at `startIndex = cutIndexes.IndexOf(currentIndex)`:
  - Reverse path: steps from `startIndex - 1` down to `finalIndex` (`startIndex - cutIndexes.Count` if loop, else 0), stopping when reaching `polygonFirstVertex` or `connection.item1`.
  - Forward path: steps from `startIndex + 1` up to `finalIndex` (`startIndex + cutIndexes.Count` if loop, else `cutIndexes.Count`), stopping when reaching `polygonFirstVertex` or `connection.item1`.
- For each connected candidate path:
  - Combines candidate path with `polygonStart` and creates a candidate face via `m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(closure, false)`.
  - Calculates polygon area via `Math.PolygonArea(vertices, indexes)`.
  - Selects the candidate face with minimal positive surface area (`area < bestArea`), marking all larger/enclosing candidate faces in `facesToDelete`.

6. Mesh Finalization:
- Collects helper vertex indices created solely for cut routing: `(data.types & VertexTypes.NewVertex) != 0 && (data.types & VertexTypes.VertexInShape) == 0`.
- Deletes temporary helper vertices: `m_Mesh.DeleteVertices(verticesIndexesToDelete)`.
- Deletes original face: `m_Mesh.DeleteFace(m_TargetFace)`.
- Reconstructs and cleans mesh buffers: `m_Mesh.ToMesh(); m_Mesh.Refresh(); m_Mesh.Optimize();`.
- Updates selection: `MeshSelection.ClearElementSelection(); m_Mesh.SetSelectedFaces(newFaces); ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();`.
- Calls `Clear()` to reset tool state.

```csharp
        internal ActionResult DoCut()
        {
            if (m_TargetFace == null || m_CutPath.Count < 2)
            {
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Canceled, L10n.Tr("Not enough elements selected for a cut"));
            }

            if(!m_IsCutValid)
            {
                return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Failure, L10n.Tr("The current cut overlaps itself"));
            }

            UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Execute Cut");

            List<Vertex> meshVertices = new List<Vertex>();
            m_Mesh.GetVerticesInList(meshVertices);
            Vertex[] formerVertices = new Vertex[m_MeshConnections.Count];
            for(int i = 0; i < m_MeshConnections.Count; i++)
            {
                formerVertices[i] = meshVertices[m_MeshConnections[i].item2];
            }

            //Insert cut vertices in the mesh
            List<Vertex> cutVertices = InsertVertices();
            m_Mesh.GetVerticesInList(meshVertices);
            //Retrieve indexes of the cut points in the mesh vertices
            int[] cutIndexes = cutVertices.Select(vert => meshVertices.IndexOf(vert)).ToArray();

            //Update mesh connections with new indexes
            for(int i = 0; i<m_MeshConnections.Count; i++)
            {
                SimpleTuple<int, int> connection = m_MeshConnections[i];
                connection.item1 = meshVertices.IndexOf(cutVertices[connection.item1]);
                connection.item2 = meshVertices.IndexOf(formerVertices[i]);
                m_MeshConnections[i] = connection;
            }

            List<Face> newFaces = new List<Face>();
            // If the cut defines a loop in the face, create the polygon corresponding to that loop
            if (isALoop)
            {
                Face f = m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(cutIndexes, false);
                f.submeshIndex = m_TargetFace.submeshIndex;

                if(f == null)
                    return new ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Failure, L10n.Tr("Cut Shape is not valid"));

                Vector3 nrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, f);
                Vector3 targetNrm = Math.Normal(m_Mesh, m_TargetFace);
                // If the shape is define in the wrong orientation compared to the former face, reverse it
                if(Vector3.Dot(nrm,targetNrm) < 0f)
                    f.Reverse();

                newFaces.Add(f);
            }

            //Compute the rest of the new faces (faces outside of the loop or division of the original face)
            List<Face> faces = ComputeNewFaces(m_TargetFace, cutIndexes);
            if(!isALoop)
                newFaces.AddRange(faces);

            //Remove inserted vertices only if they were inserted for the process
            List<int> verticesIndexesToDelete = new List<int>();
            for(int i = 0; i < m_CutPath.Count; i++)
            {
                if(( m_CutPath[i].types & VertexTypes.NewVertex ) != 0
                && ( m_CutPath[i].types & VertexTypes.VertexInShape ) == 0)
                    verticesIndexesToDelete.Add(cutIndexes[i]);
```

```csharp
        List<Face> ComputeNewFaces(Face face, IList<int> cutVertexIndexes)
        {
            List<Face> newFaces = new List<Face>();

            //Get Vertices from the mesh
            Dictionary<int, int> sharedToUnique = m_Mesh.sharedVertexLookup;
            var cutVertexSharedIndexes = cutVertexIndexes.Select(ind => sharedToUnique[ind]).ToList();

            //Parse peripheral edges to unique id and find a common point between the peripheral edges and the cut
            var peripheralEdges = WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency(face);
            var peripheralEdgesUnique = new List<Edge>();
            int startIndex = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < peripheralEdges.Count; i++)
            {
                Edge eShared = peripheralEdges[i];
                Edge eUnique = new Edge(sharedToUnique[eShared.a], sharedToUnique[eShared.b]);
                peripheralEdgesUnique.Add(eUnique);

                if (startIndex == -1 && ( cutVertexSharedIndexes.Contains(eUnique.a)
                                          || m_MeshConnections.Exists(tup => sharedToUnique[tup.item2] == eUnique.a)))
                    startIndex = i;
            }

            //Create a polygon for each cut reaching the mesh edges
            List<Face> facesToDelete = new List<Face>();
            List<int> polygon = new List<int>();
            for (int i = startIndex; i <= peripheralEdgesUnique.Count + startIndex; i++)
            {
                 polygon.Add(peripheralEdges[i % peripheralEdgesUnique.Count].a);
                 Edge e = peripheralEdgesUnique[i % peripheralEdgesUnique.Count];

                 if(polygon.Count > 1)

                     int index = -1;
                     if(cutVertexSharedIndexes.Contains(e.a)) // get next vertex
                     {
                         index = e.a;
                     }
                     else if(m_MeshConnections.Exists(tup => sharedToUnique[tup.item2] == e.a))

                         SimpleTuple<int, int> connection = m_MeshConnections.Find(tup => sharedToUnique[tup.item2] == e.a);
                         polygon.Add(connection.item1);
```

```csharp
        Face ComputeFaceClosure( List<int> polygonStart, int currentIndex, List<int> cutIndexes, out List<Face> facesToDelete)
        {
            List<Vertex> meshVertices = new List<Vertex>();
            IList<SharedVertex> uniqueIdToVertexIndex = m_Mesh.sharedVertices;
            Dictionary<int, int> sharedToUnique = m_Mesh.sharedVertexLookup;

            int polygonFirstVertex = polygonStart[0];
            int startIndex = cutIndexes.IndexOf(currentIndex);

            SimpleTuple<int,int> connection = m_MeshConnections.Find(tup => sharedToUnique[tup.item2] == sharedToUnique[polygonFirstVertex]);

            List<List<int>> closureCandidates = new List<List<int>>();

            //Go through the cut in reverse direction
            int index;
            int finalIndex = isALoop ?(startIndex - cutIndexes.Count) : 0;
            bool connected = false;
            List<int> candidate = new List<int>();
            for(index = startIndex - 1; index >= finalIndex; index--)
            {
                int vertexIndex = uniqueIdToVertexIndex[cutIndexes[(index + cutIndexes.Count) % cutIndexes.Count]][0];
                candidate.Add(vertexIndex);
                if(sharedToUnique[vertexIndex] == sharedToUnique[polygonFirstVertex] ||
                   sharedToUnique[vertexIndex] == sharedToUnique[connection.item1])
                {
                    connected = true;
                    break;
                }
            }

            //If we find a valid candidate for the connection, add it to the list
            if(connected)
                closureCandidates.Add(candidate);

            //Go through the cut in forward direction
            finalIndex = isALoop ? (startIndex + cutIndexes.Count) : cutIndexes.Count;
            connected = false;
            candidate = new List<int>();
            for(index = startIndex + 1; index < finalIndex; index++)
            {
                int vertexIndex = uniqueIdToVertexIndex[cutIndexes[index % cutIndexes.Count]][0];
                candidate.Add(vertexIndex);
                if(sharedToUnique[vertexIndex] == sharedToUnique[polygonFirstVertex] ||
                   sharedToUnique[vertexIndex] == sharedToUnique[connection.item1])
                {
                    connected = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
```

```csharp
            //Go through the different candidate and keep the best one
            facesToDelete = new List<Face>();
            Face bestFace = null;
            float bestArea = 0f;
            foreach(var closure in closureCandidates)
            {
                closure.AddRange(polygonStart);

                Face face = m_Mesh.CreatePolygon(closure, false);
                m_Mesh.GetVerticesInList(meshVertices);
                uniqueIdToVertexIndex = m_Mesh.sharedVertices;
                sharedToUnique = m_Mesh.sharedVertexLookup;

                if(bestFace != null)
                {
                    Vector3[] vertices = meshVertices.Select(vertex => vertex.position).ToArray();
                    int[] indexes = face.indexesInternal.Select(i => uniqueIdToVertexIndex[sharedToUnique[i]][0]).ToArray();
                    float area = Math.PolygonArea(vertices, indexes);
                    if(area < bestArea)
                    {
                        facesToDelete.Add(bestFace);
                        bestArea = area;
                        bestFace = face;
                    }
                    else
                        facesToDelete.Add(face);
                }
                else
                {
                    bestFace = face;
                    if (face.indexesInternal != null)
                    {
                        Vector3[] vertices = meshVertices.Select(vertex => vertex.position).ToArray();
                        int[] indexes = face.indexesInternal.Select(i => uniqueIdToVertexIndex[sharedToUnique[i]][0]).ToArray();
                        bestArea = Math.PolygonArea(vertices, indexes);
                    }
                }
            }

            return bestFace;
        }
```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, splitting an arbitrary polygon face requires sorting boundary half-edges and calculating polygon area via triangulation (or `Geometry2D.triangulate_polygon` projected onto the face plane). Area comparison guarantees that the smaller valid sub-polygon is preserved without self-overlap.

### UNDO/CANCEL

The `CutTool` integrates with the Unity Undo system and provides keybindings and UI actions to delete points, cancel in-progress cuts, and recover state.

1. Backspace Point Deletion:
- Handled inside `HandleKeyEvent(Event evt)` on `KeyCode.Backspace`.
- If `m_CutPath.Count > 0`:
  - Records undo state on the mesh: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Delete Selected Points")`.
  - Removes the last point in the list: `m_CutPath.RemoveAt(m_CutPath.Count - 1)`.
  - Sets `m_Dirty = true` to trigger `RebuildCutShape()` on the next update.
  - Consumes the event with `evt.Use()`.

2. Escape Key and Cancellation:
- Handled on `KeyCode.Escape` in `HandleKeyEvent` or clicking the "Cancel" button in `OnOverlayGUI`.
- Calls `ExitTool()`, which resets state via `Clear()` and restores the previous active tool via `ToolManager.RestorePreviousTool()`.
- `Clear()` resets `m_Mesh = null`, `m_TargetFace = null`, `m_CurrentFace = null`, `m_PlacingPoint = false`, `m_CurrentCutCursor = null`, `m_CutPath.Clear()`, `m_MeshConnections.Clear()`, `m_SelectedVertices = null`, `m_SelectedEdges = null`, calls `EditorHandleDrawing.ClearHandles()`, and refreshes the ProBuilder window via `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

3. Undo and Redo Callback Integration:
- The tool subscribes to `Undo.undoRedoPerformed += UndoRedoPerformed` in `OnActivated()` and unsubscribes in `OnWillBeDeactivated()`.
- Point additions record the tool instance: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(this, "Add Vertex On Path")` in `AddCurrentPositionToPath`.
- Full cut operations record the mesh instance: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Execute Cut")` in `DoCut`.
- Inside `UndoRedoPerformed()`:
  - If `m_CutPath.Count == 0 && m_Mesh != null`, resets `m_TargetFace = null` and re-extracts `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges` across all mesh faces.
  - Resets `m_SelectedIndex = -1`.
  - Clears `m_MeshConnections.Clear()`.
  - Sets `m_Dirty = true`, forcing recomputation of mesh boundary connections and cut shape validation in `RebuildCutShape()`.

```csharp
        {

                    if (m_CutPath.Count > 0)
                    {
                        UndoUtility.RecordObject(m_Mesh, "Delete Selected Points");
                        m_CutPath.RemoveAt(m_CutPath.Count - 1);
                        m_Dirty = true;
                    }

                    evt.Use();
                    break;
                }

                case KeyCode.Escape:
                    evt.Use();
                    ExitTool();
                    break;

                case KeyCode.KeypadEnter:
                case KeyCode.Return:
                case KeyCode.Space:
                    evt.Use();
                    ExecuteCut();
                    ExitTool();
                    break;
            }
        }
```

### MULTI-FACE CUTS

Analysis of multi-face cut capabilities in `CutTool`:

1. Target Face Restriction:
- The ProBuilder `CutTool` is strictly constrained to a single target face (`m_TargetFace`).
- When the tool starts, `m_TargetFace` is `null`. Placing the first cut point binds `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace` inside `AddCurrentPositionToPath`:
  `m_TargetFace = m_CurrentFace;`
  `var edges = m_TargetFace.edges;`
  `m_SelectedVertices = edges.Select(e => e.a).ToArray();`
  `m_SelectedEdges = edges.ToArray();`

2. Behavior Across Multiple Faces:
- When the user moves the mouse cursor outside `m_TargetFace` onto another face (`m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace`), the tool does not permit extending the cut path onto the adjacent face.
- In `CheckPointInMesh()`, the edge set is forced to the target face's boundary: `if (m_TargetFace != null && m_CurrentFace != m_TargetFace) peripheralEdges = WingedEdge.SortEdgesByAdjacency(m_TargetFace);`.
- The cursor position is projected back onto the nearest peripheral edge ray of `m_TargetFace` using vector dot/cosine math:
  `Vector3 a = m_CurrentPosition - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  `Vector3 b = vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].b].position - vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`
  `float angle = Vector3.Angle(b, a);`
  `m_CurrentPosition = Vector3.Magnitude(a) * Mathf.Cos(angle * Mathf.Deg2Rad) * b / Vector3.Magnitude(b) + vertices[peripheralEdges[bestIndex].a].position;`

3. Topological Isolation:
- In `DoCut()`, face deletion and polygon regeneration are performed exclusively on `m_TargetFace`: `m_Mesh.DeleteFace(m_TargetFace)`.
- No cross-face spanning paths or continuous multi-face cuts are supported within a single operation. To cut multiple adjacent faces, the user must cut and complete each face sequentially in separate operations.

### STATE MACHINE

The `CutTool` lifecycle, menu integration, and state machine track tool activation, event listening, point placement, dragging, and geometric validation.

1. Tool Registration and Menu Action:
- Tool Attribute: `[EditorTool("Cut Tool", typeof(ProBuilderMesh), typeof(PositionToolContext))]`.
- Menu Action: `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.CutToolAction` inheriting from `MenuAction`.
  - Toolbar Group: `ToolbarGroup.Tool`.
  - Shortcut: Alt+Shift+C (`keyCommandAlt, keyCommandShift, 'C'`).
  - Valid Modes: `SelectMode.Vertex | SelectMode.Edge | SelectMode.Face`.
  - Enabled Condition: `MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount == 1`.
  - Execution: Toggles tool via `ToolManager.SetActiveTool<CutTool>()` or `ToolManager.RestorePreviousTool()`, then focuses `SceneView.lastActiveSceneView.Focus()`.

2. Lifecycle Callbacks:
- `IsAvailable()`: Returns `true` when `MeshSelection.selectedObjectCount == 1`.
- `OnEnable()`: Initializes `s_HandleColorUseExistingVertex` and `s_HandleColorAddVertexOnEdge` to `Handles.selectedColor`, loads preferences `VertexInsertion.snapToGeometry` (default false) and `VertexInsertion.snappingDistance` (default 0.1f), and loads cursor textures `Cursors/cutCursor` and `Cursors/cutCursor-add`.
- `OnActivated()`: Sets `m_Mesh = MeshSelection.activeMesh`, clears selection `m_Mesh.ClearSelection()`, extracts `m_SelectedVertices` and `m_SelectedEdges`, and subscribes to events: `Undo.undoRedoPerformed += UndoRedoPerformed`, `MeshSelection.objectSelectionChanged += UpdateTarget`, `ProBuilderEditor.selectModeChanged += OnSelectModeChanged`, and `EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged += OnPlayModeStateChanged`.
- `OnWillBeDeactivated()`: Invokes `ExecuteCut(false)` to finalize any pending cut, and unsubscribes from all events.
- `OnPlayModeStateChanged()`: If exiting edit or play mode, calls `ExitTool()`.
- `OnSelectModeChanged()`: Invokes `ToolManager.RestorePreviousPersistentTool()`.
- `UpdateTarget()`: If `MeshSelection.activeMesh != m_Mesh`, calls `Clear()` and rebinds to the newly active mesh.

3. Internal Operational States:
- Idle / Uninitialized (`m_CutPath.Count == 0`, `m_TargetFace == null`): Cursor is `m_CutCursorTexture`. Clicking on empty space passes mouse events to `ProBuilderEditor.instance.HandleMouseEvent`.
- Drawing Path (`m_CutPath.Count > 0`, `m_TargetFace != null`): Cursor is `m_CutAddCursorTexture`. Displays polyline and dotted guide line to the cursor.
- Placing / Dragging Point (`m_PlacingPoint == true` or `m_ModifyingPoint == true` with `m_SelectedIndex >= 0`): Updates existing vertex position on `MouseDrag`.
- Loop Closure State (`isALoop == true`): Detected when `m_CutPath.Count >= 3` and `Math.Approx3(m_CutPath[0].position, m_CutPath[m_CutPath.Count - 1].position)`. Automatically invokes `ExecuteCut()`.
- Cut Validity State (`m_IsCutValid`): Evaluated in `ValidateCutShape()` by performing 2D segment intersection tests using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect` on screen-projected coordinates (`HandleUtility.WorldToGUIPoint`). Tests all cut segments against other cut segments and mesh connections. If any segments intersect, `m_IsCutValid = false`, coloring the cut line red and preventing execution.

## F03: Texture manipulation tools

### TEXTURE MOVE

The `TextureMoveTool` class derives from `TextureTool` and implements in-scene 3D handle manipulation for translating UV texture coordinates on selected mesh elements.\n\n### UV Channel Target\nAll texture translations operate strictly on UV channel 0 (`k_TextureChannel = 0`). The tool retrieves original UV coordinates using `ProBuilderMesh.GetUVs(0, m_Textures)` and applies modified coordinates via `selection.mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, positions)`.\n\n### Selection and Scale Caching\n`TextureMoveTool` defines a nested class `TranslateTextureSelection` inheriting from `MeshAndTextures`:\n- In the constructor `TranslateTextureSelection(ProBuilderMesh mesh, PivotPoint pivot)`, it caches `m_FaceAndScale` as an array of `(Face, Vector2)` pair tuples by iterating over `mesh.selectedFaceIndexes` and calling `UvUnwrapping.GetUVTransform(mesh, faces[x]).scale`.\n- `GetElementSelection(ProBuilderMesh mesh, PivotPoint pivot)` overrides the base method to instantiate and return `TranslateTextureSelection`.\n\n### In-Scene Translation Workflow\n1. In `DoToolGUI()`, when `!isEditing`, the internal translation accumulator `m_Position` is reset to `Vector3.zero`.\n2. The handle transformation matrix is set via `Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one)` within `EditorHandleUtility.PushMatrix()` and `EditorHandleUtility.PopMatrix()`.\n3. The user interacts with the handles (a 2D planar slider on the local XY plane, a vertical 1D slider along `Vector3.up`, or a horizontal 1D slider along `Vector3.right`).\n4. When `EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()` detects user interaction:\n   - If editing has not started (`!isEditing`), `BeginEdit("Translate Textures")` is called to register undo with `UndoUtility.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo` and pause lightmapping.\n   - Snapping is evaluated: `m_Position = EditorSnapping.MoveSnap(m_Position)`.\n   - The UV translation delta vector is constructed as `var delta = new Vector4(m_Position.x, -m_Position.y, 0f, 0f)`.\n   - **Y-Axis Inversion Rationale**: The Y component is inverted (`-m_Position.y`) because dragging a handle upward in 3D space increases the V coordinate in UV space, which on standard texture mapping moves the texture image downward across the surface. Negating Y ensures that moving the handle upward visually moves the texture pattern upward on the 3D surface.\n   - **Transform Lossy Scale Compensation**: For each mesh in `elementSelection`, the delta is scaled by `k_Vector3Magnitude / selection.mesh.transform.lossyScale.magnitude`, where `k_Vector3Magnitude = Vector3.one.magnitude` (approximately 1.7320508f). This prevents object scaling from making handle motion feel overly sensitive or sluggish.\n   - **Face Mode vs Vertex/Edge Mode**:\n     - In face selection mode (`ProBuilderEditor.selectMode == SelectMode.TextureFace`), textures on scaled faces would visually appear to translate faster or slower relative to handle motion. To guarantee 1:1 visual lockstep between handle movement and texture motion, the tool iterates over `selection.faceAndScale` and computes a per-face delta `faceDelta = new Vector4(delta.x / face.item2.x, delta.y / face.item2.y, 0f, 0f)`. For each vertex index in `face.item1.distinctIndexes`, `positions[index] = origins[index] + faceDelta`.\n     - In vertex or edge selection mode (`SelectMode.TextureVertex` or `SelectMode.TextureEdge`), the tool iterates over `value.elementGroups` and assigns `positions[index] = origins[index] + delta` directly for each index in `group.indices`.\n   - Finally, `selection.mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, positions)` commits the translated coordinates to the Unity mesh.

```csharp
        {
            SimpleTuple<Face, Vector2>[] m_FaceAndScale;

                m_FaceAndScale = mesh.selectedFaceIndexes.Select(x =>
                    new SimpleTuple<Face, Vector2>(faces[x], UvUnwrapping.GetUVTransform(mesh, faces[x]).scale))
```

```csharp
            if (EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck())
            {
                if (!isEditing)
                    BeginEdit("Translate Textures");

                m_Position = EditorSnapping.MoveSnap(m_Position);

                // invert `y` because to users it's confusing that "up" in UV space visually moves the texture down
                var delta = new Vector4(m_Position.x, -m_Position.y, 0f, 0f);

                foreach (var value in elementSelection)
                {
                    var selection = value as TranslateTextureSelection;

                    if (selection == null)
                        continue;

                    // Account for object scale
                    delta *= k_Vector3Magnitude / selection.mesh.transform.lossyScale.magnitude;

                    var origins = selection.origins;
                    var positions = selection.textures;

                    // Translating faces is treated as a special case because we want the textures in scene to visually
                    // match the movement of the translation handle. When UVs are scaled, they have the appearance of
                    // moving faster or slower (even though they are translating the correct distances). To avoid this,
                    // we cache the UV scale of each face and modify the translation delta accordingly. This isn't perfect,
                    // as it will not be able to find the scale for sheared or otherwise distorted face UVs. However, for
                    // most cases it maps quite well.
                    if (ProBuilderEditor.selectMode == SelectMode.TextureFace)
                    {
                        foreach (var face in selection.faceAndScale)
                        {
                            var faceDelta = new Vector4(delta.x / face.item2.x, delta.y / face.item2.y, 0f, 0f);

                            foreach (var index in face.item1.distinctIndexes)
                                positions[index] = origins[index] + faceDelta;
                        }
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        foreach (var group in value.elementGroups)
                        {
                            foreach (var index in group.indices)
                                positions[index] = origins[index] + delta;
                        }
                    }

                    selection.mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, positions);
                }
            }
```

### TEXTURE ROTATE

The `TextureRotateTool` class derives from `TextureTool` and implements in-scene rotation of UV texture coordinates using a 3D disc handle drawn in the Scene view.\n\n### State Fields and Initialization\n`TextureRotateTool` maintains three rotation state fields:\n- `float m_Rotation`: Accumulated rotation angle in degrees around the Z axis.\n- `Vector3 m_Euler`: Temporary Euler angle representation storing `(0f, 0f, m_Rotation)`.\n- `Quaternion m_Quaternion`: Temporary Quaternion representation storing `Quaternion.Euler(m_Euler)`.\n\nWhen `isEditing` is false (before the user drags), `m_Rotation` is reset to `0f`.\n\n### Pivot Point for UV Rotation\nRotation of UV coordinates in UV space is centered around the 2D bounding box center of the selection:\n1. The base class `MeshAndTextures` calculates the center of all selected UV coordinates via `Bounds2D.Center(m_Origins, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`.\n2. It initializes `preApplyMatrix = Matrix4x4.Translate(-Bounds2D.Center(m_Origins, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal))` and `postApplyMatrix = preApplyMatrix.inverse`.\n3. In UV space, each original coordinate `origins[index]` is transformed to the local origin via `mat.preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index])`.\n4. ProBuilder method `Math.RotateAroundPoint(point, Vector2.zero, -m_Rotation)` rotates the 2D point around `Vector2.zero` by angle `-m_Rotation`.\n5. The rotated point is transformed back to its original UV centroid via `mat.postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint(...)`.\n\n### Angle Direction and Snapping\n- **Negated Rotation Angle (`-m_Rotation`)**: The angle passed to `Math.RotateAroundPoint` is `-m_Rotation`. This sign negation guarantees that turning the in-scene disc handle clockwise rotates the visible texture clockwise on the mesh surface.\n- **Snapping**: When `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.Relative`, the disc handle passes `EditorSnapping.incrementalSnapRotateValue` to `Handles.Disc`, and `m_Rotation = EditorSnapping.RotateSnap(m_Rotation)` snaps the rotation in discrete degree increments.\n\n### Step-by-Step Rotation Algorithm\n1. In `DoToolGUI()`, `EditorHandleUtility.PushMatrix()` sets `Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one)`.\n2. `Handles.Disc` renders a circular rotation handle of radius `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_HandlePosition)` perpendicular to `Vector3.forward`.\n3. On drag change (`EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()`):\n   - If `!isEditing`, calls `BeginEdit("Rotate Textures")`.\n   - If snapping is active, snaps `m_Rotation`.\n   - For each `mesh` in `elementSelection` cast to `MeshAndTextures`:\n     - For each `group` in `mat.elementGroups`:\n       - For each `index` in `group.indices`:\n         - `positions[index] = mat.postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint(Math.RotateAroundPoint(mat.preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index]), Vector2.zero, -m_Rotation));`\n     - Calls `mesh.mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, positions)` on UV channel 0.

```csharp
            if (!isEditing)
                m_Rotation = 0f;

            EditorGUI.BeginChangeCheck();

            var size = HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_HandlePosition);

            EditorHandleUtility.PushMatrix();

            Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one);

            Handles.color = Color.blue;
            m_Euler.z = m_Rotation;
            m_Quaternion = Quaternion.Euler(m_Euler);
```
