            m_Euler = m_Quaternion.eulerAngles;
            m_Rotation = m_Euler.z;

            EditorHandleUtility.PopMatrix();

### TEXTURE SCALE

The `TextureScaleTool` class derives from `TextureTool` and implements both per-axis and uniform scaling of UV texture coordinates directly in the Scene view.\n\n### State Fields and Reset Logic\n`TextureScaleTool` maintains two scaling state fields:\n- `Vector2 m_Scale`: Independent scaling along local X (`m_Scale.x`, horizontal U) and local Y (`m_Scale.y`, vertical V).\n- `float m_UniformScale`: Proportional scaling factor applied equally across both axes.\n\nWhen `!isEditing`, these values reset to identity defaults:\n```csharp\nm_Scale.x = 1f;\nm_Scale.y = 1f;\nm_UniformScale = 1f;\n```\n\n### Per-Axis vs Uniform Scaling Handles\n`TextureScaleTool.DoToolGUI()` draws three distinct scaling handles at `m_HandlePosition` with rotation `m_HandleRotation`:\n1. **Horizontal U Scale Handle (Red)**: `Handles.ScaleSlider(m_Scale.x, Vector3.zero, Vector3.right, Quaternion.identity, size, snap.x)` controls `m_Scale.x`.\n2. **Vertical V Scale Handle (Green)**: `Handles.ScaleSlider(m_Scale.y, Vector3.zero, Vector3.up, Quaternion.identity, size, snap.y)` controls `m_Scale.y`.\n3. **Uniform Scale Handle (Blue Cube)**: `Handles.ScaleValueHandle(m_UniformScale, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity, size, Handles.CubeHandleCap, snap.x)` controls `m_UniformScale`.\n\nSnapping uses `EditorSnapping.activeScaleSnapValue` for both independent and uniform scaling.\n\n### Composite Scale Calculation and Inversion Rationale\nWhen changes are detected (`EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck()`):\n1. The combined scale vector is computed: `var delta = m_Scale * m_UniformScale;`\n2. The scale delta is inverted component-wise:\n   ```csharp\n   delta.x = 1f / delta.x;\n   delta.y = 1f / delta.y;\n   ```\n3. **Inversion Rationale**: In standard UV mapping, multiplying UV coordinates by a factor greater than 1 increases texture tiling frequency, causing the visual pattern to shrink on the mesh surface. By inverting `delta` (`1f / delta`), dragging the scale handle outward (scale factor > 1) expands the visible texture on the 3D surface, matching user intuition.\n\n### UV Coordinate Transformation\nScaling is centered around the 2D bounding box center of the selection calculated by `Bounds2D.Center(m_Origins, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`:\n1. `mat.preApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(origins[index])` translates the UV coordinates to center `(0,0)`.\n2. `Vector2.Scale(centeredUV, delta)` multiplies the centered UV coordinates by the inverted scale vector.\n3. `mat.postApplyMatrix.MultiplyPoint(...)` translates the scaled UV coordinates back from `(0,0)` to the original UV centroid.\n4. `mesh.mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, positions)` commits the updated coordinates to UV channel 0.

### TEXTURE TOOL BASE

The `TextureTool` abstract class provides the foundation for all in-scene texture manipulation tools (`TextureMoveTool`, `TextureRotateTool`, `TextureScaleTool`). It inherits from `VertexManipulationTool` and implements state management, caching, selection structures, and Auto vs Manual UV mode conversion.\n\n### Constants and Configuration\n- `const bool k_CollectCoincidentVertices = false`: UV manipulation must operate only on the selected geometric elements and must NOT collect coincident 3D vertices across UV seams. Coincident vertex collection is disabled.\n- `protected const int k_TextureChannel = 0`: All texture tools exclusively target UV channel 0.\n\n### Selection Wrapper: `MeshAndTextures`\n`TextureTool` defines an internal class `MeshAndTextures` inheriting from `MeshAndElementSelection`:\n- `List<Vector4> m_Origins`: Snapshot of UV coordinates at the beginning of the manipulation.\n- `List<Vector4> m_Textures`: Working list of modified UV coordinates.\n- `Matrix4x4 m_PreApplyMatrix` and `Matrix4x4 m_PostApplyMatrix`: Translation matrices that center UV coordinates at `(0,0)` during transformation and restore them back to their original UV centroid afterwards.\n- In the constructor `MeshAndTextures(ProBuilderMesh mesh, PivotPoint pivot)`:\n  - Calls `base(mesh, k_CollectCoincidentVertices)`.\n  - Reads UV channel 0: `mesh.GetUVs(k_TextureChannel, m_Textures)`.\n  - Clones into `m_Origins = new List<Vector4>(m_Textures)`.\n  - Computes the bounding center of selected UVs via `Bounds2D.Center(m_Origins, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)` and assigns `preApplyMatrix = Matrix4x4.Translate(-Bounds2D.Center(...))` and `postApplyMatrix = preApplyMatrix.inverse`.\n\n### Tool Lifecycle Hooks\n- `OnToolEngaged()`: Invoked when manipulation starts in `BeginEdit()`. Calls `MeshSelection.InvalidateCaches()` to ensure all selection geometry and bounds are refreshed.\n- `OnToolDisengaged()`: Invoked when the mouse is released in `FinishEdit()`. Handles Auto vs Manual UV synchronization.\n\n### Auto vs Manual UV Mode Interaction\nWhen the tool is disengaged (`OnToolDisengaged()`), ProBuilder handles Auto vs Manual UV modes depending on the current selection mode:\n1. **Face Selection Mode (`SelectMode.TextureFace` or `SelectMode.Face`)**:\n   - Manipulating an entire face preserves planar projection coherence.\n   - The tool filters selected faces that are currently in Auto UV mode: `mesh.mesh.selectedFacesInternal.Where(x => !x.manualUV)`.\n   - It invokes `UvUnwrapping.SetAutoAndAlignUnwrapParamsToUVs(mesh.mesh, ...)` on those faces.\n   - `SetAutoAndAlignUnwrapParamsToUVs` calculates new `AutoUnwrapSettings` (`offset`, `rotation`, `scale`) that match the newly manipulated UVs and assigns them to `face.uv` while keeping `face.manualUV = false`. Auto UV faces remain in Auto UV mode with updated parameters.\n   - Faces with `face.manualUV == true` retain their modified UVs without updating `AutoUnwrapSettings`.\n2. **Vertex or Edge Selection Mode (`SelectMode.TextureVertex` or `SelectMode.TextureEdge`)**:\n   - Moving individual vertices or edges distorts planar projection, breaking Auto UV mathematical assumptions.\n   - The tool gathers all modified vertex indices into a `HashSet<int> indices = new HashSet<int>(mesh.elementGroups.SelectMany(x => x.indices))`.\n   - For every face in the mesh (`mesh.mesh.facesInternal`), if any vertex index in `face.distinctIndexesInternal` is contained within `indices`, the face is converted to Manual UV mode: `face.manualUV = true`.\n   - Sub-face UV edits permanently convert affected faces from Auto UV to Manual UV.

        protected override void OnToolEngaged()
        {
            MeshSelection.InvalidateCaches();
        }

        protected override void OnToolDisengaged()
        {
            var isFaceMode = ProBuilderEditor.selectMode.ContainsFlag(SelectMode.TextureFace | SelectMode.Face);

            foreach (var mesh in elementSelection)
            {
                if (!(mesh is MeshAndTextures))
                    continue;

                var textures = ((MeshAndTextures)mesh).textures;
                mesh.mesh.SetUVs(k_TextureChannel, textures);

                if (isFaceMode)
                {
                    UvUnwrapping.SetAutoAndAlignUnwrapParamsToUVs(mesh.mesh, mesh.mesh.selectedFacesInternal.Where(x => !x.manualUV));
                }
                else
                {
                    var indices = new HashSet<int>(mesh.elementGroups.SelectMany(x => x.indices));

                    foreach (var face in mesh.mesh.facesInternal)
                    {
                        foreach (var index in face.distinctIndexesInternal)
                        {
                            if (indices.Contains(index))
                            {
                                face.manualUV = true;
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

### HANDLE RENDERING

Texture manipulation handles are rendered in the Scene view using Unity `Handles` API, positioned and oriented according to active element selection context.\n\n### Coordinate Frame Setup\nAll texture tools set up the local handle matrix before rendering handles:\n1. `EditorHandleUtility.PushMatrix()` saves the current handle matrix.\n2. `Handles.matrix = Matrix4x4.TRS(m_HandlePosition, m_HandleRotation, Vector3.one)` establishes a local transformation frame:\n   - `m_HandlePosition`: Computed by `MeshSelection.GetHandlePosition()`. When `VertexManipulationTool.pivotPoint` is `PivotPoint.ActiveElement` or `PivotPoint.IndividualOrigins`, it returns the active element world position (`active.elementGroups.Last().position`). When `PivotPoint.Center`, it returns selection bounds center (`bounds.center`).\n   - `m_HandleRotation`: Computed by `MeshSelection.GetHandleRotation()`. When `VertexManipulationTool.handleOrientation` is `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, it aligns with the surface normal and tangent frame of the active element (`active.elementGroups.Last().rotation`). When `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, it uses the GameObject rotation (`active.mesh.transform.rotation`). When `HandleOrientation.World`, it uses `Quaternion.identity`.\n3. `EditorHandleUtility.PopMatrix()` restores the previous matrix stack state.\n\n### Constant Screen-Space Sizing\nHandle dimensions scale with distance from the Scene view camera using `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_HandlePosition)` or `HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_Position)`, ensuring handles remain a consistent pixel size on screen.\n\n### Handle Drawing by Tool\n- **TextureMoveTool (`TextureMoveTool.DoToolGUI`)**:\n  - Planar translation (XY plane): `Handles.color = Color.blue`, followed by `Handles.Slider2D(m_Position, Vector3.forward, Vector3.right, Vector3.up, HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_Position) * .2f, Handles.RectangleHandleCap, 0f, false)`.\n  - Vertical 1D translation (Y / V axis): `Handles.color = Color.green`, followed by `Handles.Slider(m_Position, Vector3.up, HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_Position), Handles.ArrowHandleCap, 0f)`.\n  - Horizontal 1D translation (X / U axis): `Handles.color = Color.red`, followed by `Handles.Slider(m_Position, Vector3.right, HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_Position), Handles.ArrowHandleCap, 0f)`.\n  - Color reset: `Handles.color = Color.white`.\n- **TextureRotateTool (`TextureRotateTool.DoToolGUI`)**:\n  - Rotation disc: `Handles.color = Color.blue`, `Handles.Disc(m_Quaternion, Vector3.zero, Vector3.forward, size, false, snap)`.\n  - The disc lies in the local XY plane facing normal `Vector3.forward` with radius `size = HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(m_HandlePosition)`.\n- **TextureScaleTool (`TextureScaleTool.DoToolGUI`)**:\n  - Horizontal U scale slider: `Handles.color = Color.red`, `Handles.ScaleSlider(m_Scale.x, Vector3.zero, Vector3.right, Quaternion.identity, size, snap.x)`.\n  - Vertical V scale slider: `Handles.color = Color.green`, `Handles.ScaleSlider(m_Scale.y, Vector3.zero, Vector3.up, Quaternion.identity, size, snap.y)`.\n  - Uniform scale cube: `Handles.color = Color.blue`, `Handles.ScaleValueHandle(m_UniformScale, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity, size, Handles.CubeHandleCap, snap.x)`.\n\n### Snapping System Integration\n- Translation uses `EditorSnapping.MoveSnap(m_Position)` with `EditorSnapping.activeMoveSnapValue`.\n- Rotation uses `EditorSnapping.RotateSnap(m_Rotation)` with `EditorSnapping.incrementalSnapRotateValue` when `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.Relative`.\n- Scale passes `EditorSnapping.activeScaleSnapValue` directly to the scale slider methods.

# Visual Rendering

## G01: Editor handle drawing - wireframes, selection overlays

### WIREFRAME OVERLAY

ProBuilder renders custom wireframe overlays directly onto editable meshes during scene view interaction, completely overriding Unity's default selection wireframe.

1. Unity Selection Wireframe Override:
- When ProBuilder enters edit mode, it suppresses Unity's native wireframe rendering on the target `MeshRenderer` components via `ProBuilderEditor.SetOverrideWireframe(bool overrideWireframe)`.
- It executes `EditorUtility.SetSelectionRenderState(mesh.renderer, overrideWireframe ? k_DefaultSelectedRenderState & ~(EditorSelectedRenderState.Wireframe) : k_DefaultSelectedRenderState)` where `k_DefaultSelectedRenderState = EditorSelectedRenderState.Highlight | EditorSelectedRenderState.Wireframe`.
- When ProBuilder is active, the `EditorSelectedRenderState.Wireframe` bit is cleared, preventing Unity from drawing default green/orange wireframe outlines. When ProBuilder is closed or selection changes away, the default selection render state is restored.

2. Wireframe Drawing Execution & Selection Modes:
- Wireframes are drawn during `EventType.Repaint` events in `EditorHandleDrawing.DrawSceneHandles(SelectMode mode)`.
- When `SelectMode` is `SelectMode.Face`, `SelectMode.TextureFace`, `SelectMode.Vertex`, `SelectMode.TextureVertex`, or default (`SelectMode.None` / `SelectMode.Object`), wireframe geometry is drawn from cached `wireHandles` (or `s_WireHandles`) using `wireframeColor`: `Render(wireHandles, m_ForceWireframeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : wireMaterial, wireframeColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)`.
- When `SelectMode` is `SelectMode.Edge` or `SelectMode.TextureEdge`, wireframe lines represent unselected edges and are rendered using `edgeMaterial` with `edgeUnselectedColor`: `Render(wireHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : edgeMaterial, edgeUnselectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)`.
- If drag-and-drop operations are active (`SceneDragAndDropListener.isDragging == true`), `SelectMode.None` is passed into `DrawSceneHandles`, which falls back to the default wireframe rendering path.

3. Line Width, DPI Scaling, and GL Fallback:
- Wireframe thickness is governed by the preference `s_WireframeLineSize` (`Pref<float>("graphics.wireframeLineSize", .5f, SettingsScope.User)`).
- Screen density scaling is applied in `SetMaterialsScaleAttribute()`: `wireMaterial.SetFloat("_Scale", s_WireframeLineSize * EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoint)`.
- If `s_WireframeLineSize.value < k_MinLineWidthForGeometryShader` (where constant `k_MinLineWidthForGeometryShader = 0.01f`), `m_ForceWireframeLinesGL` becomes `true`. Under GL fallback mode, `glWireMaterial` (`Shader.Find(BuiltinMaterials.faceShader)`) is used instead of `wireMaterial` (`LineBillboard.shader` / `LineBillboardMetal.shader`).

4. Depth Testing and Render Configuration:
- Wireframe rendering calls `Render(handles, material, color, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)`.
- The material uniform `_HandleZTest` is set to `(int)CompareFunction.LessEqual` (value 4), and `_HandleZWrite` is set to `0` (disabled).
- Wireframe lines only draw where geometry is not occluded by foreground surfaces in the scene depth buffer.

```csharp
        public static void DrawSceneHandles(SelectMode mode)
        {
            if (Event.current.type != EventType.Repaint)
                return;

            // Update the scale based on EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoints in case the DPI would have changed.
            SetMaterialsScaleAttribute();

            switch(mode)
            {
                case SelectMode.Edge:
                case SelectMode.TextureEdge:
                {
                    // When in Edge mode, use the same material for wireframe
                    Render(wireHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : edgeMaterial, edgeUnselectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    if(xRay) Render(s_SelectedEdgeHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_EdgeMaterial, edgeSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater);
                    Render(s_SelectedEdgeHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_EdgeMaterial, edgeSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual);
                    break;
                }
                case SelectMode.Face:
                case SelectMode.TextureFace:
                {
                    Render(wireHandles, m_ForceWireframeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : wireMaterial, wireframeColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    if(xRay) Render(s_SelectedFaceHandles, s_FaceMaterial, faceSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater);
                    Render(s_SelectedFaceHandles, s_FaceMaterial, faceSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual);
                    break;
                }
                case SelectMode.Vertex:
                case SelectMode.TextureVertex:
                {
                    Render(s_WireHandles, m_ForceWireframeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_WireMaterial, wireframeColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    Render(s_VertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexUnselectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    if(xRay) Render(s_SelectedVertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater, false);
                    Render(s_SelectedVertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    break;
                }
                default:
                {
                    Render(wireHandles, m_ForceWireframeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : wireMaterial, wireframeColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false);
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

```csharp
        internal static void CreateEdgeMesh(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Mesh target)
        {
            int edgeCount = 0;
            int faceCount = mesh.faceCount;

            for (int i = 0; i < faceCount; i++)
                edgeCount += mesh.facesInternal[i].edgesInternal.Length;

            s_IndexList.Clear();
            s_IndexList.Capacity = edgeCount * 2;

            int edgeIndex = 0;

            for (int i = 0; i < faceCount && edgeIndex < edgeCount; i++)
            {
                for (int n = 0; n < mesh.facesInternal[i].edgesInternal.Length && edgeIndex < edgeCount; n++)
                {
                    var edge = mesh.facesInternal[i].edgesInternal[n];
                    s_IndexList.Add(edge.a);
                    s_IndexList.Add(edge.b);

                    edgeIndex++;
                }
            }

            target.Clear();
            target.indexFormat = edgeCount * 2 > ushort.MaxValue ? Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt32 : Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt16;
            target.name = "ProBuilder::EdgeMesh" + target.GetObjectId();
            target.vertices = mesh.positionsInternal;
            target.subMeshCount = 1;
            target.SetIndices(s_IndexList, MeshTopology.Lines, 0);
        }

To override Godot's built-in selection outlines, editor plugins disable default gizmo selection highlights on selected nodes and draw custom wireframe geometry in _redraw().

### FACE HIGHLIGHT

Selected faces in ProBuilder are highlighted using solid fill geometry rendered with a semi-transparent dithered shader.

1. Multi-Pass Selected Face Rendering:
- In `DrawSceneHandles(SelectMode mode)` when mode is `SelectMode.Face` or `SelectMode.TextureFace`, face handles stored in `s_SelectedFaceHandles` are rendered using `s_FaceMaterial`.
- Visible Pass: `Render(s_SelectedFaceHandles, s_FaceMaterial, faceSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual)` renders unoccluded faces with depth test `CompareFunction.LessEqual` and `_HandleZWrite = 0`.
- Occluded / X-Ray Pass: When `xRay` is enabled (`s_XRayView.value == true`), an additional pass renders `Render(s_SelectedFaceHandles, s_FaceMaterial, faceSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater)` behind occluding scene objects.

2. Face Mesh Generation:
- `MeshHandles.CreateFaceMesh(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Mesh target)` constructs the handle mesh by assigning `target.vertices = mesh.positionsInternal;` and flattening face triangle indices via `target.triangles = mesh.selectedFacesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.indexes).ToArray();`.
- For arbitrary face sets (e.g. hovered or temporary faces), `MeshHandles.CreateFaceMeshFromFaces(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IList<Face> faces, Mesh target)` flattens `faces.SelectMany(x => x.indexes).ToArray()` into `target.triangles`.

3. Shader Properties and Dithering:
- `faceMaterial` is instantiated with shader `BuiltinMaterials.faceShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/FaceHighlight"`.
- The shader sets `ZTest [_HandleZTest]`, `ZWrite [_HandleZWrite]`, `Cull Off`, `Lighting Off`, and alpha blending `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`.
- In the fragment shader, dithering is computed across pixel screen positions: `float checker = -frac(i.pos.x + i.pos.y); clip(lerp(1, checker, _Dither)); return _Color;`.
- The `_Dither` uniform is updated in `ResetPreferences()`: `faceMaterial.SetFloat("_Dither", (s_UseUnityColors || s_DitherFaceHandle) ? 1f : 0f);`.

4. Colors and Transparency:
- `faceSelectedColor` returns `s_UseUnityColors ? Handles.selectedColor : s_SelectedFaceColorPref`.
- `s_SelectedFaceColorPref` defaults to `Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f)` (cyan). In Unity, `Handles.selectedColor` defaults to cyan/yellow with alpha transparency.

5. Unselected Face Dimming and Hover Preselection:
- Unselected faces are not rendered with a fill mesh overlay in edit mode, leaving the underlying object material/texture visible behind the wireframe overlay.
- Hovered faces are drawn in `DrawSceneSelection(SceneSelection selection)` using `TriangleDrawingScope(preselectionColor)`: it calls `GL.MultMatrix(mesh.transform.localToWorldMatrix)` and issues `GL.Vertex(positions[ind[i]])` for all triangle vertex indexes.
- Interactive tools like `CutTool` call `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightFaces(mesh, faces, highlightColor)` to build transient face meshes in `s_TemporaryHandles` and render them with `CompareFunction.LessEqual`.

### EDGE HIGHLIGHT

Edge selection overlay rendering in ProBuilder draws distinct unselected, occluded, and visible line segments with geometry shaders or screen-space billboard fallbacks.

1. Edge Selection Render Passes:
- In `DrawSceneHandles(SelectMode mode)` when mode is `SelectMode.Edge` or `SelectMode.TextureEdge`:
  - Unselected Pass: `Render(wireHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? glWireMaterial : edgeMaterial, edgeUnselectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)` renders unselected mesh edges as wireframe.
  - Occluded Selected Pass: If `xRay` is enabled, `Render(s_SelectedEdgeHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_EdgeMaterial, edgeSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater)` renders occluded segments with darkened tint.
  - Visible Selected Pass: `Render(s_SelectedEdgeHandles, m_ForceEdgeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_EdgeMaterial, edgeSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual)` renders visible selected edges.

2. Mesh Topology and Billboard Math:
- If geometry shaders are supported (`BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported == true`) or GL mode is forced (`m_ForceEdgeLinesGL == true`), `MeshHandles.CreateEdgeMesh(mesh, target, edges)` generates `MeshTopology.Lines`. Indices `edge.a` and `edge.b` are pushed to `s_IndexList`, with 32-bit index format enabled if `vertexCount > ushort.MaxValue`.
- If geometry shaders are not supported (e.g. Metal on macOS), `MeshHandles.CreateEdgeBillboardMesh(mesh, target, edges)` builds screen-space billboard quads (`MeshTopology.Quads`):
  - For each edge with endpoints $a = \text{vertices}[\text{edge.a}]$ and $b = \text{vertices}[\text{edge.b}]$, it computes tangent target $c = b + (b - a)$.
  - Adds 4 vertices to `s_Vector3List`: $[a, a, b, b]$.
  - Adds 4 tangent vectors to `s_Vector4List`:
    - Vertex 0 (at $a$): `Vector4(b.x, b.y, b.z, 1f)`
    - Vertex 1 (at $a$): `Vector4(b.x, b.y, b.z, -1f)`
    - Vertex 2 (at $b$): `Vector4(c.x, c.y, c.z, 1f)`
    - Vertex 3 (at $b$): `Vector4(c.x, c.y, c.z, -1f)`
  - Quad index order: $[n+0, n+1, n+3, n+2]$.

3. Shaders and Line Thickness:
- `s_EdgeMaterial` uses `BuiltinMaterials.lineShader` (`"Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboard"`) or `BuiltinMaterials.lineShaderMetal` (`"Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboardMetal"`).
- In `LineBillboard.shader`, geometry shaders compute the screen perpendicular: `perp = normalize(float2(-(p[1].pos.y - p[0].pos.y), p[1].pos.x - p[0].pos.x)) * _Scale` and extrude a triangle strip.
- In `LineBillboardMetal.shader`, vertex shaders use tangent direction $d = \text{normalize}(b - a)$ and perpendicular $p = (-d.y, d.x)$ to offset `a.xy += p * v.tangent.w * _Scale`.
- Thickness is set by user preference `s_EdgeLineSize` (`Pref<float>("graphics.edgeLineSize", 1f, SettingsScope.User)`), scaled as `_Scale = s_EdgeLineSize * EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoint`.

4. Colors and Tool Highlighting:
- `edgeSelectedColor` defaults to `Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f)` (`s_SelectedEdgeColorPref`).
- `edgeUnselectedColor` defaults to `Color(44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 1f)` (`s_UnselectedEdgeColorPref`).
- `EditorHandleDrawing.HighlightEdges(mesh, edges, highlightColor)` builds temporary edge meshes in `s_TemporaryHandles` for tools like `CutTool`.

        internal static void CreateEdgeMesh(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Mesh target, Edge[] edges)
        {
            int edgeCount = edges.Length;
            int vertexCount = edgeCount * 2;

            s_IndexList.Clear();
            s_IndexList.Capacity = vertexCount;

            for (int n = 0; n < edgeCount; n++)
            {
                var edge = edges[n];
                s_IndexList.Add(edge.a);
                s_IndexList.Add(edge.b);
            }

            target.Clear();
            target.indexFormat = vertexCount > ushort.MaxValue ? Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt32 : Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt16;
            target.name = "ProBuilder::EdgeMesh" + target.GetObjectId();
            target.vertices = mesh.positionsInternal;
            target.subMeshCount = 1;
            target.SetIndices(s_IndexList, MeshTopology.Lines, 0);
        }

        internal static void CreateEdgeBillboardMesh(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Mesh target, ICollection<Edge> edges)
        {
            target.Clear();

            const ushort k_MaxPointCountUShort = ushort.MaxValue / 4;

            var lineCount = edges.Count;

            target.indexFormat = lineCount > k_MaxPointCountUShort
                ? Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt32
                : Rendering.IndexFormat.UInt16;

            var vertices = mesh.positionsInternal;

            s_Vector3List.Clear();
            s_Vector4List.Clear();
            s_IndexList.Clear();
            s_Vector3List.Capacity = lineCount * 4;
            s_Vector4List.Capacity = lineCount * 4;
            s_IndexList.Capacity = lineCount * 4;

            int n = 0;

            foreach (var edge in edges)
            {
                Vector3 a = vertices[edge.a], b = vertices[edge.b];
                Vector3 c = b + (b - a);

                s_Vector3List.Add(a);
                s_Vector3List.Add(a);
                s_Vector3List.Add(b);
                s_Vector3List.Add(b);

                s_Vector4List.Add(new Vector4(b.x, b.y, b.z, 1f));
                s_Vector4List.Add(new Vector4(b.x, b.y, b.z, -1f));
                s_Vector4List.Add(new Vector4(c.x, c.y, c.z, 1f));
                s_Vector4List.Add(new Vector4(c.x, c.y, c.z, -1f));

                s_IndexList.Add(n + 0);
                s_IndexList.Add(n + 1);
                s_IndexList.Add(n + 3);
                s_IndexList.Add(n + 2);

                n += 4;
            }

            target.SetVertices(s_Vector3List);
            target.SetTangents(s_Vector4List);
            target.subMeshCount = 1;
            target.SetIndices(s_IndexList, MeshTopology.Quads, 0);
        }
    }

### VERTEX DOTS

Vertex points in ProBuilder are rendered as square billboard dots with distinct handling for shared vertex clusters and active selections.

1. Vertex Selection Render Passes:
- In `DrawSceneHandles(SelectMode mode)` when mode is `SelectMode.Vertex` or `SelectMode.TextureVertex`:
  - Wireframe Pass: `Render(s_WireHandles, m_ForceWireframeLinesGL ? s_GlWireMaterial : s_WireMaterial, wireframeColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)`.
  - Unselected Vertices Pass: `Render(s_VertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexUnselectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)` renders all unique shared vertex points.
  - Occluded Selected Vertices Pass: If `xRay` is true, `Render(s_SelectedVertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater, false)` draws occluded selected vertices.
  - Visible Selected Vertices Pass: `Render(s_SelectedVertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexSelectedColor, CompareFunction.LessEqual, false)` draws unoccluded selected vertices.

2. Shared Vertex Clustering vs Selected Indexes:
- Unselected vertices use `MeshHandles.CreateVertexMesh(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Mesh target)`: it iterates through `mesh.sharedVerticesInternal` and extracts only the first index `mesh.sharedVerticesInternal[i][0]` of each shared cluster into `s_SharedVertexIndexList`. This guarantees exactly one dot is rendered per spatial vertex position, preventing duplicate overlapping draws on split normal/UV seams.
- Selected vertices use `MeshHandles.CreateVertexMesh(mesh, handle.mesh, mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)` to render all active selection indices.

3. Point Mesh Primitives vs Billboard Quad Expansion:
- If geometry shaders are supported (`BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported == true`), `MeshHandles.CreatePointMesh` configures `MeshTopology.Points`. The `PointBillboard.shader` geometry shader emits a 4-vertex quad triangle strip around each point in screen coordinates.
- If geometry shaders are unsupported, `MeshHandles.CreatePointBillboardMesh` expands each vertex into 4 quad vertices in object space (`s_Vector3List.Add(positions[index])` x4), assigning billboard UV offsets: `k_Billboard0 = (-1f, -1f)`, `k_Billboard1 = (-1f, 1f)`, `k_Billboard2 = (1f, -1f)`, `k_Billboard3 = (1f, 1f)`, and quad indices `[i*4+0, i*4+1, i*4+3, i*4+2]` with `MeshTopology.Quads`.

4. Point Size and Colors:
- Size is set by preference `s_VertexPointSize` (`Pref<float>("graphics.vertexPointSize", 3f, SettingsScope.User)`).
- Material scale uniform: `vertMaterial.SetFloat("_Scale", s_VertexPointSize * EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoint)`.
- Constant cap size for gizmo/dot cap handles: `EditorHandleDrawing.dotCapSize = s_VertexPointSize * 0.0125f`.
- `vertexSelectedColor` defaults to `Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f)` (`s_SelectedVertexColorPref`).
- `vertexUnselectedColor` returns `k_VertexUnselectedDefault = Color(.7f, .7f, .7f, 1f)` when `s_UseUnityColors` is true, or `s_UnselectedVertexColorPref = Color(44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 1f)` when custom colors are active.

### DEPTH/OCCLUSION

ProBuilder handles depth testing, occlusion, and X-Ray overlay rendering through configurable material uniforms and multi-pass draw calls.

1. Shader Uniform Depth Control:
- Instead of relying on static graphics pipeline state changes, all ProBuilder overlay shaders (`FaceHighlight.shader`, `LineBillboard.shader`, `LineBillboardMetal.shader`, `PointBillboard.shader`, `VertexShader.shader`) expose depth properties:
  - `_HandleZTest ("_HandleZTest", Int) = 8` (corresponding to Unity's `UnityEngine.Rendering.CompareFunction` enum: `LessEqual` = 4, `Greater` = 5, `Always` = 8).
  - `_HandleZWrite ("_HandleZWrite", Int) = 0` (0 disables depth buffer writing; 1 enables depth buffer writing).
- In `EditorHandleDrawing.Render(handles, material, color, func, zWrite)`:
  - `material.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)func);`
  - `material.SetFloat("_HandleZWrite", zWrite ? 1 : 0);`
  - `material.SetColor("_Color", color);`

2. X-Ray Mode Two-Pass Rendering Strategy:
- X-Ray view is configured via `s_XRayView = new Pref<bool>("graphics.xRayView", true, SettingsScope.User)` and exposed via `EditorHandleDrawing.xRay`.
- Occlusion Tint Constant: `k_OccludedTint = new Color(.75f, .75f, .75f, 1f)`.
- When `xRay` is enabled, selected elements are rendered in two sequential passes:
  - Pass 1 (Occluded Pass): Renders selected elements with `CompareFunction.Greater` and dimmed tint `selectedColor * k_OccludedTint`. This pass executes only for pixels where scene geometry is in front of the selected element, producing a ghosted see-through effect.
  - Pass 2 (Visible Pass): Renders selected elements with `CompareFunction.LessEqual` and undiluted `selectedColor`. This pass renders the unoccluded portions.
- If `xRay` is disabled, Pass 1 is omitted entirely, causing occluded elements to be hidden behind foreground geometry.

3. Z-Fighting Mitigation:
- All overlay shaders incorporate hardware depth offsets (`Offset -1, -1` in line and face shaders, `Offset 0, -2` in `PointBillboard.shader`) to bias the computed depth toward the camera, preventing coplanar z-fighting between the wireframe/selection handles and the underlying mesh surface.

4. Obsolete Settings:
- The legacy preference `s_DepthTestHandles = new Pref<bool>("graphics.handleZTest", true, SettingsScope.User)` is marked `[Obsolete]` because depth testing is now dynamically managed per render pass via `CompareFunction`.

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, two-pass X-Ray overlay rendering can be implemented using two surfaces or two draw calls with render_priority. The occluded pass uses a material with depth_draw_mode = DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED, render_priority = 0, and an albedo tinted by Color(0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 1.0). The visible pass uses normal depth testing with render_priority = 1. Depth bias can be set via render_mode unshaded, depth_draw_never or adjusting DEPTH = FRAGCOORD.z - 0.0001 in shader code.

### MESH HANDLE

ProBuilder encapsulates GL draw caching and mesh pooling inside the `MeshHandle` class and `EditorHandleDrawing` cache dictionaries.

1. MeshHandle Data Structure:
- `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshHandle` is a sealed class containing:
  - `Transform m_Transform`: The transform matrix reference of the target ProBuilder mesh.
  - `Mesh m_Mesh`: The cached Unity `Mesh` containing GPU buffers.
  - `public Mesh mesh { get { return m_Mesh; } }`: Property returning the backing mesh.
  - `DrawMeshNow(int submeshIndex)`: Executes `Graphics.DrawMeshNow(m_Mesh, m_Transform.localToWorldMatrix, submeshIndex)`.

2. Handle Caching Dictionaries:
- `EditorHandleDrawing` caches handles per `ProBuilderMesh`:
  - `s_WireHandles`: Unselected wireframe edges.
  - `s_VertexHandles`: Unselected vertex dots.
  - `s_SelectedFaceHandles`: Selected face fill geometry.
  - `s_SelectedEdgeHandles`: Selected edge lines.
  - `s_SelectedVertexHandles`: Selected vertex dots.
  - `s_TemporaryHandles`: Transient handles for hover preselection and interactive tools.

3. Object Pooling Lifecycle:
- Mesh instances are managed by `ObjectPool<Mesh> s_MeshPool2` initialized with capacity `(0, 8, CreateMesh, DestroyMesh)`.
- `CreateMesh()` instantiates a `Mesh` with `mesh.name = "EditorMeshHandles.MeshHandle" + mesh.GetObjectId()` and `mesh.hideFlags = HideFlags.HideAndDontSave`.
- `ClearHandlesInternal(Dictionary<ProBuilderMesh, MeshHandle> handles)` enqueues all cached `Mesh` instances back to `meshPool.Enqueue(kvp.Value.mesh)` and clears the dictionary.

4. Rebuild Triggers and Lifecycle:
- Handle rebuilds are triggered via `ProBuilderEditor.UpdateMeshHandles()` in response to:
  - Selection modifications (`MeshSelection.topInternal` updates).
  - Selection mode transitions (switching between Object, Face, Edge, Vertex modes).
  - Geometric mutations (vertex translations, extrusions, cuts, vertex deletions, undo/redo operations).
  - Preference changes in `HandleColorPreferences`.
- Rebuild execution in `RebuildSelectedHandles(IEnumerable<ProBuilderMesh> meshes, SelectMode selectionMode)`:
  - Calls `ClearHandles()` to return all meshes to `meshPool`.
  - Iterates over active meshes and calls `GetMeshHandle(mesh, dictionary)` to dequeue a mesh from `meshPool`.
  - Calls `MeshHandles` builders (`CreateVertexMesh`, `CreateEdgeMesh`, `CreateEdgeBillboardMesh`, `CreateFaceMesh`) to populate vertices, tangents, UVs, and indices.

5. Domain Reload & Play Mode Reset:
- `[InitializeOnEnterPlayMode] ResetStaticsOnLoad()` and `ReleaseResources()` clear all handles, dispose `s_MeshPool2`, and destroy all cached handle materials (`s_FaceMaterial`, `s_EdgeMaterial`, `s_VertMaterial`, `s_WireMaterial`, `s_LineMaterial`, `s_GlWireMaterial`).

        static MeshHandle GetMeshHandle(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Dictionary<ProBuilderMesh, MeshHandle> cache)
        {
            MeshHandle handle;

            if(!cache.TryGetValue(mesh, out handle))
            {
                var m = meshPool.Dequeue();
                handle = new MeshHandle(mesh.transform, m);
                cache.Add(mesh, handle);
            }

            return handle;
        }

        static void RebuildMeshHandle(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Dictionary<ProBuilderMesh, MeshHandle> list, Action<ProBuilderMesh, Mesh> ctor)
        {
            var handle = GetMeshHandle(mesh, list);
            ctor(mesh, handle.mesh);

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, MeshHandle equivalents can wrap an ArrayMesh or ImmediateMesh alongside a Node3D/Transform3D reference. Handle caching can use a Dictionary mapping ProBuilderMesh nodes to ArrayMesh instances, with an Array[ArrayMesh] pool to recycle mesh allocations on selection or edit updates, avoiding runtime garbage collection pauses.

### DRAWING SCOPES

ProBuilder uses structured `IDisposable` drawing scopes to encapsulate GL state management, matrix transformations, and immediate-mode handle rendering.

1. PointDrawingScope (struct `IDisposable`):
- Manages immediate vertex point rendering.
- Constructor dequeues a pooled `Mesh` from `meshPool`, initializes `m_Points` and `m_Indices` lists, and assigns `m_Matrix = Matrix4x4.identity`.
- `Begin()` sets `vertMaterial.SetColor("_Color", color)`, `vertMaterial.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)zTest)`, and executes `vertMaterial.SetPass(0)`.
- `Draw(Vector3 point)` adds coordinates to `m_Points`.
- `End()` clears `m_Mesh`, assigns vertices/indices (using `MeshTopology.Points` or `MeshHandles.CreatePointBillboardMesh` for fallback), and issues `Graphics.DrawMeshNow(m_Mesh, m_Matrix, 0)`.
- `Dispose()` calls `End()` and returns the mesh to `meshPool.Enqueue(m_Mesh)`.

2. LineDrawingScope (struct `IDisposable`):
- Manages dynamic line segment rendering with customizable thickness, color, matrix, and depth testing.
- Mode determination: `m_Wire = m_Thickness < k_MinLineWidthForGeometryShader || lineMaterial == null;` and `m_LineTopology = m_Wire || BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported;`.
- `Begin()` applies line color, thickness (`_Scale`), and `_HandleZTest` to `lineMaterial`, or falls back to `HandleUtility.ApplyWireMaterial(zTest)`.
- `DrawLine(Vector3 a, Vector3 b)`:
  - In billboard mode: computes $c = b + (b - a)$, adds 4 positions $[a, a, b, b]$, and 4 tangents with signs $\pm 1$.
  - In wire mode: adds 2 positions $[a, b]$, colors, and line indices.
- `End()` submits `m_LineMesh` via `Graphics.DrawMeshNow(m_LineMesh, m_Matrix)` and clears vertex lists.
- `Dispose()` calls `End()` and enqueues `m_LineMesh` back to `meshPool`.

3. TriangleDrawingScope (class `IDisposable`):
- Manages immediate-mode GL triangle drawing.
- `Begin()` configures `faceMaterial.SetColor("_Color", color)`, `faceMaterial.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)zTest)`, calls `faceMaterial.SetPass(0)`, and starts a GL batch: `GL.PushMatrix(); GL.Begin(GL.TRIANGLES);`.
- `Draw(Vector3 a, Vector3 b, Vector3 c)` issues `GL.Vertex(a); GL.Vertex(b); GL.Vertex(c);`.
- `End()` and `Dispose()` terminate the batch with `GL.End(); GL.PopMatrix();`.

4. HandleGUI (sealed class `IDisposable`):
- RAII wrapper that calls `Handles.BeginGUI()` in its constructor and `Handles.EndGUI()` in `Dispose()`.

5. EditorHandleUtility Gizmos and Matrix Stack:
- `PushMatrix()` and `PopMatrix()` manage a matrix stack `s_HandleMatrix` using `Handles.matrix`.
- `DrawGizmo` and `DrawTransformOriginGizmo` render coordinate axes and orientation indicators using `LineDrawingScope` and `Handles.DotHandleCap`.
- `PositionHandle2d`, `RotationHandle2d`, and `ScaleHandle2d` provide immediate 2D GUI handles with mouse tracking and `HandleConstraint2D` masking.

```csharp
        public struct PointDrawingScope : IDisposable
        {
            Color m_Color;
            CompareFunction m_ZTest;
            bool m_IsDisposed;
            Mesh m_Mesh;
            List<Vector3> m_Points;
            List<int> m_Indices;
            Matrix4x4 m_Matrix;

            public Color color
            {
                get { return m_Color; }
                set
                {
                    End();
                    m_Color = value;
                    Begin();
                }
            }

            public CompareFunction zTest
            {
                get { return m_ZTest; }

                set
                {
                    End();
                    m_ZTest = value;
                    Begin();
                }
            }

            public Matrix4x4 matrix
            {
                get { return m_Matrix; }
                set { m_Matrix = value; }
            }

            public PointDrawingScope(Color color, CompareFunction zTest = CompareFunction.LessEqual)
            {
                m_Color = color;
                m_ZTest = zTest;
                m_IsDisposed = false;
                m_Mesh = meshPool.Dequeue();
                m_Points = new List<Vector3>(64);
                m_Indices = new List<int>(64);
                m_Matrix = Matrix4x4.identity;
                Begin();
            }

            void Begin()
            {
                vertMaterial.SetColor("_Color", color);
                vertMaterial.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)zTest);

                if (!vertMaterial.SetPass(0))
                    throw new Exception("Failed initializing vertex material.");

                m_Points.Clear();
            }

            void End()
            {
                m_Mesh.Clear();

                if (BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported)
                {
                    for (int i = 0, c = m_Points.Count; i < c; ++i)
                        m_Indices.Add(i);

                    m_Mesh.SetVertices(m_Points);

                    m_Mesh.SetIndices(m_Indices, MeshTopology.Points, 0, false);
                }
                else
                {
                    MeshHandles.CreatePointBillboardMesh(m_Points, m_Mesh);
                }

                Graphics.DrawMeshNow(m_Mesh, m_Matrix, 0);
            }

            public void Dispose()
            {
                if (m_IsDisposed)
                    return;

                m_IsDisposed = true;

                End();

            Mesh m_LineMesh;
            List<Vector3> m_Positions;
            List<Vector4> m_Tangents;
            List<Color> m_Colors;
            List<int> m_Indices;

            public Color color

                    End();
                m_Color = color;
                if (!m_Wire)
                    Begin();

            {

            public LineDrawingScope(Color color, float thickness = -1f, CompareFunction zTest = CompareFunction.LessEqual)
                : this(color, Matrix4x4.identity, thickness, zTest) { }

            public LineDrawingScope(Color color, Matrix4x4 matrix, float thickness = -1f, CompareFunction zTest = CompareFunction.LessEqual)
            {
                m_LineMesh = meshPool.Dequeue();
                m_IsDisposed = false;
                m_Matrix = matrix;
                m_Color = color;
                m_Thickness = thickness < 0f ? s_EdgeLineSize : thickness;
                m_ZTest = zTest;

                m_Positions = new List<Vector3>(4);
                m_Tangents = new List<Vector4>(4);
                m_Colors = new List<Color>(4);
                m_Indices = new List<int>(4);

                m_Wire = m_Thickness < k_MinLineWidthForGeometryShader || lineMaterial == null;
                m_LineTopology = m_Wire || BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported;

                Begin();
            }

            void Begin()
            {
                if (!m_Wire)
                {
                    lineMaterial.SetColor("_Color", color);
                    lineMaterial.SetFloat("_Scale", thickness * EditorGUIUtility.pixelsPerPoint);
                    lineMaterial.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)zTest);
                }

                if (m_Wire || !lineMaterial.SetPass(0))
                    HandleUtility.ApplyWireMaterial(zTest);
            }

            void End()
            {
                m_LineMesh.Clear();
                m_LineMesh.SetVertices(m_Positions);
                if(m_Wire)
                    m_LineMesh.SetColors(m_Colors);
                else
                    m_LineMesh.SetTangents(m_Tangents);
                m_LineMesh.subMeshCount = 1;
                m_LineMesh.SetIndices(m_Indices, m_LineTopology ? MeshTopology.Lines : MeshTopology.Quads, 0);

            CompareFunction m_ZTest;

                faceMaterial.SetFloat("_HandleZTest", (int)zTest);

                GL.Vertex(b);
                GL.Vertex(c);

### COLORS

ProBuilder defines an extensive color and size preference system for selection, wireframes, preselection, and interactive gizmos.

1. User Preferences and Settings Keys (`EditorHandleDrawing.cs`):
- `s_UseUnityColors`: `Pref<bool>("graphics.handlesUseUnityColors", true, SettingsScope.User)` determines whether to use Unity editor theme colors or user custom colors.
- `s_DitherFaceHandle`: `Pref<bool>("graphics.ditherFaceHandles", true, SettingsScope.User)` enables face overlay checkerboard dithering.
- `s_XRayView`: `Pref<bool>("graphics.xRayView", true, SettingsScope.User)` enables see-through rendering for occluded selected elements.
- `s_SelectedFaceColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userSelectedFaceColor", new Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Cyan: `RGBA(0.0, 0.824, 0.937, 1.0)`).
- `s_WireframeColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userWireframeColor", new Color(125f / 255f, 155f / 255f, 185f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (`RGBA(0.490, 0.608, 0.725, 1.0)`).
- `s_UnselectedEdgeColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userUnselectedEdgeColor", new Color(44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Dark Charcoal: `RGBA(0.173, 0.173, 0.173, 1.0)`).
- `s_SelectedEdgeColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userSelectedEdgeColor", new Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Cyan: `RGBA(0.0, 0.824, 0.937, 1.0)`).
- `s_UnselectedVertexColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userUnselectedVertexColor", new Color(44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 44f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Dark Charcoal: `RGBA(0.173, 0.173, 0.173, 1.0)`).
- `s_SelectedVertexColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userSelectedVertexColor", new Color(0f, 210f / 255f, 239f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Cyan: `RGBA(0.0, 0.824, 0.937, 1.0)`).
- `s_PreselectionColorPref`: `Pref<Color>("graphics.userPreselectionColor", new Color(179f / 255f, 246f / 255f, 255f / 255f, 1f), SettingsScope.User)` (Ice Blue: `RGBA(0.702, 0.965, 1.0, 1.0)`).

2. Builtin Color Constants:
- `k_OccludedTint`: `new Color(.75f, .75f, .75f, 1f)` (Occlusion multiplier for X-Ray rendering).
- `k_VertexUnselectedDefault`: `new Color(.7f, .7f, .7f, 1f)` (Light gray default unselected vertex color when Unity colors active).
- `k_WireframeDefault`: `new Color(94.0f / 255.0f, 119.0f / 255.0f, 155.0f / 255.0f, 1f)` (Slate blue: `RGBA(0.369, 0.467, 0.608, 1.0)`).
- `BuiltinMaterials.previewColor`: `new Color(.5f, .9f, 1f, .56f)` (Cyan tint for shape generation and tool previews).

3. 2D Handle GUI Color Constants (`EditorHandleUtility.cs`):
- `k_HandleColorUp`: `new Color(0f, .7f, 0f, .8f)` (Y-axis green).
- `k_HandleColorRight`: `new Color(0f, 0f, .7f, .8f)` (X-axis blue).
- `k_HandleColorRotate`: `new Color(0f, .7f, 0f, .8f)` (Rotation circle green).
- `k_HandleColorScale`: `new Color(.7f, .7f, .7f, .8f)` (Center scale square light gray).

4. Size Preferences and Metrics:
- `s_WireframeLineSize`: `Pref<float>("graphics.wireframeLineSize", .5f, SettingsScope.User)` (slider range 0f to 10f).
- `s_EdgeLineSize`: `Pref<float>("graphics.edgeLineSize", 1f, SettingsScope.User)` (slider range 0f to 10f).
- `s_VertexPointSize`: `Pref<float>("graphics.vertexPointSize", 3f, SettingsScope.User)` (slider range 1f to 10f).
- `k_MinLineWidthForGeometryShader`: `0.01f` (threshold below which GL lines are forced).
- `k_DefaultGizmoSize`: `0.2f`.
- `dotCapSize`: `s_VertexPointSize * .0125f`.

5. Runtime Color Resolvers:
- `wireframeColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? k_WireframeDefault : s_WireframeColorPref`.
- `faceSelectedColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? Handles.selectedColor : s_SelectedFaceColorPref`.
- `preselectionColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? Handles.preselectionColor : s_PreselectionColorPref`.
- `edgeSelectedColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? Handles.selectedColor : s_SelectedEdgeColorPref`.
- `edgeUnselectedColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? k_WireframeDefault : s_UnselectedEdgeColorPref`.
- `vertexSelectedColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? Handles.selectedColor : s_SelectedVertexColorPref`.
- `vertexUnselectedColor`: `s_UseUnityColors ? k_VertexUnselectedDefault : s_UnselectedVertexColorPref`.

## G02: Shaders for picking and overlay rendering

### FACE HIGHLIGHT SHADER

The face highlight shader (`Hidden/ProBuilder/FaceHighlight`) renders selection highlights, hover overlays, and GL wireframe faces on top of geometry. The shader defines four properties: `_Color` (`Color Tint`, default `(1,1,1,1)`), `_Dither` (`Dithering`, float, default `0`), `_HandleZTest` (`Int`, default `8` which corresponds to `UnityEngine.Rendering.CompareFunction.Always`), and `_HandleZWrite` (`Int`, default `0` for depth-write disabled).

SubShader Configuration:
- Tags: `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `Queue="Transparent"`.
- Fixed Function State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest [_HandleZTest]`, `ZWrite [_HandleZWrite]`, `Cull Off`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`.
- Culling is disabled (`Cull Off`) so both front and back faces are highlighted when selected. Alpha blending computes `FinalColor = _Color.rgb * _Color.a + DestColor.rgb * (1.0 - _Color.a)`.

Vertex Program (`vert`):
- Vertex struct `appdata` receives `float4 vertex : POSITION`.
- Vertex transformation invokes `UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffset(v.vertex.xyz)` from `ProBuilderCG.cginc`. This function transforms local coordinates into view space via `UnityObjectToViewPos(pos)`, applies depth scaling (`ret.xyz *= lerp(.99, 1, unity_OrthoParams.w)` and `ret.z *= lerp(1, 0.95, unity_OrthoParams.w)`), and multiplies by `UNITY_MATRIX_P` to output clip position `o.pos` pulled slightly toward the camera to eliminate z-fighting with the underlying mesh geometry.

Fragment Program (`frag`):
- When dithering is enabled (`_Dither > 0`), the fragment program evaluates a screen-space checkerboard dither mask on `i.pos.xy`:
  1. `i.pos.xy = floor(i.pos.xy * 1) * .5;`
  2. `float checker = -frac(i.pos.x + i.pos.y);`
  3. `clip(lerp(1, checker, _Dither));`
- When `_Dither == 0`, `lerp(1, checker, 0) == 1 >= 0`, no pixels are discarded and the overlay renders as a solid tinted fill. When `_Dither == 1`, `checker` is negative for pixels where `frac(i.pos.x + i.pos.y) > 0`, discarding alternating pixels in a 2x2 grid pattern.
- Returns `_Color`.

Related unlit overlay shaders:
- `ProBuilder/Unlit Solid Color` (`UnlitSolidColor.shader`): Tags `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `Queue="Transparent"`, `Lighting Off`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Back`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`. Outputs uniform `_Color` via standard `UnityObjectToClipPos(v.vertex)`.
- `ProBuilder/UnlitVertexColor` (`UnlitVertexColor.shader`): Tags `Queue="Transparent"`, `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `RenderType="Transparent"`, `Lighting Off`, `ZTest LEqual`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Off`. Pass-through `v.color` in `vert` and outputs `i.color` in `frag`.

### LINE BILLBOARD

Line billboard shaders render mesh wireframes, edge selection highlights, and guide outlines with constant screen-space pixel width `_Scale`. ProBuilder provides two implementations: `Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboard` (geometry shader path for DX11/GL) and `Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboardMetal` (vertex extrusion path for platforms without geometry shaders such as Apple Metal).

1. Geometry Shader Line Expansion (`LineBillboard.shader`):
- SubShader Tags: `"ProBuilderPicker"="EdgePass"`, `"RenderType"="Geometry"`, `"Queue"="Geometry"`, `"DisableBatching"="True"`, `"ForceNoShadowCasting"="True"`, `"IgnoreProjector"="True"`.
- State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest [_HandleZTest]`, `ZWrite [_HandleZWrite]`, `Cull Off`, `Blend Off`, `Offset -1, -1`. Target `#pragma target 4.0`, excludes Metal renderer (`#pragma exclude_renderers metal`).
- Vertex Program (`vert`): Converts position to view space `float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(v.vertex.xyz), 1)`, pulls closer to camera by scaling `o.pos *= .99`, projects to clip space `mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, o.pos)`, and transforms clip coordinates to screen-space pixel coordinates `ClipToScreen(o.pos)`.
- Geometry Program (`geo`): Takes a line segment `line v2f p[2]` in screen space and computes a perpendicular normal vector: `float2 perp = normalize(float2(-(p[1].pos.y - p[0].pos.y), p[1].pos.x - p[0].pos.x)) * _Scale`. Generates a 4-vertex triangle strip quad connecting `p[1] + perp`, `p[1] - perp`, `p[0] + perp`, `p[0] - perp`, transformed back to clip coordinates via `ScreenToClip(float4)`. Emits `maxvertexcount(4)` vertices into `TriangleStream<v2f> triStream`.
- Fragment Program (`frag`): Returns `i.color * _Color`.

2. Metal & Non-Geometry Fallback Line Expansion (`LineBillboardMetal.shader`):
- Used when `BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported` is `false`.
- Mesh Data Generation (`MeshHandles.CreateEdgeBillboardMesh`): For every edge `(a, b)`, four vertices are constructed as a quad with `MeshTopology.Quads`. Vertices 0 and 1 are located at position `a` with tangents `(b.x, b.y, b.z, +1.0)` and `(b.x, b.y, b.z, -1.0)`. Vertices 2 and 3 are located at position `b` with tangents `(c.x, c.y, c.z, +1.0)` and `(c.x, c.y, c.z, -1.0)`, where `c = b + (b - a)` represents the extended direction vector.
- Vertex Program (`vert` in `LineBillboardMetal.shader`): Transforms `v.vertex.xyz` to clip coordinates with offset `UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffsetMetal(v.vertex.xyz)`. Projects both the current vertex and the tangent target vertex `v.tangent.xyz` into screen coordinates `a = ClipToScreen(o.pos)` and `b = ClipToScreen(UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffset(v.tangent.xyz))`. Calculates the screen-space direction vector `d = normalize(b - a).xy` and perpendicular vector `p = float2(-d.y, d.x)`. Shifts the screen position `a.xy += p * v.tangent.w * _Scale` and maps back to clip space `o.pos = ScreenToClip(a)`.
- Fragment Program (`frag`): Returns `_Color`.

                // pull closer to camera and into clip space
                o.pos *= .99;
                o.pos = mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, o.pos);
                // convert clip -> ndc -> screen, build billboards in geo shader, then screen -> ndc -> clip
                o.pos = ClipToScreen(o.pos);

                geo_out.color = p[0].color;

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, geometry shaders are not supported in Vulkan standard shader passes. The vertex expansion technique used in `LineBillboardMetal.shader` (generating 4 vertices per line segment in `MeshTopology.Quads` / `PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES` and expanding screen-space perpendiculars in the vertex shader) is the exact recommended approach for screen-space wireframe and line rendering in Godot 4.

### POINT BILLBOARD

Point billboard shaders render individual mesh vertices as screen-space square dot handles facing the camera. ProBuilder implements two techniques: `Hidden/ProBuilder/PointBillboard` (geometry shader path expanding points into quads) and `Hidden/ProBuilder/VertexShader` (vertex shader quad expansion fallback).

1. Geometry Shader Point Expansion (`PointBillboard.shader`):
- Tags: `"ProBuilderPicker"="VertexPass"`, `"RenderType"="Geometry"`, `"Queue"="Geometry"`, `"IgnoreProjector"="True"`, `"ForceNoShadowCasting"="True"`, `"DisableBatching"="True"`.
- State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest [_HandleZTest]`, `ZWrite [_HandleZWrite]`, `Cull Off`, `Blend Off`, `Offset 0, -2`.
- Mesh Data: Prepared by `MeshHandles.CreatePointMesh` with `MeshTopology.Points` containing 1 vertex per point position.
- Vertex Program (`vert`): Converts object coordinate to view position `float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(v.vertex.xyz), 1)`. Scales coordinates by `lerp(1, .95, ORTHO)` where `#define ORTHO (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3])` to bias depth. Projects to clip space and converts to screen coordinates via `ClipToScreen(output.pos)`.
- Geometry Program (`geo`): Takes a single point `point GS_INPUT p[1]` and outputs 4 vertices (`maxvertexcount(4)`) forming a screen-space rectangle centered at `(p[0].pos.x, p[0].pos.y)`:
  - Vertex 0 (bottom-right): `(p[0].pos.x + _Scale, p[0].pos.y - _Scale, p[0].pos.z, p[0].pos.w - ScreenDepthModifier)`
  - Vertex 1 (top-right): `(p[0].pos.x + _Scale, p[0].pos.y + _Scale, p[0].pos.z, p[0].pos.w - ScreenDepthModifier)`
  - Vertex 2 (bottom-left): `(p[0].pos.x - _Scale, p[0].pos.y - _Scale, p[0].pos.z, p[0].pos.w - ScreenDepthModifier)`
  - Vertex 3 (top-left): `(p[0].pos.x - _Scale, p[0].pos.y + _Scale, p[0].pos.z, p[0].pos.w - ScreenDepthModifier)`
  - Screen depth modifier `#define ScreenDepthModifier (lerp(.00001, 0, ORTHO))` offsets the depth in perspective projections. Converts each vertex back to clip space with `ScreenToClip(float4)` and appends to `triStream`.
- Fragment Program (`frag`): Outputs `_Color * input.color`.

2. Vertex Quad Dot Expansion (`VertexShader.shader`):
- Used when `BuiltinMaterials.geometryShadersSupported` is `false` (referenced as `BuiltinMaterials.dotShader`).
- Mesh Data: Prepared by `MeshHandles.CreatePointBillboardMesh`. For each point, four vertices are created at identical 3D positions, with `TEXCOORD0` (`texcoord`) storing corner offsets: `k_Billboard0 = (-1f, -1f)`, `k_Billboard1 = (-1f, 1f)`, `k_Billboard2 = (1f, -1f)`, `k_Billboard3 = (1f, 1f)`. Triangle index order is `[i*4+0, i*4+1, i*4+3, i*4+2]` (`MeshTopology.Quads`).
- Vertex Program (`vert` in `VertexShader.shader`):
  1. `o.pos = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(v.vertex.xyz), 1);`
  2. `o.pos.xyz *= lerp(.99, .95, ortho);` where `ortho = (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3])`.
  3. `o.pos = mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, o.pos);`
  4. Converts to screen coordinates: `clip.xy /= clip.w; clip.xy = clip.xy * .5 + .5; clip.xy *= _ScreenParams.xy;`
  5. Expands screen position by corner offset: `clip.xy += v.texcoord.xy * _Scale;`
  6. Converts back to clip coordinates: `clip.xy /= _ScreenParams.xy; clip.xy = (clip.xy - .5) / .5; clip.xy *= clip.w;`
- Fragment Program (`frag`): Returns `_Color`.

            v2f vert (appdata v)
            {
                float ortho = (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3]);
                v2f o;

                o.pos = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(v.vertex.xyz), 1);
                o.pos.xyz *= lerp(.99, .95, ortho);
                o.pos = mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, o.pos);

                // convert vertex to screen space, add pixel-unit xy to vertex, then transform back to clip space.
                float4 clip = o.pos;

                clip.xy /= clip.w;
                clip.xy = clip.xy * .5 + .5;
                clip.xy *= _ScreenParams.xy;

                clip.xy += v.texcoord.xy * _Scale;
                clip.xy /= _ScreenParams.xy;
                clip.xy = (clip.xy - .5) / .5;
                clip.xy *= clip.w;

                o.pos = clip;

                return o;
            }

### PICKER SHADERS

ProBuilder performs element picking (faces, edges, vertices) by rendering an offscreen lookup texture using specialized picker shaders where every pickable element's unique index is encoded into RGBA vertex colors.

1. Color Encoding & Decoding Algorithm (`SelectionPickerRenderer.EncodeRGBA` & `DecodeRGBA`):
- A 24-bit unsigned integer ID is packed into RGB channels with alpha fixed to 255 (1.0).
- Little-Endian Encoding:
  - `r = (byte)((hash >> 16) & 0xFF)`
  - `g = (byte)((hash >> 8) & 0xFF)`
  - `b = (byte)(hash & 0xFF)`
  - `a = 255`
- Little-Endian Decoding:
  - `uint hash = ((uint)color.r << 16) | ((uint)color.g << 8) | (uint)color.b;`
- Hash ID allocation conventions:
  - `k_PickerHashNone = 0x00` (Background / clear color / no selection).
  - `k_PickerHashMin = 0x01` (Face picking begins at index 0, where `EncodeRGBA(0)` maps to `(0,0,0,255)` with `a=255` distinct from background).
  - Vertex and edge picking begin at `index = 0x02` to avoid black/zero ambiguity.
  - Maximum addressable elements: `k_PickerHashMax = 0x00FFFFFF` (16,777,215 elements per picker pass).

2. Selection Picker Master Shader (`SelectionPicker.shader` / `SelectionPickerURP.shader`):
- Contains 3 subshaders tagged with `"ProBuilderPicker"`:
  - SubShader with `"ProBuilderPicker"="EdgePass"` -> `UsePass "Hidden/ProBuilder/EdgePicker/EDGES"`
  - SubShader with `"ProBuilderPicker"="VertexPass"` -> `UsePass "Hidden/ProBuilder/VertexPicker/VERTICES"`
  - SubShader with `"ProBuilderPicker"="Base"` -> `UsePass "Hidden/ProBuilder/FacePicker/BASE"`
- In Built-in pipeline, `SelectionPickerRendererStandard` invokes `renderCam.RenderWithShader(BuiltinMaterials.selectionPickerShader, "ProBuilderPicker")`. Unity replaces object shaders matching the tag `"ProBuilderPicker"` with the corresponding SubShader pass.

3. Individual Picker Shaders:
- `Hidden/ProBuilder/FacePicker` (`FacePicker.shader`): Tags `"ProBuilderPicker"="Base"`, `"LightMode"="Always"`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Back`, `Blend Off`. Vertex shader runs `o.pos = UnityObjectToClipPos(v.vertex); o.color = v.color;`. Fragment shader returns `i.color`.
- `Hidden/ProBuilder/EdgePicker` (`EdgePicker.shader`): Tags `"ProBuilderPicker"="EdgePass"`, `"LightMode"="Always"`, `"IgnoreProjector"="True"`, `"DisableBatching"="True"`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Off`, `Blend Off`. Pass uses `AlphaTest Greater .25`. Vertex shader calls `o.pos = UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffset(v.vertex.xyz)`. Fragment shader returns `i.color`.
- `Hidden/ProBuilder/VertexPicker` (`VertexPicker.shader`): Tags `"ProBuilderPicker"="VertexPass"`, `"RenderType"="Transparent"`, `"LightMode"="Always"`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Off`, `Blend Off`, `Offset -1, -1`. Mesh has 4 vertices per shared vertex index with UV2 offsets (`t_uv2[0] = -up - right`, `t_uv2[1] = -up + right`, `t_uv2[2] = up - right`, `t_uv2[3] = up + right`). Vertex shader computes `o.pos = GetPickerColor(o.pos, v.texcoord1)` which expands the vertex quad in screen space by 3.5 pixels (`clip.xy += texcoord1.xy * 3.5; clip.z -= .0001 * (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3]);`).

4. Standard vs URP Picker Shader Differences:
- Language: Standard shaders use CG/HLSL blocks with `UnityCG.cginc` and `ProBuilderCG.cginc`. URP variants (`FacePickerURP.shader`, `EdgePickerURP.shader`, `VertexPickerURP.shader`, `SelectionPickerURP.shader`) use HLSL blocks with `Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl` and `ProBuilderCG_URP.hlsl`.
- Pipeline Tags: URP subshaders declare `"RenderPipeline"="UniversalPipeline"` and `PackageRequirements { "com.unity.render-pipelines.universal": "17.0" }`. Pass tag is `"LightMode"="ProBuilderPickerA"`.
- Edge Picker Alpha Test: Standard uses fixed-function `AlphaTest Greater .25`. URP shader executes manual discard in fragment shader: `clip(input.color.a - 0.75);`.
- Coordinate Transforms: Standard uses `UnityObjectToViewPos` / `UnityObjectToClipPos`. URP uses `GetVertexPositionInputs(input.positionOS.xyz)` (`positions.positionVS`, `positions.positionCS`).
- Fallback: URP shaders include explicit fallbacks (`Fallback "Hidden/ProBuilder/FacePicker"`, `Fallback "Hidden/ProBuilder/EdgePicker"`, `Fallback "Hidden/ProBuilder/VertexPicker"`).
- Render Execution: In URP, `SelectionPickerRendererURP` injects `URPSelectionPickerPass` (`ScriptableRenderPass` at `RenderPassEvent.AfterRendering`) with `ShaderTagId("ProBuilderPickerA")` to render elements into the temporary picker `RenderTexture`.

        /// <summary>
        /// Decodes Color32.RGB values to a 32-bit unsigned int, using the RGB as the little bytes. Discards the hi byte (alpha).
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="color">The color to decode.</param>
        /// <returns>32-bit unsigned int containing the decoded RGB values.</returns>
        public static uint DecodeRGBA(Color32 color)
        {
            uint r = (uint)color.r;
            uint g = (uint)color.g;
            uint b = (uint)color.b;

            if (System.BitConverter.IsLittleEndian)
                return r << 16 | g << 8 | b;
            else
                return r << 24 | g << 16 | b << 8;
        }

### TRANSPARENT OVERLAY

The transparent overlay shader (`Hidden/ProBuilder/TransparentOverlay`) renders texture mapping previews, texture UV overlays, and interactive drag overlays directly on top of model surfaces.

1. Shader Properties & Render State (`TransparentOverlay.shader`):
- Properties: `_MainTex ("Texture", 2D) = "white" {}`.
- Tags: `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `RenderType="Transparent"`, `Queue="Transparent"`.
- Fixed Function State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Back`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`.
- Alpha blending evaluates `FinalColor = TextureColor * VertexColor * Alpha + DestColor * (1.0 - Alpha)`.

2. Vertex & Fragment Processing:
- Vertex input `appdata` accepts `float4 vertex : POSITION`, `float4 color : COLOR`, `float4 texcoord0 : TEXCOORD0`.
- Vertex output `v2f` passes `float4 pos : SV_POSITION`, `float4 color : COLOR`, `float2 uv : TEXCOORD0`.
- Vertex transformation: `o.pos = UnityObjectToClipPos(v.vertex); o.uv = v.texcoord0.xy; o.color = v.color;`.
- Fragment processing: Samples the main texture and modulates by vertex color: `return tex2D(_MainTex, i.uv) * i.color;`.

3. Vertex Culling Utility (`HideVertices.shader`):
- Shader `Hidden/ProBuilder/HideVertices` collapses all vertex geometry to zero clip coordinates: `o.pos = fixed4(0,0,0,0);`.
- Render State: `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `RenderType="Geometry"`, `Lighting Off`, `ZTest On`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Back`.
- Fragment shader outputs `return fixed4(0,0,0,0);`.
- Used by ProBuilder when certain submesh elements or temporary geometry must be completely culled from rendering without removing indices or reallocating vertex buffers.

### NORMAL PREVIEW

The normal preview shader (`Hidden/ProBuilder/NormalPreview`) visualizes vertex and surface normal directions as 3D colored vector arrows extending from mesh vertices during smoothing group editing or normal inspection.

1. Shader Configuration (`NormalPreview.shader`):
- Tags: `Queue="AlphaTest"`, `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `RenderType="Geometry"`.
- State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest LEqual`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Off`.
- Uniform Property: `float _Scale;` controls the world-space extrusion length of the normal vectors. In `SmoothGroupEditor.cs`, scale is computed per frame as `normalPreviewMaterial.SetFloat("_Scale", s_NormalsSize * HandleUtility.GetHandleSize(trs.GetComponent<MeshRenderer>().bounds.center))`.

2. Mesh Geometry Construction (`SmoothGroupEditor.RebuildNormalsMesh`):
- For each source vertex `i` (up to `ushort.MaxValue / 2`), two vertices `a = i * 2` (arrow base) and `b = i * 2 + 1` (arrow tip) are constructed:
  - `positions[a] = srcPositions[i]`, `positions[b] = srcPositions[i]` (both initially share the vertex local position).
  - `tangents[a] = Vector4(normal.x, normal.y, normal.z, 0f)` (base has extrusion factor `w = 0f`).
  - `tangents[b] = Vector4(normal.x, normal.y, normal.z, 1f)` (tip has extrusion factor `w = 1f`).
  - Indices: `indexes[a] = a`, `indexes[b] = b` with `MeshTopology.Lines`.

3. Vertex Transformation & Normal Coloring Algorithm:
- Vertex shader reads the normal vector packed into `v.tangent.xyz` and the extrusion weight in `v.tangent.w`:
  1. Transforms local vertex position to world space: `float4 world = mul(unity_ObjectToWorld, v.vertex);`.
  2. Transforms tangent normal to world-space normal direction: `float3 nrm = UnityObjectToWorldNormal(v.tangent.xyz);`.
  3. Extrudes the tip along the world normal: `float4 extruded = world + float4((nrm * v.tangent.w * _Scale), 0);`.
  4. Multiplies by view-projection matrix: `o.pos = mul(UNITY_MATRIX_VP, extruded);`.
  5. Color encoding: `o.color = float4(abs(v.tangent.xyz), 1);`. Taking the absolute value of the local normal coordinates maps normal directions directly to RGB space (X normals appear Red, Y normals appear Green, Z normals appear Blue).
- Fragment shader returns the interpolated normal color `return i.color;`.

            struct appdata

                float4 tangent : TANGENT;

            {
                float4 pos : SV_POSITION;
                float4 color : COLOR;

                float4 world = mul(unity_ObjectToWorld, v.vertex);
                float3 nrm = UnityObjectToWorldNormal(v.tangent.xyz);

                o.color = float4(abs(v.tangent.xyz), 1);

### SMOOTHING PREVIEW

The smoothing preview shader (`Hidden/ProBuilder/SmoothingPreview`) renders face surfaces with distinct color tints corresponding to their assigned smoothing group IDs, with configurable opacity and optional screen-space dithering.

1. Shader Properties & Uniforms (`SmoothingPreview.shader`):
- Property: `_Opacity ("Opacity", Float) = .5`.
- Uniforms: `float _Opacity;` and `float _Dither;`.
- Tags: `IgnoreProjector="True"`, `RenderType="Geometry"`.
- Fixed Function State: `Lighting Off`, `ZTest LEqual`, `ZWrite On`, `Cull Back`, `Blend SrcAlpha OneMinusSrcAlpha`.

2. Mesh Preparation (`SmoothGroupEditor.RebuildPreviewMesh`):
- Iterates over all active smoothing groups (`smoothGroup.Key > Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone`).
- Generates a distinct pseudo-random color for each group ID: `Color32 color = GetDistinctColor(smoothGroup.Key)`.
- Assigns vertex colors `colors32[i] = color` for all vertex indices belonging to faces within the smoothing group.

3. Vertex Program (`vert` in `SmoothingPreview.shader`):
- Transforms vertex to view space: `o.pos = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(v.vertex.xyz), 1);`.
- Depth bias: `o.pos.xyz *= .98;` pulls the smoothing preview geometry 2% closer to the camera in view space to avoid z-fighting with the underlying model.
- Projects to clip coordinates: `o.pos = mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, o.pos);`.
- Passes vertex color: `o.color = v.color;`.

4. Fragment Program (`frag` in `SmoothingPreview.shader`):
- Dither pattern calculation:
  1. `i.pos.xy = floor(i.pos.xy * 1) * .5;`
  2. `float checker = -frac(i.pos.x + i.pos.y);`
  3. `clip(lerp(1, checker, _Dither));`
- When `_Dither` is `0`, all pixels are retained. When `_Dither` is `1`, pixels are discarded in an alternating 2x2 grid.
- Alpha modulation: Multiplies vertex color alpha by the opacity factor `half4 c = half4(i.color.rgb, i.color.a * _Opacity); return c;`.

### COMMON CG INCLUDE

The common shader include file `ProBuilderCG.cginc` (and its URP counterpart `ProBuilderCG_URP.hlsl`) provides shared helper macros, coordinate transformations, and depth-offset algorithms across all ProBuilder shaders.

1. Camera Mode Macros & Constants:
- `#define ORTHO (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3])`: In standard projection matrices, `UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3]` is `0.0` for perspective projections and `1.0` for orthographic projections. Therefore `ORTHO` evaluates to `1.0` in perspective mode and `0.0` in orthographic mode.
- `const float ORTHO_CAM_OFFSET = .0001;`: Defines the depth bias pulled toward the camera in orthographic mode to resolve depth contention.

2. Coordinate Space Transformation Functions:
- `inline float4 ClipToScreen(float4 v)`: Converts homogeneous clip-space position `[-w, w]` into screen-space pixel coordinates `[0, _ScreenParams.x] x [0, _ScreenParams.y]`:
  1. `v.xy /= v.w;` (perspective divide to NDC `[-1, 1]`)
  2. `v.xy = v.xy * .5 + .5;` (maps NDC `[-1, 1]` to normalized UV coordinates `[0, 1]`)
  3. `v.xy *= _ScreenParams.xy;` (scales normalized UVs to pixel dimensions)
- `inline float4 ScreenToClip(float4 v)`: Inverts screen pixel coordinates back into homogeneous clip coordinates:
  1. `v.z -= ORTHO_CAM_OFFSET * ORTHO;` (applies camera depth offset in orthographic mode)
  2. `v.xy /= _ScreenParams.xy;` (normalizes pixels to `[0, 1]`)
  3. `v.xy = (v.xy - .5) / .5;` (maps `[0, 1]` to NDC `[-1, 1]`)
  4. `v.xy *= v.w;` (multiplies by clip `w` component to recover clip coordinates)

3. Depth Offset & Z-Fighting Prevention Functions:
- `inline float4 UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffset(float3 pos)`: Transforms local position `pos` to clip space with adaptive depth biasing based on projection type (`unity_OrthoParams.w`):
  - View position: `float4 ret = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(pos), 1);`
  - In perspective (`unity_OrthoParams.w == 0`): scales view vector `ret.xyz *= 0.99` to pull edges 1% closer to the eye without shifting screen positions.
  - In orthographic (`unity_OrthoParams.w == 1`): leaves `ret.xyz` unscaled and pulls depth component `ret.z *= 0.95` closer by 5%.
  - Projects: `return mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, ret);`.
- `inline float4 UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffsetMetal(float3 pos)`: Metal-specific implementation applying `ret *= lerp(.99, .95, ORTHO)` prior to multiplying by `UNITY_MATRIX_P`.
- `inline float4 GetPickerColor(float4 pos, float2 texcoord1)`: Used in vertex picker shaders (`VertexPicker.shader` / `VertexPickerURP.shader`). Converts clip position `pos` to screen pixel coordinates, expands the billboard by `texcoord1.xy * 3.5` pixels, applies orthographic depth offset `clip.z -= .0001 * (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3])`, and transforms back to clip space.

<details><summary>Source Evidence</summary>

**../probuilder-ref/Content/Shader/ProBuilderCG.cginc:1-35**
```csharp
// Is the camera in orthographic mode? (1 yes, 0 no)
#define ORTHO (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3])

// How far to pull vertices towards camera in orthographic mode
const float ORTHO_CAM_OFFSET = .0001;

inline float4 ClipToScreen(float4 v)
{
    v.xy /= v.w;
    v.xy = v.xy * .5 + .5;
    v.xy *= _ScreenParams.xy;
    return v;
}

inline float4 ScreenToClip(float4 v)
{
    v.z -= ORTHO_CAM_OFFSET * ORTHO;
    v.xy /= _ScreenParams.xy;
    v.xy = (v.xy - .5) / .5;
    v.xy *= v.w;
    return v;
}

inline float4 UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffset(float3 pos)
{
    float4 ret = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(pos), 1);
    //Offsetting the edges to avoid z-fighting problems
	//Do not offset when using orthographic camera as XY are
    //screen coords, this would shift the rendering
    ret.xyz *= lerp(.99, 1, unity_OrthoParams.w);
    //Moving edges closer
	//.99 is not sufficient for Orthographic Camera
    ret.z *= lerp(1, 0.95, unity_OrthoParams.w);
    return mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, ret);
}
```

**../probuilder-ref/Content/Shader/ProBuilderCG.cginc:37-61**
```csharp
inline float4 UnityObjectToClipPosWithOffsetMetal(float3 pos)
{
    float4 ret = float4(UnityObjectToViewPos(pos), 1);
    ret *= lerp(.99, .95, ORTHO);
    return mul(UNITY_MATRIX_P, ret);
}

inline float4 GetPickerColor(float4 pos, float2 texcoord1)
{
    // convert vertex to screen space, add pixel-unit xy to vertex, then transform back to clip space.
    float4 clip = pos;

    clip.xy /= clip.w;
    clip.xy = clip.xy * .5 + .5;
    clip.xy *= _ScreenParams.xy;

    clip.xy += texcoord1.xy * 3.5;
    clip.z -= .0001 * (1 - UNITY_MATRIX_P[3][3]);

    clip.xy /= _ScreenParams.xy;
    clip.xy = (clip.xy - .5) / .5;
    clip.xy *= clip.w;

    return clip;
}
```

</details>

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4 shaders, camera mode is tested via `PROJECTION_MATRIX[3][3] == 1.0` (orthographic). Screen-to-clip and clip-to-screen transformations use `VIEWPORT_SIZE` and `INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX`. Depth bias can be applied via `POSITION.z -= bias` in clip coordinates or setting `render_priority` on materials.
