# Interaction & Undo

## K01: Interaction toggles, undo, editor styles, hierarchy, drag-and-drop

### HANDLE ORIENTATION TOGGLE: Cycles World → ActiveObject → ActiveElement. How it affects gizmo rendering and transform application.

The `ToggleHandleOrientation` action (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ToggleHandleOrientation`) is a `MenuAction` within `ToolbarGroup.Selection` with `toolbarPriority = 0`. It provides single-click and shortcut ('P') cycling between three coordinate orientation modes defined by the `HandleOrientation` enum: `HandleOrientation.World` (0), `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject` (1), and `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement` (2).

### Orientation Modes and Tooltips
- **World** (`HandleOrientation.World`): Displays icon `Modes/ToolHandleGlobal`. Tooltip title `"Global"`, description `"The transform handle is oriented in a fixed direction."` The scene gizmo remains fixed along world Cartesian axes ($X, Y, Z$) regardless of mesh rotation or element normals.
- **ActiveObject** (`HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`): Displays icon `Modes/ToolHandleLocal`. Tooltip title `"Local"`, description `"The transform handle is aligned with the active object rotation."` The gizmo matches the active target `Transform.rotation`.
- **ActiveElement** (`HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`): Displays icon `Modes/ToolHandleElement`. Tooltip title `"Element"`, description `"The transform handle is aligned with the active element selection."` The gizmo aligns to the normal and tangent basis of the active face, edge, or vertex group.

### Execution and Synchronization Pipeline
1. **Menu Action Invocation** (`PerformActionImplementation`):
   - Cycles to the next enum value via `handleOrientation = InternalUtility.NextEnumValue(handleOrientation)`.
   - Invokes `VertexManipulationTool.handleOrientation = value`, followed by `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh(false)`.
   - Returns `ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Success, "Set Handle Orientation\n" + k_Tooltips[(int)handleOrientation].title)`.
2. **State Storage and Unity Pivot Synchronization** (`VertexManipulationTool.cs`):
   - Persisted across sessions via `Pref<HandleOrientation> s_HandleOrientation = new Pref<HandleOrientation>("editor.handleOrientation", HandleOrientation.World, SettingsScope.User)`.
   - In the `handleOrientation` property setter:
     - When setting `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`, sets Unity's native `Tools.pivotRotation = PivotRotation.Local`.
     - When setting `HandleOrientation.World`, sets Unity's native `Tools.pivotRotation = PivotRotation.Global`.
     - When setting `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`, leaves Unity's native `Tools.pivotRotation` untouched.
     - Caches `s_PivotRotation = Tools.pivotRotation`.
     - Calls `MeshSelection.InvalidateCaches()`.
     - Fires `pivotRotationChanged?.Invoke()`.
     - Repaints the Unity editor toolbar via reflection (`UnityEditor.Toolbar.RepaintToolbar`).
     - Fires `handleOrientationChanged?.Invoke()`.
   - In the `handleOrientation` property getter, executes `SyncPivotRotation()`: if Unity's native `Tools.pivotRotation` was changed by the user in the main toolbar, synchronizes `s_HandleOrientation` to `ActiveObject` (for `PivotRotation.Local`) or `World` (for `PivotRotation.Global`).
3. **Gizmo Rendering and Transform Calculations** (`MeshSelection.GetHandleRotation()`):
   - When drawing gizmos or computing vertex translations, rotations, or scaling in `PositionTool`, `RotateTool`, and `ScaleTool`, the active handle rotation is resolved as follows:
     - `HandleOrientation.World`: Returns `Quaternion.identity`.
     - `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`: Returns `active.mesh.transform.rotation`.
     - `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`: Retrieves the last active element group's rotation `active.elementGroups.Last().rotation`. If `active.elementGroups.Count == 0`, falls back to `active.mesh.transform.rotation`.
   - Transform deltas during interactive manipulation are converted from this handle rotation space into world space or local vertex coordinate offsets.

### SELECT BACK FACES: What 'hidden' means - backface culling during selection. How it affects rect select and click select.

The `ToggleSelectBackFaces` action (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ToggleSelectBackFaces`) controls whether ProBuilder includes or filters out obscured geometry and backfacing polygons during selection operations across `SelectMode.Vertex`, `SelectMode.Edge`, `SelectMode.Face`, and `SelectMode.TextureFace`.

### Action Properties and Preferences
- **Toolbar Group and Priority**: `ToolbarGroup.Selection`, priority `1`.
- **Icons**: Dual icons loaded via `IconUtility.GetIcon("Toolbar/Selection_SelectHidden-OFF")` (index 0) and `IconUtility.GetIcon("Toolbar/Selection_SelectHidden-ON")` (index 1).
- **Menu Title**: Dynamically evaluates `ProBuilderEditor.backfaceSelectionEnabled ? "Select Hidden: On" : "Select Hidden: Off"`.
- **Tooltip**: Title `"Set Hidden Element Selection"`, text `"Setting Hidden Element Selection to On allows you to select faces that are either obscured by geometry or facing away from the scene camera (backfaces).\n\nThe default value is On."`
- **Persistence**: Managed by `s_BackfaceSelectEnabled` in `ProBuilderEditor.cs` (`Pref<bool>("editor.backFaceSelectEnabled", true, SettingsScope.User)`).
- **Culling Mode Mapping**: Changing `ProBuilderEditor.backfaceSelectionEnabled` updates `s_Instance.m_ScenePickerPreferences.cullMode = value ? CullingMode.None : CullingMode.Back` and notifies listeners via `backfaceSelectionEnabledChanged`.

### Behavioral Difference in Selection Algorithms
1. **Click Selection (Raycasting)**:
   - In `EditorSceneViewPicker.cs`, `FaceRaycast` executes `HandleUtility.FaceRaycast(ray, mesh, out hit, Mathf.Infinity, pickerOptions.cullMode)`.
   - When `cullMode` is `CullingMode.Back` (Select Hidden: Off), raycasts test triangle winding against ray direction. If $\vec{N} \cdot \vec{D} > 0$ (triangle faces away from camera), the intersection is culled.
   - When `cullMode` is `CullingMode.None` (Select Hidden: On), raycasts hit both front-facing and back-facing polygons, returning the closest geometric collision.
2. **Rect Selection (Frustum / Marquee Drag)**:
   - Rect selection maps `cullMode == CullingMode.Back` to `options.depthTest = true` in `EditorSceneViewPicker.cs`.
   - **Depth Test Enabled (Select Hidden: Off)**:
     - For `RectSelectMode.Partial`: ProBuilder executes an offscreen GPU color-picker pass (`SelectionPickerRenderer`) that renders mesh elements to a custom `RenderTexture` with depth testing enabled. Only pixels that pass the Z-buffer test are read back, preventing occluded backfaces from being selected.
     - For `RectSelectMode.Complete`: ProBuilder projects all element vertices to 2D screen space and verifies rect containment, then tests element center occlusion using `!HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, centerPoint)`.
   - **Depth Test Disabled (Select Hidden: On)**:
     - ProBuilder skips the GPU render pass entirely. It transforms every vertex into 2D camera viewport coordinates (`cam.WorldToScreenPoint` / `cam.ScreenToGuiPoint`) and checks 2D rectangle containment mathematically. All elements falling inside the drag box are selected regardless of camera distance, occlusion by foreground geometry, or surface normal direction.

### X-RAY TOGGLE: What X-ray mode does visually. How it affects selection (makes all elements selectable regardless of occlusion).

The `ToggleXRay` action (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ToggleXRay`) controls the visual depth rendering of selected sub-mesh geometry in the Scene view. It is assigned the shortcut `Alt + Shift + X` (`keyCommandAlt`, `keyCommandShift`, `'x'`) and operates across `SelectMode.Vertex`, `SelectMode.Edge`, `SelectMode.Face`, and `SelectMode.TextureFace`.

### Action Configuration and State
- **Toolbar Visibility**: `hidden = true` (accessed primarily via main menu or keyboard shortcut `Alt + Shift + X`).
- **Menu Title**: `EditorHandleDrawing.xRay ? "X-Ray: On" : "X-Ray: Off"`.
- **Tooltip**: Title `"Toggle X-Ray View"`, text `"When enabled, selected mesh elements that are occluded by geometry will be rendered with a faded appearance."`
- **Preference Property**: Stored in `EditorHandleDrawing.cs` as `Pref<bool> s_XRayView = new Pref<bool>("graphics.xRayView", true, SettingsScope.User)`.
- **Action Execution**: `PerformActionImplementation` toggles `EditorHandleDrawing.xRay = !EditorHandleDrawing.xRay; SceneView.RepaintAll();` and returns `ActionResult(ActionResult.Status.Success, "Set X-Ray Vision\n" + (EditorHandleDrawing.xRay ? "On" : "Off"))`.

### Visual Rendering Mechanism (`EditorHandleDrawing.cs`)
During Scene view repaint passes in `EditorHandleDrawing.OnSceneGUI`:
1. **Unselected Elements Pass**: Wireframes, unselected edges, and unselected vertices are rendered with depth test `CompareFunction.LessEqual`.
2. **Occluded Selection Pass (X-Ray Pass)**:
   - If `EditorHandleDrawing.xRay` is `true`, ProBuilder issues a dedicated rendering call for selected elements (`s_SelectedEdgeHandles`, `s_SelectedFaceHandles`, or `s_SelectedVertexHandles`).
   - This pass uses depth comparison `CompareFunction.Greater`, targeting only fragments that lie behind opaque scene geometry.
   - The draw call applies an occluded tint multiplier `k_OccludedTint = new Color(0.75f, 0.75f, 0.75f, 1f)`:
     - Edges: `Render(s_SelectedEdgeHandles, edgeMaterial, edgeSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater)`
     - Faces: `Render(s_SelectedFaceHandles, s_FaceMaterial, faceSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater)`
     - Vertices: `Render(s_SelectedVertexHandles, s_VertMaterial, vertexSelectedColor * k_OccludedTint, CompareFunction.Greater, false)`
3. **Visible Selection Pass**:
   - Issues a final draw call for selected elements with `CompareFunction.LessEqual` using unmodified selection colors (`edgeSelectedColor`, `faceSelectedColor`, `vertexSelectedColor`).

### Architectural Distinction from Selection Toggles
`ToggleXRay` is strictly a visual feedback mechanism. It ensures that elements that are currently selected remain perceptible to the user even when hidden behind occluding geometry by rendering them with a dimmed tint. Selection inclusion of obscured elements during drag/click picking is governed separately by `ToggleSelectBackFaces`.

### DRAG RECT MODE: Partial vs Complete intersection toggle.

The `ToggleDragRectMode` action (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ToggleDragRectMode`) toggles the geometric criteria used to evaluate whether edges and faces inside a scene view marquee selection box are selected.

### Action Properties and Select Modes
- **Toolbar Group and Priority**: `ToolbarGroup.Selection`, priority `0`.
- **Valid Select Modes**: Enabled only when `SelectMode.Edge`, `SelectMode.Face`, or `SelectMode.TextureFace` is active (`SelectMode.Vertex` does not use partial intersection since a vertex is a 0D point).
- **Icons**: `Toolbar/DragSelect_Off` (for `RectSelectMode.Partial`), `Toolbar/DragSelect_On` (for `RectSelectMode.Complete`).
- **Menu Title**: `mode == RectSelectMode.Complete ? "Rect: Complete" : "Rect: Intersect"`.
- **Tooltip**: Title `"Set Drag Rect Mode"`, description `"Sets whether or not a mesh element (edge or face) needs to be completely encompassed by a drag to be selected.\n\nThe default value is Intersect, meaning if any part of the elemnent is touched by the drag rectangle it will be selected."`
- **Enum Values**: `RectSelectMode.Partial` (0) and `RectSelectMode.Complete` (1).
- **Persistence**: Managed by `s_DragSelectRectMode` in `ProBuilderEditor.cs` (`Pref<RectSelectMode>("editor.dragSelectRectMode", RectSelectMode.Partial, SettingsScope.User)`).

### Mathematical Intersection Algorithms (`SelectionPicker.cs`)
1. **Face Selection** (`SelectionPicker.PickFacesInRect`):
   - **Complete Mode** (`RectSelectMode.Complete`):
     - Evaluates all distinct vertex screen points `screenPoints[index]` for each face `face`.
     - Rejects the face if any vertex lies behind the camera (`screenPoints[index].z < cam.nearClipPlane`).
     - Verifies that every distinct vertex index in `face.distinctIndexesInternal` satisfies `rect.Contains(screenPoints[index])`. If a single vertex falls outside the rectangle, the face is rejected.
     - If depth testing is active, additionally verifies `!HandleUtility.PointIsOccluded(cam, pb, trs.TransformPoint(Math.Average(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal)))`.
   - **Partial / Intersect Mode** (`RectSelectMode.Partial`):
     - Builds a 2D bounding box `Bounds2D poly = new Bounds2D(screenPoints, face.edgesInternal)`.
     - Tests broadphase `poly.Intersects(rect)`.
     - Tests three narrowphase conditions in sequence:
       1. *Vertex in Rect*: Checks if any vertex `p` satisfies `p.z > cam.nearClipPlane && rect.Contains(p)`.
       2. *Rect Corner in Polygon*: Evaluates 4 marquee corners ($tl, tr, bl, br$) against the face polygon via `Math.PointInPolygon(screenPoints, poly, face.edgesInternal, corner)`.
       3. *Edge-Edge Intersection*: Iterates all face edges and checks 2D segment intersection with the 4 rect boundaries via `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect`.
     - If any test succeeds, the face is added to selection.
2. **Edge Selection** (`SelectionPicker.PickEdgesInRect`):
   - **Complete Mode**: Both endpoints $a$ and $b$ must project in front of near clip and both satisfy `rect.Contains(a) && rect.Contains(b)`.
   - **Partial Mode**: Evaluates segment-rect intersection via `Math.RectIntersectsLineSegment(rect, a, b)`. If the segment crosses any boundary or is contained inside, the edge is selected.

### UNDO: RegisterCompleteObjectUndo usage. How ProBuilder tracks undo for mesh changes. What state is captured.

The `UndoUtility` class (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.UndoUtility`) provides the undo/redo tracking infrastructure for all ProBuilder operations, bridging Unity's `UnityEditor.Undo` engine with `ProBuilderMesh` components.

### Undo/Redo Callback and Synchronization
`UndoUtility` is marked `[InitializeOnLoad]` and subscribes to `Undo.undoRedoEvent += UndoRedoEventCallback` in its static constructor:
- During drag operations (`SceneDragAndDropListener.isDragging == true`), callbacks return immediately to prevent redundant mesh generation on intermediate preview frames.
- Otherwise, it queries `Selection.GetFiltered<ProBuilderMesh>(SelectionMode.TopLevel)` and wraps each target in `using (new ProBuilderMesh.NonVersionedEditScope(mesh)) EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh);` to update Unity's native `MeshFilter.sharedMesh` without dirtying version timestamps.
- Calls `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()` to refresh handles and inspector state.

### Complete Object vs Property Diffing (The 256 Vertex Rule)
Unity's default `Undo.RecordObject(s)` inspects serialized property diffs across arrays. On high-density meshes, serialized diffing causes significant main-thread latency. `UndoUtility` enforces an explicit optimization threshold:
- **Meshes $\le 256$ vertices**: Uses `Undo.RecordObject(pb, msg)` or `Undo.RecordObjects(pb, msg)`.
- **Meshes $> 256$ vertices**: Automatically switches to `Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(pb, msg)` or `Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(Object[], msg)`.
- `RecordMeshAndTransformSelection(string message)`: Creates a composite array containing all selected `ProBuilderMesh` instances and their associated `Transform` components (`new Object[count * 2]`), registering the entire array via `Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo` to record geometric and transform modifications simultaneously in a single atomic record.

### Interactive Preview Scopes
For tools requiring interactive undoable previews (such as shape generation or material dragging):
- `StartPreview()`: Checks if an existing preview is open (`s_PreviewGroupIndex != -1`), reverts it via `Undo.RevertAllDownToGroup(s_PreviewGroupIndex)`, and records the current group index `s_PreviewGroupIndex = Undo.GetCurrentGroup()`.
- `UndoPreview()`: Calls `Undo.RevertAllDownToGroup(s_PreviewGroupIndex)` to purge intermediate preview states from the redo stack, resetting `s_PreviewGroupIndex = -1`.
- `ExitAndValidatePreview()`: Sets `s_PreviewGroupIndex = -1`, committing the preview actions.

### Captured Mesh State
When `RegisterCompleteObjectUndo` captures a `ProBuilderMesh`, Unity serializes all private and internal backing fields, including:
- `Vector3[] m_Positions`: Vertex positions in local space.
- `Face[] m_Faces`: Array of constituent faces with index buffers, smoothing groups, auto-UV settings, manual UVs, submesh indexes, and texture group flags.
- `SharedVertex[] m_SharedVertices`: Coincident vertex index sets defining hard/soft topology.
- `SharedVertex[] m_SharedTextures`: Coincident UV seam topology.
- `Color[] m_Colors`: Per-vertex color assignments.
- `Vector4[] m_Tangents` and `Vector3[] m_Normals`: Cached vertex tangents and normal vectors.
- `Material[] m_Materials`: Assigned material references per submesh.

```csharp
        static UndoUtility()
        {
            Undo.undoRedoEvent += UndoRedoEventCallback;
        }

        static void UndoRedoEventCallback(in UndoRedoInfo info)
        {
            // material preview when dragging in scene-view is done by applying then undoing changes. we don't want to
            // rebuild the mesh every single frame when dragging.
            if (SceneDragAndDropListener.isDragging)
                return;

            foreach (var mesh in Selection.GetFiltered<ProBuilderMesh>(SelectionMode.TopLevel))
            {
                using (new ProBuilderMesh.NonVersionedEditScope(mesh))
                        EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh);
            }

            ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();
        }
```

```csharp
        /**
         * Record an object for Undo.
         */
        public static void RecordObject(Object obj, string msg)
        {
            if (obj is ProBuilderMesh && ((ProBuilderMesh)obj).vertexCount > 256)
            {
#if PB_DEBUG
                Debug.LogWarning("RecordObject()  ->  " + ((pb_Object)obj).vertexCount);
#endif
                RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(obj as ProBuilderMesh, msg);
            }
            else
            {
                Undo.RecordObject(obj, msg);
            }
        }

        /**
         * Record objects for Undo.
         */
        public static void RecordObjects(IEnumerable<Object> objs, string msg)
        {
            if (objs == null)
                return;

            Object[] obj = objs.Where(x => !(x is ProBuilderMesh)).ToArray();
            ProBuilderMesh[] pb = objs.OfType<ProBuilderMesh>().ToArray();

            if (obj.Length > 0)
                Undo.RecordObjects(obj, msg);

            RecordSelection(pb, msg);
        }
```

### EDITOR SNAPPING: How ProBuilder's own snapping wraps Unity/ProGrids snapping.

The `EditorSnapping` static class (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.EditorSnapping`) implements grid and increment snapping for ProBuilder manipulation tools (`PositionTool`, `RotateTool`, `ScaleTool`), providing a unified interface that mediates between Unity's built-in snapping (`EditorSnapSettings`, `GridSettings`) and the external `ProGrids` package.

### Enums and Settings
- `SnapAxis`:
  - `ActiveAxis` (0): When modifying vertices, snap positions only along the axis currently being dragged.
  - `AllAxes` (1): When modifying vertices, snap vertex positions along all Cartesian axes simultaneously.
- `SnapMode`:
  - `None` (0): Snapping disabled.
  - `Relative` (1): Incremental snapping relative to starting transform/position.
  - `World` (2): Absolute snapping to global grid lines.
- User Settings (`SettingsScope.User`):
  - `s_SnapAsGroup`: `Pref<bool>("ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAsGroup", true)`. When enabled, selected elements maintain their relative spacing and offsets when snapping. When disabled, every element snaps to the grid independently.
  - `s_SnapAxis`: `Pref<SnapAxis>("ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAxis", SnapAxis.ActiveAxis)`.

### Snapping Resolution Pipeline
1. **Snap Mode Evaluation** (`EditorSnapping.snapMode`):
   - Checks `EditorSnapSettings.incrementalSnapActive`: if true, returns `SnapMode.Relative`.
   - Else checks `ProGridsInterface.SnapEnabled() || (EditorSnapSettings.gridSnapActive && Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Global)`: if true, returns `SnapMode.World`.
   - Otherwise returns `SnapMode.None`.
2. **ProGrids Delegation**:
   - `snapAsGroup`: If `ProGridsInterface.IsActive()` is true, queries `ProGridsInterface.GetSnapAsGroup()`; otherwise reads `s_SnapAsGroup.value`.
   - `snapMethod`: If `ProGridsInterface.IsActive()` is true, queries `ProGridsInterface.GetSnapMethod()`; otherwise reads `s_SnapAxis.value`.
3. **Active Snap Value Resolution**:
   - **Movement** (`activeMoveSnapValue`):
     - `SnapMode.Relative`: Returns `EditorSnapSettings.move` (`Vector3`).
     - `SnapMode.World`: If ProGrids is active, returns `ProGridsInterface.SnapValue() * Vector3.one`; otherwise returns `GridSettings.size` (`Vector3`).
     - `SnapMode.None`: Returns `Vector3.zero`.
   - **Scale** (`activeScaleSnapValue`):
     - `SnapMode.Relative` or `SnapMode.World`: Returns `Vector3.one * EditorSnapSettings.scale`.
     - `SnapMode.None`: Returns `Vector3.zero`.
   - **Rotation** (`activeRotateSnapValue`):
     - `SnapMode.Relative` or `SnapMode.World`: Returns `EditorSnapSettings.rotate` (`float`).
     - `SnapMode.None`: Returns `0f`.
4. **Snapping Math Wrappers**:
   - `MoveSnap(float value)`: Returns `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(value, activeMoveSnapValue.x)` (where `Snap(val, snap)` computes `snap * Mathf.Round(val / snap)`).
   - `MoveSnap(Vector3 value)`: Returns `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(value, activeMoveSnapValue)`.
   - `RotateSnap(float value)`: Returns `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(value, activeRotateSnapValue)`.
   - `ScaleSnap(Vector3 value)`: Returns `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(value, Vector3.one * activeRotateSnapValue)`.

### HIERARCHY LISTENER: What happens when objects are reparented, duplicated, deleted in the hierarchy.

The `HierarchyListener` static class (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.HierarchyListener`) monitors scene hierarchy modifications, assembly reloads, and prefab lifecycle events to ensure `ProBuilderMesh` components maintain unique internal state and valid `MeshFilter` synchronization.

### Subscriptions and Event Stream Processing
Marked with `[InitializeOnLoad]`, its static constructor registers listeners for:
- `AssemblyReloadEvents.afterAssemblyReload += OnAfterAssemblyReload;`
- `PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceUpdated += PrefabInstanceUpdated;`
- `PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceReverted += PrefabInstanceUpdated;`
- `PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceReverting += PrefabInstanceReverting;`
- `ProBuilderMesh.meshWasInitialized += OnMeshInitialized;`
- `ObjectChangeEvents.changesPublished += ObjectEventChangesPublished;`

### Handling Duplication, Reparenting, and Hierarchy Changes
In `ObjectEventChangesPublished(ref ObjectChangeEventStream stream)`:
1. **GameObject Creation and Structure Changes** (`ObjectChangeKind.CreateGameObjectHierarchy`, `ObjectChangeKind.ChangeGameObjectStructure`):
   - Resolves target GameObject via `GetGameObject(data)`.
   - Invokes `CheckForProBuilderMeshesCreatedOrModified(go)`, which traverses the transform tree recursively.
   - For every `ProBuilderMesh` encountered, invokes `OnObjectCreated(mesh)`.
2. **Duplication and Copy/Paste Detection** (`OnObjectCreated`):
   - Compares the serialized version index with the non-serialized version index:
     `mesh.versionIndex != ProBuilderMesh.k_UnitializedVersionIndex && mesh.nonSerializedVersionIndex == ProBuilderMesh.k_UnitializedVersionIndex`
   - When an object is duplicated or pasted, Unity clones its serialized data (so `versionIndex` is initialized), but non-serialized fields are reset to defaults (`k_UnitializedVersionIndex`).
   - On detecting this state:
     - Calls `mesh.MakeUnique()`, which allocates a new distinct `UnityEngine.Mesh` instance and deep-copies index arrays.
     - Registers undo: `Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo(mesh.gameObject, "Paste ProBuilderMesh")`.
     - Calls `mesh.Optimize()`.
3. **Hierarchy Restructuring** (`ObjectChangeKind.ChangeGameObjectStructureHierarchy`):
   - Occurs during Prefab Replace or structural hierarchy edits.
   - Retrieves all child `ProBuilderMesh` components via `go.GetComponentsInChildren<ProBuilderMesh>()` and synchronizes their `MeshFilter` instances via `EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh)`.
   - Invokes `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

### Prefab Revert and Update Handling
- `PrefabInstanceReverting(GameObject go)`: To prevent Unity mesh memory leaks when reverting prefabs (before the serialized reference `m_Mesh` is reset to null), iterates all `ProBuilderMesh` components in the hierarchy and calls `mesh.DestroyUnityMesh()`.
- `PrefabInstanceUpdated(GameObject go)`: If the editor is not in play mode, iterates all child meshes, calls `EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh)`, `mesh.Rebuild()`, `mesh.Optimize()`, and `ProBuilderEditor.Refresh()`.

### Gizmo Icon Suppression
In `OnAfterAssemblyReload()`, queues a deferred call `EditorApplication.delayCall += () => EditorUtility.SetGizmoIconEnabled(typeof(ProBuilderMesh), false);`. This suppresses drawing the component's gizmo icon in the Scene view while preserving the inspector icon metadata.

<details><summary>Source Evidence</summary>

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/HierarchyListener.cs:13-60**
```csharp
        static HierarchyListener()
        {
            AssemblyReloadEvents.afterAssemblyReload += OnAfterAssemblyReload;
            PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceUpdated += PrefabInstanceUpdated;
            PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceReverted += PrefabInstanceUpdated;
            PrefabUtility.prefabInstanceReverting += PrefabInstanceReverting;
            ProBuilderMesh.meshWasInitialized += OnMeshInitialized;
            ObjectChangeEvents.changesPublished += ObjectEventChangesPublished;
        }

        static void ObjectEventChangesPublished(ref ObjectChangeEventStream stream)
        {
            for (int i = 0, c = stream.length; i < c; ++i)
            {
                var type = stream.GetEventType(i);

                if (type == ObjectChangeKind.CreateGameObjectHierarchy)
                {
                    stream.GetCreateGameObjectHierarchyEvent(i, out var data);
                    var go = GetGameObject(data);
                    if (go != null) CheckForProBuilderMeshesCreatedOrModified(go);
                }
                else if (type == ObjectChangeKind.ChangeGameObjectStructure)
                {
                    stream.GetChangeGameObjectStructureEvent(i, out var data);
                    var go = GetGameObject(data);
                    if (go != null) CheckForProBuilderMeshesCreatedOrModified(go);
                }
                else if (type == ObjectChangeKind.ChangeGameObjectStructureHierarchy)
                {
                    // Note 2 : This needs to be called when using a Prefab>Replace action in the menus to refresh the current
                    // ProBuilder Mesh, this is still a problem in 2023.3 as it does not automatically refresh the mesh
                    // Note 1 : that this is leaking meshes when reverting! in 2023.1+ we handle it correctly, but 2022 and
                    // 2021 have the PPtr reset to the serialized value (null) before we have any access. orphaned
                    // mesh assets are cleaned up on scene or domain reloads, so we'll live with it.
                    stream.GetChangeGameObjectStructureHierarchyEvent(i, out var data);
                    var go = GetGameObject(data);

                    if (go != null)
                    {
                        var meshes = go.GetComponentsInChildren<ProBuilderMesh>();
                        foreach (var mesh in meshes)
                            EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh);
                    }
                    ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();
                }
            }
        }
```

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/HierarchyListener.cs:79-101**
```csharp
        static void CheckForProBuilderMeshesCreatedOrModified(GameObject go)
        {
            if(go.TryGetComponent<ProBuilderMesh>(out var mesh))
                OnObjectCreated(mesh);
            var childCount = go.transform.childCount;
            if (childCount > 0)
            {
                for(int childIndex = 0; childIndex < childCount; ++childIndex)
                    CheckForProBuilderMeshesCreatedOrModified(go.transform.GetChild(childIndex).gameObject);
            }
        }

        // used by tests
        internal static void OnObjectCreated(ProBuilderMesh mesh)
        {
            if (mesh.versionIndex != ProBuilderMesh.k_UnitializedVersionIndex &&
                mesh.nonSerializedVersionIndex == ProBuilderMesh.k_UnitializedVersionIndex)
            {
                mesh.MakeUnique();
                Undo.RegisterCompleteObjectUndo( mesh.gameObject, "Paste ProBuilderMesh");
                mesh.Optimize();
            }
        }
```

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/HierarchyListener.cs:108-139**
```csharp
        static void OnAfterAssemblyReload()
        {
            // The inspector icon for ProBuilderMesh is set in the component metadata. However, this also serves as the
            // scene view gizmo icon, which we do not want. To avoid drawing an icon for every mesh in the Scene View,
            // we simply tell the AnnotationManager to not render the icon. This _does_ put ProBuilderMesh in the
            // "Recently Changed" list, but only when it is modified the first time.
            // The alternative method of setting an icon is to place it in a folder named "Editor Default Resources/Icons",
            // however that requires that the resources directory be in "Assets", which we do not want to do.
            EditorApplication.delayCall += () => EditorUtility.SetGizmoIconEnabled(typeof(ProBuilderMesh), false);
        }

        static void PrefabInstanceReverting(GameObject go)
        {
            // revert will leak meshes unless we clean up before ProBuilderMesh.m_Mesh is set to null
            foreach (var mesh in go.GetComponentsInChildren<ProBuilderMesh>())
                mesh.DestroyUnityMesh();
        }

        static void PrefabInstanceUpdated(GameObject go)
        {
            if (EditorApplication.isPlayingOrWillChangePlaymode)
                return;

            foreach (var mesh in go.GetComponentsInChildren<ProBuilderMesh>())
            {
                EditorUtility.SynchronizeWithMeshFilter(mesh);
                mesh.Rebuild();
                mesh.Optimize();
            }

            ProBuilderEditor.Refresh();
        }
```

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, scene hierarchy events can be monitored by connecting to `SceneTree.node_added`, `SceneTree.node_removed`, and `SceneTree.node_renamed`. When duplicating a custom mesh node in Godot, ensure `ArrayMesh` resources are duplicated (`mesh.duplicate(true)`) so multiple nodes do not inadvertently share the same mesh instance.

### DRAG AND DROP: Material/texture drag onto ProBuilder faces.

The `SceneDragAndDropListener` static class (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.SceneDragAndDropListener`) intercepts Scene view drag-and-drop events during `SceneView.duringSceneGui` to enable real-time material previews and targeted face material assignment.

### Lifecycle and Preview Mesh Setup
- `[InitializeOnLoad]` initializes static delegates and constructs `s_PreviewMesh` with `HideFlags.HideAndDontSave` and name `"pb_DragAndDropListener::PreviewMesh"`.
- Cleans up `s_PreviewMesh` via `UObject.DestroyImmediate` on `AssemblyReloadEvents.beforeAssemblyReload`.
- Exposes `isDragging` (`s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop`), which is checked by `UndoUtility` to suspend heavy mesh rebuilds during drag events.

### Material and Texture Resolution (`GetMaterialFromDragReferences`)
When assets are dragged into the Scene view from the Project Browser:
1. Inspects `DragAndDrop.objectReferences` for an existing `Material` instance.
2. If a `Texture2D` is dragged and `createMaterialForTexture` is true:
   - Queries default material shader via reflection (`Material.GetDefaultMaterial`) or falls back to `Shader.Find("Standard")`.
   - Instantiates a new `Material`, assigns `mat.mainTexture = tex`.
   - Generates a unique asset path `<texture_path_without_extension>.mat` via `AssetDatabase.GenerateUniqueAssetPath`.
   - Saves the material to disk using `AssetDatabase.CreateAsset(mat, texPath)` and refreshes the asset database.
   - Returns the created `Material`.

### Scene GUI Interaction States (`OnSceneGUI`)
1. **DragUpdated**:
   - Sets `s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop = true`.
   - Raycasts object under cursor via `HandleUtility.PickGameObject(evt.mousePosition, out submeshIndex)`.
   - Calls `SetMeshPreview(go.GetComponent<ProBuilderMesh>())`:
     - Checks `isFaceMode` (`SelectMode.Face | SelectMode.TextureFace`). If face mode is active, `s_PreviewMaterial != null`, and `mesh.selectedFaceCount > 0`, enables `s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled = true`.
     - Populates `s_PreviewMesh` with vertex positions, vertex colors, normals, and UVs from the target mesh.
     - Sets `s_PreviewMesh.triangles = mesh.selectedFacesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.indexes).ToArray()`.
     - Stores `s_Matrix = mesh.transform.localToWorldMatrix`.
   - If face override is active, sets `DragAndDrop.visualMode = DragAndDropVisualMode.Copy` and consumes the event via `evt.Use()`.
2. **Repaint**:
   - When `s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled` is true, calls `s_PreviewMaterial.SetPass(0)` and draws the preview mesh at `s_Matrix` via `Graphics.DrawMeshNow(s_PreviewMesh, s_Matrix, 0)`.
3. **DragPerform**:
   - Sets `s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop = false`.
   - If `s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled` is true:
     - Records undo states: `UndoUtility.RecordObject(s_CurrentPreview, "Set Face Material")` and `UndoUtility.RecordObject(s_CurrentPreview.renderer, "Set Face Material")`.
     - Applies material to selected faces: `s_CurrentPreview.SetMaterial(s_CurrentPreview.selectedFacesInternal, s_PreviewMaterial)`.
     - Cleans up empty submesh slots: `InternalMeshUtility.FilterUnusedSubmeshIndexes(s_CurrentPreview)`.
     - Rebuilds mesh components: `s_CurrentPreview.ToMesh()`, `s_CurrentPreview.Refresh()`, `s_CurrentPreview.Optimize()`.
     - Consumes event via `evt.Use()`.
   - Resets preview via `SetMeshPreview(null)`.
4. **DragExited**:
   - Cleans up preview state and resets `s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop = false`.

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/SceneDragAndDropListener.cs:79-117**
```csharp
        static Material GetMaterialFromDragReferences(UObject[] references, bool createMaterialForTexture)
        {
            Material mat = references.FirstOrDefault(x => x is Material) as Material;

            if (!createMaterialForTexture || mat != null)
                return mat;

            Texture2D tex = references.FirstOrDefault(x => x is Texture2D) as Texture2D;
            string texPath = tex != null ? AssetDatabase.GetAssetPath(tex) : null;

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(texPath))
            {

                var defaultMaterial = GetDefaultMaterial();

                if (defaultMaterial == null)
                    mat = new Material(Shader.Find("Standard"));
                else
                    mat = new Material(defaultMaterial.shader);

                if (mat.shader == null)
                {
                    UObject.DestroyImmediate(mat);
                    return null;
                }

                mat.mainTexture = tex;

                int lastDot = texPath.LastIndexOf(".", StringComparison.InvariantCulture);
                texPath = texPath.Substring(0, texPath.Length - (texPath.Length - lastDot));
                texPath = AssetDatabase.GenerateUniqueAssetPath(texPath + ".mat");
                AssetDatabase.CreateAsset(mat, texPath);
                AssetDatabase.Refresh();

                return mat;
            }

            return null;
        }
```

**../probuilder-ref/Editor/EditorCore/SceneDragAndDropListener.cs:119-151**
```csharp
        static void SetMeshPreview(ProBuilderMesh mesh)
        {
            if (s_CurrentPreview != mesh)
            {
                s_PreviewMesh.Clear();
                s_CurrentPreview = mesh;

                if (s_CurrentPreview != null)
                {
                    s_PreviewMaterial = GetMaterialFromDragReferences(DragAndDrop.objectReferences, false);
                    s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled = isFaceMode && s_PreviewMaterial != null && mesh.selectedFaceCount > 0;

                    if (s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled)
                    {
                        s_PreviewMesh.vertices = mesh.positionsInternal;

                        if (mesh.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Color))
                            s_PreviewMesh.colors = mesh.colorsInternal;
                        if (mesh.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Normal))
                            s_PreviewMesh.normals = mesh.normalsInternal;
                        if (mesh.HasArrays(MeshArrays.Texture0))
                            s_PreviewMesh.uv = mesh.texturesInternal;

                        s_Matrix = mesh.transform.localToWorldMatrix;
                        s_PreviewMesh.triangles = mesh.selectedFacesInternal.SelectMany(x => x.indexes).ToArray();
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled = false;
                }
            }
        }
```

```csharp
        static void OnSceneGUI(SceneView sceneView)
        {
            var evt = Event.current;

            if (evt.type == EventType.DragUpdated)
            {
                if (!s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop)
                    s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop = true;

                int submeshIndex;
                GameObject go = HandleUtility.PickGameObject(evt.mousePosition, out submeshIndex);

                SetMeshPreview(go != null ? go.GetComponent<ProBuilderMesh>() : null);

                if (s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled)
                {
                    DragAndDrop.visualMode = DragAndDropVisualMode.Copy;
                    evt.Use();
                }
            }
            else if (evt.type == EventType.DragExited)
            {
                if (s_IsFaceDragAndDropOverrideEnabled)
                {
                    DragAndDrop.visualMode = DragAndDropVisualMode.Copy;
                    evt.Use();
                    SetMeshPreview(null);
                }

                s_IsSceneViewDragAndDrop = false;
            }
```

### EDITOR STYLES AND ENUMS: Common UI GUIStyles, Assets, Scene Text Boxes, and Toolbar Enums.

The `EditorStyles` class (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.UI.EditorStyles`) and `EditorEnum.cs` define shared UI visual formatting, custom embedded font resources, texture assets, and toolbar layout enumeration types.

### GUIStyles and Visual Resources (`EditorStyles.cs`)
- **Custom Typography**: Embedded font `"About/Font/Asap-Regular.otf"` loaded via `FileUtility.LoadInternalAsset<Font>(k_FontAsap)` and applied to `s_HeaderLabel`.
- **Color Tokens**: Light and dark skin support (`UnityEditor.EditorGUIUtility.isProSkin`):
  - Pro skin normal text: `Color(0.7f, 0.7f, 0.7f, 1f)`
  - Pro skin hover text: `Color(0.7f, 0.7f, 0.7f, 1f)`
  - Pro skin active text: `Color(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f, 1f)`
  - Personal skin falls back to `Color.black`.
- **Standard GUIStyle Instances**:
  - `buttonStyle`: ProBuilder toolbar and action button styling. Built with 9-slice textures `Toolbar/Background/RoundedRect_Normal`, `RoundedRect_Hover`, `RoundedRect_Pressed`. Configured with `alignment = TextAnchor.MiddleCenter`, 3px border (`RectOffset(3, 3, 3, 3)`), 4px margin/padding, stretch width enabled.
  - `toolbarHelpIcon`: Fixed dimensions 18x18px, zero margin/padding, centered alignment for header help buttons.
  - `settingsGroup`: Background texture `Toolbar/RoundedBorder`, 3px border, 4px margin, padding (4, 4, 4, 6) for indented panel parameter groups.
  - `rowStyle`: Background `EditorGUIUtility.whiteTexture`, 4px margin and padding for alternating list rows.
  - `headerLabel`: Based on `UnityEditor.EditorStyles.boldLabel`, 18pt font size, lower left alignment, Asap font.
  - `sceneTextBox`: Built upon `GUI.skin.box`, background texture `Scene/TextBackground`, 2px border, 4px padding, upper left alignment, `richText = true`, `wordWrap = false`, text color `k_TextColorWhiteNormal`. Used for in-scene dimension and coordinate readouts.

### Editor Enumerations (`EditorEnum.cs`)
- `SceneToolbarLocation`: Defines the anchor position of floating scene view toolbars relative to the Scene view viewport rect:
  - `UpperCenter` (0)
  - `UpperLeft` (1)
  - `UpperRight` (2)
  - `BottomCenter` (3)
  - `BottomLeft` (4)
  - `BottomRight` (5)
- `SelectionRenderState` (`[System.Flags]`):
  - `None = 0x0`: Do not render extra selection indicators.
  - `Wireframe = 0x1`: Render mesh wireframe overlay on selected objects.
  - `Outline = 0x2`: Render selection outline shader around selected objects.

# Topology

## L01: WingedEdge data structure and topology traversal

### WINGED EDGE DATA STRUCTURE

The `WingedEdge` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.WingedEdge`) is the core boundary-representation data structure used for topological analysis, element traversal, edge loop/ring identification, and quad reconstruction across ProBuilder meshes. Each `WingedEdge` instance represents a directed half-edge belonging to a single `Face`, holding directional pointers to adjacent edges within the same polygon and an opposite pointer to the adjacent wing on a neighboring polygon across a shared universal edge.

1. Structural Properties and Fields:
- `edge` (`EdgeLookup`): Stores the directed edge with both local vertex indices (`edge.local.a`, `edge.local.b`) indexing into `ProBuilderMesh.positionsInternal` and universal shared vertex indices (`edge.common.a`, `edge.common.b`) referencing coincident vertex clusters in `ProBuilderMesh.sharedVertexLookup`.
- `face` (`Face`): Reference to the parent polygon face that owns this directed boundary edge.
- `next` (`WingedEdge`): Reference to the next `WingedEdge` in sequence around the face boundary, connected at vertex `edge.local.b` (`edge.y`).
- `previous` (`WingedEdge`): Reference to the preceding `WingedEdge` in sequence around the face boundary, connected at vertex `edge.local.a` (`edge.x`).
- `opposite` (`WingedEdge`): Reference to the coincident `WingedEdge` on an adjacent face sharing the same universal common edge (`edge.common`), or `null` if the edge lies on an open boundary / mesh hole.
- `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary` (`Dictionary<Edge, WingedEdge>`): Static lookup cache cleared and repopulated during topology generation to pair opposite boundary wings across faces.

2. Equality, Hash Codes, and Sequence Methods:
- `Equals(WingedEdge other)` and `Equals(object obj)`: Equality comparison is strictly determined by local edge identity (`edge.local.Equals(other.edge.local)`). Other pointer fields (`face`, `next`, `previous`, `opposite`) are ignored for identity checks.
- `GetHashCode()`: Returns `edge.local.GetHashCode()`, consistent with equality semantics.
- `Count()`: Computes the cycle length of edges comprising the face perimeter by advancing `current = current.next` in a `do-while` loop until looping back to `this`. Returns 3 for triangles, 4 for quads, and N for N-gons.
- `GetAdjacentEdgeWithCommonIndex(int common)`: Evaluates whether `next.edge.common` or `previous.edge.common` contains the specified shared vertex index `common`, returning the matching wing or `null`.

3. Adjacency and Quad Construction Utilities:
- `SortEdgesByAdjacency(Face face)` / `SortEdgesByAdjacency(List<Edge> edges)`: Reorders face edges in-place so each edge's endpoint `edges[i-1].b` matches either endpoint `a` or `b` of the subsequent edge `edges[i]`.
- `GetSpokes(List<WingedEdge> wings)`: Inverts the wing list into a dictionary mapping each common vertex index (`edge.common.a` and `edge.common.b`) to a `List<WingedEdge>` of all wings incident upon that vertex.
- `SortCommonIndexesByAdjacency(List<WingedEdge> wings, HashSet<int> common)`: Filters wings with both endpoints in `common`, verifies the matching count equals `common.Count`, sorts the perimeter edges by adjacency, and returns the ordered common index path.
- `MakeQuad(WingedEdge left, WingedEdge right)`: Evaluates two triangle wings (`left.Count() == 3` and `right.Count() == 3`), gathers 6 `EdgeLookup` entries, verifies exactly 1 common edge is shared (`matches == 1`), extracts the 4 boundary edges (`dup[i] < 1`), chains indices `edges[0].local.a`, `edges[0].local.b`, `quad[2]`, `quad[3]` by matching common index continuity, and returns the 4-vertex quad array `int[4]` or `null` on topology failure.

4. Supporting `Triangle` Struct:
- `Triangle` (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Triangle`): Struct storing serialized indices `m_A`, `m_B`, `m_C` with public accessors `a`, `b`, `c`, `indices`. Implements `IEquatable<Triangle>` with FNV-397 hash code calculation. Provides `IsAdjacent(Triangle other)` by testing containment of directed edges `Edge(a, b)`, `Edge(b, c)`, and `Edge(c, a)`.

> **Godot Note:** In Godot 4, half-edge and winged-edge structures are typically constructed for surface editing operations via GDScript or C++ GDExtension. Godot's built-in `MeshDataTool` maintains internal vertex/edge/face adjacency arrays (`get_edge_vertex`, `get_edge_face`, `get_face_edge`). Implementing `WingedEdge` in C# provides an exact analog to ProBuilder's directional traversal and non-destructive quad assembly.

### TOPOLOGY TRAVERSAL

Topology generation is performed by `WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges`, which constructs a fully linked graph of `WingedEdge` nodes from a `ProBuilderMesh` instance and its constituent `Face` collection.

1. Construction Algorithm in `GetWingedEdges`:
- Input: `ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IEnumerable<Face> faces`, and `bool oneWingPerFace = false`.
- Step 1 (Lookup Initialization): Retrieves `var lookup = mesh.sharedVertexLookup`, mapping local vertex indices to universal shared vertex handles.
- Step 2 (Opposite Dictionary Reset): Clears the static `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary.Clear()` to prepare for edge pairing across faces.
- Step 3 (Face Loop Processing): Iterates through each `Face f` in `faces`:
  - Calls `SortEdgesByAdjacency(f)` to order the face's edges into a contiguous winding sequence `edges` of length `edgeLength`.
  - Initializes pointer anchors `WingedEdge first = null, prev = null`.
  - Loops index `n` from `0` to `edgeLength - 1`:
    - Instantiates a new `WingedEdge w`.
    - Initializes `w.edge = new EdgeLookup(lookup[e.a], lookup[e.b], e.a, e.b)` and `w.face = f`.
    - For the first edge (`n == 0`), records `first = w`.
    - For subsequent edges (`n > 0`), sets intra-face links: `w.previous = prev; prev.next = w;`.
    - For the final edge (`n == edgeLength - 1`), closes the face perimeter loop: `w.next = first; first.previous = w;`.
    - Updates `prev = w`.
    - Opposite Wing Linking: Queries `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary.TryGetValue(w.edge.common, out opp)`:
      - If found: assigns mutual opposite pointers `opp.opposite = w; w.opposite = opp;`.
      - If not found: sets `w.opposite = null;` and registers the edge into `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary.Add(w.edge.common, w);`.
    - Collection Filter: If `!oneWingPerFace || n < 1`, appends `winged.Add(w)`.
- Step 4: Returns `winged` list.

2. Performance Characteristics:
- Time Complexity: $O(E)$ linear time with respect to the total number of edges $E = \sum \text{face.edges.Length}$. Edge sorting within each face takes $O(k^2)$ where $k$ is face degree ($k=3$ for triangles, $k=4$ for quads, giving $O(1)$ constant time per polygon). Shared vertex dictionary lookups and `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary` lookups operate in $O(1)$ average time.
- Space Complexity & Memory Allocation: Allocates 1 `WingedEdge` object instance per face edge (or 1 per face when `oneWingPerFace` is true). Reuses the static `k_OppositeEdgeDictionary` allocation across invocations to minimize GC pressure.
- Manifold vs Non-Manifold Behavior: For 2-manifold surfaces, every internal edge is visited twice and pairs cleanly. For boundary edges, `w.opposite` remains `null`. For non-manifold edges where 3 or more faces meet, the first pair encountered is linked as opposites, while subsequent wings overwrite dictionary entries or remain unlinked to the primary pair.

```csharp
        /// <summary>
        /// Sorts the specified list of edges by adjacency, such that each edge's common Y value matches the next edge's common X value.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="edges">The edges to sort in-place.</param>
        public static void SortEdgesByAdjacency(List<Edge> edges)
        {
            if (edges == null)
                throw new ArgumentNullException("edges");

            for (int i = 1; i < edges.Count; i++)
            {
                int want = edges[i - 1].b;

                for (int n = i + 1; n < edges.Count; n++)
                {
                    if (edges[n].a == want || edges[n].b == want)
                    {
                        Edge swap = edges[n];
                        edges[n] = edges[i];
                        edges[i] = swap;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
```

### WINGED EDGE ENUMERATOR

The `WingedEdgeEnumerator` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.WingedEdgeEnumerator`) implements `IEnumerator<WingedEdge>` to provide forward circular iteration around the boundary edges of a polygon face by following the `WingedEdge.next` pointer chain.

1. State Fields and Lifecycle:
- `m_Start` (`WingedEdge`): References the initial `WingedEdge` where enumeration begins.
- `m_Current` (`WingedEdge`): References the current position in the traversal cycle, initialized to `null`.
- Constructor `WingedEdgeEnumerator(WingedEdge start)`: Assigns `m_Start = start` and sets `m_Current = null`.
- `Reset()`: Resets `m_Current = null`, repositioning the enumerator prior to the first element.
- `Current` (`WingedEdge`): Returns `m_Current`. Throws `InvalidOperationException` if called outside valid range.
- `Dispose()`: No-op implementation satisfying the `IDisposable` interface.

2. Traversal Iteration Flow (`MoveNext`):
- First Call: When `m_Current` is `null`, sets `m_Current = m_Start` and returns `m_Current != null`.
- Subsequent Calls: Advances `m_Current = m_Current.next`.
- Termination Condition: Evaluates `!ReferenceEquals(m_Current, null) && !ReferenceEquals(m_Current, m_Start)`. Traversal halts when the next pointer returns to the starting node `m_Start` or encounters a `null` broken link.
- Cycle Length: For a triangular face, iterates 3 times; for a quad face, iterates 4 times.

3. Vertex Spoke Fan Traversal Pattern (`ElementSelection.GetSpokes` and `NextSpoke`):
- Traversal around a shared vertex pivot is driven by `ElementSelection.GetSpokes(WingedEdge wing, int sharedIndex, bool allowHoles = false)`.
- Uses helper `NextSpoke(WingedEdge wing, int pivot, bool opp)`:
  - When `opp == true`: jumps across faces to `wing.opposite`.
  - When `opp == false`: steps within the same face to `wing.next` (if `wing.next.edge.common.Contains(pivot)`) or `wing.previous` (if `wing.previous.edge.common.Contains(pivot)`).
- `GetSpokes` alternates `opp = !opp` on each step, circulating around the pivot vertex. If an open boundary is hit (`cur == null`) and `allowHoles == true`, it fans in the opposite direction starting from `wing.opposite`, reverses the fragment, and concatenates it to return the complete radial fan of edges.

### ELEMENT SELECTION ALGORITHMS

The `ElementSelection` static class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.ElementSelection`) implements topological selection algorithms including edge rings, edge loops, face rings, face loops, selection growth, flood selection, perimeter element detection, and mesh hole detection.

1. Perimeter Extraction Algorithms:
- `GetPerimeterEdges(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces)`: Collects all constituent face edges `face.edgesInternal`, converts them to universal edges via `mesh.sharedVertexLookup`, and groups them in `Dictionary<Edge, List<Edge>> dup`. Edges belonging to the selection perimeter appear exactly once (`dup[uni].Count < 2`), returning the boundary edge collection.
- `GetPerimeterFaces(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces)`: Maps all face edges to universal edges. Returns all faces containing at least one edge whose universal occurrence count across the selection group is less than 2.
- `GetPerimeterVertices(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int[] indexes, Edge[] universal_edges_all)`: Translates vertex indices to shared handles, counts incident edge connections to other selected vertices, identifies `min` connection count, and selects all vertex indices with `connections[i] <= min`.

2. Edge Ring Traversal (`GetEdgeRing` and `GetEdgeRingIterative`):
- Traversal helper `EdgeRingNext(WingedEdge edge)`: Steps dual pointers `next = edge.next` and `prev = edge.previous` simultaneously around the face boundary until `next == prev` or `next == edge`, incrementing step counter `i`. If `i % 2 == 0` or `next == edge`, returns `null`. For quad faces (4 edges), `next` and `prev` meet at the opposite face edge on step 1, returning the opposite edge across the quad.
- Full Ring Search (`GetEdgeRing`): Builds `wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(pb)`. For each selected edge, walks in forward direction (`cur = EdgeRingNext(cur)` followed by `cur = cur.opposite`) and backward direction (`cur = EdgeRingNext(we.opposite)` followed by `cur = cur.opposite`) until hitting a boundary or already visited edge in `used = HashSet<EdgeLookup>`.
- Iterative Ring Search (`GetEdgeRingIterative`): Traverses exactly 1 step forward and 1 step backward per selected edge.

3. Edge Loop Traversal (`GetEdgeLoop` and `GetEdgeLoopIterative`):
- Algorithm in `GetEdgeLoopInternal(WingedEdge start, int startIndex, HashSet<EdgeLookup> used)`:
  - Tracks current pivot vertex `ind = startIndex`.
  - At each step, queries vertex spokes: `spokes = GetSpokes(cur, ind, true).DistinctBy(x => x.edge.common).ToList()`.
  - Verifies quad-grid valence: If `spokes.Count == 4`, selects the opposite spoke `cur = spokes[2]`, updates pivot vertex `ind = cur.edge.common.a == ind ? cur.edge.common.b : cur.edge.common.a`, and continues until encountering a boundary or a visited edge.
  - If the loop does not close in the forward direction, restarts from `wings[i].edge.common.a` to cover the opposite direction.
- Iterative Loop Search (`GetEdgeLoopInternalIterative`): Adds at most one edge at each extremity (spokes at `edge.a` and `edge.b`).

4. Face Loop and Ring Traversal (`GetFaceLoop`, `GetFaceRingAndLoop`):
- `GetFaceLoop(List<WingedEdge> wings, Face face, bool ring)`: Finds starting wing `start = wings.FirstOrDefault(x => x.face == face)`. If `ring == true`, shifts start to the perpendicular edge `start = start.next ?? start.previous`. Executes 2 passes (`i = 0` for forward direction, `i = 1` starting from `start.opposite` for backward direction). Traverses quad chains (`cur.Count() == 4`) by advancing `cur = cur.next.next.opposite`.

5. Selection Growth and Flood Selection:
- `GrowSelection(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face> faces, float maxAngleDiff = -1f)`: Scans all wings of selected faces using `WingedEdgeEnumerator`. For each boundary wing with `w.opposite != null && !source.Contains(w.opposite.face)`, evaluates normal angle `Vector3.Angle(srcNormal, oppNormal) < maxAngleDiff` (when `maxAngleDiff > 0f`) and appends `w.opposite.face` to the expanded selection.
- `FloodSelection(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IList<Face> faces, float maxAngleDiff)`: Recursively propagates selection across adjacent coplanar or angle-restricted faces using `Flood(pb, opp, oppNormal, maxAngle, selection)`.

6. Hole Detection (`FindHoles` and `FindNextEdgeInHole`):
- Scans `wings` for unvisited boundary edges (`c.opposite == null`).
- Traces boundary perimeter using `FindNextEdgeInHole(it, ind)`: Searches adjacent wing sharing common vertex `next = wing.GetAdjacentEdgeWithCommonIndex(common)`. If `next.opposite != null`, fans through `next.opposite.GetAdjacentEdgeWithCommonIndex(common)` until reaching an open boundary edge (`opposite == null`).
- Detects closed loop points (`splits`) where `wing.edge.common.b == hole[p].edge.common.a`, isolating nested and multi-segment hole boundary loops up to `k_MaxHoleIterations = 2048`.

```csharp
        static WingedEdge EdgeRingNext(WingedEdge edge)
        {
            if (edge == null)
                return null;

            WingedEdge next = edge.next, prev = edge.previous;
            int i = 0;

            while (next != prev && next != edge)
            {
                next = next.next;

                if (next == prev)
                    return null;

                prev = prev.previous;

                i++;
            }

            if (i % 2 == 0 || next == edge)
                next = null;

            return next;
```

### QUAD UTILITY AND DETECTION

The `QuadUtility` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.QuadUtility`) converts triangulated polygon meshes into quadrilateral faces by scoring triangle pairs and merging mutually optimal neighbor pairs.

1. Quad Conversion Pipeline (`ToQuads`):
- Input: `ProBuilderMesh mesh`, `IList<Face> faces`, and `bool smoothing = true`.
- Step 1 (Wing Generation): Constructs winged edge topology `wings = WingedEdge.GetWingedEdges(mesh, faces, true)`.
- Step 2 (Connection Scoring): Allocates `connections = Dictionary<EdgeLookup, float>()`. Iterates all face wings via `WingedEdgeEnumerator`. For each boundary edge with `border.opposite != null`, computes `score = mesh.GetQuadScore(border, border.opposite)` and registers `connections.Add(border.edge, score)`.
- Step 3 (Mutual Best-Neighbor Matching):
  - Iterates each face in `wings`. If not already in `processed = HashSet<Face>()`:
  - Evaluates all border wings of the face via `WingedEdgeEnumerator`.
  - For each border with `border.opposite != null` and unprocessed opposite face, queries `borderScore` in `connections`.
  - Matching Constraint: The edge is selected if `borderScore > bestScore` AND the opposite face's best neighbor is confirmed to be this face via `face.face == GetBestQuadConnection(border.opposite, connections)`.
  - If a mutual match `buddy` is found, registers `processed.Add(buddy)` and records the paired faces `quads.Add(new KeyValuePair<Face, Face>(face.face, buddy))`.
- Step 4 (Pair Merging): Invokes `MergeElements.MergePairs(mesh, quads, smoothing)` to combine each face pair into a unified 4-sided `Face`.

2. Quad Quality Scoring Algorithm (`GetQuadScore`):
- Signature: `float GetQuadScore(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, WingedEdge left, WingedEdge right, float normalThreshold = 0.9f)`.
- Step 1 (Topology Validation): Invokes `WingedEdge.MakeQuad(left, right)`. If the resulting vertex array `quad` is null (not exactly two triangles sharing 1 edge), returns `0f`.
- Step 2 (Normal Coplanarity Test):
  - Computes triangle normals: `leftNormal = Math.Normal(v[quad[0]], v[quad[1]], v[quad[2]])` and `rightNormal = Math.Normal(v[quad[2]], v[quad[3]], v[quad[0]])`.
  - Calculates dot product `score = Vector3.Dot(leftNormal, rightNormal)`.
  - If `score < normalThreshold` (default $0.9$, corresponding to an angle $\approx 25.84^\circ$), returns `0f`.
- Step 3 (Corner Orthogonality Test):
  - Computes normalized perimeter vectors: `a = (v[1]-v[0]).normalized`, `b = (v[2]-v[1]).normalized`, `c = (v[3]-v[2]).normalized`, `d = (v[0]-v[3]).normalized`.
  - Calculates absolute dot products between adjacent edges: `da = |a·b|`, `db = |b·c|`, `dc = |c·d|`, `dd = |d·a|`.
  - For right angles ($90^\circ$), adjacent dot products equal 0.
  - Adds orthogonality contribution: `score += 1f - ((da + db + dc + dd) * 0.25f)`.
- Step 4 (Opposite Edge Parallelism Test):
  - Calculates absolute dot products between opposite edges: `|a·c|` and `|b·d|`.
  - Adds parallelism contribution: `score += |a·c| * 0.5f + |b·d| * 0.5f`.
- Step 5 (Normalization): Scales total accumulated score (3 metric contributions of up to 1.0 each) by $0.33f$: `return score * 0.33f`.

3. Quad Verification and Conversion on `Face` (`Face.IsQuad` and `Face.ToQuad`):
- `Face.IsQuad()`: Verifies whether `edgesInternal != null && edgesInternal.Length == 4`.
- `Face.ToQuad()`: Validates `IsQuad()` and constructs an ordered 4-vertex quad array `int[4] { edgesInternal[0].a, edgesInternal[0].b, -1, -1 }`. Chains `quad[2]` by matching `edgesInternal[i].a == quad[1]`, then chains `quad[3]` by matching `edgesInternal[j].a == quad[2]`. Throws `InvalidOperationException` if the face is not representable as a quad.

```csharp
         * normalThreshold will discard any quads where the dot product of their normals is less than the threshold.
         * @todo Abstract the quad detection to a separate class so it can be applied to pb_Objects.
         */
        static float GetQuadScore(this ProBuilderMesh mesh, WingedEdge left, WingedEdge right, float normalThreshold = .9f)
        {
            Vertex[] vertices = mesh.GetVertices();

            int[] quad = WingedEdge.MakeQuad(left, right);

            if (quad == null)
                return 0f;

            // first check normals
            Vector3 leftNormal = Math.Normal(vertices[quad[0]].position, vertices[quad[1]].position, vertices[quad[2]].position);
            Vector3 rightNormal = Math.Normal(vertices[quad[2]].position, vertices[quad[3]].position, vertices[quad[0]].position);

            float score = Vector3.Dot(leftNormal, rightNormal);

            if (score < normalThreshold)
                return 0f;

            // next is right-angle-ness check
            Vector3 a = (vertices[quad[1]].position - vertices[quad[0]].position);
            Vector3 b = (vertices[quad[2]].position - vertices[quad[1]].position);
            Vector3 c = (vertices[quad[3]].position - vertices[quad[2]].position);
            Vector3 d = (vertices[quad[0]].position - vertices[quad[3]].position);

            a.Normalize();
            b.Normalize();
            c.Normalize();
            d.Normalize();

            float da = Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(a, b));
            float db = Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(b, c));
            float dc = Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(c, d));
            float dd = Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(d, a));

            score += 1f - ((da + db + dc + dd) * .25f);

            // and how close to parallel the opposite sides area
            score += Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(a, c)) * .5f;
            score += Mathf.Abs(Vector3.Dot(b, d)) * .5f;

            // the three tests each contribute 1
            return score * .33f;
        }
    }
```

```csharp
        public bool IsQuad()

        /// <summary>
        /// Converts a two-triangle face to a quad representation.
        /// </summary>
        /// <returns>A quad (an array of four indices); or null if indices are not able to be represented as a quad.</returns>
        public int[] ToQuad()
        {
            if (!IsQuad())
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Face is not representable as a quad. Use Face.IsQuad to check for validity.");

            int[] quad = new int[4] { edgesInternal[0].a, edgesInternal[0].b, -1, -1 };

            if (edgesInternal[1].a == quad[1])
                quad[2] = edgesInternal[1].b;
            else if (edgesInternal[2].a == quad[1])
                quad[2] = edgesInternal[2].b;
            else if (edgesInternal[3].a == quad[1])
                quad[2] = edgesInternal[3].b;

            if (edgesInternal[1].a == quad[2])
                quad[3] = edgesInternal[1].b;
            else if (edgesInternal[2].a == quad[2])
                quad[3] = edgesInternal[2].b;
            else if (edgesInternal[3].a == quad[2])
                quad[3] = edgesInternal[3].b;

            return quad;
        }
```

### SUBMESH MAPPING AND TOPOLOGY

The `Submesh` class (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Submesh`) encapsulates a subset of mesh indices assigned to a specific material slot, maintaining topology format (`MeshTopology.Triangles` or `MeshTopology.Quads`) and managing conversion between triangles and quads.

1. Structural Properties and Fields:
- `m_Indexes` (`int[]`): Backing array of vertex indices defining the submesh geometry. Exposed via public property `indexes` (`IEnumerable<int>`), which returns a `ReadOnlyCollection<int>(m_Indexes)` on read and copies via `m_Indexes = value.ToArray()` on write.
- `m_Topology` (`MeshTopology`): Stores the submesh primitive topology. ProBuilder explicitly supports `MeshTopology.Triangles` and `MeshTopology.Quads`. Exposed via property `topology`.
- `m_SubmeshIndex` (`int`): Zero-based integer index corresponding to the material index in `Renderer.sharedMaterials`. Exposed via property `submeshIndex`.

2. Submesh Generation Algorithm (`GetSubmeshes`):
- Signature: `Submesh[] GetSubmeshes(IEnumerable<Face> faces, int submeshCount, MeshTopology preferredTopology = MeshTopology.Triangles)`.
- Step 1 (Validation): Throws `NotImplementedException` if `preferredTopology` is neither `MeshTopology.Triangles` nor `MeshTopology.Quads`. Throws `ArgumentNullException` if `faces` is null.
- Step 2 (Index Bucket Allocation): Allocates `List<int>[] tris = new List<int>[submeshCount]` and conditional quad list array `List<int>[] quads = wantsQuads ? new List<int>[submeshCount] : null`.
- Step 3 (Face Partitioning):
  - Iterates through each `Face face` in `faces`.
  - Clamps face submesh index to valid range: `int submeshIndex = Math.Clamp(face.submeshIndex, 0, maxSubmeshIndex)`.
  - Updates tracking index: `maxSubmeshIndexUsed = Mathf.Max(submeshIndex, maxSubmeshIndexUsed)`.
  - If `wantsQuads && face.IsQuad()`: appends the 4 quad indices from `face.ToQuad()` to `quads[submeshIndex]`.
  - Otherwise: appends triangle indices `face.indexesInternal` to `tris[submeshIndex]`.
- Step 4 (Submesh Array Assembly):
  - Resizes submesh array count to `maxSubmeshIndexUsed + 1`.
  - Case `MeshTopology.Triangles`: Instantiates `new Submesh(submeshIndex, MeshTopology.Triangles, tris[submeshIndex])` for each submesh slot.
  - Case `MeshTopology.Quads` with Mixed Fallback: For each submesh slot, if `tris[submeshIndex].Count > 0` (submesh contains a mix of triangles and quads), the submesh falls back entirely to `MeshTopology.Triangles`. It converts all quad indices into triangles (6 indices per quad) using the winding pattern:
    - Triangle 1: `(quad[i + 0], quad[i + 1], quad[i + 2])`
    - Triangle 2: `(quad[i + 2], quad[i + 3], quad[i + 0])`
    - Combines them into `int[] triangles = new int[triCount + ((quadCount / 4) * 6)]`.
  - If pure quads (`tris[submeshIndex].Count == 0`), instantiates `new Submesh(submeshIndex, MeshTopology.Quads, quads[submeshIndex])`.

3. Submesh Material Synchronization:
- `GetSubmeshCount(ProBuilderMesh mesh)`: Computes submesh count by taking `Mathf.Max(count, face.submeshIndex) + 1` across `mesh.facesInternal`.
- `MapFaceMaterialsToSubmeshIndex(ProBuilderMesh mesh)`: Synchronizes face material assignments with `mesh.renderer.sharedMaterials`. For each face with a assigned `face.material`, finds `index = Array.IndexOf(materials, face.material)`, clamps to `[0, submeshCount - 1]`, writes to `face.submeshIndex`, and clears legacy `face.material = null`.

# Boolean/CSG

## M01: CSG boolean operations

### CSG ALGORITHM

The Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) implementation in ProBuilder is based on Binary Space Partitioning (BSP) trees, adapted from Evan Wallace's csg.js and Tomasz Dabrowski's csgjs-cpp libraries. The algorithm executes three fundamental Boolean operations: `Union`, `Subtract`, and `Intersect` via recursive plane-based polygon clipping and tree merging.

1. Algorithmic Foundation and Representation:
- Geometry is represented as solid volumes bounded by planar polygons. A BSP tree (`Node`) recursively partitions 3D space with splitting hyperplanes.
- Inside the BSP tree, internal nodes store partitioning planes (`Plane`) and coplanar polygons (`polygons`), while child links (`front` and `back`) represent positive half-space (outside) and negative half-space (inside) solid regions.

2. Union Operation (`Node.Union(Node a1, Node b1)`):
- Operation definition: $A \cup B$.
- Step 1: Deep-clones both input BSP trees into working instances `Node a = a1.Clone()` and `Node b = b1.Clone()`.
- Step 2: `a.ClipTo(b)` removes all polygons in BSP tree `a` that lie inside the solid interior of BSP tree `b`.
- Step 3: `b.ClipTo(a)` removes all polygons in BSP tree `b` that lie inside the solid interior of BSP tree `a`.
- Step 4: `b.Invert()` inverts tree `b` (swapping interior solid space and exterior empty space).
- Step 5: `b.ClipTo(a)` clips the inverted tree `b` against `a`, which eliminates coplanar faces with identical orientations to prevent duplicate coincident geometry.
- Step 6: `b.Invert()` restores tree `b` back to its original orientation.
- Step 7: `a.Build(b.AllPolygons())` inserts all remaining polygons from `b` into tree `a`.
- Step 8: `new Node(a.AllPolygons())` compiles and returns the merged BSP tree.

3. Subtraction Operation (`Node.Subtract(Node a1, Node b1)`):
- Operation definition: $A - B = A \cap \neg B$.
- Step 1: Deep-clones both input BSP trees into `Node a = a1.Clone()` and `Node b = b1.Clone()`.
- Step 2: `a.Invert()` flips solid space and empty space in tree `a`.
- Step 3: `a.ClipTo(b)` removes portions of `a` inside `b`.
- Step 4: `b.ClipTo(a)` removes portions of `b` inside inverted `a`.
- Step 5: `b.Invert()` flips tree `b`.
- Step 6: `b.ClipTo(a)` clips inverted `b` against `a`.
- Step 7: `b.Invert()` restores tree `b`.
- Step 8: `a.Build(b.AllPolygons())` merges surviving polygons from `b` into `a`.
- Step 9: `a.Invert()` reinverts tree `a` back to solid space.
- Step 10: `new Node(a.AllPolygons())` returns the subtracted solid tree.

4. Intersection Operation (`Node.Intersect(Node a1, Node b1)`):
- Operation definition: $A \cap B = \neg(\neg A \cup \neg B)$.
- Step 1: Deep-clones both input BSP trees into `Node a = a1.Clone()` and `Node b = b1.Clone()`.
- Step 2: `a.Invert()` flips solid space and empty space in tree `a`.
- Step 3: `b.ClipTo(a)` clips tree `b` against inverted `a`.
- Step 4: `b.Invert()` flips tree `b`.
- Step 5: `a.ClipTo(b)` clips `a` against inverted `b`.
- Step 6: `b.ClipTo(a)` clips `b` against `a`.
- Step 7: `a.Build(b.AllPolygons())` inserts surviving polygons of `b` into tree `a`.
- Step 8: `a.Invert()` reinverts tree `a` back to solid space.
- Step 9: `new Node(a.AllPolygons())` returns the intersection solid tree.

```csharp
        public static Node Union(Node a1, Node b1)
        {
            Node a = a1.Clone();
            Node b = b1.Clone();
        
            a.ClipTo(b);
            b.ClipTo(a);
            b.Invert();
            b.ClipTo(a);
            b.Invert();
        
            a.Build(b.AllPolygons());
        
            Node ret = new Node(a.AllPolygons());
        
            return ret;
        }
```

### NODE

The `Node` class in `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Csg` represents a single node in a Binary Space Partitioning (BSP) tree. Each node holds partitioning plane data, coplanar polygon lists, and recursive child node links.

1. Node Structure and Storage Fields:
- `public List<Polygon> polygons`: Stores all coplanar `Polygon` instances situated precisely on this node's partitioning hyperplane.
- `public Node front`: Reference to the child subtree containing polygons in front of the splitting plane (positive half-space: $N \cdot P - w > 0$).
- `public Node back`: Reference to the child subtree containing polygons behind the splitting plane (negative half-space: $N \cdot P - w < 0$).
- `public Plane plane`: The splitting `Plane` containing normal unit vector `normal` and signed distance offset `w`.

2. Node Construction and Cloning:
- `public Node()`: Default constructor, initializes `front = null` and `back = null`.
- `public Node(List<Polygon> list)`: Invokes `Build(list)` to partition input polygons into this node and its descendant subtrees.
- `public Node(List<Polygon> list, Plane plane, Node front, Node back)`: Parameterized constructor initializing all four core members.
- `public Node Clone()`: Creates a shallow copy of the node referencing current `polygons`, `plane`, `front`, and `back`.

3. BSP Tree Construction (`Build(List<Polygon> list)`):
- Early exit: If `list.Count < 1`, returns immediately.
- Splitting plane selection: If `plane == null || !plane.Valid()`, initializes `plane = new Plane()` adopting `list[0].plane.normal` and `list[0].plane.w`.
- Coplanar allocation: If `polygons == null`, allocates `new List<Polygon>()`.
- Polygon partitioning: Iterates through `list`, calling `plane.SplitPolygon(list[i], polygons, polygons, listFront, listBack)`.
- Front recursive build: If `listFront.Count > 0`, checks `if (newNode && list.SequenceEqual(listFront))` to catch numerical epsilon partitioning failure; if detected, appends `listFront` directly to `polygons`. Otherwise, allocates `front = new Node()` if null and calls `front.Build(listFront)`.
- Back recursive build: If `listBack.Count > 0`, checks `if (newNode && list.SequenceEqual(listBack))`; if detected, appends `listBack` to `polygons`. Otherwise, allocates `back = new Node()` if null and calls `back.Build(listBack)`.

4. Solid Inversion (`Invert()`):
- Iterates `polygons` and calls `this.polygons[i].Flip()` on each polygon (reversing vertex order and inverting normals).
- Inverts splitting plane orientation via `this.plane.Flip()` (negating `normal` and `w`).
- Recursively invokes `Invert()` on `front` and `back` subtrees.
- Swaps child references: `Node tmp = this.front; this.front = this.back; this.back = tmp;`.

5. Polygon Clipping (`ClipTo(Node other)` and `ClipPolygons(List<Polygon> list)`):
- `ClipTo(Node other)`: Replaces `this.polygons = other.ClipPolygons(this.polygons)` and recursively calls `front.ClipTo(other)` and `back.ClipTo(other)`.
- `ClipPolygons(List<Polygon> list)`: If `!this.plane.Valid()`, returns input `list`. Splits each polygon in `list` using `this.plane.SplitPolygon(list[i], list_front, list_back, list_front, list_back)`. Recursively clips `list_front` through `this.front.ClipPolygons(list_front)`. If `this.back != null`, clips `list_back` through `this.back.ClipPolygons(list_back)`; if `this.back == null`, calls `list_back.Clear()` (discarding polygons embedded in solid interior). Merges `list_front.AddRange(list_back)` and returns `list_front`.

6. Polygon Aggregation (`AllPolygons()`):
- Collects `this.polygons` and concatenates `front.AllPolygons()` and `back.AllPolygons()`, returning the complete list of surviving polygons in the BSP tree.

```csharp
        public void ClipTo(Node other)
        {
            this.polygons = other.ClipPolygons(this.polygons);

            if (this.front != null)
            {
                this.front.ClipTo(other);
            }

            if (this.back != null)
            {
                this.back.ClipTo(other);
            }
        }

        // Convert solid space to empty space and empty space to solid space.
        public void Invert()
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < this.polygons.Count; i++)
                this.polygons[i].Flip();

            this.plane.Flip();

            if (this.front != null)
            {
                this.front.Invert();
            }

            if (this.back != null)
            {
                this.back.Invert();
            }

            Node tmp = this.front;
            this.front = this.back;
            this.back = tmp;
        }
```

```csharp
        public void Build(List<Polygon> list)
        {
            if (list.Count < 1)
                return;

            bool newNode = plane == null || !plane.Valid(); 

            if (newNode)
            {
                plane = new Plane();
                plane.normal = list[0].plane.normal;
                plane.w = list[0].plane.w;
            }

            if (polygons == null)
                polygons = new List<Polygon>();
                
            var listFront = new List<Polygon>();
            var listBack = new List<Polygon>();

            for (int i = 0; i < list.Count; i++)
                plane.SplitPolygon(list[i], polygons, polygons, listFront, listBack);
            
            
            if (listFront.Count > 0)
            {                
                // SplitPolygon can fail to correctly identify coplanar planes when the epsilon value is too low. When
                // this happens, the front or back list will be filled and built into a new node recursively. This 
                // check catches that case and sorts the front/back lists into the coplanar polygons collection.
                if (newNode && list.SequenceEqual(listFront))
                    polygons.AddRange(listFront);
                else
                    (front ?? (front = new Node())).Build(listFront);
            }

            if (listBack.Count > 0)
            {
                if (newNode && list.SequenceEqual(listBack))
                    polygons.AddRange(listBack);
                else
                    (back ?? (back = new Node())).Build(listBack);
            }
        }
```
